[See A^ajorN , below.] A^ujira fulaAnN xamosapF mino waladihi [ Such a one became entitled to a reward for five of his children, by their death, (for it is believed that the Muslim will be rewarded in Paradise for a child that has died in infancy)], (S,) and A^ujira waladahu , (A,) and A^ujira fiy A^awolaAdihi , (K,) mean that his children died, and became [causes of] his reward. (TA.) ― -b3- A^ajarahu , aor. , (L, Msb, K,) and , (Msb, K,) inf. n. A^ajorN , (L, K,) He let him (namely his slave) on hire, or for pay, or wages; (L, * Msb, * K;) as also ↓ A=jrhu , inf. n. A_iyjaArN ; ('Eyn, Mgh, Msb, K;) and ↓ A=jrhu , inf. n. mw^Ajrp : (K:) all these are good forms of speech, used by the Arabs: (L:) or ↓ A=jrhu having for its inf. n. mw^Ajrp signifies he appointed him (namely another man) hire, pay, or wages, for his work; (Mj, Mgh;) or he engaged with him to give him hire, pay, or wages; (A, Mgh, Msb;) and can have only one objective complement: whereas, ↓ when it is of the measure A^afoEala it is doubly trans.; (Mgh, Msb;) so that one says, mamoluwkahu ↓ A=jaraniy He let me his slave on hire. A_iyjaArN ,] He let to him the house on hire: (S, A, Mgh, Msb:) the latter verb being of the measure A^afoEala , not of the measure faAEala : (A, Mgh, Msb:) and the vulgar say, waAjara : (S:) some, however, say, Ald~aAra ↓ A=jarotu , inf. n. muw^aAjarapN , making the verb of the measure fAEl : (Msb, TA:) some also say, Ald~aAra zayod~aA ↓ A=jarotu [ I let the house to Zeyd ], inverting the order of the words: (Msb, TA:) and the lawyers say, Ald~aAra mino zayodK ↓ A=jarotu [in the same sense, like as biEotu mino zayodK Ald~aAri means the same as biEotu zayodAF Ald~aAra ]. (Msb: [but in the Mgh, the like of this is said to be vulgar.])

definition: A recompense, compensation, or reward, (S, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: A recompense, compensation, or reward, (S, K, &c.,) for what one has done; (K;) i. q. vawaAbN ; (S;) as also ↓ A_ijaArapN and ↓ A^ajaArapN and ↓ A^NjaArapN , (K,) of which three forms the first is the most generally known and the most chaste, (TA,) and ↓ A^ujorapN : (TA:) or, as some say, there is a distinction between A^ajorN and vawaAbN : El-'Eynee says, in the Expos. of El-Bukháree, that what is obtained by the fundamental practices of the law, and by obligatory religious services, is termed vwAb ; and what is obtained by supererogatory acts of religion, Ajr ; for vwAb is properly a substitute for a thing itself; and Ajr , for the profit arising from a thing; though each is sometimes used in the sense of the other: (TA:) it is well known that Ajr signifies a recompense, or reward, from God to a man, for righteous conduct; (MF;) and ↓ A_ijaArapN , recompense, compensation, hire, pay, or wages, from one man to another, for work; (Mgh, MF;) and hence AlA^ajiyru ; (MF;) and ↓ A^ujorapN also has this latter signification, (Mgh, TA,) and is syn. with kiraA='N ; (S, Mgh, K;) [signifying likewise rent for a house, and the like; ] but A^ajorN is used [sometimes] in the sense of A_ijaArapN and in that of A^ujorapN : (Msb:) the pl. of A^ajorN is A^ujuwrN (Msb, K) and A=jaArN ; (K;) but the latter form was unknown to MF: (TA:) the pl. of ↓ A^ujorapN is A^ajarN and A^ujuraAtN and A^ujaraAtN . (Msb.) [One says, A^ajoruka Ealay All~`hi Thy recompense is due from God. And, to console a person for the death of a relation or friend, EaZ~ama All~`hu A^ajoraka fiyhi May God largely compensate thee for him! i. e., for the loss of him.] By the expression A^ajorK kiriymK in the Kur xxxvi. 10 is said to be meant Paradise. (TA.) ― -b2- (tropical:) A dowry, or nuptial gift; a gift that is given to, or for, a bride: (K:) pl. A^ujuwrN : so in the Kur xxxiii. 49 [&c.]. (TA.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) Praise; good fame. (K.) So, as some say, in the Kur xxix. 26. (TA.)

rawSourceText: A recompense, compensation, or reward, (S, K, &c.,) for what one has done; (K;) i. q. vawaAbN ; (S;) as also ↓ A_ijaArapN and ↓ A^ajaArapN and ↓ A^NjaArapN , (K,) of which three forms the first is the most generally known and the most chaste, (TA,) and ↓ A^ujorapN : (TA:) or, as some say, there is a distinction between A^ajorN and vawaAbN : El-'Eynee says, in the Expos. of El-Bukháree, that what is obtained by the fundamental practices of the law, and by obligatory religious services, is termed vwAb ; and what is obtained by supererogatory acts of religion, Ajr ; for vwAb is properly a substitute for a thing itself; and Ajr , for the profit arising from a thing; though each is sometimes used in the sense of the other: (TA:) it is well known that Ajr signifies a recompense, or reward, from God to a man, for righteous conduct; (MF;) and ↓ A_ijaArapN , recompense, compensation, hire, pay, or wages, from one man to another, for work; (Mgh, MF;) and hence AlA^ajiyru ; (MF;) and ↓ A^ujorapN also has this latter signification, (Mgh, TA,) and is syn. with kiraA='N ; (S, Mgh, K;) [signifying likewise rent for a house, and the like; ] but A^ajorN is used [sometimes] in the sense of A_ijaArapN and in that of A^ujorapN : (Msb:) the pl. of A^ajorN is A^ujuwrN (Msb, K) and A=jaArN ; (K;) but the latter form was unknown to MF: (TA:) the pl. of ↓ A^ujorapN is A^ajarN and A^ujuraAtN and A^ujaraAtN . definition: , signifying The podex, or the anus, (K,) or signifying the former, and sometimes used as meaning the latter, (S in art.
sourceDefinition: , signifying The podex, or the anus, (K,) or signifying the former, and sometimes used as meaning the latter, (S in art. sth ,) is with a conjunctive hemzeh, [written A@sotN , when not immediately preceded by a quiescence,] and its final radical letter is clided; for the original form is satahN ; (Msb;) and it is mentioned in art. sth . (K.) [It is of the fem. gender.] It is said in a prov., applied to him who fails of attaining the object that he seeks, A^axoTaA^ati A@sotuhu AlHuforapa [ His anus missed the hole in the ground ]. (Meyd.) — [Hence,] Aisotu Ald~ahori (tropical:) The first, or beginning, of time; (A;) old, or ancient, time. (IB, A, * K. *) One says, maA zaAla EalaY A@soti Ald~ahori majonuwnFA (tropical:) [ He ceased not, or has not ceased, from the beginning of time, or from old time, to be insane, or mad; or] he always was, or always has been, known as being insane, or mad: like as one says, EalaY A_is~i Ald~ahori . (AZ, S.) And Aboo-Nukheyleh says, maA zaAla mu*o kaAna EalaY A@ soti Ald~ahori *aA HumuqK yanomiY waEaqolK yaHor$Y (tropical:) [ He ceased not, or has not ceased, to be, since he was in the beginning of time, or in old time, i. e., from the first of his existence, a person of increasing foolishness, and of decreasing intellect ]. (AZ, S.) IB says, J has erred in mentioning Ast in this section [of the S]; its proper place being in art. sth , where he has also mentioned it; for its hemzeh is conjunctive, by common consent; and if conjunctive, it is augmentative: also, his saying that they have changed the [final] s in A_is~N into t , like as they have changed the [final] s of Tas~N into t , making this word TasotN , is a mistake; for, were it so, the hemzeh of Ast would be disjunctive [in every case; whereas it is always conjunctive except after a pause, when it is pronounced with kesr]: moreover, he has attributed this assertion to AZ, who never made it, but only mentioned Ast Aldhr with As~ Aldhr because of their agreement in meaning. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence also,] Aisotu Alkalobapi (assumed tropical:) Calamity, or misfortune: (K:) adversity; difficulty; distress; affliction: (TA:) what is hated, disliked, disapproved, foul, abominable, or evil. (K.) ― -b3- And Aisotu Almatoni (assumed tropical:) The desert: (K:) or the wide desert. (TA.) ― -b4- See also art. sth .

definition: , aor. , inf. n. A^asafN , (M, Msb, K,) He grieved, lamented, or regretted: and he was angry: (Msb:) or he grieved exceedingly: and he was exceedingly angry: (M:) or he grieved most intensely: (K:)...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. A^asafN , (M, Msb, K,) He grieved, lamented, or regretted: and he was angry: (Msb:) or he grieved exceedingly: and he was exceedingly angry: (M:) or he grieved most intensely: (K:) some say that A^asafN signifies the grieving for a thing that has escaped; not in an absolute sense: (MF:) or it properly signifies the rising, or swelling, or mantling, of the blood of the heart, from desire of vengeance; and when this is against an inferior, it is anger; but when against a superior, it is grief. (Er-Rághib.) Mo- hammad, being asked respecting sudden death, answered, saying, raAHapN lilomuw^omini waA^axo*apu A^asafK lilokaAfiri , or accord. to one recital, ↓ A^asifK , i. e. [ Rest, or ease, to the believer, and an act of punishment ] of anger [ to the unbeliever ], or of one who is angry. (K.) You say, A^asifa EalaY maA faAtahu , inf. n. as above; (S;) and ↓ tA^s~f ; (S, M, * K; *) He grieved, or lamented, for, or at, or regretted, most intensely, what had escaped him: (S, M, * K:) and A^asifa Ealayohi , (S, K,) inf. n. as above, (S,) he was angry with him, or at it: (S, K:) or A^asifa fulaAnN EalaY ka*aA waka*aA and ↓ tA^s~f , signify, accord. to some, such a one grieved, or lamented, for, or at, such and such things which had escaped him: or, accord. to others, grieved, or lamented, most intensely. definition: A measure of distance [&c.
sourceDefinition: A measure of distance [&c.]; as in the saying, kamo A^amotu bayonaka maA bayona Alkuwfapi What is the measure of the distance between thee and El-Koofeh? (T, TA.) -A2- Doubt: (Th, T, M:) said to be so termed because this word signifies the “ computing, or conjecturing, measure, quantity, and the like, ” in which there is doubt. (T, TA.) [See 1.] So in the following ex.: Alxamoru Harumato laA A^amota fiyhaA Wine is unlawful: there is no doubt respecting the unlawfulness of it: (Sh, Th, T, K:) or the meaning is, there is no indulgence, or lenity, with respect to it; from A^amotN as signifying “feebleness, or weakness,” in a journey, or pace. (T, TA.) And in the saying, layosa fY Alxamori A^amotN There is no doubt respecting wine, that it is unlawful. (Th, M.) [Or in the like of these two instances it signifies] Disagreement, or diversity of opinion, ( AixotilaAfN ,) respecting a thing ( fiY $aYo'K ). (M, K.) -A3- Curvity, crookedness, distortion, or unevenness: (M, K:) ruggedness in one place and smoothness in another; (K;) [ inequality of surface; ] one part being higher, or more prominent, than another: (TA:) an elevated place: (T, S, K:) small mounds: (Fr, Th, T, S, M, K:) or what is elevated, of ground: or, as some say, water-courses of valleys, such as are low, or depressed: (Fr, T, TA:) small hills; hillocks: (M, TA:) a hollow, or depressed place, between any two elevated portions of ground &c.: (IAar, T, M:) depression and elevation, or lowness and highness, (S, M, A, K,) in the ground; (A;) used in this sense in the Kur xx. 106; (S;) and the same in a water-skin not completely filled: (S, A: *) or laxity in a water-skin when it is not well filled so as to overflow: (T, * TA:) or a [ consequence of ] pouring [ water ] into a skin until it doubles, or creases, and not filling it; so that one part of it is higher, or more prominent, than another: (M, TA:) pl. A_imaAtN (M, K, TA, but in some copies of the K A=maAtN , and in the CK AamAtN ,) and A^umuwtN . (M, K.) You say, Asotawati AlA^aroDu famaA bahaA A^amotN The earth, or ground, was even, so that there was not in it any depression and elevation. (A, TA.) And AimotalaA^a Als~iqaA='u famaA bihi A^amotN The skin became full, so that there was not in it any depression [ of one part of its surface ] and elevation [ of another part ]. (S, A. *) Az says, (TA,) I have heard the Arabs say, qado malaA^a Alqirobapa maloA^F laA A^amota fiyhi He had filled the water-skin so full that there was no laxity in it. (T, TA.) ― -b2- A fault, a defect, an imperfection, a blemish, or the like, (T, M, K,) in the mouth, and in a garment, or piece of cloth, and in a stone. (M, K.) [Hence the saying,] A^amotN fiY AlHajari laA fiyka i. e. [ May there be a defect, or the like, ] in stones; not in thee: meaning, may God preserve thee when the stones shall have perished: (Sb, M:) Amt is here put in the nom. case, though the phrase is significant of a prayer, because it is not a verbal word: the phrase is like Alt~urAbu laho : and the commencing the sentence with an indeterminate noun is approvable because it is virtually a prayer. (M.) This prov. is mentioned by the expositors of the Tes-heel: not by Meyd. (TA.) ― -b3- Weakness; feebleness; (T, K;) langour; remissness. (TA.) You say, sironaA sayorFA laA A^amota fiyhi We performed a journey, or went a pace, in which was no weakness, or feebleness [&c.]. (T, TA.) -A4- A good way, course, mode, or manner, of acting, or conduct, or the like. (T, K.)

(TA.)

definition: Sociableness; companionableness; conversableness; inclination to company or converse; friendliness; amicableness; socialness; familiarity: cheerfulness; gayness; gladsomeness: contr. of waHo$apN :...
sourceDefinition: Sociableness; companionableness; conversableness; inclination to company or converse; friendliness; amicableness; socialness; familiarity: cheerfulness; gayness; gladsomeness: contr. of waHo$apN : (T, S, A, K:) joy; gladness; happiness: (Har p. 652:) or ease, or tranquillity: (M:) or ease, or tranquillity, of heart, and freedom from shrinking, or from aversion: (Msb:) an inf. n. of 1, (S, M,) as are also ↓ A^anasN and ↓ A^anasapN (S, K) and ↓ A_inosN , (M,) but this is rare as signifying the contr. of waHo$apN : (T, TA:) or ↓ A_inosN is the inf. n. of A^anisa bihi ; but A^unusN is not: (AZ, AHát, Msb, TA:) this latter is a subst. from that verb [signifying as explained above]: (Msb:) or only signifying converse, and companionship, or familiarity, with women; (AZ, AHát, TA;) or amatory conversation and conduct; or the talk of young men and young women: (Fr, TA:) [but of all the forms above, A^unosN is that which is most commonly used, at least in post-classical works, as signifying the contr. of waHo$apN .] ― -b2- [Also (assumed tropical:) Delight, as meaning a cause of delight, or thing that gives delight. ] A poet says, yaA saAkiniY mak~apa laA zilotumu A^unosFA lanaA A_in~iYa lamo A^anosakumo maA fiykumu EayobN siwaY qawolikumo Einoda All~iqaA A^awoHa$anaA A^unosukumo [ O inhabitants of Mekkeh, may ye not cease to be a delight to us: verily I have not forgotten you: there is in you no fault beside your saying, at meeting, Your sociableness, or companiableness, &c., has made us feel lonely and sad; meaning, in your absence]. (TA in art. wH$ .) [See A^awoHa$a . But this signification, though allowable as tropical, is perhaps post-classical.] ― -b3- Aibonu A^unos : and fulaAnN A@bonu A^unosi fulaAnK : and kayofa A@bonu A^unosika : and kayofa taraY A@bona A^unosika : see A_inosN .

definition: -A2- (tropical:) A chosen, select, particular, or special, friend or companion;
sourceDefinition: : see A^unosN , in two places. -A2- (tropical:) A chosen, select, particular, or special, friend or companion; (S, K;) as also Aibonu A_inosK (S, K,) or ↓ Aibonu A^unosK . (So in a copy of the A.) You say, h`*aA A_inosiY ; (S;) and A_inosuka , and A@bonu A_inosika ; (K;) (tropical:) This is my chosen, or particular, friend; (S;) and thy chosen, or particular, friend. (K.) And fulaAnN A@bonu A_inosi fulaAnK (S,) or flAn ↓ Abn A^unosi (A,) (tropical:) Such a one is the chosen, or particular, friend of such a one. (S, A.) One also says, kayofa A@bonu A_inosika and ↓ A^unosika , (S, M,) or kayofa taray A@bona A_inosika (AZ, Fr, A) and ↓ A^unosika , (A,) meaning himself, (AZ, Fr, S, S TA,) i. e., (assumed tropical:) How dost thou regard me in my companionship with thee? (S:) or the meaning is, (tropical:) how dost thou find thyself? (A:) or how is thyself? (M, TA.) -A3- Mankind; (S, M, A, K;) the opposite of jin~N ; (Msb;) as also ↓ A^anasN , (Akh, S, TA,) and ↓ A_inosaAnN ; (A, K;) the last being a gen. n., (Msb,) but applied to the male (S, * Msb) and female, (S, Msb, K,) and sing. and pl.: (Msb:) one is [also] termed ↓ A_inosiY~N and ↓ A^anasiY~N ; (S, K;) the former of which is a rel. n. from A_inosN ; (M;) [and the latter, from A^anasN : the fem. of each is with p :] the vulgar apply to a woman, instead of ↓ A_inosaAnN , [which is the more approved,] ↓ A_inosaAnapN : (S, K:) this latter [accord. to some] should not be used: (S:) but it is correct, though rare: it is said in the K to occur in poetry, but supposed to be post-classical: it occurs, however, in classical poetry, and has been transmitted by several authors: (MF:) the pl. (of A_inosN , M, TA) is A=naAsN ; (M, K, TA;) and (of the same, K in art. nws , or of ↓ A_inosaAnN , M) A^unaAsN , (M, K ubi suprà,) with which naAsN is syn., (S, M, Msb, K,) being a contraction thereof; (Sb, S, M, Msb;) and (of ↓ A_inosiY~N , S, M, or ↓ A^anasiY~N , S, or of ↓ A_inosaAnN , Lh, S, M, Msb) A^anaAsiY~N , (Lh, S, M, Msb, K,) like as karaAsiY~u is pl. of kurosiY~N , or like as saraAHynu is pl. of sirHaAnN , but Y being substituted for n , (M, TA,) after the same manner as they say A^araAnK for A^araAnibu ; (Fr, TA;) and A^anaAsK , (Lh, M,) in the accus. case A^anaAsiYa , as the word is read in the Kur xxv. 51, by Ks, (TA,) and by Yahyà Ibn-El-Hárith, (K, TA,) dropping the Y between the second and last radical letters, [for, with some others, it seems, they held the word to be derived from the root nsY ,] (TA,) and A^anaAsiyapN , (S, M, K,) in which the p is a substitute for one of the two yás in A^anaAsiY~u , a pl. of A_inosaAnN ; or, accord. to Mbr, A^anaAsiyapN is pl. of A_inosiY~N , [in the TA, of A_inosiy~apN , which I regard as a mistranscription,] and is like zanaAdaqapN for zanaAdiyqu , and faraAzitapN for faraAziynu ; (M, TA;) and you say also A_inosay~uwna . (TA.) naAsN is masc., as in the Kur ii. 19, &c.; and sometimes fem., as meaning A tribe, or a body of men, qabiylapN , or TaAy^ifapN ; as in the phrase, mentioned by Th, jaA='atoaka Aln~aAsu , meaning, The tribe, or portion of people ( qiToEap ), came to thee. (M, TA.) ↓ banuwAlA_inosaAni means The sons of Adam. (M.) And Aln~aAsu Aln~aAsu , an expression mentioned by Sb, means, Men in every place and in every state are men: a poet says, bilaAdN bahaA kun~aA wakun~aA nuHib~uhaA A_i*i Aln~aAsu naAsN waAlbilaAdu bilaAdu meaning [ A country in which we were, and which we used to love,] since the men were ingenuous men, and the country was a fruitful country. (M.) The following trad., lawo A^aTaAEa A@ll~`hu Aln~aAsa fiY Aln~aAsi lamo yakuno naAsN If God complied with the prayer of men with respect to men there would be no men, is said to mean, that men love to have male children born to them, and not females, and if there were no females, or if the females were not, men would cease to be. (TA.) (T. sourceDefinition: , (As, T,) and Abd~ bayonahumo AlEaTaA='a , (S, M, L, K,) and A^abad~ahumo AlEaTaA='a , (M, A, Mgh,) He divided among them the gift, giving to each of them his lot, or share, or portion, (S, M, A, Mgh, L, K,) singly, not giving a portion to be shared by two: (As, T, M, * Mgh, L:) said with respect to food and property and any other thing. (M.) You say, A^abodadotuhumo AlmaAla wa AlT~aEaAma I divided among them, in shares, the property and the food. (IAar, T.) [Hence,] A^abid~iyhimo tamorapF tamorapF (T, S, A, Mgh, from a trad.) [ Give thou to each of them a date; or] distribute thou among them to each a date: (T:) said by Umm-Selemeh, (T, A, Mgh,) to a slave-girl, when beggars had become numerous. (A.) A_ibodaAdN in relation to a gift signifies The giving [persons] one by one; and qiraAnN , the “ giving two by two. ” (A 'Obeyd, T.) [See also 3.] ― -b2- yubid~uhumo is used by a poet, referring to a saying, and is explained by IAar as meaning It (the saying) shall be distributed among them ( yuf~arqu fiyhimo ); opposed to yajomaEu [i. e. yajomaEuhumo ; which shows that the former means it shall be addressed to them one by one, or separately ]. (M, TA. [The author of the former adds, “ I know not, in discourse, A^abodadotuhu as meaning far~aqotuhu : ” but this is not what I Aar means.]) ― -b3- A^abid~ahumaA naEojatayona Allot thou to them (namely, two lambs,) two ewes, to each lamb a ewe, to suckle it: said when one ewe is not sufficient for both the lambs. (T, * S.) ― -b4- Abd~ DaboEayohi He extended his upper arms, separating them from his sides, in prostrating himself in prayer. (T, A, Mgh, L.) ― -b5- Abd~ yadahu A_ilay AlA^aroDi He extended his arm, or hand, to the ground, or earth, (T, S, Mgh, L,) as one does when he takes up something from it. (L.) ― -b6- Abd~ naZarahu He prolonged his look. (T, L.) And Abd~hu baSarahu (T, A, L) He prolonged his look at him, or it; as one does when he sees a thing that he dislikes. (T, L.)

definition: He was, or became, alone;
sourceDefinition: He was, or became, alone; independent of others; (S, M, L, Msb, K; in the first and last expl. by tafar~ada ; and in the others, by Ainofarada ;) exclusively of others; (L;) without any to share, or participate, with him; or he had none to share, or participate, with him: (Msb:) bihi [ in it; i. e. he had it, or kept it, to himself, exclusively, with none to share with him in it ]: (K:) and bika*aA [ in such a thing ]: (S, L:) and biraA^oyihi [ in his opinion; i. e. he followed his own opinion only, with none to agree with him; or he was singular in his opinion ]: (M, L:) and biA^amorK [ in a thing, or an affair ]: (L, Msb:) and biA^amorihi [ in his affair ]; meaning he obtained [absolute] predominance, or control, over his affair, so that people would not hear [or obey] any other. (A.) It is said in a trad., kun~aA naray A^an~a lanaAfiYi h`*aA AlA^amori Haq~aA faA@sotabadotumo EalayonaA [ We used to opine that we had a right to act in this affair, and ye have been alone the actors, predominant over us ]. (L.) And you say, Astbd~ AlA^amoru bifulaAnK , meaning (tropical:) The thing, or affair, overcame such a one, so that he could not manage it well, or thoroughly. (A.)

definition: as signifying A separating oneself, or an artifice whereby one may avoid a thing or escape from it, (MF,) or an avoiding a thing, (Msb,) is not used but in negative phrases, (Msb, MF,) except by post-classical writers.
sourceDefinition: as signifying A separating oneself, or an artifice whereby one may avoid a thing or escape from it, (MF,) or an avoiding a thing, (Msb,) is not used but in negative phrases, (Msb, MF,) except by post-classical writers. (MF.) You say, laA bud~a mino ka*aA (T, S, M, &c.) There is no separating oneself from such a thing: (AA, T, S, A, K:) or there is no artifice whereby one may avoid it, or escape from it: (M, K:) or there is no avoiding it: (Msb:) it is absolutely necessary: it is not possible to separate oneself from it, nor is there anything that can serve in its stead. sourceDefinition: ; (T, S;) in which bdAd is indecl., with kesr for its termination because it deviates from its original form, i. e., the inf. n. badadN ; and it is indecl. because it deviates from its original form and is of the fem. gender and has the quality of an epithet; for two of these causes render it imperfectly decl., and the three render it indecl.; (S;) or badaAdi badaAdi , and badaAda badaAda , (Lh, M, K,) the last indecl. with fet-h for its termination, (TA,) and ↓ badada badada , (Lh, M, K,) also indecl., with fet-h, (TA,) and composed in the same manner as xamosapa Ea$ara , (Lh, M, TA,) and ↓ badadFA badadFA ; (Lh, M, K;) all of these indecl. except the last, and each virtually in the accus. case as a denotative of state, except the last, (MF,) which is literally in the accus. case, as an inf. n.; (M, MF;) The horses, or horsemen, came in a state of dispersion: (T, S, M, K:) or one by one; or one after another. (T, L.) And taf~r~aqa Alqawomu badaAd The people, or company of men, became separated, in a state of dispersion. (S.) And *ahaba Alqawomu badaAdi badAdi The people, or company of men, went away [ in a state of dispersion; or] one by one; or one after another. (T, L.) [See also A^abaAdiyd .] It is said in a form of prayer, Aall`hum~a A^aHoSihimo EadadFA ↓ A@qotulohumo badadFA [ O God, slay them one by one, and reckon them by number ]: (M:) or A^aHoSihimo EadadFA wa A@loEanohumo bidadFA , or, accord. to one recital, waA@qotulohumo bidadFA , pl. of ↓ bid~apN , the meaning being [ reckon them by number, and ] curse them, or slay them, with a cursing, or slaughter, distributed among them by shares. (Mgh.) ― -b2- yaA qawomi badaAdi badaAdi means O my people, take each one of you his adversary, or opponent [ with whom to fight ]. (As, T, S, K. *) Here bdAd is indecl., with kesr for its termination, because it is an imperative verbal noun, and the imperative is alike uninfluenced with respect to its termination by any governing word; and it is said to be with kesr because two quiescent letters would otherwise occur together, [and] because it occupies the place of an imperative verb [which in like manner is terminated with kesr when it is necessary to prevent the occurrence of two quiescent letters together]. (S.) ― -b3- With the article, you say, AlbadaAdu , (As, T,) which signifies The going forth to encounter another in fight, or to single combat; as in the saying, lawo kaAna AlbadaAdu lamaA A^aTaAquwnaA Had we gone forth to encounter them in fight, (As, T, S, K,) man to man, [ they had not been able to cope with us; ] (As, T;) or man by man. (S, K.) You say also, laquwA badaAdahumo , explained above: see 6. -A2- See also bud~N . -A3- And see 3.

sourceDefinition: : see bud~N . -A2- Also A stuffed lining put beneath a [ camel's saddle of the kind called ] qatab , to defend the animal's back from being hurt thereby: there is one such on each side: (T:) or, of a horse's saddle, and of a qatab , (S, M, K,) the stuffed thing, or pad, that is placed beneath, in order that it may not gall the animal's back; (M, K;) as also ↓ badiydN : (K:) or the bidaAdaAni and ↓ badiydaAni are two bags ( xariyTataAni ), which are stuffed, and placed under the curved pieces of wood, in order that the wood may not gall the animal's back; derived from bad~a rijolayohi “ he parted his legs: ” (S:) [see also badiydN :] or the bidaAdaAni of a qatab are two things like provender-bags, 'which are stuffed, and bound with strings, or cords, to the pieces of wood called the ZalifaAt and A^aHonaA=' : (T:) or they are, to the qatab , like the kar~ to the raHol , except that they do not appear before the Zalifap , being only within [ it ]: (M:) [see also HidojN :] pl. sourceDefinition: A man wide between the thighs, (ISk, S, M, K,) by reason of abundance of flesh: (ISk, S, M:) or wide between the arms; (K;) having the arms far from the sides: (M:) or wide between the shoulder-joints: (M:) or (so in the K; but accord. to the S, “and”) large in make, (T, S, M, K,) having one part far from another: (M, K:) and wide in the breast: (Aboo-Málik, T:) fem. bad~aA='u : (S:) which also signifies a woman (M, L) large in the A_isokataAni [or labia majora of the vulva ], (M, L, K,) having their edges far apart: (M, L:) or having much flesh in the thighs. (T, L.) AlA^abad~N is used to signify The weaver, (T, M, K,) because of the distance between his thighs. (M.) The following saying, (K,) quoted by J, from the rájiz Aboo-Nukheyleh Es-Saadee, A^alad~u yamo$iY mi$ayapa AlA^abad~i is incorrect, and should be thus, bad~aA='u tamo$iY mi$oyapa AlA^abad~i [ A woman of large make, walking in the manner of the man of large make; or a woman wide between the thighs, &c.]; (K;) for it is descriptive of a woman, as IB and Aboo-Sahl El-Harawee have observed before the author of the K. (TA.) ― -b2- Also A horse [or any quadruped (see bad~a )] having the fore legs far apart: (M, K:) or having the fore legs far from the sides: (TA:) or wide between the legs: (Ham p. 348:) and a camel having the elbows far from the sides: (TA:) and the fem. bad~aA='u , a cow having her fore legs far apart. (S.) [Hence,] AlA^abad~u Alz~aniymu [in the CK Alr~aviymu ] The lion; (M, K;) the former epithet being applied to him because his fore legs are far apart, and the latter because he is [often] alone. (M.) ― -b3- katifN bad~aA='u A broad shoulder-blade, the sides of which are distant, one from another. (M, L.)

sourceDefinition: [act. part. n. of 4, q. v.]. The following words of 'Omar Ibn-Abee-Rabee'ah, A^amubid~N suw^aAlaka AlEaAlamiyna are said to signify Dost thou distribute thy petition among mankind one by one, so as to include them universally? or dost thou constrain them by thy petition? from the saying, maA laka minohu bud~N [“ thou hast no means, ” or “ way, ” “ of separating thyself from it, ” or “ avoiding it ”]. (M, L.)

definition: He looked at it;
sourceDefinition: He looked at it; namely, a thing: or looked long at it: or glanced lightly at it: like ramaqahu : (TA:) or he sought, or endeavoured, to see it: (Mgh:) or i. q. A^aboSarahu , in a sense explained above; see 4. (M.) You say also, tabaS~aro liY fulaAnFA [ Consider thou, or examine thou, for me, such a one, that thou mayest obtain a clear knowledge of him ]. (TA.) And tbS~r fiY $aYo'K He considered a thing, endeavouring to obtain a clear knowledge of it; he looked into it, considered it, examined it, or studied it, repeatedly, until he knew it: he sought, or sought leisurely, or repeatedly, after the knowledge of it, until he knew it. (S, * K, * TA.) And tbS~r fiY raA^oyihi signifies the same as fiyhi ↓ AstbSr , i. e. He sought, or endeavoured, to see, or discover, what would happen to him, of good and evil. (M.)

sourceDefinition: The sense of sight, (Lth, S,) or of the eye: (M, K:) or the light whereby the organ [ of sight ] ( AljaAriHap ) perceives the things seen ( AlmuboSaraAt ): (Msb:) pl. A^aboSaArN . (M, Msb, K.) [Hence,] SalaApu AlbaSari The prayer of sunset: or, as some say, of daybreak: because performed when the darkness becomes mixed with the light: (TA:) or because performed when the stars are seen: also called SalaApu Al$~aAhidi : (TA in art. $hd :) or because performed at a time when the eyes see corporeal forms, after the intervention of darkness, or before it. And laqiyahu baSarFA He met him when eyes saw one another: or at the beginning of darkness, when there remained enough light for objects to be distinguished thereby: [accord. to some,] the noun is used [in the sense which it here bears] only as an adv. n. [Hence,] AlbaSiyru , as a name of God, The All-seeing; He who sees all things, both what are apparent thereof and what are occult, without any organ [ of vision ]. (TA.) And The dog; (M;) as also A^abuw baSiyrK : (Msb:) because it is one of the most sharp-sighted of animals. (M.) ― -b2- Endowed with mental perception; (B;) knowing; skilful; possessing understanding, intelligence, or skill: (S, M, A, Msb, K:) pl. as above. (A.) One says, A^anaA baSiyrN bihi I am knowing in it, or respecting it. (Msb.) And A_in~ahu labaSiyrN biAlA^a$oyaA='i Verily he is knowing, or skilful, in things. (Lh, M.) And rajulN baSiyrN biAlEilomi A man knowing, or skilful, in science. (M.) And huwa mina AlbuSaraA='i biAlit~jaArapi He is of those who are knowing, or skilful, in commerce. (A.) ― -b3- It is also an epithet applied to A blind man; (A'Obeyd, M, B;) and so A^abuw baSiyrK : (TA in art. Ewr :) so applied as meaning endowed with mental perception; (B;) or as meaning a believer; (A'Obeyd, M;) or as an epithet of good omen: (M:) and A^abuw baSiyrK is used as meaning AlA^aEo$aY [ the weaksighted, &c.,] for this last reason. (M.) -A2- See also baSiyrapN .

definition: Mental perception;
sourceDefinition: Mental perception; the perceptive faculty of the mind; as also ↓ baSarN : (B:) knowledge; (Msb;) as also ↓ baSarN (S, Msb) and AisotiboSaArN : (Msb:) understanding; intelligence; skill: (M, K:) AlbaSiyrapu signifies AlAi sotiboSaAru fiY Al$~aYo'i [which implies all the meanings above: see 10]: (S:) and Alqalobi ↓ baSaru [in like manner] signifies mental perception or vision or view; idea, or opinion, occurring to the mind: (M, K:) the pl. of baSiyrapN is baSaAy^ru ; (M, B;) and the pl. of ↓ baSarN , as syn. therewith, A^aboSaArN . (B.) [Sometimes it is opposed to baSarN , as in the first and second of the following exs.] A^ahuwnu mino EimaY AlbaSaAy^iri ↓ EamaY AlA^aboSaAri [ Blindness of the eyes is a lighter thing than blindness of the perceptive faculties of the mind ]. (A.) When Mo'áwiyeh said to Ibn-'Abbás, yaAbaniY ↓ haA$imK tuSaAbuwna fiY A^aboSaArikumo [ O sons of Háshim, ye are afflicted in your eyes ], the latter replied, waA^anotumo yaA baniY A^umay~apa tuSaAbuwna fiY baSaAy^irikumo [ And ye, O sons of Umeiyeh, are afflicted in your perceptive faculties of the mind ]. (M.) And the Arabs say, A^aEomaY A@ll~`hu baSaAy^irapu May God blind his faculties of understanding! And one says, lahu firaAsapN *aAtu baSiyrapK , and baSaAy^ira , (tropical:) He possesses true intuitive perception. (A.) And raA^ayotu Ealayoka *aAta AlbaSaAy^iri (tropical:) [ I saw impressed upon thee the signs of perceptive faculties of the mind ]. (A.) ― -b2- Also Belief, or firm belief, of the heart, or mind. (M, K.) And EalaY baSiyrapK According to, or agreeably with, knowledge and assurance: (TA:) and purposely; intentionally. (M, TA.) And EalaY gayori baSiyrapK Without certainty. (M, TA.) ― -b3- Constancy, or firmness, in religion. (TA.) ― -b4- An evidence, a testimony, a proof, an argument, or the like; as also ↓ maboSarapN (S, K) and ↓ maboSarN . (K.) ― -b5- [And hence,] Blood, (M,) or somewhat thereof, (As, S, K,) by which one is directed to an animal that has been shot, or to the knowledge thereof: (As, AA, S, M, K:) or blood upon the ground; (AZ, S;) what sticks upon the ground, not upon the body: (M:) what adheres to the body is termed jadiy~apN : (AZ, S:) or a portion of blood of the size of a dirhem: (TA:) or what is of a round form, like a shield: or what is of an oblong form: or what is of the size of the firosin [or foot ] of the camel: in all these explanations, blood being meant: or blood not flowing: or what flows thereof at one single time: (M:) or a portion of blood that glistens: (B:) and (as some say, M) the blood of a virgin: (M, K:) and blood-revenge: and a fine for homicide: (TA:) pl. baSaAy^iru , as above: (S, M:) and ↓ baSiyrN , which occurs in a verse cited by AHn, may also be a pl. of baSiyrapN , applied to blood, [or rather a coll. gen. n., of which bSyrp is the n. un.,] like as $aEiyrN is of $aEiyrapN ; or it may be for bSyrp , the p being elided by poetic license; or it may be a dial. var. of bSyrp , like as one says bayaADN and bayaADapN . (M.) ElAs'ar El-Joafee says, raAHwA baSaAy^iruhumo EalaY A^akotaAfihimo wabaSiyratiY yaEoduw bihaA EatadN waA^aY [ They went with their blood upon their shoulderblades; but my blood, a ready and swift and strong horse runs with it ]; meaning, they neglected the blood of their father, and left it behind them; i. e., they did not take revenge for it; but I have sought my blood-revenge: (S, M: *) but see another explanation in what follows. (S. [See also Ham p. 59.]) ― -b6- (tropical:) A witness: (Lh, S, * M, Mgh, K:) an observer and a witness. (A.)

sourceDefinition: , in the Kur [lxxv. 14], means (tropical:) Nay, the man shall be witness against himself: (S, Mgh:) or it means that his arms, or hands, and his legs, or feet, and his tongue, shall be witnesses against him on the day of resurrection: (M:) Akh says that it is like the saying to a man, A^anota Huj~apN EalaY nafosika : (S:) the p is added because the members are meant thereby; (B;) or to give intensiveness to the signification, (Mgh, B,) as in Eal~aAmapN and raAwiyapN ; (B;) or because the meaning is EayonN baSiyrapN . (Mgh.) You say also, AijoEaloniY baSiyrapF Ealayohimo (tropical:) Make thou me an observer of them and a witness against them. (Lh, * M, * A.) ― -b2- An example by which one is admonished: (K:) pl. baSaAy^iru ; which is said to be used agreeably with this interpretation in the Kur xxviii. 43. (TA.) You say, A^amaA laka baSiyrapN fiyhi (tropical:) Hast thou not an example whereby thou shouldst be admonished in him? (TA.) -A2- A shield: (AO, S, M, K:) or a glistening shield: or an oblong shield: (TA:) and a coat of mail: (AO, S, M, K:) and any defensive armour: (M, TA:) and baSaAy^iru Als~ilaAHi any arms that are worn: and biSaArN , as well as baSaAy^iru , is a pl. thereof. (TA.) Accord. to AO, the verse of El-Joafee cited above commences thus: HamaluwA baSaAy^irahumo EalaY A^akotaAfihimo and the meaning is, [ They bore ] their shields [ upon their shoulder-blades ]; or their coats of mail. (S.) -A3- An oblong piece of cloth (K, TA) of cotton or other material. (TA.) [See buSorN .] Such is hung upon the door of a dwelling. (TA.) And you say, raA^ayotu Ealayohi baSiyrapF , i. e. $uq~apF mulaf~aqapF [app. meaning I saw upon him a garment composed of two oblong pieces of cloth joined and sewed together ]. (TA.) ― -b2- What is between the two oblong pieces of cloth [i. e. between any two of such pieces ] of a bayot [or tent ]; (S, K;) and what is between the two pieces of a mazaAdap and the like; what is sewed, thereof, in the manner termed baSorN [inf. n. of baSara : see 1, last sentence]: (B:) pl. baSaAy^iru : (S:) and ↓ baASirN signifies [in like manner] what is joined and sewed together ( mulaf~aq ) between two oblong pieces of cloth or two pieces of rag. (TA.)

definition: ― -b2- lamoHN baASirN (tropical:) An intent, or a hard, glance: (M, K:) or a very intent or hard glance.
sourceDefinition: : see baSiyrN . ― -b2- lamoHN baASirN (tropical:) An intent, or a hard, glance: (M, K:) or a very intent or hard glance. (S.) You say, A^arayotuhu lamoHFA baASirFA (tropical:) I showed him a very intent or hard glance: (S, M: *) bASrA being here used for the augmented epithet [ muboSirFA ]; (M;) or it is a possessive epithet, (Yaakoob, M,) like laAbinN and taAmirN , meaning *uw baSarK , from A^aboSarotu , like mawotN maAy^itN from A^amat~u ; and it means I showed him a severe thing. (S.) And laqiYa minohu lamoHFA baASirFA (tropical:) He experienced from him a manifest, or an evident, thing. (M. [See also art. lmH .]) And raA^aY fulaAnN lamoHFA baASirFA (tropical:) Such a one beheld a terrible thing. (Lth, TA.) And A^araAniY Alz~amaAnu lamoHFA baASirFA (tropical:) Fortune showed me a terrifying thing. (A.) ― -b3- It is said in a prov., xayoru AlgadaA='i bawaAkiruhu waxayoru AlEa$aA='i bawaASiruhu , [the word bawaASiru being pl. of ↓ baASirapN ,] meaning [ The best kinds of morning-meal are those thereof that are early; and the best kinds of evening-meal are those thereof ] in which the food is seen, before the invasion of night. (Meyd. See Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 442.) ― -b4- baASirapN [as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates]: see baSarN . -A2- See also baSayrapN , last sentence.

sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, &c.,) aor. yabiyEu , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. bayoEN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and mabiyEN , (S, Msb, K,) which latter is anomalous, (S,) the regular form being mabaAEN , (S, K,) has two contr. significacations: He sold it: and he bought it: (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) and ↓ AbAEhu is a dial. var. of the same: (IKtt, Msb:) [but app. only in the former sense:] or this last signifies he offered it for sale; or exposed it to sale: (S, K:) and ↓ AbtAEhu , as well as baAEahu , signifies he bought it. (S, * Mgh, * Msb, K.) The primary signification of bayoEN is The exchanging, or exchange, of property; or the making an exchange with property; as in the phrases bayoEN raAbiHN [ an exchange of property bringing gain ], and bayoEN xaAsirN [ an exchange of property occasioning loss ]: and this is a proper signification when it relates to real substances: but it is tropically used to signify the making the contract [ of sale and purchase ]; because this is the means of giving [and obtaining] possession: [though this signification is what is termed HaqiyqapN Eurofiy~apN , i. e., a sense so common as to be conventionally regarded as proper:] the phrase SaH~a AlbayoEu , or baTala , and the like, mean Safoqapu AlbayoEi ; [i. e. The contract of sale, or purchase, was valid, or was null; ] but the prefixed n. being suppressed, and its complement [alone] used for it, and this being masc., the verb is made masc. (Msb.) baAEa [mostly signifies He sold; and] is doubly trans., both by itself and by means of mino prefixed to the second object; (Mgh, Msb;) this prep. being thus used as a corroborative: (Msb:) you say, baAEahu Al$~aYo'a and baAEahu minohu [ He sold to him the thing and He sold it to him ]: (Mgh:) and biEotu zayodFA Ald~aAra and biEotu mino zayodK Ald~aAra [ I sold to Zeyd the house: (see also an explanation of the phrase AisotabaEotuhu Al$~aYo'a : and see baAEahu mina Als~uloTaAni : to which might be added countless similar instances; for when bAE signifies he sold, mino is generally prefixed to the noun or pronoun denoting the person to whom the thing is sold:)] and sometimes li is put in the place of mino ; so that you say, biEotuka Al$~aYo'a and biEotuhu laka [ I sold to thee the thing and I sold it to thee ]; the l being redundant [when the verb has this meaning, though not when it has the contr. meaning, as will be seen below]. (Msb.) Of the contr. signification we have an ex. in the saying of ElFarezdak, A_in~a Al$~abaAba laraAbiHN mano baAEahaA waAl$~ayobu layosa libaAy^iEiyhi tijaAru [ Verily youthfulness, he who buys it is a gainer; but hoariness, there are no traffickers for its sellers; the part. a. being here from the verb in the former sense]: (S, TA:) and [often in a case in which the verb is followed by l ; as] in baAEa lahu Al$~aYo'a He bought for him the thing; (Mgh;) [the l not being redundant when the verb is used in this sense;] and as in the saying of Tarafeh, wayaA^otiyka bAloA^axobaAri mano lamo tabiEo lahu bataAtFA walamo taDoribo lahu waqota mawoEidi [ And he will bring thee tidings for whom thou hast not bought travelling-provisions, and for whom thou hast not assigned an appointed time for his bringing them]: (TA:) and in the saying, baAEa dunoyaAhu biA=xiratihi (tropical:) [ He purchased his enjoyments of the present world at the expense of his enjoyments of the world to come ]: (Z, TA:) and [in like manner] you say, zayodN Ald~aAra ↓ AbtAE , meaning Zeyd bought the house: and ligayorihi ↓ AbtAEhA He bought it for another person. (Msb.) The verb has this signification, also, in the trad., laA yabiEo baEoDukumo EalaY bayoEi A^axiyhi [ One of you shall not buy in opposition to the buying of his brother when an agreement has been manifested but the contract has not been concluded ]; (S, IAth, Mgh, Msb; [but in the S and Msb and by IAth, the trad. is related thus; laA yaxoTubi Alr~ajulu EalaY xiTobapi A^axiyhi walaA yabiEo EalaY bayoEi A^axiyhi ; (see art. xTb ;)]) as is shown by the relation of Bkh, Alr~ajulu EalaY bayoEi A^axiyhi ↓ laA yabotaAEu : (Mgh, Msb:) or it may here have the contr. meaning: (IAth:) Az says that the seller and buyer are equal in offence when either of them does thus to another. (TA.) [Similar to this is the saying, laA yasuwmu Alr~ajulu EalaY sawomi A^axiyhi : see art. swm . See also baAEa EalaY bayoEihi below, used in a tropical sense.] You say also, baAEa Ealayohi AlqaADiY , meaning The judge sold against his will; (Mgh;) sold without his consent. (Msb.) ― -b2- The pass. form is biyEa [ It was sold: and it was bought ]: (S, K:) optionally either [thus] with kesr to the b , or [ buyoEa ] with damm to the b , (S,) [or rather with a sound between that of damm and that of kesr, which pronunciation is termed A_i$omaAmN ;] and some say buwEa ; (S, K;) changing the Y into w : and thus in the cases of kiyla and qiyla and the like: (S:) [but Ibn-Málik requires damm or A$mAm in the passive of a verb of which the medial radical is Y , and kesr or A$mAm in the passive of a verb of which the medial radical is w , to prevent the mistaking of an active verb for a passive in such cases as biEotu and sumotu : others, however, only prefer what Ibn-Málik absolutely requires in these cases. (See I'Ak p. 131.)] ― -b3- You say also, baAEahu mina Als~uloTaAni , [lit. He sold him to the Sultán, ] meaning (tropical:) he slandered him, or calumniated him, to the Sultán. (S, * Mgh, * Msb, K.) The primary signification of bayoEN is The exchanging, or exchange, of property; or the making an exchange with property; as in the phrases bayoEN raAbiHN [ an exchange of property bringing gain ], and bayoEN xaAsirN [ an exchange of property occasioning loss ]: and this is a proper signification when it relates to real substances: but it is tropically used to signify the making the contract [ of sale and purchase ]; because this is the means of giving [and obtaining] possession: [though this signification is what is termed HaqiyqapN Eurofiy~apN , i. e., a sense so common as to be conventionally regarded as proper:] the phrase SaH~a AlbayoEu , or baTala , and the like, mean Safoqapu AlbayoEi ; [i. e. The contract of sale, or purchase, was valid, or was null; ] but the prefixed n. being suppressed, and its complement [alone] used for it, and this being masc., the verb is made masc. (Msb.) baAEa [mostly signifies He sold; and] is doubly trans., both by itself and by means of mino prefixed to the second object; (Mgh, Msb;) this prep. being thus used as a corroborative: (Msb:) you say, baAEahu Al$~aYo'a and baAEahu minohu [ He sold to him the thing and He sold it to him ]: (Mgh:) and biEotu zayodFA Ald~aAra and biEotu mino zayodK Ald~aAra [ I sold to Zeyd the house: (see also an explanation of the phrase AisotabaEotuhu Al$~aYo'a : and see baAEahu mina Als~uloTaAni : to which might be added countless similar instances; for when bAE signifies he sold, mino is generally prefixed to the noun or pronoun denoting the person to whom the thing is sold:)] and sometimes li is put in the place of mino ; so that you say, biEotuka Al$~aYo'a and biEotuhu laka [ I sold to thee the thing and I sold it to thee ]; the l being redundant [when the verb has this meaning, though not when it has the contr. meaning, as will be seen below]. (Msb.) Of the contr. signification we have an ex. in the saying of ElFarezdak, A_in~a Al$~abaAba laraAbiHN mano baAEahaA waAl$~ayobu layosa libaAy^iEiyhi tijaAru [ Verily youthfulness, he who buys it is a gainer; but hoariness, there are no traffickers for its sellers; the part. a. being here from the verb in the former sense]: (S, TA:) and [often in a case in which the verb is followed by l ; as] in baAEa lahu Al$~aYo'a He bought for him the thing; (Mgh;) [the l not being redundant when the verb is used in this sense;] and as in the saying of Tarafeh, wayaA^otiyka bAloA^axobaAri mano lamo tabiEo lahu bataAtFA walamo taDoribo lahu waqota mawoEidi [ And he will bring thee tidings for whom thou hast not bought travelling-provisions, and for whom thou hast not assigned an appointed time for his bringing them]: (TA:) and in the saying, baAEa dunoyaAhu biA=xiratihi (tropical:) [ He purchased his enjoyments of the present world at the expense of his enjoyments of the world to come ]: (Z, TA:) and [in like manner] you say, zayodN Ald~aAra ↓ AbtAE , meaning Zeyd bought the house: and ligayorihi ↓ AbtAEhA He bought it for another person. (Msb.) definition: , (S, Mgh, TA,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, TA,) inf. n. mubaAyaEapN and biyaAEN , (TA,) is from AlbayoEu ; and so is ↓ Alt~abaAyuEu ; (S, TA;) this being syn. with AlmubaAyaEapu . (K, TA.) You say, baAyaEaA and ↓ tabaAyaEaA , meaning They two sold and bought, each with the other: (TK:) and ↓ tabaAyaEonaA [ We sold and bought, one with another ]: (Mgh:) and bAyEhu also signifies He bartered, or exchanged commodities, with him. (TA.) [See 1; where a citation from the Msb indicates that this latter is the primary signification accord. to the author of that work.] ― -b2- It is also from AlbayoEapu ; and so is ↓ Alt~abaAyuEu : (S, TA: *) AlmubaAyaEapu and ↓ Alt~abaAyuEu from AlbayoEapu signifying The making a covenant, a compact, an engagement, or the like; as though each of the two parties sold what he had to the other, and gave him his own special property, and his obedience, and all that pertained to his case. (TA.) [Hence,] bAyE AlA^amiyra He promised, or swore, allegiance to the prince; making a covenant with him to submit to him the judgment of his own case and of the cases of the Muslims [ in general ], not to dispute with him in respect of anything thereof, but to obey him in whatever command he might impose upon him, pleasing and displeasing: in doing which, it was usual for the person making this covenant to place his hand in the hand of the prince, in confirmation of the covenant, like as is done by the seller and buyer; wherefore the act was termed bayoEapN , an inf. n. [of un.] of baAEa . (Ibn-Khaldoon, in De Sacy's Chrest. Ar., 2nd ed., ii. 256 — 7.) [And hence the phrases, buwyiEa biAlixilaAfapi and buwyiEa lahu biAlxilaAfapi He had the promise, or oath, of allegiance made to him as being Khaleefeh. ] You say also, bAyEhu Ealayohi , inf. n. mubaAyaEapN , He made a covenant, a compact, an engagement, or the like, with him, respecting it, or to do it: and ↓ tbAyEwA EalaY AlA^amori [ they made a covenant, &c., respecting, or to do, the thing, or affair ]; like as you say A^aSofaquwA Ealayohi . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: Sold: and bought: as also ↓ maboyuwEN : (S, K:) in the latter sense syn. with ↓ mubotaAEN . (Msb.) Kh says that the letter suppressed in mabiyEN is the w of the measure mafoEuwlN , because it is augmentative: but Akh says that the letter suppressed is the medial radical; for when they made the Y quiescent, they transferred its vowel to the letter before it, so that it became madmoomeh, [the word thus being altered to mabuyowEN ,] then they changed the dammeh into kesreh because of the Y after it, then the Y was suppressed, and the w was changed into Y , like the w of miyzaAnN , because of the kesreh: accord. to El-Mázinee, each of these sayings is good; but that of Akh is the more agreeable with analogy. (S.)

sourceDefinition: , (K,) inf. n. A_itoqaAnN , (JK, S,) i. q. A^aHokamahu [ He made it, or rendered it, (namely, a thing, JK, or an affair, S and K,) firm, stable, strong, solid, compact, sound, or free from defect or imperfection, by the exercise of skill; he made it firmly, strongly, solidly, compactly, so that it was firmly and closely joined or knit together, soundly, thoroughly, skilfully, judiciously, or well; he so constructed, constituted, established, settled, arranged, did, performed, or executed, it; he put it into a firm, solid, sound, or good, state, or on a firm, solid, sound, or good, footing ]. (JK, S, K.) [And Atqn lahu signifies the same as Atqnhu : or he exercised, or possessed, the skill requisite for it; namely, an affair.] Al~a*iy A^atoqana kul~a $~aYo'K , in the Kur xxvii. 90, means Who hath created everything firmly, strongly, solidly, &c., ( A^aHokama xaloqahu ,) and made it, fashioned it, or disposed it, in the fit, proper, or right, manner. (Bd.) [You say also, Atqn Eilomahu , meaning He made his knowledge sound; or made himself thoroughly learned. ] And Atqn Eanohu He knew it, or learned it, (namely, a tradition [&c.],) soundly, thoroughly, or well, from him. (TA in art. *br .)

definition: The rusaAbap of water, (JK, Mgh, K,) in a rivulet or in the channel of a torrent, (K,) in the [ season called ] rabiyE ;
sourceDefinition: The rusaAbap of water, (JK, Mgh, K,) in a rivulet or in the channel of a torrent, (K,) in the [ season called ] rabiyE ; (Lth, JK, Mgh;) i. e., (Mgh,) [ its sediment, or] the thick matter that is borne by it [ and that sinks to the bottom; used for improving land ]: (Lth, JK, Mgh:) and (K) the turonuwq of a well (Mgh, K) and of the channel of a torrent; i. e., the slime, mixed with black, or black and fetid, mud; accord. to the Jámi' of El-Ghooree. (Mgh.) ― -b2- A thing by means of which one subsists, and makes good, or improves, the performance, or execution, or management, of an affair; as iron, and other things, of the jawaAhir [i. e. precious stones, or native ores, ] of the earth: and anything by means of which a thing is made good, or improved, is called its tiqon . (TA.) ― -b3- A skilful man: (JK, S, K:) pl. A^atoqaAnN . (TA.) ― -b4- [Hence, probably,] tiqonN [or Aibonu tiqonK ] is also the name [or surname] of a certain man proverbial for his excellence in shooting. (S, K. [In the latter it is implied that this name or surname is Alt~iqonu .]) The rájiz says, yaramiY bihaA A^aromaY mini A@boni tiqoni [ One more skilled in shooting than Ibn-Tikn shoots it ]. (S.) ― -b5- Nature, or natural disposition. (JK, S, K.) You say, AlfaSaAHapu mino tiqonihi Chasteness of speech, or eloquence, is [a quality] of his nature. (S.)

definition: The sediment, or settlings, of anything;
sourceDefinition: The sediment, or settlings, of anything; (S;) the dregs; lees; or thick, or turbid, portion that sinks to the bottom of a thing, (T, M, Msb, K,) beneath the clear portion; (T, Msb;) as, for instance, of water, and of broth, (TA,) and of medicine, (T, TA,) and the like, and of a cookingpot, [i. e. of its contents,] (T,) &c.; (TA;) as also ↓ vaAfilN . (IDrd, M, K.) ― -b2- (tropical:) Grain, (T, S, M, K, TA,) and whatever is eaten of flesh-meat or bread or dates; and particularly when people are in want of milk: (T:) or flour; and what is not drunk, as bread, and the like: (TA:) or the refuse, or worse sort, of TaEaAm [i. e. wheat, or other food ]. (Ham p. 768.) You say, $ariba AlmaA='a EalaY gayori vufolK (tropical:) [ He drank water, or the water, not upon, i. e. not having eaten, grain, or flesh-meat, &c.]. (A in art. bHt .) ― -b3- See also vifaAlN .

definition: The thing by which the mill is preserved from the ground;
sourceDefinition: The thing by which the mill is preserved from the ground; as also ↓ vufolN : (M, K:) it is a skin that is spread beneath the hand-mill to preserve the flour from the dust; (T;) a skin, (S, Msb,) or the like, that is put beneath the mill, (Msb,) [i. e.,] which is spread, and whereon is placed the mill, which is turned with the hand, (S,) in order that the flour may fall upon it. definition: A huntsman beat, or disciplined, or trained, his dog for the purpose of the chase ( Darabahu EalaY AlS~ayodi );
sourceDefinition: : see jirowN , in three places. A huntsman beat, or disciplined, or trained, his dog for the purpose of the chase ( Darabahu EalaY AlS~ayodi ); and thereupon it was said, Daraba jirowatahu [app. meaning He beat, or disciplined, or trained, his whelp ]: and hence this phrase became proverbially used, in instances here following. (Z, TA.) ― -b2- I. q. nafosN [as meaning Self ]. (TA.) You say, Daraba Ealayohi jirowatahu , meaning (assumed tropical:) He disposed and subjected himself to it; (S, TA;) namely, a thing, an affair, or a case: and he endured it with patience: and in like manner, Daraba jirowapa nafosihi : (TA:) and A^aloqaY fulaAnN jrowatahu he endured the thing with patience. (S, TA.) Also Darabotu jirowatiY Eanohu (assumed tropical:) I endured with patience the want, or loss, of it: (TA:) or my mind became at ease [ respecting it ]. (AA, IB, TA.) -A2- Also (K, TA, [in the CK ↓ jirowN ,]) (tropical:) A short she-camel. (K, TA.)

definition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor (Msb, K,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor (Msb, K,) inf. n. jazomN , (Msb,) He cut it, or cut it off; (S, Msb, K) namely, a thing: (Msb:) [like jaramahu &c.] ― -b2- jazama Aln~axola He cut off the fruit of the palmtrees: (Msb:) [like jarama Alnxl : but see another explanation, below.] And jazama mina Aln~axolapi jizomFA [ He cut off a portion of the fruit from the palmtree ]. (TA.) ― -b3- jazama AlHarofa , (S, ISd, Msb, K,) aor. as above, (TA,) and so the inf. n., (S,) He made the letter quiescent; (S, ISd, Msb, K;) i.e., the final letter of a declinable word; (S, ISd, Msb;) he cut it off from motion: (Msb:) or as though he cut off from it declinability: (Mbr, TA:) from jazama in the first of the senses explained above: jazomN in a declinable word being like sukuwnN in an indeclinable word. (S.) It is said in a trad. of En-Nakha'ee, Alt~akobiyru jazomN wAlt~asoliymu jazomN , meaning that neither should be prolonged in utterance, and that the last letter in each should be without a case-ending, i.e., be quiescent; so that one should not say [in prayer] Aall~`hu A^akobaru [nor Als~alaAmu Ealayokumo waraHomapu A@ll~`hi , but A^akobaro in the former instance, and A@ll~`ho in the latter]: or, accord. to Z, that one should not exceed the due bounds in the pronunciation of the hemzeh and the medd: (TA:) or that one should abstain from giving fulness and depth to the sound of the vowel, and should elide it entirely in the places of pausing, and avoid excess in the pronunciation of the hemzeh and the medd. (Mgh.) ― -b4- jazama EalaY fulaAnK ka*aA waka*aA , He made such and such things to be binding, or obligatory, on such a one. (K.) And jazama Alyamiyna , (K,) inf.n. as above, (TA,) i. q. A^amoDaAhaA ; (K) i. e., He made the oath to be unconditional, without exception, absolutely or decidedly or irreversibly binding; (TK;) A^amoDaAhaA Albat~apa . (TA.) One says also, Halafa yamiynFA HatomFA jazomFA [ He swore an oath in an absolute, a decided, or an irreversible, manner ]. (TA.) And jazama AlA^amora , (K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He decided the affair irreversibly. (K.) And jazamotu maA bayoniY wabayonahu I decided the matter between me and him. (TA.) And A^afoEalu *`lika jazomFA I will do that decidedly; without any indulgence therein. (Msb.) And jazama bihi [ He asserted it decisively ]. (TA passim.) And jazama EalaY AlA^amori He decided, or determined, upon, or upon doing, the thing, or affair. (TA.) ― -b5- Also, this last phrase, He was silent respecting the affair; and so ↓ jz~m . (K,* TA.) ― -b6- And jazama Eanohu He held back, or refrained, from it through cowardice; and was unable to do it; and so ↓ jz~m : (K:) or Alqawomu ↓ jz~m the people lacked power or ability. (S) ― -b7- jazama AlbaEiyru famaA yaboraHu [app., The camel stopped, and would not quit his place ]. (TA: but the verb jzm is there without any syll. sign.) -A2- jazama Aln~axola , (A'Obeyd, S, K,) inf. n. as above; (TA;) and ↓ Ajtzmhu ; (K; and the act. part. n. of the latter is also mentioned in the S;) like jaramahu (S) [and Ajtrmhu ]; He computed by conjecture the quantity of fruit upon the palm-trees. (A'Obeyd, S, K.) ― -b2- And jazomN also signifies The selling, or buying, fruit [by conjecture, while yet in a rudimental state,] in its calyxes, for money. (IAar, TA.) -A3- Also jazama (S, K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He filled a skin; (S, K;) and so ↓ jz~m , (S, *K,) inf. n. tajoziymN (S.) ― -b2- jazamati AlA_ibilu , (Fr, K,) inf. n. as above, (Fr, TA,) The camels satisfied their thirst [as though they filled themselves ] with water. (Fr, K.)― -b3- And jazama , (IAar, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (IAar, TA,) He ate one meal and was filled thereby: (IAar, K) or he ate one meal in every day and night. (Th, K.) -A4- jazama AlqiraA='apa , (Lth, K,) inf. n. as above, (Lth, TA,) He performed the reading, or recitation, so as to put the letters in their proper places, in a distinct, or perspicuous, and leisurely, manner. (Lth, K.) ― -b2- And jazomN in writing means The making the letters even. (K.) -A5- jazama bisaloHihi He voided part of his excrement, part thereof remaining: or he cast forth his excrement. (K.)

sourceDefinition: aor. , inf. n. ja$omN (S, Msb, K) and ja$aAmapN , (Msb, K,) He took, or imposed, upon himself the affair, or he undertook it, as a task, or in spite of difficulty or trouble or inconvenience; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ tj$~mhu , (S, Msb, * K,) and tjs~mhu : (Aboo-Turáb, TA:) or ↓ the second and third signify he constrained himself to do it, or perform it: (Aboo-Mihjen, Aboo-Turáb, TA in art. jsm :) and ka*aA waka*aA darr; tj$~m He did such and such things against his will, and in spite of difficulty or trouble or inconvenience. (TA.) [See also an ex. of ↓ tj$~m in art . jsm ;conj. 5, last sentence.] ja$imotu A_ilayoka Earaqa Alqirobapi is said to mean [ I have imposed upon myself difficulty or trouble or inconvenience, in coming to thee, ] so that I have journeyed, and become in want of the water of the water-skin in the journey: or the meaning is, I have suffered, and imposed upon myself, difficulty or trouble or inconvenience, so that I have sweated like the water-skin: or by the Earaq of the qirobap is meant its Ealaq , i. e., its miEolaAq , by which it is carried; and the phrase means A_ilayoka ↓ taja$~amotu Hamola Alqirbapi [ I have impose upon myself, in spite of difficulty &c., in coming to thee, the carrying of the water-skin ]; alluding to journeying and its difficulties: (Har p. 511:) [and in like manner,] one says, laka Earaqa Alqirobapa ↓ taja$~amotu (S in art. Erq .) The sportsman, when he has not taken any game, and has returned disappointed, says, maA ja$imotu A_ilayoka ZilofFA [app. meaning I have not had the trouble of bringing to thee so much as a hoof of a gazelle or the like ]. (AZ, TA.) And maA ja$imotu Alyawoma TaEaAmFA i. e., I have not eaten, to-day, food, is said on the occasion of the disappointment of any one seeking a thing. (AZ, TA.)

definition: A live, or burning, coal;
sourceDefinition: A live, or burning, coal; a piece of smokeless burning fire: (Msb:) or burning fire: (K:) [but the former is the correct explanation:] when cold, [before it is kindled,] it is called faHomN (TA) [or HaTabN &c.]: and when reduced to powder by burning, ramaAdN : (L in art. rmd :) from jam~ara “ he collected together: ” (Mgh:) pl. ↓ jamorN (S, Msb, K) [or rather this is a coll. gen. n.] and jamaraAtN and jimaArN . (Msb.) ― -b2- [Hence,] fiY ↓ Aljamoru kabidiY (tropical:) [ Live coals are in my liver ]. (A.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] AljamaraAtu Alv~alaAvu (assumed tropical:) [ The three live coals; meaning the first three degrees of heat]: the first is in the air; the second, in the earth, or dust; and the third, in the water: [or, accord. to the modern Egyptian almanacs, the first is in the air, and is cold, or cool; the second, in the water, and is lukewarm; and the third, in the earth, or dust, and is hot: the first falling exactly a zodiacal month before the vernal equinox; and each lasting seven days:] whence the saying, kaAna *`lika Einoda suquwTi Aljamorapi (assumed tropical:) [ That was at the time of the falling of the live coal ]; i. e., when the heat had acquired strength. (TA.) -A2- Any body of men that have united together, and become one band, and that do not form a confederacy with any others: (S:) or a body of men that congregate by themselves, because of their strength and their great valour; [said to be] from the same word signifying “ a live coal: ” (Msb:) or any people that endure patiently fighting with those who fight them, not forming a confederacy with any others, nor uniting themselves to any others: (Lth, TA:) or a tribe that does not unite itself to any other: (K:) or that comprises three hundred horsemen, (K,) or the like thereof: (TA:) or a tribe that fights with a company of tribes: (TA:) pl. jamaraAtN . (S, Msb, K.) You say, banuw fulaAnK jamorapN The sons of such a one are a people able to defend themselves, and strong. (TA.) jamaraAtu AlEarabi is an appellation especially applied to three tribes; namely, Benoo-Dabbeh Ibn-Udd, and Benu-l-Hárith Ibn-Kaab, and Benoo-Numeyr Ibn-' Ámir; (S, A, K;) the first of which became extinguished by confederating with Er-Ribáb, and the second by confederating with Medhhij; the third only remaining [a jmrp ] because it formed no confederacy: (S:) or it is applied to 'Abs and El-Hárith and Dabbeh; all the offspring of a woman who dreamt that three live coals issued from her faroj . (S, K.) ― -b2- Also A thousand horsemen. (S, K.) One says jamorapN kaAljamorapi [ A troop of a thousand horsemen like the live coal ]. (S, TA.) -A3- A pebble: (S, K:) or a stone: (Msb:) or a small stone or pebble: pl. jimaArN (Mgh, Msb, Et-Towsheeh, TA) and jamaraAtN . (Mgh, Msb.) ― -b2- Also sing. of jamaraAtN (S, Msb, K) and of jimaArN (TA) in the appellations jamaraAtu minFY (Msb) or jamaraAtu AlmanaAsiki (S, K) and jimaAru AlmanaAsiki , (TA,) which were three in number, (S, Msb, K,) called Aljamorapu AlA^uwlaY and Aljamorapu AlwusoTaY and jamorapu AlEaqabapi , (K,) at which jamaraAt (i. e. small pebbles, TA) were cast; (S, K;) each of these being a heap of pebbles, at Minè, and each two heaps [or rather each heap and that next to it] being about a bow-shot apart: (Msb:) accord. to Th, from jamarahu “ he put him aside, apart, away, or at a distance: ” or from A^ajomara “ he hastened; ” because Adam pelted Iblees in Minè, and he hastened away before him: (K, * TA:) or from tjm~rwA “ they collected together: ” (Mgh:) or from jamarahu “ he collected it together. ” (Msb.) -A4- See also jamiyrapN .

sourceDefinition: (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) and ↓ jaAmuwrN (K) [each a coll. gen. n.] The heart, or pith, [or cerebrum, ] of the palm-tree, (S, A, Msb, K, TA,) that is in the summit of its head, which part is cut off, and its outer portion is stripped off from the pith within it, which is a white substance, like a piece of the hump of a camel, large and soft: it is eaten with honey: (TA:) from it come forth the fruit and the branches; and when it is cut off, the tree dies: (Msb:) the spathe comes forth from it, amid the part whence two branches divide: (TA:) the head of the palmtree; a soft, white substance: from jam~ara “ he collected together; ” for a similar reason termed kavarN : (Mgh:) n. un. jum~aArapN . (A, TA.) [See also qalobN .] You say, lahu saAqN kaAljum~aArapi He has a shank like a piece of the heart of the palm-tree. (A.) And Aljum~aAru fiY xalaAxilihin~a (tropical:) [ Legs like the heart of the palm-tree are within their anklets ]. (A.) Sakhr El-Hudhalee says, using a double trope, likening the fresh juicy stalks of the barodiY~ to the pith of the palm-tree, and then applying this expression to the legs of a woman, A_i*aA EuTifato xalaAxuluhun~a gaS~abo bijum~aAraAti barodiY~K xidaAli (tropical:) [ When their anklets are bent, (for the anklet of the Arab woman is formed of a piece of silver, or other metal, which is bent round so that the two ends nearly meet,) they are choked, or entirely filled up, with plump legs like the pith of the papyrus ]. (A, TA.)

definition: , (S, * TA,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, * TA,) aor. yajuwbu , (S, TA,) inf. n. jawobN (S, A, K, TA) and tajowaAbN , (Har p. 336,) He made a hole in it; or rent, or tore, it; (S, A, K, TA;) as also ↓ AjtAbhu : (K, * TA:) he made a hole through, or in, or into, it; perforated, pierced, or bored, it: (TA:) he cut it: (S, A, K, TA:) he cut it in like manner as one cuts a jayob [or an opening at the neck and bosom of a shirt &c. ]: (L, TA:) he made, or cut, a hole in the middle of it; cut a piece out of the middle of it; hollowed it out; or excavated it. (TA.) You say, jAb AlS~axorapa He made a hole in the rock; (A, TA;) perforated, pierced, or bored, it. (TA.) Hence, in the Kur [lxxxix. 8], wavamuwda Al~a*iyna jaAbuwA AlS~axora biAlwaAdi (Fr, S, TA) And Thamood, who made holes in the rocks, (Fr, TA,) or cut the rocks, (Bd, Jel,) [or hollowed them out, ] and made them dwellings, in the valley, (Fr, Bd, Jel, TA,) i. e., in Wádi-l-Kurà. (Bd, Jel.) You say also, jAb AlqamiySa , (S, A, K,) aor. bajuwbu , [inf. n. jawobN ;] (S, K, and Msb in art. jyb ;) and aor. yajiybu , (S, K,) [inf. n., app., jiybN , originally jawobN ; see a verse cited below, and a remark of Sh thereon;] and ↓ jw~bhu ; (A, K;) He hollowed out, or cut out in a round form, the jayob of the shirt: (S, and Msb in art. jyb :) or he cut the jayob of the shirt: (A:) or he made a jayob to the shirt; (K;) as also jay~abahu , (S, and Msb in art. jyb ,) inf. n. tajoyiybN . (S.) And jAb Alv~awoba He cut the garment, or piece of cloth; [or cut it out; ] as also ↓ AjtAbhu . (A.) And jAb Aln~aEola , inf. n. jawobN , He cut out the sandal. (TA.) And jAb Alqaronu [i. e. jAb All~aHoma ] The horn cut the flesh and came forth. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, also,] jAb , (S, A, Msb, TA,) aor. yajuwbu (S, Msb, TA) and yajiybu , (S, TA,) inf. n. jawobN ; (TA;) and ↓ AjtAb ; (S, A, TA;) (tropical:) He traversed, or crossed, (S, A, * Msb, TA,) or cut through by journeying, (TA,) a country, (S, TA,) or a land, (Msb,) and a desert, and the darkness: (A, * TA:) and jawobN signifies likewise the pouncing down of a bird. (TA.) A rájiz says, baAtato tajiybu A^adoEaja AlZ~alaAmi jiyba AlbiyaTori midoraEa AlhumaAmi (assumed tropical:) [ She passed the night cutting through the black darkness, like as the tailor cuts through the woollen tunic of the valiant chief, making the opening at the neck and bosom ]: (S: [but in one copy, instead of jiyba , I here find jayoba ; and in art. bTr , $aq~a :]) and Sh remarks that this [verb tjyb , or the inf. n. jyb ,] is not from Aljayobu [meaning “ the opening at the neck and bosom ” of a shirt &c.], because its medial radical is w , and that of Aljyb is Y : (TA:) [i. e., jAb , aor. yjyb , is originally jawaba , aor. yajowibu .] One says also, of news, yajuwbu AlA^aroDa mino baladK A_ilaY baladK (assumed tropical:) [ It traverses the earth from country to country, or the land from town to town ]. (S, TA.) And of proverbs, tajuwbu AlbilaAda (assumed tropical:) They are current in the countries, or towns. (TA.) ― -b3- It is said in a trad., jiybati AlEarabu Ean~aA kamaA jiybati Alr~aHaA Eano quTobihaA (assumed tropical:) The Arabs were rent from us, like as the mill-stone is rent from its pivot; we being in the midst, and they around us. (TA.) -A2- jaAbati Ald~aEowapu : see A^ajowabu .

sourceDefinition: , [see 4,] in the following question, put to Mohammad, (TA,) A^aY~uAll~ayoli A^ajowabu daEowapF is either from jubotu AlA^aroDa (K, TA) “ I traversed the land, ” (TA,) and signifies (tropical:) More, or most, penetrating to the places whence the answer is imagined to proceed; (K, TA;) or [it signifies more, or most, quick in being answered, ] from Ald~aEowapu ↓ jaAbati , of the measure faEulat , [i. e., originally jawubat ,] “ the prayer became answered, ” which, however, is a verb not in use, like as faqiyrN and $adiydN are imagined to be derived from faqura and $aduda : (Z, TA:) or it signifies more, or most, quick of answer, [from A^ajaAba ,] and is [anomalous, and] similar to A^aTowaEu [“ more obedient ”], from AlT~aAEapu , [i. e. from A^aTaAEa “ he obeyed, ”] (M, L, TA,) and to A^aEoTaY [“ more, or most, excellent in giving, ” from A^aEoTaY “ he gave ”], and lawaAqiHa [pl. of laAqiHapN a “ fecundating ” wind, (in the Kur xv. 22,) from A^aloqaHa “ he, or it, fecundated ”], (M, L, K, TA,) and the like; (M, L, TA;) and if so, the word is anomalous because a word of the measure A^afoEalu of this kind is not derived from a verb of more than three letters, except in certain cases of deviation from the constant course of speech: (L, TA:) the meaning is, (tropical:) What part of the night is that [in which prayer most quickly penetrates? or] in which prayer is most quick in being answered? (Mgh:) or what part of the night is that in which God is most quick in answering prayer? (L, TA.)

definition: (S A, Mgh, Msb, K) and ↓ HujorN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and ↓ HajorN , (S, K,) of which the first is the most chaste, (S,) and ↓ maHojarN (S, K) and ↓ HaAjuwrN (K) [and ↓ maHojuwrN ], Forbidden, prohibited, unlawful, inviolable, or sacred.
sourceDefinition: (S A, Mgh, Msb, K) and ↓ HujorN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and ↓ HajorN , (S, K,) of which the first is the most chaste, (S,) and ↓ maHojarN (S, K) and ↓ HaAjuwrN (K) [and ↓ maHojuwrN ], Forbidden, prohibited, unlawful, inviolable, or sacred. (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K.) Each of the first three forms occurs in different readings of the Kur vi. 139. (S.) You say, h`*aA HijorN Ealayoka This is forbidden, or unlawful, to thee. (A.) In the time of paganism, a man meeting another whom he feared, in a sacred month, used to say, ↓ HijorFA maHojuwrFA , meaning It is rigorously forbidden to thee [to commit an act of hostility against me] in this month: and the latter, thereupon, would abstain from any aggression against him: and so, on the day of resurrection, the polytheists, when they see the punishment, will say to the angels, thinking that it will profit them: (Lth, S: *) but Az says that I' Ab and his companions explain these words [occurring in the Kur xxv. 24] otherwise, i. e., as said by the angels, and meaning, the joyful annunciation is forbidden to be made to you: and accord. to El-Hasan, the former word will be said by the sinners, and the latter is said by God, meaning it will be forbidden to them to be granted refuge or protection as they used to be in their former life in the world: but Az adds, it is more proper to regard the two words as composing one saying: (TA:) and the latter word is a corroborative of the former, like maAy^itN in the expression mawotN maAy^itN . (Bd.) The same words in the Kur xxv. 55 signify A strong mutual repugnance, or incongruity; as though each said what one says who seeks refuge or protection from another: or, as some say, a defined limit. (Bd.) A man says to another, “ Dost thou so and so, O such a one?” and the latter replies HijorFA , or ↓ HujorFA , or ↓ HajorFA , meaning [I pray for] preservation, and acquitment, from this thing; a meaning reducible to that of prohibition, and of a thing that is prohibited. (Sb.) The Arabs say, on the occasion of a thing that they disapprove, lahu ↓ HujorFA , with damm, meaning, May it be averted. (S.) ― -b2- Homeyd Ibn-Thowr says, fahamamotu A^ano A^ago$aY A_ilayohaA maHojarFA walamivoluhaA yugo$aY A_ilayohi AlmaHojaru meaning, And I purposed doing to her a forbidden action: and verily the like of her is one to whom that which is forbidden is done. (S, K.) ↓ maHojarN is also explained as signifying HuromapN ; [app. meaning a thing from which one is bound to refrain, from a motive of respect or reverence; ] and to have this meaning in the verse above. (Az.) ― -b3- Also, the first of these words, Any HaAy^iT [i. e. garden, or walled garden of palm-trees, ] which one prohibits [ to the public ]. (S.) ― -b4- And AlHijoru That [ space ] which is comprised by [ the curved wall called ] the HaTiym , (S, A, Mgh, K,) which encompasses the Kaabeh on the north [or rather north-west ] side; (S, A, K;) on the side of the spout: (Mgh:) or the HTym [ itself ], which encompasses the Kaabeh on the side of the spout. (Msb.) [It is applied to both of these in the present day; but more commonly to the former.] ― -b5- Also, HijorN , The anterior pudendum of a man and of a woman; and so ↓ HajorN : (K, TA:) the latter the more chaste. (TA.) ― -b6- A mare; the female of the horse: (S, A, Msb, K:) and a mare kept for breeding; (A;) as though her womb were forbidden to all but generous horses: (T:) but in the latter sense the sing. is scarcely ever used; though its pl., the first of the following forms, (as well as the second, A,) is used to signify mares kept for breeding: (K:) ↓ HijorapN , as a sing., is said by F and others to be a barbarism: it occurs in a trad.; but perhaps the p is there added to assimilate it to bagolapN , with which it is there coupled: (MF:) the pl. [of pauc.] is A^aHojaArN (Msb, K) and [of mult.] HujuwrN (A, Msb, K) and HujuwrapN . (K.) A poet says, A_i*aA xarisa AlfaHolu wasoTa AlHujuwri waSaAHa AlkilaAbu waEaq~a Alwalado When the stallion, seeing the army and the gleaming swords, is mute in the midst of the mares kept for breeding, and does not look towards them, and the dogs bark at their masters, because of the change of their appearances, and children behave undutifully to their mothers whom fear diverts from attending to them. (A.) ― -b7- Relationship [ that prohibits marriage ]; nearness with respect to kindred. (Msb, K.) ― -b8- Understanding, intelligence, intellect, mind, or reason: (S, A, Msb, K:) so in the Kur lxxxix. 4: (S, Bd:) thus called because it forbids that which it does not behoove one to do. (Bd.) One says, fiY *`lika EiborapN li*iy HijorK In that is an admonition to him who possesses understanding, &c. (A.) -A2- See also HajurN , in three places.

sourceDefinition: [ A stone; explained in the K by SaxorapN ; but this means “a rock,” or “a great mass of stone” or “of hard stone”]; (S, K, &c.;) so called because it resists, by reason of its hardness; (Mgh;) and ↓ A^uHojur~N signifies the same: (Fr, K:) pl. (of pauc., of the former, S) A^aHojaArN (S, Mgh, K) and A^aHojurN (K) and (of mult, S) HijaArN and [more commonly] HijaArapN , (S, K,) which last is extr. [with respect to rule], (S,) or agreeable with a usage of the Arabs, which is, to add p to any pl. of the measure fiEaAlN or of that of fuEuwlN , as in the instances of *ikaArapN and fiHaAlapN and *ukuwrapN and fuHuwlapN . (AHeyth.) And (metonymically, TA) (tropical:) Sand: (IAar, K;) pl. A^aHojaArN . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] A^aholu AlHajari The people of the desert, who dwell in stony and sandy places: occurring in a trad., coupled with A^aholu Almadari . (TA.) ― -b3- AlHajaru AlA^asowadu , and simply AlHajaru , The [ Black ] Stone of the Kaabeh. (K, TA.) El-Farezdak applies to it, in one instance, the pl. AlA^aHojaAru , considering the sing. as applicable to every part of it. (TA.) ― -b4- One says, fulaAnN Hajaru AlA^aroDi , meaning (assumed tropical:) Such a one is unequalled. (TA.) And rumiYa fulaAnN biHajari AlA^aroDi (tropical:) Such a one has had a very sagacious and crafty and politic man made to be an assailant against him. (K, * TA.) El-Ahnaf Ibn-Keys said to 'Alee, when Mo'á- wiyeh named 'Amr Ibn-El-'Ás as one of the two umpires, qado rumiyta biHajari AlA^aroDi faA@joEalo maEahu A@bona Eab~aAsK faA_in~ahu laA yaEoqidu EuqodapF A_il~aA Hal~ahaA (assumed tropical:) Thou hast had a most exceedingly sagacious and crafty and politic man made to be an assailant against thee: so appoint thou with him Ibn-'Abbás; for he will not tie a knot but he shall untie it: meaning one that shall stand firm like a stone upon the ground. (L from a trad.) One says also, rumYa fulaAnN biHajarihi , meaning (tropical:) Such a one was coupled [or opposed ] with his like: (A:) [as though he had a stone suited to the purpose of knocking him down cast at him.] ― -b5- liloEaAhiri AlHajaru , occurring in a trad., means (assumed tropical:) For the fornicator, or adulterer, disappointment, and prohibition: accord. to some, it is meant to allude to stoning; [and it may have had this meaning in the first instance in which it was used;] but [in general] this is not the case; for every fornicator is not to be stoned. (IAth, TA.) [See also art. Ehr .] ― -b6- AlHajaru Gold: and silver. (K.) Both together are called AlHajaraAni . (S.)

sourceDefinition: A severe year, that confines men to their tents, or houses, so that they slaughter their generous camels to eat them. (L in art. nbt , on a verse of Zuheyr.) -A2- A side; an adjacent tract or quarter; (ISd, K;) as also ↓ HajorapN : (EM p. 281:) pl. of the former ↓ HajorN , [or rather this is a coll. gen. n., of which the former is the n. un.,] and HajaraAtN (S, K) and ↓ HawaAjiru : (K:) the last is mentioned by ISd as being thought by him to be a pl. of HajorapN in the sense above explained, contr. to analogy.
