sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. rujuwEN (S, Msb, K, &c.) and rajoEN , (M, Msb,) but the former is that which commonly obtains and is agreeable with analogy as inf. n. of the intrans. v., and the latter as inf. n. of the trans. v., (MF, TA,) and marojaEN , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) which is anomalous, because inf. ns. [of this kind] of verbs of the measure faEala having the aor. of the measure yafoEilu are [by rule] only with fet-h [to the medial radical], (S, K,) and marojiEapN , which is in like manner anomalous, (K,) and rujoEaY , (S, Msb, K,) [not rujoEFY as in the Lexicons of Golius and Freytag,] and rujoEaAnN , (K,) He returned; he went, or came, back [to the same place, or person, or (assumed tropical:) state, or (assumed tropical:) occupation, or (assumed tropical:) action, or (assumed tropical:) saying, &c.]; he reverted; contr. of *ahaba ; (ISk, Msb;) i. q. AnoSarafa : (K:) rujuwEN signifies the returning to a former place, or (assumed tropical:) quality, or (assumed tropical:) state; (Kull p. 196;) the returning to that from which was the commencement, or from which the commencement is supposed to have been, whether it be a place, or (assumed tropical:) an action, or (assumed tropical:) a saying, and whether the returning be by the [ whole ] person or thing, or by a part thereof, or by an action thereof. (Er-Rághib.) Hence the saying in the Kur [lxiii. 8], lay^ino rajaEonaA A_ilaY Almadiynapi [ Verily if we return to the city ]. (Er-Rághib.) And [in the same, xii. 63,] falam~aA rajaEuwA A_ilaY A^abiyhimo [ And when they returned to their father ]. (Idem.) And in the same, [vi. 164, and xxxix. 9,] vum~a A_ilaY rab~ikumo marojiEukumo [ Then unto your Lord shall be your return ]: (S:) the like of which occurs in the same, vi. 60: but it may be either from [the intrans. inf. n.] rujuwEN or from [the trans.] rajoEN : (Er-Rághib:) it cannot be a n. of place, because it is made trans. by means of A_ilaY , and also because it occurs in the Kur [v. 53, &c.], followed by jamiyEFA , as a denotative of state: (L:) in like manner Alr~ujoEaY also occurs in the Kur xcvi. 8. (TA.) You say also, rajaEati AlmaroA^apu A_ilaY A^aholihaA The woman returned to her family by reason of the death of her husband or by reason of divorcement. (Msb.) ― -b2- rajaEa A_ilaY AlS~iH~api (assumed tropical:) [ He returned to soundness, or health ], or AlmaraDi [ disease, or sickness ]; and A_ilaY HaAlapi Alfaqori (assumed tropical:) [ to the state of poverty ], or AlginaY (assumed tropical:) [ wealth, or competence, or sufficiency ]. (Kull p. 196.) ― -b3- rajaEa Eawodahu EalaY badoy^ihi He returned in the way by which he had come. (Kull ibid.) ― -b4- rajaEa mino safarihi He returned from his journey. (Msb.) ― -b5- rajaEa Eani AlA^imori (assumed tropical:) He returned [or reverted ] from the affair. (Msb.) ― -b6- rajaEa Eani Al$~aYo'i (assumed tropical:) He left, or relinquished, the thing. (Kull p. 197.) ― -b7- rajaEa Eani Al*~anobi (assumed tropical:) [ He relinquished sin; i. e.] he repented; and so rajaEa alone, agreeably with the usage in the Kur iii. 65, &c. (Er-Rághib.) ― -b8- [Several other phrases, in which this verb occurs, will be found in other arts.: as rajaEa EalaY Zahorihi in art. Zhr : rajaEotu AlqahoqaraY in art. qhqr : rajaEa darajahu , and variations thereof, in art. drj : &c.] ― -b9- rajaEa A_ilayohi [sometimes signifies the same as rajaEa Ealayohi ] He returned against him; he returned to attack him. (TA.) ― -b10- Saram~niY vum~a rajaEa yakal~imuniY (tropical:) [ He cut me, or ceased to speak to me; then he returned to speaking to me ]. (TA.) ― -b11- xaAlafaniY vum~a rajaEa A_ilaY qawoliY (tropical:) [ He opposed me, or disagreed with me; then he returned, or had regard, to my saying ]. (TA.) ― -b12- maA rujiEa A_ilayohi fiY xaTobK A_il~aA kafaY (tropical:) [ Re course was not had to him in an affair, or an affliction, but he sufficed. ] (TA.) [ rajaEa A_ilayohi often means He had recourse, or he recurred, to him, or it. ] ― -b13- rajaEa bihi EalaY $ariykihi (assumed tropical:) He made a claim for restitution of it upon his co-partner. (IAth, TA in art. xlT .) And [in like manner you say,] EalaY Algariymi ↓ AirotajaEa , and Almut~ahami , (assumed tropical:) He sued, prosecuted, or made a demand upon, the debtor, and the suspected, for his right, or due. (TA: [in which it is said, immediately before this, that ArtjE is like rajaEa .]) ― -b14- rajaEa Alkalobu fiY qayoy^ihi The dog returned to his vomit, (Msb, TA,) and ate it. (Msb.) ― -b15- Hence, rajaEa fiY hibatihi (tropical:) He took back his gift; repossessed himself of it; restored it to his possession; (Msb;) as also ↓ ArtjEhA , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) and ↓ AstrjEhA . (Msb, TA.) And minohu Al$~aYo' ↓ AstrjE (assumed tropical:) He took back from him the thing which he had given to him. (S, K.) ― -b16- [Hence also, rajaEa fiY qawolihi , and fiY Hukomihi (assumed tropical:) He retracted, or revoked, his saying, and his judgment, or sentence. ] ― -b17- huwa yarojiEu A_ilaY manoSibi SidoqK (assumed tropical:) He traces back his lineage to an excellent origin. (TA in art. nSb .) ― -b18- [ yarojiEu A_ilaY maEonaY ka*aA (assumed tropical:) It (a word used in a certain sense) is referrible, or reducible, to such a meaning. And yurojiEu A_ilaY ka*aA , said of a word, also means (assumed tropical:) It relates to such a thing; i. e., to such another word, in grammatical construction.] ― -b19- rajaEa A_ilaY qadori ka*aA (assumed tropical:) It (wine when cooked) became reduced to such a quantity; syn. A=la . (S in art. Awl .) ― -b20- rajaEa AlHawoDu A_ilaY A_izaAy^ihi The water of the trough, or tank, became much in quantity [ so that it returned to the height of the place whence it poured in ]. (TA.) ― -b21- ↓ rijaAEN , also, is an inf. n. of this verb, (L,) and is used as signifying The returning of birds after their migrating to a hot country. (S, L, K.) You say, rajaEati AlT~ayoru AlqawaATiEu , inf. n. rijaAEN and rajoEN , The migratory birds returned. (L.) ― -b22- Also inf. n. of rajaEato said of a-she camel, and of a she-ass, signifying (assumed tropical:) She raised her tail, and compressed her two sides ( quTorayohaA ), and cast forth her urine in repeated discharges, so that she was imagined to be pregnant, (S, K,) and then failed of fulfilling her [ apparent ] promise: (S: [in some copies of which, as is said in the TA, the inf. n. of the verb in this sense is written rujuwE :]) or she conceived, and then failed of fulfilling her promise; because she who does so goes back from what is hoped of her: (TA:) or, said of a she-camel, she cast forth her fœtus in an imperfect state: (AZ, TA,) or, as some say, her embryo in a fluid state: (TA:) or in an unformed state; inf. n. rijaAEN . (Msb in art. xdj .) [See also raAjiEN , below.] -A2- , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. rajaEahu , (Mgh,) inf. n. rajoEN and marojaEN and marojiEN , (K,) He made, or caused, him, or it, to return, go back, come back, or revert; sent back, turned back, or returned, him, or it; syn. rad~ahu ; (Mgh, Msb, K;) and Sarafahu ; (K;) Eani Al$~aYo'i from the thing; and A_ilayohi to it; (Msb, K;) as also ↓ ArjEhu ; (S, Msb, K;) but the former is the more chaste word, and is that which is used in the Kur-án, in ix. 84 [and other places]: (Msb:) the latter is of the dial. of Hudheyl; (S, Msb;) and is said by MF to be of weak authority, and bad; but [SM says,] I do not find this asserted by any of the leading authorities: (TA:) ↓ ArtjEhu , also, signifies [the same, i. e.] the same as rad~ahu in like manner followed by A_ilaY . (TA.) Thus in the Kur ix. 84, referred to above, faA_ino rajaEaka A@ll~`hu [ And if God make thee to return, or restore thee ]. (Msb.) ― -b2- rajaEa fulaAnN EaliY A^anofi baEiyirhi Such a one put back, or restored, the nose-rein [ AlxiTaAma being understood] upon the nose of his camel; it having become displaced. (TA.) ― -b3- rajaEa A_ilaY~a AljawaAba , aor. , inf. n. rajoEN and rujoEaAnN , He returned to me the answer. (S, TA: [in the latter of which, this is said to be tropical; but when a written answer is meant, it is evidently not so.]) ― -b4- rajaEotu AlkalaAma (assumed tropical:) I returned the speech; or I repeated it; or I rebutted, or rejected, or repudiated, it, in reply, or replication; syn. radadotuhu . (Msb.) [In like manner,] yarojiEu baEoDuhumo A_ilaY baEoDK Alqawola , in the Kur [xxxiv. 30], means (assumed tropical:) Holding a colloquy, or a disputation, or debate, one with another: (Bd:) [or it means (assumed tropical:) rebutting one another's sayings: ] or (assumed tropical:) blaming one another. (S.) ― -b5- Alr~ajoEu , (K,) or rajoEu Ald~aAb~api yadayohaA fiY Als~ayori , (S,) (tropical:) The stepping of the beast, (S, K,) or her returning her fore legs, [ drawing the fore feet backwards towards the body, by lifting them high, ] in going; (K;) and ↓ Alt~arojiyEu , (K,) or tarojiyEu Ald~aAb~pi yadayohaA fiY Als~ayori , (S,) signifies the same: (S, K:) or rajoEN signifies a beast's elevating, or lifting high, the fore foot and hind foot, in going. (KL.) You say, Ald~aAb~apu yadayohaA fiY ↓ raj~aEati Als~ayori (tropical:) [ The beast stepped, &c.; like as you say, rajaEat ]. (TA.) ― -b6- rajoEu AlwaA$mapi , and ↓ tarojayEuhaA , (assumed tropical:) The female tattooer's making marks or lines [ upon the skin ]: (S, K: *) [or rather, as the former phrase is explained in the EM p. 143, “ her retracing ” those marks or lines, and renewing their blackness; for] you say also, Alnaqo$a ↓ raj~aEa , and Alwa$oma , [and rajaEahu ,] (assumed tropical:) He retraced the marks, or lines, of the variegated work, and of the tattooing, and renewed their blackness, one time after another. (TA.) And AlkitaAbapa ↓ raj~aEa , [and rajaEahaA ,] (assumed tropical:) He retraced, or renewed, the writing. (TA.) ― -b7- rajaEa naAqapF , and ↓ ArtjEhA , and ↓ trj~EhA , He purchased a she-camel with the price of another that he sold: (S, TA:) or he purchased a she-camel with the price of a he-camel that he sold; and ↓ rijaEN , which is app. an inf. n., signifies the selling males and purchasing females: (TA:) or maAlFA ↓ ArtjE signifies he sold the aged and the younglings of his came's, and purchased such as were in a state of youthful vigour: or, as some say, he sold the males, and purchased females: (Lh:) or ↓ AirotijaAEN signifies the selling a thing, and purchasing in its place what one imagines to be more youthful, and better: (Lh in another place:) regard is bad, therein, to the meaning of a return, virtual, or understood, though not real: (Er-Rághib:) also A_ibilFA ↓ ArjE he sold old and weak camels, and purchased such as were in a state of youthful vigour: or he sold male camels, and purchased females: (TA:) and A_ibilFA ↓ ArtjE biA_ibilihi he took camels in exchange for his camels: or, as some say, ↓ AirotijaAEN signifies the taking one in the place, and with the price, of two. (Mgh.) ― -b8- rajaEa AlEalafu fiY Ald~aAb~api (tropical:) The fodder, or food, produced an effect, or showed its effect, upon the beast. (K, * TA.) And rajaEa kalaAmiY fiyhi (tropical:) My speech produced a beneficial effect upon him. (K, * TA.)

And [in the same, xii. 63,] falam~aA rajaEuwA A_ilaY A^abiyhimo [ And when they returned to their father ]. (Idem.) And in the same, [vi. 164, and xxxix. 9,] vum~a A_ilaY rab~ikumo marojiEukumo [ Then unto your Lord shall be your return ]: (S:) the like of which occurs in the same, vi. 60: but it may be either from [the intrans. inf. n.] rujuwEN or from [the trans.] rajoEN : (Er-Rághib:) it cannot be a n. of place, because it is made trans. by means of A_ilaY , and also because it occurs in the Kur [v. 53, &c.], followed by jamiyEFA , as a denotative of state: (L:) in like manner Alr~ujoEaY also occurs in the Kur xcvi. 8. (TA.) You say also, rajaEati AlmaroA^apu A_ilaY A^aholihaA The woman returned to her family by reason of the death of her husband or by reason of divorcement. (Msb.) ― -b2- rajaEa A_ilaY AlS~iH~api (assumed tropical:) [ He returned to soundness, or health ], or AlmaraDi [ disease, or sickness ]; and A_ilaY HaAlapi Alfaqori (assumed tropical:) [ to the state of poverty ], or AlginaY (assumed tropical:) [ wealth, or competence, or sufficiency ]. (Kull p. 196.) ― -b3- rajaEa Eawodahu EalaY badoy^ihi He returned in the way by which he had come. (Kull ibid.) ― -b4- rajaEa mino safarihi He returned from his journey. (Msb.) ― -b5- rajaEa Eani AlA^imori (assumed tropical:) He returned [or reverted ] from the affair. (Msb.) ― -b6- rajaEa Eani Al$~aYo'i (assumed tropical:) He left, or relinquished, the thing. (Kull p. 197.) ― -b7- rajaEa Eani Al*~anobi (assumed tropical:) [ He relinquished sin; i. e.] he repented; and so rajaEa alone, agreeably with the usage in the Kur iii. 65, &c. (Er-Rághib.) ― -b8- [Several other phrases, in which this verb occurs, will be found in other arts.: as rajaEa EalaY Zahorihi in art. Zhr : rajaEotu AlqahoqaraY in art. qhqr : rajaEa darajahu , and variations thereof, in art. drj : &c.] ― -b9- rajaEa A_ilayohi [sometimes signifies the same as rajaEa Ealayohi ] He returned against him; he returned to attack him. (TA.) ― -b10- Saram~niY vum~a rajaEa yakal~imuniY (tropical:) [ He cut me, or ceased to speak to me; then he returned to speaking to me ]. (TA.) ― -b11- xaAlafaniY vum~a rajaEa A_ilaY qawoliY (tropical:) [ He opposed me, or disagreed with me; then he returned, or had regard, to my saying ]. (TA.) ― -b12- maA rujiEa A_ilayohi fiY xaTobK A_il~aA kafaY (tropical:) [ Re course was not had to him in an affair, or an affliction, but he sufficed. ] (TA.) [ rajaEa A_ilayohi often means He had recourse, or he recurred, to him, or it. ] ― -b13- rajaEa bihi EalaY $ariykihi (assumed tropical:) He made a claim for restitution of it upon his co-partner. (IAth, TA in art. xlT .) And [in like manner you say,] EalaY Algariymi ↓ AirotajaEa , and Almut~ahami , (assumed tropical:) He sued, prosecuted, or made a demand upon, the debtor, and the suspected, for his right, or due. (TA: [in which it is said, immediately before this, that ArtjE is like rajaEa .]) ― -b14- rajaEa Alkalobu fiY qayoy^ihi The dog returned to his vomit, (Msb, TA,) and ate it. (Msb.) ― -b15- Hence, rajaEa fiY hibatihi (tropical:) He took back his gift; repossessed himself of it; restored it to his possession; (Msb;) as also ↓ ArtjEhA , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) and ↓ AstrjEhA . (Msb, TA.) And minohu Al$~aYo' ↓ AstrjE (assumed tropical:) He took back from him the thing which he had given to him. (S, K.) ― -b16- [Hence also, rajaEa fiY qawolihi , and fiY Hukomihi (assumed tropical:) He retracted, or revoked, his saying, and his judgment, or sentence. ] ― -b17- huwa yarojiEu A_ilaY manoSibi SidoqK (assumed tropical:) He traces back his lineage to an excellent origin. (TA in art. nSb .) ― -b18- [ yarojiEu A_ilaY maEonaY ka*aA (assumed tropical:) It (a word used in a certain sense) is referrible, or reducible, to such a meaning. And yurojiEu A_ilaY ka*aA , said of a word, also means (assumed tropical:) It relates to such a thing; i. e., to such another word, in grammatical construction.] ― -b19- rajaEa A_ilaY qadori ka*aA (assumed tropical:) It (wine when cooked) became reduced to such a quantity; syn. A=la . (S in art. Awl .) ― -b20- rajaEa AlHawoDu A_ilaY A_izaAy^ihi The water of the trough, or tank, became much in quantity [ so that it returned to the height of the place whence it poured in ]. (TA.) ― -b21- ↓ rijaAEN , also, is an inf. n. of this verb, (L,) and is used as signifying The returning of birds after their migrating to a hot country. (S, L, K.) You say, rajaEati AlT~ayoru AlqawaATiEu , inf. n. rijaAEN and rajoEN , The migratory birds returned. (L.) ― -b22- Also inf. n. of rajaEato said of a-she camel, and of a she-ass, signifying (assumed tropical:) She raised her tail, and compressed her two sides ( quTorayohaA ), and cast forth her urine in repeated discharges, so that she was imagined to be pregnant, (S, K,) and then failed of fulfilling her [ apparent ] promise: (S: [in some copies of which, as is said in the TA, the inf. n. of the verb in this sense is written rujuwE :]) or she conceived, and then failed of fulfilling her promise; because she who does so goes back from what is hoped of her: (TA:) or, said of a she-camel, she cast forth her fœtus in an imperfect state: (AZ, TA,) or, as some say, her embryo in a fluid state: (TA:) or in an unformed state; inf. n. rijaAEN . (Msb in art. xdj .) [See also raAjiEN , below.] -A2- , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. rajaEahu , (Mgh,) inf. n. rajoEN and marojaEN and marojiEN , (K,) He made, or caused, him, or it, to return, go back, come back, or revert; sent back, turned back, or returned, him, or it; syn. rad~ahu ; (Mgh, Msb, K;) and Sarafahu ; (K;) Eani Al$~aYo'i from the thing; and A_ilayohi to it; (Msb, K;) as also ↓ ArjEhu ; (S, Msb, K;) but the former is the more chaste word, and is that which is used in the Kur-án, in ix. 84 [and other places]: (Msb:) the latter is of the dial. of Hudheyl; (S, Msb;) and is said by MF to be of weak authority, and bad; but [SM says,] I do not find this asserted by any of the leading authorities: (TA:) ↓ ArtjEhu , also, signifies [the same, i. e.] the same as rad~ahu in like manner followed by A_ilaY . (TA.) Thus in the Kur ix. 84, referred to above, faA_ino rajaEaka A@ll~`hu [ And if God make thee to return, or restore thee ]. (Msb.) ― -b2- rajaEa fulaAnN EaliY A^anofi baEiyirhi Such a one put back, or restored, the nose-rein [ AlxiTaAma being understood] upon the nose of his camel; it having become displaced. (TA.) ― -b3- rajaEa A_ilaY~a AljawaAba , aor. , inf. n. rajoEN and rujoEaAnN , He returned to me the answer. (S, TA: [in the latter of which, this is said to be tropical; but when a written answer is meant, it is evidently not so.]) ― -b4- rajaEotu AlkalaAma (assumed tropical:) I returned the speech; or I repeated it; or I rebutted, or rejected, or repudiated, it, in reply, or replication; syn. radadotuhu . (Msb.) [In like manner,] yarojiEu baEoDuhumo A_ilaY baEoDK Alqawola , in the Kur [xxxiv. 30], means (assumed tropical:) Holding a colloquy, or a disputation, or debate, one with another: (Bd:) [or it means (assumed tropical:) rebutting one another's sayings: ] or (assumed tropical:) blaming one another. (S.) ― -b5- Alr~ajoEu , (K,) or rajoEu Ald~aAb~api yadayohaA fiY Als~ayori , (S,) (tropical:) The stepping of the beast, (S, K,) or her returning her fore legs, [ drawing the fore feet backwards towards the body, by lifting them high, ] in going; (K;) and ↓ Alt~arojiyEu , (K,) or tarojiyEu Ald~aAb~pi yadayohaA fiY Als~ayori , (S,) signifies the same: (S, K:) or rajoEN signifies a beast's elevating, or lifting high, the fore foot and hind foot, in going. (KL.) You say, Ald~aAb~apu yadayohaA fiY ↓ raj~aEati Als~ayori (tropical:) [ The beast stepped, &c.; like as you say, rajaEat ]. (TA.) ― -b6- rajoEu AlwaA$mapi , and ↓ tarojayEuhaA , (assumed tropical:) The female tattooer's making marks or lines [ upon the skin ]: (S, K: *) [or rather, as the former phrase is explained in the EM p. 143, “ her retracing ” those marks or lines, and renewing their blackness; for] you say also, Alnaqo$a ↓ raj~aEa , and Alwa$oma , [and rajaEahu ,] (assumed tropical:) He retraced the marks, or lines, of the variegated work, and of the tattooing, and renewed their blackness, one time after another. (TA.) And AlkitaAbapa ↓ raj~aEa , [and rajaEahaA ,] (assumed tropical:) He retraced, or renewed, the writing. (TA.) ― -b7- rajaEa naAqapF , and ↓ ArtjEhA , and ↓ trj~EhA , He purchased a she-camel with the price of another that he sold: (S, TA:) or he purchased a she-camel with the price of a he-camel that he sold; and ↓ rijaEN , which is app. an inf. n., signifies the selling males and purchasing females: (TA:) or maAlFA ↓ ArtjE signifies he sold the aged and the younglings of his came's, and purchased such as were in a state of youthful vigour: or, as some say, he sold the males, and purchased females: (Lh:) or ↓ AirotijaAEN signifies the selling a thing, and purchasing in its place what one imagines to be more youthful, and better: (Lh in another place:) regard is bad, therein, to the meaning of a return, virtual, or understood, though not real: (Er-Rághib:) also A_ibilFA ↓ ArjE he sold old and weak camels, and purchased such as were in a state of youthful vigour: or he sold male camels, and purchased females: (TA:) and A_ibilFA ↓ ArtjE biA_ibilihi he took camels in exchange for his camels: or, as some say, ↓ AirotijaAEN signifies the taking one in the place, and with the price, of two. (Mgh.) ― -b8- rajaEa AlEalafu fiY Ald~aAb~api (tropical:) The fodder, or food, produced an effect, or showed its effect, upon the beast. (K, * TA.) And rajaEa kalaAmiY fiyhi (tropical:) My speech produced a beneficial effect upon him. (K, * TA.)

definition: , inf. n. tarojiyEN , He, or it, made, or caused, him, or it, to return, go back, come back, or revert, again and again, or time after time; sent back, turned back, or returned, him, or it, again and...
sourceDefinition: , inf. n. tarojiyEN , He, or it, made, or caused, him, or it, to return, go back, come back, or revert, again and again, or time after time; sent back, turned back, or returned, him, or it, again and again, or time after time; made, or caused, him, or it, to go, or move, repeatedly to and fro; so to go and come; to reciprocate: he repeated it; iterated it; or rather reiterated it: he reproduced it: he renewed it: syn. rad~adahu . (Mgh.) [All these significations are well known, as pertaining to the two verbs here mentioned, and of frequent occurrence in classical and postclassical writings: and hence several phrases here following.] ― -b2- See 1, last quarter of the paragraph, in five places. ― -b3- Hence, (Mgh,) Alt~arojiyEu fiY AlA^a*aAni , (S, Mgh, K,) because the two professions of the faith [for which see the word A^a*aAnN ] are uttered in the A*An [or call to prayer] in a low voice [and then repeated in a high voice]; (Mgh;) [for] this phrase means (tropical:) The repeating the two professions of the faith in a raised, or loud, voice, after uttering them in a low, or faint, voice; (Sgh, K, TA;) or the lowering of the voice in the A*An in uttering the two professions of the faith, and then raising it in uttering them: (KT:) or rj~E fiY A^a*aAnihi signifies he uttered the two professions of the faith in his A*An once to repeat them. (Msb: [but this is a strange explanation; and probably corrupted by a copyist: it seems that, instead of “ to repeat them, ” we should read “ and repeated them. ”]) ― -b4- [Hence also,] Alt~arojiyEu , (K, TA,) or tarojiyEu AlS~awoti , (S,) (assumed tropical:) [ The act of quavering, or trilling; rapidly repeating many times one very short note, or each note of a piece; a general characteristic of Arabian chanting and singing and piping, and often continued throughout the whole performance;] the reiterating ( tarodiyd ) of the voice in the throat, or fauces, (S, K, TA,) like [ as is done in ] chanting, (S,) or which is practised in reading or reciting, or singing, or piping, or other performances, of such as are accompanied with quavering, or trilling: (TA:) or, as some say, the mutual approximation of the various kinds of movements in the voice: 'Abd-Allah Ibn-Mughaffal, in his trjyE , by the prolonging of the voice, in reading, or reciting, imitated the like of A=A A=A A=A . (TA.) You say also, rj~E AlHamaAmu fiY ginaAy^ihi (assumed tropical:) [ The pigeons quavered in their singing, or cooing ]; as also ↓ AstrjE . (TA.) And rj~E AlbaEiyru fiY $iqo$iqatihi (assumed tropical:) The camel brayed, or reiterated his voice, in his $q$qp [or bursa faucium ]. (TA.) And rj~Et Aln~aAqapu fiY HaniynihaA (assumed tropical:) The she-camel interrupted her yearning cry to, or for, her young one [ and then, app., quickly repeated it, and did so again and again ]. (TA.) And rj~Et Alqawosu (assumed tropical:) The bow made a sound [ by the vibration of its string; because the sound so made is a repeated sound]. (AHn.) ― -b5- See also 4. ― -b6- And see 10.

definition: He (a man) returned to good or to evil.
sourceDefinition: He (a man) returned to good or to evil. (TA.) [See also 6.] ― -b2- rAjEt Aln~aAqapu , (K,) inf. n. rijaAEN , (TA,) The she-camel returned, or reverted, from one kind of pace, which she had been going, to another pace. (K, * TA.) ― -b3- rAjEhu (assumed tropical:) It returned to him: said of pain [&c.]. (TA in art. Ed .) ― -b4- rAjE A@moraA^atahu (tropical:) [ He returned to his wife, or restored her to himself, or took her back by marriage or to the marriage-state, after having divorced her; (see also 6;)]; (S;) and ↓ ArtjEhA signifies the same. (TA.) ― -b5- [See also a verse cited voce radaAdN ; whence it seems that rAjE also signifies He restored, or brought back, anything.] ― -b6- rAjEhu signifies also He endeavoured to turn him [from, or to, a thing]; syn. raAwadahu , and raAd~ahu . (L in art. rwd .) ― -b7- rAjEhu AlkalaAma , (S and K in this art., and A and Mgh and Msb in art. Hwr ,) and fiY AlkalaAmi , (Bd in xviii. 32,) and simply raAjEhu , (Msb in this art., and Jel. in lviii. l,) inf. n. muraAjaEapN (S, TA) and rijaAEN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He returned him answer for answer, or answers for answers; held a dialogue, or colloquy, or conference, or a disputation, or debate, with him; bandied words with him; syn. HaAwarahu , (A and Mgh and Msb in art. Hwr , and Bd in xviii. 32,) [i. e.] HaAwarahu AlkalaAma ; (TA;) or EaAwadahu ; (S and Msb and K in this art.;) or jaAdalahu . (Jel in lviii. 1.) And rAjEhu , or rAjEhu Alqawola , (assumed tropical:) He disputed with him, rebutting, or rejecting, or repudiating, in reply to him, what he said; he bandied words with him; syn. raAd~ahu Alqawola . (A in art. rd .) You say, rAjEhu fiY muhim~aAtihi He held a colloquy, or conference, or a disputation, or debate, with him respecting his affairs of difficulty; syn. HaAwarahu . (TA.) [And rAjEhu fiY ka*aA He addressed him repeatedly, or time after time, respecting such a thing. ] And raAjaEuwA Euquwlahumo [ They consulted their understandings, or minds; as though they held a colloquy, or conference, or a disputation, or debate, therewith]. (Bd in xxi. 65.) [ rAjE often signifies He consulted, or referred to, a person, a book, a passage in a book, &c.]

definition: (assumed tropical:) [ The she-camel returned to her former condition, either of leanness or fatness: ] (assumed tropical:) the she-camel became lean [ after having been fat ]: and (assumed tropical:)...
sourceDefinition: (assumed tropical:) [ The she-camel returned to her former condition, either of leanness or fatness: ] (assumed tropical:) the she-camel became lean [ after having been fat ]: and (assumed tropical:) became in good condition after leanness: (Ks, T, TA:) or ArjEt AlA_ibilu (assumed tropical:) the camels became lean and then became fat; (S, O, K;) so says Ks. (S.) You say also, Al$~ayoxu yamoraDu yuwomayoni falaA yurojiEu $ahorFA (assumed tropical:) i. e. [ The old man is sick two days, and ] does not return to a healthy state of body, and to strength, in a month. sourceDefinition: inf. n. of un. of 1; A return; a single act of returning, of going back, coming back, or reverting: (TA:) [and] i. q. rujuwEN , i. e. the act of returning, &c. (Msb.) ― -b2- The returning to the present state of existence (S, Msb, K) after death. (S, K.) So in the phrase, fulaAnN yuw^ominu biAlr~ajoEapi [ Such a one believes in the returning to the present state of existence after death ]. (S, Msb, K. *) This was a tenet of some of the Arabs in the Time of Ignorance, and of a sect of Muslim innovators, and of a sect of the raAfiDap , who say that 'Alee the son of Aboo-Tálib is concealing himself in the clouds, to come forth when he shall be summoned to do so. (L.) ― -b3- The returning, or homeward course, of a military expedition; opposed to badoA^apN , q. v. (T and Mgh in art. bdA^ .) ― -b4- The return of a party of warriors to war after their having come back from an expedition. (TA.) ― -b5- Also, and ↓ rijoEapN , (S, A, Nh, Mgh, Msb, K,) but the former is the more chaste, (S, Msb, TA,) though the latter is mentioned before the former in the K, (TA,) (tropical:) A man's returning to his wife, or restoring her to himself, or taking her back by marriage or to the marriage-state, after having divorced her; (IF, Msb;) the returning of the divorcer to the divorced woman: (K:) or the taking back to marriage a woman who has been divorced, but not by an absolutely-separating sentence, without a new contract. (Nh.) You say, lahu EalaY A@moraA^atihi rajoEapN and ↓ rijoEapN (tropical:) [ He has a right of returning to, or taking back, his wife after having divorced her ]: (S, Mgh:) and yamoliku Alr~ajoEapa EalaY zawojatihi (tropical:) [ He possesses the right of returning &c.]: (Msb:) and Tal~aqa fulaAnN fulaAnapa TalaAqFA yamoliku fiyhi Alr~ajoEapa (tropical:) [ Such a man divorced such a woman by a divorce in which he possessed the right of returning &c.]. (TA.) ― -b6- Also the former, (S, Msb, TA,) and ↓ rijoEapN likewise, (Msb,) and ↓ rujoEapN (K) and ↓ rujoEaY [which is originally an inf. n.] and ↓ rujoEaAnN [which is also originally an inf. n.] and ↓ marojuwEN (S, K) and ↓ marojuwEapN and ↓ rajuwEapN and ↓ rajoEN , (K,) the last of these is allowable, (TA,) [being an inf. n. used in the sense of a pass. part. n.,] (tropical:) The reply, or answer, of an epistle. (S, Msb, * K, TA.) You say, halo jaA='a rajoEapu kitaAbika (S, TA) and ↓ rujoEaAnuhu (TA) (tropical:) Hath the reply, or answer, of thine epistle come:? (S, TA:) and ↓ A^arosaltu A_ilayoka famaA jaA='aniY rujoEaY risaAlatiY (tropical:) I sent to thee, and the reply, or answer, of my epistle came not to me; i. e. ↓ marojuwEuhaA : (S, K, * TA:) and fulaAnK Ealayoka ↓ maA kaAna mino marojuwEi (tropical:) What was [the purport] of the reply, or answer, of such a one to thee? (S, TA.) And [in like manner] Alr~i$oq ↓ rajoEu signifies (assumed tropical:) What is returned against, or in opposition to, [or in reply to, ] the simultaneous discharge of a number of arrows in a particular direction. (TA.) ― -b7- See also rijoEapN .

definition: ― -b2- A return, or profit, obtained by the expenditure of the price of camels sold: see an ex.
sourceDefinition: : see rajoEapN , in three places. ― -b2- A return, or profit, obtained by the expenditure of the price of camels sold: see an ex. above, voce AirotajaEa : (S, K:) or camels taken in exchange for other camels: or one that is taken in the place, and with the price, of two: (Mgh:) also the young, or younglings, of camels, which are purchased from the market with the price of others, or taken from the market in exchange for others: (K:) or, as Khálid says, the [ return obtained by ] bringing bad camels into the market and taking back good ones: or, as some say, the [ return obtained by ] bringing in males and taking back females: (TA:) [the words which I have here twice inserted in brackets are perhaps not necessary to complete the sense intended, as will be seen at the close of this sentence; but they seem to be required in the opinion of SM, for he has immediately added the further explanation which here next follows, and which is also, but less fully, given by J, immediately after the first explanation in this paragraph:] and rijoEapN has a similar meaning in relation to the poor-rates; being applied to camels taken by the collector of the poor-rates older or younger than those which their owner is bound to give: (S, * TA:) and camels which are purchased by the Arabs of the desert, [app. in exchange-for others, ] not of their own breeding nor bearing their marks; as also ↓ rajoEapN : (TA, [see 8:]) IB says that the pl. of rijoEapN is ↓ rujaEN ; and that it was said to a tribe of the Arabs, “ By what means have your beasts become many? ” and they answered, A^awoSaAnaA A^abuwnaA biAln~ujaEi waAlr~ujaEi : but Th says, ↓ bAln~ijaEi wAlr~ijaEi : [both are probably correct; for it seems that the original forms are Aln~ujaE and Alr~ijaE ; and that, in one case, the latter is assimilated to the former; in the other, accord. to a usage less common, the former to the latter:] accord. to Th, the meaning is, [ Our father charged us with the seekings after herbage in the places thereof, and ] the selling the old and weak beasts and purchasing others in a state of youthful vigour: or, accord. to another explanation, the meaning is, the selling males and purchasing females: thus explained, rijaEN seems to be an inf. n. (TA. [See rajaEa naAqapF .]) [See also rajiyEa .] ― -b3- [(assumed tropical:) Any return, profit, or gain, accruing from a thing, or obtained by the sale or exchange thereof; as also ↓ marojuwEN ; and rajoEN , q. v.] You say, jaA='ato rijoEapu AlD~iyaAEi (assumed tropical:) The return, or increase, accruing to the owner of the lands came, or arrived. (Lh.) And jaA='a fulaAnN birijoEapK HasanapK (assumed tropical:) Such a one brought a good thing which he had purchased in the place of a bad thing; or in the place of a thing that was inferior to it. (TA.) And ↓ h`*aA mataAEN lahu marojuwEN (assumed tropical:) This is a commodity for which there will be a return, or profit, or gain. (S, * TA) And ↓ daAb~apN lahaA marojuwEN (assumed tropical:) A beast that may be sold after having been used. (El-Isbahánee.) And ↓ layosa lih`*aA AlbayoEi marojuwEN (tropical:) There is not, or will not be, any return, or profit, or gain, for this sale. (TA.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) An argument, or allegation, by which one rebuts in a litigation, or dispute; a proof; an evidence. (Ibn-'Abbád.)

definition: . [ Made, or caused, to return, go back, come back, or revert; sent back, turned back, or returned: repeated: rebutted, rejected, or repudiated, in reply, or replication: like ↓ marojuwEN : and used...
sourceDefinition: . [ Made, or caused, to return, go back, come back, or revert; sent back, turned back, or returned: repeated: rebutted, rejected, or repudiated, in reply, or replication: like ↓ marojuwEN : and used in all these senses; as will be seen from what follows: and also, like ↓ muraj~aEN ,] made, or caused, to return, go back, come back, or revert, again and again, or time after time; sent back, turned back, or returned, again and again, or time after time; made, or caused, to go, or move, repeatedly to and fro; so to go and come; to reciprocate: reiterated: reproduced: renewed: syn. murad~adN : [in the CK maroduwdN :] applied to anything: (S, K:) or to anything that is said or done: (Msb, TA:) because meaning ↓ marojuwEN , i. e. maroduwdN : (S, Msb, TA:) or, applied to speech, (assumed tropical:) returned to its author; or repeated to him; or rebutted, rejected, or repudiated, in reply to him; syn. maroduwdN A_ilaY SaAHibihi : (Lth, K:) or, so applied, (tropical:) repeated: (A, TA:) or, so applied, (assumed tropical:) reiterated: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or, so applied, (assumed tropical:) disapproved, or disliked. (TA.) You say, A_iy~aAka waAlr~ajiyEa mina Alqawoli (tropical:) Avoid thou the saying that is repeated; (A, TA;) [or rebutted, &c.;] or disapproved. (TA.) ― -b2- Applied to a beast, (S, TA,) and [particularly] to a camel, (K,) it signifies Made to return from journey to journey: (S, TA:) and also means (assumed tropical:) fatigued, or jaded, (S, K,) by journeying: (K:) fem. with rujuEN (S, K:) or (tropical:) lean, or emaciated: (Er-Rághib, K:) in the K is here added, or which thou hast made to return from a journey, meaning from journey to journey; but this is identical with the first explanation of the word applied to a beast: (TA:) pl. rujuEN ; (K;) or [app. of the fem., agreeably with analogy, and as seems to be indicated by J,] rajaAy^iEu . (S.) rajiyEu safarK and safarK ↓ rijoEu [in like manner] signify Made to return repeatedly, or several times, in journeying; applied to a she-camel: (K:) and the former signifies, applied to a beast, and [particularly] to a camel, a he-camel, ( baEiyr ,) which one makes to return again and again, or time after time, or to come and go repeatedly, in journeying, and drags along: (TA:) both also mean (tropical:) lean, or emaciated: and are in like manner applied to a man: (Er-Rághib, TA:) and ↓ rajoEiY~N and ↓ marojaEaAniY~N , also, but the latter is vulgar, (assumed tropical:) lean, or emaciated, by journeying; applied to a beast. (TA.) You say also saforN rajiyEN Travellers returning from a journey. (TA.) And safarN rajiyEN A journey in which are repeated returnings. (IAar.) ― -b3- Any food returned to the fire [ to be heated again ], having became cold: (K:) [and particularly] roasted meat heated a second time. (As.) ― -b4- A rope, or cord, undone, and then twisted a second time: (L, K:) and, as some say, anything done a second time. (L.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) Writing retraced with the pen, in order that it may became more plain: (KL:) and ↓ marojuwEN [signifies the same: and also] (assumed tropical:) tattooing repeated and renewed; (EM p. 108;) tattooing of which the blackness has been restored: (TA:) pl. of the latter maraAjiyEu . (TA, and EM ubi suprà.) ― -b6- (tropical:) Dung, ordure, or excrement, of a solid-hoofed animal; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ rajoEN ; (K;) and of a man; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ the latter word; (TA;) and of a beast of prey; as also ↓ the latter: (S, TA:) because it returns from its first state, (Mgh, Msb, TA,) after having been food or fodder &c.; (TA;) having the meaning of an act. part. n., (Er-Rághib, Msb,) or, it may be, of a pass. part. n. (Er-Rághib.) ― -b7- (tropical:) The cud which is ruminated by camels and the like: (S, * K:) because it returns to be eaten. (TA.) So in the saying of El-Aashà, wafalaApK kaA^an~ahaA Zahoru turosK layosa A_il~aA Alr~ajiyEa fiyhaA EalaAqu i. e. [ Many a desert, or waterless desert, as though it were the back of a shield, ] in which there is not found by the camels anything to serve for the support of life except the cud. (S.) ― -b8- (assumed tropical:) Sweat: (K:) because, having been water, it returns as sweat. (TA.) ― -b9- See also rajoEN , in three places. ― -b10- Also (assumed tropical:) The [ part called ] faA^os of a bit: (Ibn-' Abbád, K:) [because of its returning motion.] ― -b11- And (assumed tropical:) Niggardly, tenacious, or avaricious; syn. baxiylN [in the CK and a MS. copy of the K, naxiyl ]. (Ibn-' Abbád, K, TA.)

definition: Young men of the lowest, or basest, or meanest, sort, or of the refuse of mankind;
sourceDefinition: Young men of the lowest, or basest, or meanest, sort, or of the refuse of mankind; or low, ignoble, mean, or sordid, young men, such as serve for the food of their bellies: (S, K:) or the lowest, basest, or meanest, sort, or refuse, of mankind, or people: or a medley, or mixed or promiscuous multitude or collection, of men, or people; or of the lowest or basest or meanest sort, or refuse, thereof: (Msb:) and raEaAEu Aln~aAsi the lowest, basest, or meanest, sort, or refuse, of mankind, or of the people; the medley of men, or of such men: (TA:) n. un. with p : (Msb, TA:) Az mentions his having read in the handwriting of Sh AlrEAE mn AlnAs , like AlzjAj [in form, app. meaning ↓ Alr~uEaAEu , like Alz~ujaAju , for this is the most chaste form of the latter word, and the most usual with classical writers], as meaning the refuse, and weak, of mankind, or of the people, who, when frightened, fly. (TA.) ― -b2- [The n. un.] raEaAEapN signifies [also] One without heart and without intellect or intelligence. (AA, K.) ― -b3- And An ostrich; (Abu-l-'Omeythil, K;) because always as though frightened. (Abu-l-'Omeythil.)

sourceDefinition: , (T,) or raf~a lawonuhu , (S, M, O, K,) aor. , inf. n. raf~N and rafiyfN , Its colour shone, or glistened; (T, S, M, O, K;) said of a thing; (T;) as also ↓ Artf~ . (K.) Thus raf~ato A^asonaAnuhu , His teeth shone, or glistened. (M.) El-Aashà says, describing the front teeth of a woman, ya$ofiY Almutay~ama *aA AlHaraAraho wamahFA tarif~u guruwbuhu [ And clean, white, lustrous front teeth, the abundance of their saliva shining, or glistening; that would cure of his malady the enslaved by love who has burning in his heart]. (T, O, S.) And one says also, raf~a Albaroqu , aor. and , (M,) inf. n. raf~N , (M, K,) The lightning gleamed, or shone; or flashed faintly, and then disappeared, and then flashed again. (M, K. *) ― -b2- raf~a Aln~abaAtu , aor. , inf. n. rafiyfN , The plant, or herbage, quivered, or became tall, ( Aihotaz~a ,) being green and glistening; and wariyfN is a dial. var. of the inf. n. ra*iyfN in this sense: (Lth, T:) or quivered, or became tall, ( Ahtz~ ,) and was luxuriant, or flourishing, and fresh, or succulent: or, as AHn says, became glistening, or bright, in its sap: (M:) and raf~a Al$~ajaru , aor. and inf. n. as above, The trees appeared beautiful and bright in their greenness by reason of their succulence and luxuriance; as also warifa , aor. yarifu , inf. n. wariyfN . (T in art. wrf .) ― -b3- raf~ato Eayonuhu , aor. and , inf. n. raf~N , His eye quivered, or throbbed: (M, K:) and in like manner one says of any other member, or part of the person, (M,) or of other things; (IAar, T, K;) as, for instance, of the eyebrow. (IAar, T, M.) ― -b4- raf~a said of a bird: see R. Q. 1, in two places. ― -b5- raf~a , aor. , [said of a man,] He exulted; rejoiced overmuch, or above measure; or exulted greatly, or excessively; and was exceedingly brisk, lively, or sprightly: and behaved proudly, or haughtily; was proud, haughty, or self-conceited; or walked with a proud, or haughty, and selfconceited, gait. (M.) ― -b6- raf~a A_ilaY ka*aA He was, or became, brisk, lively, or sprightly, at, or to do, such a thing; syn. AirotaAHa : (K:) and so said of the heart. (TK.) ― -b3- raf~a All~abana , (TK,) inf. n. raf~N , (K,) He drank milk every day. (K, TK.) ― -b4- [Hence, perhaps,] A^axa*atohu AlHum~aY raf~FA The fever attacked him every day. And r~f~a AlmaroA^apa , (M, O,) or AljaAriyapa , (IAar, L in art. mSd ,) aor. , (M, O,) inf. n. raf~N , (O,) He sucked in the woman's, or the girl's, saliva from her mouth: (IAar, M, and L ubi suprà:) or he kissed her with the extremities of his lips. definition: A thing resembling a TaAq , [i.
sourceDefinition: A thing resembling a TaAq , [i. e. a kind of arched construction, app. like the Suf~ap described and figured in the Introduction to my work on the Modern Egyptians,] (El-Fárábee, S, Msb, K,) upon which are placed the TaraAy^if [or choice articles, such as vessels and other utensils &c.,] of the house; as also ↓ raforafN : (IAar, T, K:) the raf~ that is [commonly] used in houses is well known [as being a wooden shelf, generally extending along one or more of the sides of a room]: IDrd says that the word is Arabic: (Msb:) the pl. is rufuwfN (T, S, O, Mgh, Msb, K) and rifaAfN . (O, Mgh, Msb.) The latter pl. occurs in the saying of Kaab Ibn-El-Ashraf, A^amaA A_in~a rifaAfiY taqaS~afu tamorFA Verily my shelves are breaking with dates, by reason of the large quantity thereof. (Mgh.) rufuwfu Alxa$abi , also, means The planks of the laHod [or lateral hollow of a grave ]. (Mgh.) [And accord. to Golius, on the authority of a gloss. in the KL, raf~N also signifies A small arched window in a wall. ] -A2- [When the raf~ of a bayot is mentioned, by byt may sometimes be meant a tent:] see raforafN . -A3- Also A flock of sheep, (Fr, T, S, M, O, K,) or of sheep or goats. (Lh, M, K.) ― -b2- A herd of oxen or cows. (Lh, O, K.) ― -b3- A row of birds. (IAar, T and TA in art. Abl .) ― -b4- A company of men. (Fr, T.) ― -b5- Large camels; (O, K;) as also ↓ rif~N : (K:) [or] a large herd of camels. (M.) -A4- An enclosure ( HaZiyrap ) for sheep or goats. (M, O, K.) -A5- Any tract of sand elevated above what is adjacent to it or around it. (K.) -A6- Wheat, corn, or other provision, which one brings for himself or his family or for sale; syn. miyrapN . (M, K.) -A7- A soft garment or piece of cloth. (K.) -A8- And, as some say, (M,) Saliva (M, K) itself [as well as the “ sucking in of saliva: ” see 1]. (M.)

definition: , (Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. raqomN , (S, Msb, TA,) He wrote (S, Msb, K) a writing, book, or letter. (Msb.) And He sealed, stamped, imprinted, or impressed. (S, TA.) And raqama AliktaAba , (K,) inf. n. as above, (JK,) He marked the writing with the dots, or points, (JK, K, TA,) and made its letters distinct, or plain. (K, * TA.) One says, huwa yaroqumu AlmaA='a , (S,) or huwa yaroqumu fiY AlmaA='i , (JK, TA,) [ He writes, &c., upon the water, ] a prov., applied to the skilful and intelligent, (JK, * TA,) meaning he is so skilful that he writes, &c., ( yaroqumu ) where the writing, &c., ( Alr~aqomu ,) will not remain fixed. (JK, S, TA.) And one says of a skilful workwoman, clever in sewing skins and the like, hiYa taroqumu AlmaA='a and taroqumu fiY AlmaA='i . (TA.) ― -b2- And raqama Alv~awoba , (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) aor. as above, (JK, Msb,) and so the inf. n.; (Msb, TA;) and ↓ rq~mhu , (S, K,) inf. n. taroqiymN ; (S, TA;) He figured, variegated, or decorated, the garment, or piece of cloth; (Mgh, Msb, TA;) and (TA) made it striped, or marked it with stripes: (K, TA:) or, accord. to IF, he figured it, variegated it, or decorated it, with a certain, or known, figuring or variegation or decoration, such as became a mark [ thereof ]. (Msb.) Also the former phrase, (JK, Mgh, TA,) and ↓ the latter likewise, (TA,) said of a trader, or dealer, (JK, Mgh,) He marked, or put a mark on, the garment, or piece of cloth, (JK, Mgh, TA,) specifying its price; he put a price-mark upon it: (Mgh:) whence, laA yajuwzu bayoEu Al$~aYo'i biraqomihi [ The sale of the thing by the putting a price-mark upon it shall not be allowable, because the express consent of the seller as well as that of the purchaser is necessary to the ratification of the sale]: (Mgh:) [or] raqamotu Al$~aYo'a signifies I marked the thing so as to distinguish it from other things, as, for instance, by writing and the like: and hence, laA yubaAEu Alv~awobu biraqomihi walaA bilamosihi [ The garment, or piece of cloth, shall not be sold by the putting a price-mark upon it, for the reason explained above, nor by the feeling it, or touching it: see 3 in art. lms ]. (Msb.) ― -b3- [Hence,] huwa yaziydu fiY Alr~aqomi is a phrase used by the relaters of traditions as meaning (assumed tropical:) He adds to his tradition, and lies: from Alr~aqomu signifying the writing upon a garment, or piece of cloth. (TA.) ― -b4- You say also, raqama AlbaEiyra (assumed tropical:) He cauterized the camel. (TA.) [And raqama Alfarasa (assumed tropical:) He (a farrier) marked the horse, making lines upon him, with a hot iron: see maroquwmN , and see also jaAEirapN .]

definition: (assumed tropical:) Any one of several small marks of cauterization upon the shanks of a beast.
sourceDefinition: (assumed tropical:) Any one of several small marks of cauterization upon the shanks of a beast. (JK, T, TA.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) One of what are termed Alr~aqomataAni : (TA:) this signifies two [ horny ] things resembling two nails (JK, S, K, TA) in the legs of a beast (JK, K, TA) or in the legs of a sheep or goat, (S,) opposite each other: (JK, S, TA:) and of the ass and horse, two marks in the inner sides of the two arms: (S:) or the jaAEirataAni ; (K, TA;) which are two black spots [or marks made by cauterization ] upon the rump of the ass: (TA:) or what borders upon the jaAEirataAni of the ass, of the mark made by cauterization: or two portions of [ callous ] flesh next to the inner side of each of the arms of the horse, having no hair upon them. (K, TA.) Agreeably with all of these renderings has been explained the trad., maA A^anotumo mina AlA^umami A_il~aA kaAlr~aqomapi mino *iraAEi Ald~aAb~api (assumed tropical:) [ Ye are no more, of the nations in general, than such as is the rqmp of the arm of the beast ]. (TA.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) A small quantity of herbage; as in the saying, maA wajadotu A_il~aA raqomapF mino kalaA^K (assumed tropical:) [ I found not save a small quantity of herbage ]. (TA.) ― -b4- A herb, or leguminous plant, of those termed A^aHoraAr [pl. of Hur~N , q. v.]: (S:) a certain plant; said to be a herb, or leguminous plant, inclining to bitterness, and having a small red flower; (JK;) as some say, (JK, TA,) the xub~aAzaY [or mallow ]. (JK, K, TA.) ― -b5- A meadow ( rawoDapN , S, K) is sometimes thus termed. (S.) ― -b6- Also The side of a valley: (S, K:) or the place where its water collects; (K;) the part, of a valley, in which is the water. (Fr, JK, TA.)

definition: and ↓ AirotamayonaA [ We cast, or shot, (generally the latter,) one with another, or one at another;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ AirotamayonaA [ We cast, or shot, (generally the latter,) one with another, or one at another; mostly meaning in competition, or contention; i. e. we competed, or contended, together in throwing, or shooting ]: (S, K:) and trAmY Alqawomu biAls~ihaAmi and ↓ ArtmwA The people, or party, shot arrows, [ one with another, or] one at another. (T.) ― -b2- [Hence,] trAmt bihi AlbilaAdu (tropical:) The countries cast him forth, or expelled him; (M, K, TA;) [as though they bandied him, one to another;] as also ↓ Artmt , (so in a copy of the M, [which I think correct,]) or ↓ Armt . (K.) ― -b3- And trAmY Als~aHaAbu (assumed tropical:) The clouds became drawn, or joined, together, (M, K, TA,) [as though thrown, one at another,] and heaped, or piled, up; (TA;) as also ↓ ramaY . (M, TA.) ― -b4- And trAmY A^amoruhu A_ilaY AlZ~afari ; or A_ilaY Alxi*olaAni ; i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ His affair, or case, ] came eventually [ to the attainment of what was desired, or sought; or to abandonment by God]. (T, K, TA.) Hence, (TA,) it is said in a trad., of Zeyd Ibn-Háritheh, subiYa fiY AljaAhiliy~api fataraAmaY AlA^amoru A^ano SaAralixadiyjapa , (T, TA,) i. e. (assumed tropical:) [ He was made a captive in the Time of Ignorance, and the case ] came eventually, and led, [ to his becoming the property of Khadeejeh, ( A_ilaY being understood before A^ano SaAra ,)] as though the decrees [of God] cast him thereto. (IAth, TA.) One says also, trAmY AlA^amoru , meaning taraAxaY [i. e. (assumed tropical:) The affair was sluggish, or backward ]: (K:) [or] one says of a [purulent swelling such as is termed] Hiyon , (T,) or of a wound, (S,) trAmY A_ilaY fasaAdK , (T,) or AlY AlfasaAdi , (S,) i. e. (assumed tropical:) It was in a sluggish, or backward, state, ( taraAxaY ,) and became putrid and corrupt. (T.) And trAmY A_ilayohi Alxabaru (assumed tropical:) The news, or information, came to him; or came to him by degrees. (MA.) ― -b5- trAmt saforatuhu (assumed tropical:) His journey was, or became, distant, or far-extending. (Har p. 34.) ― -b6- trAmAhu Al$~abaAbu Youthfulness, or youthful vigour, attained its full term [ in him ]. (Skr, M.)

(M, K.)

sourceDefinition: : see the next preceding paragraph, in two places. [As a subst.,] it signifies A thing, (S, M,) meaning (S) an animal (As, T, S, M, * Mgh, Msb) of the chase, (As, T, S,) that is thrown at, or cast at, or shot at, or shot, (As, T, S, M, Mgh, Msb,) by its pursuer; and any beast thrown at, cast at, shot at, or shot; (As, T;) applied to the male and the female: (As, T, Mgh, Msb:) it is originally a word of the measure faEilaypN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlapN : (Msb:) [or rather] it is made fem., (As, T,) [i. e.] it has p , (S,) because it is made a subst., (As, T, S,) not an epithet: (As, T:) it is not maromiy~apN converted into ramiy~apN : (S:) or, accord. to Sb, the p , in general, is affixed to show that the act has not yet been executed upon the object thereof; [so that the meaning is, an animal to be thrown at, cast at, shot at, or shot; ] and thus *abiyHapN is applied to “ a sheep, or goat, [to be slaughtered or sacrificed,] not yet slaughtered [or sacrificed]; ” but when the act has been executed upon it, it is [said to be] *abiyHN : (M:) the pl. is ramiy~aAtN and ramaAyaA . (Msb.) One says, biy^osa Alr~amiy~apu AlA^aronabu , meaning Very bad is the thing of those that are [or are to be ] thrown at, or cast at, or shot at, or shot, the hare. (S, M.) ― -b2- Also, (assumed tropical:) An impost which the governor imposes [so I render maA yaromiyhi AlEaAmilu ] upon his subjects. (TA.)

definition: An arrow with which one shoots (As, IAar, T) at a butt: (As, T, Mgh:) an arrow with which one learns to shoot;
sourceDefinition: An arrow with which one shoots (As, IAar, T) at a butt: (As, T, Mgh:) an arrow with which one learns to shoot; (M, K, TA;) which is the worst kind of arrows: (TA:) or a small, weak arrow: (AHn, M, K:) or an arrow with its [ head of ] iron: (Th, TA in art. Hsb :) or, like sirowapN , a round arrow-head: (AA, [so in the S, but in the TA it is IAar,] S, TA:) [and app. a missile of any kind: (see mirodFY :)] pl. maraAmK . (M.) When they see many maraAmK in the quiver of a man, they say, wanabolu AlEabodi A^akovaruhaA AlmaraAmiY [ And the arrows of the slave, most of them are those that are small and weak ]: a prov., said to mean that the free man purchases arrows at a high price, buying the broad and long iron head, because he is a man of war and of the chase; but the slave is only a pastor, and therefore is content with what are termed maraAmK , because they are cheaper if he buy them; and if he ask for them as a gift, no one gives him aught but a miromaAp . (M.) [See also the last sentence of this paragraph.] ― -b2- It is also used, tropically, as meaning (tropical:) A manojaniyq [or kind of engine for casting stones at the enemy; app. such as was called by the Romans “ onager, ” or the like thereof ]: because, like the miromaAop before mentioned, it is an instrument for casting, or shooting. (Mgh.) [See also miromFY .] And [the pl.] maraAmK also signifies (assumed tropical:) Thunderbolts; syn. SawaAEiqu . (Bd in xviii. 38.) ― -b3- Also A cloven hoof (S, Mgh, K) of a sheep or goat; because it is of the things that are thrown away: (Mgh:) [or,] accord. to A 'Obeyd, (T, S,) a thing that is between the two hoofs of a sheep or goat; (T, S, M, K;) as also ↓ maromaApN : (A 'Obeyd, T, M, K:) thus, he says, it is explained; but I know not what is its meaning: (T, S:) its dual occurs in the following trad.: lawo A^an~a A^aHadahumo duEiYa A_ilaY miromaAtayoni laA^ajaAba wahuwa laA yujiybu A_ilaY AlS~alaApi ; (T, S; related also, with some variations, in the M and Mgh;) in which it is said to be the dual of miromaApN in the former of these two senses; [i. e. If any one of you were invited to partake of two hoofs of a sheep or goat, he would obey the invitation, but he will not obey the invitation to prayer; ] (S, Mgh;) or, accord. to A 'Obeyd, it is here the dual of this word in the latter of the same two senses: (T, S:) accord. to IAar, (T, TA,) or Aboo-Sa'eed, it here means the kind of arrow called miromaApN : (T, Mgh, TA:) but in another, and similar, trad., mrmAtyn is followed by A^awoEaroqK [i. e. “ or a bone with some meat remaining upon it ”]. (T, Z, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. yariyvu , (S, Msb,) inf. n. rayovN , (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) He, or it, was, or became, slow, tardy, dilatory, late, or backward; (T, S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ try~v . (T, K.) You say, raAva EalaY~a xabaruka , (S, A,) or rAv EalayonaA xabaruhu , (T,) Thy news or the news of thee, or his news or the news of him, was slow, &c., in coming to me, or to us. (T, S, A.) And EalayonaA fulaAnN ↓ try~v Such a one was slow, &c., in coming to us. (T.) And rub~a EajalapK wa habato rayovFA , or, accord. to one relation of the saying, tahabu rayovFA , the meaning in both cases being the same, from Alhibapu ; [i. e. Many an act of haste causes (lit. gives ) slowness, &c.;] (S;) or tuEoqibu rayovFA [ occasions, as its result, slowness, &c.]: (A:) a proverb. (S, A.) And it appears from the following saying of Maakil Ibn-Khuweylid, laEamoruka laloyaA^osu gayoru Almuriyvi xayorN mina AlT~amaEi AlkaA*ibi [ By thy life, or by thy religion, assuredly despair that is not slow in its issue is better than hope that gives a false promise, if this be his meaning,] that ↓ ArAv may be a dial. var. of raAva : but the poet may mean [ that does not make a man slow, i. e.] gayoru Almuriyvi Almaro'a . (M.)

definition: A space, or measure, [ of time, ] syn.
sourceDefinition: A space, or measure, [ of time, ] syn. qadorN , (T, Msb,) or miqodaArN ; (A, K;) or a time, a while, syn. saAEapN . (Mgh.) You say, A^amohalotuhu rayovamaA faEala ka*aA , i. e. qadora maA faEalahu (Msb) or saAEapa fiEolihi (Mgh) [ I granted him a delay during the space of his doing such a thing ]. And lamo yalobavo A_il~aA rayovamaA qulotu , i. e. qadora *`lika [ He tarried not save during the space that, or as long as, or while, I said such a thing]. (TA, from a trad.) And so in the saying, maA qaEada EinodanaA fulaAnN A_il~aA rayova A^ano Had~avanaA biHadiyvK tum~a mar~a [ Such a one sat not with us, or at our abode, save during the space that, or as long as, or while, he related to us a story, or tradition; then he went away ]. (T, TA.) And it is used without mA and without An : (TA:) Aashà Báhileh says, laA yuSoEibu AlA^amora A_il~aA rayova yarokabuhu wa kul~a A^amorK siwaY AlfaHo$aA='i yaA^otamiru [ He finds not the affair difficult save while he is embarking in it; and every command but that which exceeds the bounds of rectitude he obeys ]: (M, TA:) this mode of expression is common in the dial. of El-Hijáz; accord. to which one says, yuriydu yafoEalu , i. e. A^ano yafoEala . (TA.) [See also an ex. in a verse cited voce raAjilapN , and another in a verse cited voce riyHN .]

(S, Mgh, Msb, K) and , (Ks, K,) inf. n. as above, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) He chid him; or checked, restrained, or forbade, him with rough speech: (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K:) he prevented, hindered, or withheld, him: (S, Mgh, K:) he forbade, or prohibited, him: (K:) he repelled him with strength. (MF in art. hzbr .) You say, zabarahu Eani AlA^amori He restrained him with rough speech, or forbade and prevented him, from doing the thing. (TA.) And zabara Als~aAy^ila He chid and repelled the beggar with rough speech. (As, TA.) ― -b3- zaborN is also syn. with kalaAmN [as meaning The act of speaking, or speech as a subst.]: (K:) [SM says,] thus it is found in all the copies: but [he adds] I have not found any authoritative ex. of it, so it requires consideration. (TA.) (TA. (Lth, TA.)

sourceDefinition: [A thing] written; as also ↓ zabiyrN : (K:) [or] a writing, or book; (S;) as also ↓ zabuwrN , of the measure faEuwlN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , (S, Msb, K,) like rasuwlN : (Msb, TA:) zabuwrN signifying any writing or book: or any divine book with which it is difficult to become acquainted: or a book that is confined to intel-lectual science, exclusive of legal statutes or ordinances: (TA:) ↓ Alz~abuwru signifies particularly the Book [ of the Psalms ] of David: (S, Mgh, Msb, K:) and also, and lugapu Alz~abuwri , the Syriac [or Hebrew ] language: (Mgh:) the pl. of ziborN is zubuwrN ; (S, K;) and the pl. of ↓ zabuwrN is zuburN . (S, Msb, K.) It is said in the Kur [xxi. 105], walaqado katabonaA fiY mino baEodi A@l*~ikori ↓ A@lz~abuwri , meaning And we have written in the book sent down to David, after the taworaAp [or Book of the Law revealed to Moses ]: (Aboo-Hureyreh, TA:) Sa'eed Ibn-Jubeyr read Alz~ubuwr , [pl. of Alz~iboru ,] and said that it means the Book of the Law revealed to Moses ( AltwrAp ) and the Gospel and the Kur-án [ together ]; and that Al*kr means what is in heaven: (TA:) and some also read zubuwrFA in the Kur iv. 161 and xvii. 57. (S, TA.)

definition: A piece of iron: (S, Msb, K:) or a big piece of iron: (TA:) pl.
sourceDefinition: A piece of iron: (S, Msb, K:) or a big piece of iron: (TA:) pl. zubarN (S, Msb, K) and zuburN . (S, K.) The former pl. occurs in the Kur xviii. 95. (S.) It is also said in the Kur [xxiii. 55], fataqaT~aEuwA A^amorahumo bayonahumo zuburFA , (S, TA,) and zubarFA ; (TA;) meaning qiTaEFA , (S, TA,) in both cases; (Fr;) [i.e., But they have become divided, in their state, among themselves, into parties: ] or he who reads zuburFA makes it pl. of ↓ zabuwrN , not of zuborapN ; for the measure fuEolapN does not assume the measure fuEulN in the pl.; and the meaning is, they have made their religion [to be founded upon] various books: and zubarN is pl. of zuborapN : or it may be also pl. of ↓ zabuwrN , and originally zuburN , being changed therefrom, like as some of the Arabs are related to have said judadN for the pl. of jadiydN , which is originally and regularly jududN ; after the same manner as when one says rukabaAtN for rukubaAtN , and gurafaAtN for gurufaAtN : and this opinion is strengthened by AA's allowing the reading zuburFA and zuborFA and zubarFA ; zuborFA being a contraction of zuburFA , like as EunoqN is of EunuqN . (IB, TA.) ― -b2- The anvil (K) of a blacksmith. (TA.) -A2- The upper part of the back, next the neck; or the part between the two shoulder-blades; or the part where the neck is joined to the back-bone; syn. kaAhilN : (K:) or the place of the kAhl : (S:) or a certain thing rising from the kAhl : (TA:) pl. in this sense, A^azobaArN ; or this is a pl. pl., as though it were pl. of zubarN , and this were pl. of zuborapN in this sense. (TA.) One says, $ad~a liloA^amori zuboratahu He strengthened his kaAhil and his back for the affair. (TA.) ― -b2- Also, hence, (S,) The accumulation, or mass, of hair which is between the shoulder-blades of the lion; (S in art. lbd ;) [the mane of a lion;] the collection of hair (Lth, A, K) between the shoulderblades of the lion &c., (K,) or upon the place of the kaAhil [expl. above], and upon the elbows, of the lion; (Lth, A;) and any hair in a similar collected state. (Lth, TA.) ― -b3- And [hence,] Alz~uborapu (tropical:) A certain asterism; (K;) two bright stars [d and q], (S, K,) in the kaAhil [or part of the back next the neck ], (K,) or which are the kaAhilaAni , (S,) of Leo; (S, K;) one [namely the Eleventh ] of the Mansions of the Moon: (S, K:) [also called AlxaraAtaAni : see this word: and see manaAzilu Alqamari , in art. nzl :] it is of the dial. of El-Yemen. (TA.) [This description is incorrect if applied to the constellation as at present figured; but doubtless correct when applied to it as figured by the Arabs. Kzw, in his description of Leo, says that they are two stars, on the belly, and on the projecting part of the haunch-bone, of Leo. ] ― -b4- Also The breast, or what projects of its upper part, (syn. SudorapN ,) of any beast. (TA.)

(Har p. 329.) And maA A^atakal~ama bikalimapK Hat~aY A^axoTimahaA waA^azum~ahaA (assumed tropical:) [ I say not a saying until I qualify it to be used with cogency or efficiency ]. (TA.) ― -b4- Hence also, (Mgh,) zam~a Aln~aEola , (S, Mgh, TA,) [aor. and] inf. n. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) He attached a zimaAm [q. v.] to the sandal; (S, Mgh, TA;) as also AlnEl ↓ Azm~ . (TA.) ― -b6- And zam~a biraA^osihi (tropical:) He raised his head; (K, TA;) inf. n. as above: (TA:) [and so zam~a raA^osahu : for] you say, A^axa*a Al*~iy^obu saxolapF raA^osahu ↓ fa*ahaba bihaA zaAm~FA , i. e. sourceDefinition: [as inf. n. of zamozama , and also as a simple subst.,] A distant sounding or sound, such as is confused and continued. (K.) You say, of a thing, zamozama , meaning It made a distant sound, confused and continued: and samiEotu zamozamapF I heard a distant sound, confused and continued. (TK.) ― -b2- The sounding, or sound, of thunder: (AZ, S:) or the consecutive reiteration of the sound of thunder; which is the best kind of sounding thereof, and the surest symptom of rain. (M, K.) One says, Alr~aEodu yuzamozimu The thunder sounds with consecutive reiteration. (TK.) Accord. to AHn, the zamozamap of thunder is [The sounding thereof ] when it is not loud and clear. (TA.) ― -b3- The speaking, or speech, of the Magians, on the occasion of their eating, (S, IAth,) with a low voice: (IAth:) or the gibbering, or uttering gibberish or jargon, one to another, of the Persians, or other foreigners, ( taraATunu AlEuluwji ,) over their eating, while they are [ in a manner ] speechless, not making use of tongue nor of lip [ so as to articulate ]; it being a sound which they roll in their noses and their fauces, but such that they understand one another: (K:) or zamozama , said of a Magian, means He affected, or constrained himself, to speak, on the occasion of eating, while closing his mouth: whence the saying, waA@nohawohumo Eani Alz~amozamapi [ And forbid ye them from the affecting, &c. ]. (Mgh.) ― -b4- The crying [or roaring ], or the cry [or roar ], of the lion. (K.) You say of him, zamozama [ He cried, or roared ]. definition: A thing with which one ties or binds, fastens, or makes fast: (K:) meaning [the noserein of a camel;
sourceDefinition: A thing with which one ties or binds, fastens, or makes fast: (K:) meaning [the noserein of a camel; i. e.] the cord that is tied to the burap [or xizaAm , each meaning nose-ring of a camel], or to the xi$aA$ [or wooden thing fixed in the bone of the nose ], and to which, (S, Mgh, Msb, TA,) i. e. to the end of which, (S, TA,) is tied the miqowad [or leading-rope ]: (S, Mgh, Msb, TA:) and (afterwards, Msb) also applied to the miqawod (S, Msb, TA) itself: (Msb:) pl. A^azim~apN . (Msb, K.) [See also xiTaAmN .] It is said in a trad., laA zimaAma walaA xizaAma fiY AlA_isolaAmi [ There shall be no nose-rein nor nosering by which to lead a man in El-Islám ]: meaning a practice of the devotees of the Children of Israel, who used to attach rings and reins to the noses, like as is done to the she-camel in order that she may be led thereby. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] zimaAmu AlA^amori (assumed tropical:) That by means of which the thing, or affair, subsists, and is conducted, or managed, and ordered. (TA.) And A^aloqaY fiY yadihi zimaAma A^amorihi (assumed tropical:) [ He put in his hand, or power, the means of conducting his affair, or the conduct of his affair ]: and yuS~arifu A^azim~apa AlA^umuwri (assumed tropical:) [ He disposes as he pleases the various means of conducting the affairs ]. (TA.) And huwa EalaY zimaAmK mino A^amorihi (assumed tropical:) He is on the point of accomplishing his affair. (TA.) And Aln~aAqapu zimaAmu AlA_ibili (assumed tropical:) [ The she-camel is the leader of the other camels ]: said when she goes before them. (TA.) And huwa zimaAmu qawomihi (assumed tropical:) [ He is the leader of his people, or party ]: and humo A^azim~apN qawomihimo (assumed tropical:) [ They are the leaders of their people, or party ]. (TA.) [See also De Sacy's Chrest. Arabe, sec. ed., i. 261 and 503; and see Quatremère's Hist. des Sultans Mamlouks, vol. i., sec. part, pp. 65 and 66.] ― -b3- zimaAmu Aln~aEoli (assumed tropical:) [ The zmAm of the sandal ] is the thing to which the $isoE is attached, or tied: (S:) or the thong that is between the middle toe and that next to it, to which the $isoE is attached, or tied: [but for the latter of these explanations, it seems that we should read the thong that is between the middle toe and that next to it: or the thong to which the $isoE is attached, or tied: the $isoE being the thong that passes through the sole, and between two of the toes, and to which the $iraAk is attached: for it appears that the term zimaAm is applied by some to the thong called by others the $iraAk , extending between the leg and the toes: and by some, to what is called by others the $isoE , or qibaAl : to the latter as being likened to the cord that is tied to the camel's nose-ring; and to the former as being likened to the leading-rope which is tied to that cord: it being] a metaphorical term, from the zimaAm of the camel: (Mgh:) it is [said to be] the thong lies upon the back [meaning upper side ] of the foot, [ extending ] from, or [ consisting ] of, the fore part of the $iraAk , lengthwise: [for the term $iraAk (q. v.) is sometimes used in a larger sense than that above assigned to it:] or it is like the qibaAl , [which is expl. in the same manner as the $isoE , i. e., as] being between the middle toe and that next to it: (Har p. 539:) [and thus it is expl. by J and Mtr and F in another art.;] the qibaAl of the sandal is its zimaAm , (S, and Mgh and K in art. qbl ,) i. e. its thong which is (Mgh in that art.) between the middle toe and next to it. (S and Mgh and K in that art.)

definition: Copious, or abundant, water;
sourceDefinition: Copious, or abundant, water; as also ↓ zumaAzimN : (K:) [or] the latter, (Kz, TA,) [and app. the former also,] and ↓ zumazimN , (IKh, TA,) and ↓ zamozaAmN , (Kz, TA,) brackish water; i. e. such as is between salt and sweet. (IKh, Kz, TA.) ― -b2- Also, (accord. to some copies of the S and K,) or zamozamu , (accord. to other copies of the same, and accord. to the Msb,) imperfectly decl., because of the fem. gender and a proper name, (Msb,) the name of The well of Mekkeh, (so in a copy of the S and in the Msb,) or a certain [ celebrated ] well in Mekkeh, (so in another copy of the S,) [i. e.] a certain well adjacent to the Kaabeh; (K;) so called [because its water is somewhat brackish, or] because of the copiousness of its water; (JM;) as also ↓ zumazim [i. e. zumazimN or zumazimu ], (IAar, TA,) and ↓ zumaAzimN [or zumaAzimu ], and ↓ zam~amN or zam~amu , (accord. to different copies of the K,) the last ( zam~am ) on the authority of IAar. (TA.) The names of this well, collected from trads. and lexicons, have been found to amount to more than sixty. (TA.) ― -b3- zamozam [with or without tenween] is also the name of A celebrated well at El-Medeeneh, which is regarded as a means of obtaining a blessing, and the water of which is drunk and transported [like that of the more celebrated well of the same name at Mekkeh]. (TA.) -A2- zamozamN or zamozamu (accord. to different copies of the S, [used by a poet with tenween, but probably by poetic license, for it is app. a fem. proper name, and therefore imperfectly decl.,]) is also A name of, or for, a she-camel, like EayoTal . (S.)

(M.) [See also saAy^irN , below.] ― -b2- AlS~aqori ↓ suw^orapu means (tropical:) What remains of the portion of the flesh of the game that is given to the hawk which has captured it. (A.) [See also suw^odapN .] ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) What is good, or excellent, of property, or of camels or the like: pl. suw^arN . (L.) definition: The rest, or remainder, (T, and M in art.
sourceDefinition: The rest, or remainder, (T, and M in art. syr , and Msb and K,) of a thing, (Z, M, Msb,) whether little or much; (T, Msb;) and of men, or people: (Sgh; Msb:) not the whole, or all, as many imagine it to mean, (Sgh, Msb, K,) though people use it in this latter sense, (IAth,) which Sgh asserts to be a vulgar error: (Msb:) it occurs repeatedly in trads., and always in the former sense: (IAth:) or it is sometimes used [in chaste Arabic] in the latter sense: (K:) and is correctly so used accord. to AAF and J and IJ and ElJawáleekee and IB, the last of whom confirms this signification by many examples and evident proofs: but whether, in this sense, it is derived from Als~ayor , as AAF and J and others hold, or from suwrN the “ wall which surrounds a town or city, ” as others hold, is disputed: (TA:) and saAru Al$~aYo'i is a dial. var. of saAy^iruhu . (S in art. syr .) ― -b2- An Arab of the desert became the guest of a party, and they ordered the female slave to perfume him; whereupon he said, baToniY EaT~iriY wasaAy^iriY *ariY [ My belly perfume thou, and the rest of me leave thou ]: (K:) but in other lexicons than the K, we find A^aEoTiriY . (TA in art. ETr .) This saying is a well-known prov. (TA.) [In the TA it is added that sAy^ry here signifies the whole of me, or all of me: but this is an evident mistake.] You say this to a man who gives you what you do not want, and refuses you what you want. (Sgh, TA in art. ETr .) ― -b3- It is related, also, that a hostile attack was made upon a people, and they cried out for aid to the sons of their uncle; but these held back from them until they had been made captives and taken away; then they came inquiring respecting them; and the person asked replied, A^asaAy^ira Alyawomi waqado zaAla AlZ~uhoru [ What, all the day, when the noon has passed? ] (K:) i. e., Dost thou covet what is remote, ( maA baEuda , (S, K, TA, in a copy of the S and in one of the K and in the CK maA baEodu ,) when [reason for] despair hath become manifest to thee: for when one wants the whole day, and the noon has passed, he must despair like as he despairs of accomplishing his want at sunset. (S in art. syr , and K.) This saying is a prov.; (S, A;) and is used with reference to a thing which one hopes to attain when its time has passed. (A.)

sourceDefinition: Black; (S, Msb, K;) like A^asoxamu ; (TA in art. sxm ;) applied to the crow; see suHomapN : (Lth, TA:) fem. saHomaA='u ; (Msb, TA;) applied to a plant of that colour; (ISk, TA;) and particularly to the naSiY~ when it is of that colour, and thus applied as an intensive epithet; and to a woman in the same sense: (TA:) and ↓ A_isoHimaAnN signifies anything black (ISd, K) accord. to some; but this is a mistake, for it is only A^asoHamu . (ISd, TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] AlA^asoHamu is the name of A certain idol, (K, TA,) which was black. (TA.) ― -b3- And The night. (TA.) ― -b4- [Hence likewise,] A^asoHamu signifies also Clouds ( saHaAbN ): (S, K:) or, as some say, black clouds: and saHomaA='u signifies a black cloud. (TA.) ― -b5- Also Blood into which are dipped the hands of persons swearing, one to another; (K;) or blood into which the hand is dipped on the occasion of swearing with another or others: said to have this meaning in the saying of El-Aashà, raDiyEaYo libaAni vadoYi A^um~K taHaAlafaA biA^asoHama daAjK EawoDu laA tatafar~aqu [ Two foster-brothers by the sucking of the breast of one mother swore together, by dark blood into which they dipped their hands, that you, or they, i. e. a tribe ( qabiylap ) or a company of men ( jamaAEap ), for, without the context, the meaning is doubtful, should not ever become separated ]: or it has here one, or another, of three meanings here following. (S.) ― -b6- The womb. (S.) ― -b7- The nipple of a woman's breast: (K:) or the blackness of the nipple of a woman's breast. (S.) ― -b8- A skin such as is termed ziq~ for wine: (S, K:) because of its blackness: and ↓ suHayomN also signifies a ziq~ (TA.) ― -b9- Also A horn: (S, K:) thus in the saying of Zuheyr, wata*abiybuhaA Eanohu biA^asoHama mi*owadi [ And the frequent repelling of her, or them, from him with a horn; so that m*wd is merely an explicative adjunct, for it also means a horn, or it may be rendered here an instrument for repel-ling ]: (S, * TA:) or [ AsHm is here an epithet, and] the meaning is, with a black horn. (TA.) Another poet uses the phrase ta*ub~u bisaHomaAwayoni . [so in the TA, app. a mistranscription for ta*ub~u ,] i. e., [reading ta*ub~u , She repels ] with a pair of horns; using the fem, as meaning biSiySyatayoni ; as though he said biSiySiytayoni saHomaAwayoni [ with two black horns ]. (IAar, TA.) ― -b10- The fem., Als~aHomaA='u also signifies The dubur [here meaning anus ]: (K:) because of its colour. (TA.) ― -b11- For another signification of the fem., see saHamN .

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) and , (M, K,) inf. n. sadolN , (S, M, Mgh, Msb,) He let it loose, let it down, lowered it, or let it fall; (S, M, K;) namely, his garment, (S, M,) and hair, (Fr, M, K,) and a veil, or curtain; (M;) and sadanahu signifies the same; (Fr, TA;) as also ↓ Asdlhu ; (M, K;) or this latter is a mistake; (Mgh; [but this the author asserts because, he says, he had searched through books without finding it except in the “ Nahj-el-Balághah; ”]) not allowable; (Msb;) and the former signifies he let it down, or let it fall, namely, the garment, without drawing together its two sides: (Mgh, Msb:) or, as some say, he threw it upon his head, and let it loose, let it down, or let it fall, upon his shoulders: (Mgh:) and he let it down, or let it fall, namely, hair, not maEoquwf [i. e. made recurvate at the extremities ], nor tied in knots: (Lth, TA:) and one says also, yazodulu vawobahu , changing the s into z . (Sb, M.) The sadol that is forbidden in prayer is The letting down one's garment without drawing together its two sides: or the enveloping oneself with his garment, and putting his arms within, and bowing the head and body, and prostrating oneself, in that state; as the Jews used to do; and this applies uniformly to the shirt and other garments: or the putting the middle of the A_izaAr [or waist-wrapper ] upon the head, and letting fall its two ends upon one's right and left, without making it to be upon his two shoulder-blades. (TA.) sadala EimaAmatahu bayona katifayohi is said in a trad. [as meaning He made the end of his turban to hang down between his two shoulder-blades ]. (Mgh.) And one says also, $aEarahu EalaY ↓ sd~l EaAtiqayohi waEunuqihi , [meaning He let his hair fall down abundant and long upon his shoulders and his neck, ] inf. n. tasodiylN . (ISh, TA. [See its pass. part. n., voce munosadilN .]) ― -b2- Also, aor. , (M, K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He slit it, or rent it; namely, his garment. (M, K.) ― -b3- And sadala fiY AlbilaAdi , (O, K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He went away into the countries, or provinces. (O, K.)

definition: , of the measure fiEil~aY , an arabicized word, originally, in Pers.
sourceDefinition: , of the measure fiEil~aY , an arabicized word, originally, in Pers., siho dilaho [“ three-hearted ”], as though it were three chambers in one chamber ( kaA^an~ahu valAavapu buyuwtK fiY bayotK ), like the HaAriY~ bikum~ayoni [i. e., I suppose, “ like the garment of El-Heereh with two sleeves; ” app. meaning that it signifies An oblong chamber with a wide and deep recess on either hand at, or near, one extremity thereof; so that its ground-plan resembles an expanded garment with a pair of very wide sleeves: in the present day, it is commonly applied to a single recess of the kind above mentioned, the floor of which is elevated about half a foot or somewhat more or less above the floor of the main chamber, and which has a mattress and cushions laid against one or two or each of its three sides]. (S.) [Golius explains it, as on the authority of the S, (in which is nothing relating to it but what I have given above,) thus: Pers. siydalaho seu sidaraho , i. q. sud~arN .]

definition: A certain kind of plant, (As, AHn, S, O, K,) of the plants that grow in plain, or soft, ground: (AHn, O:) n.

(AHn, O.)
