(O, K.) ― -b2- The pole, (S, A, Mgh, O, Msb,) or a pole, (K,) of a [ tent such as is called ] xibaA=' , (S, A, O, Msb, K,) or of a [ tent such as is called ] fusoTaAT . (Mgh.) ― -b3- The transverse piece of wood upon the two props of the grape-vine, with the hoops [ that are affixed upon it ]. (K.) ISh says that when a grape-vine had a raised support made for its branches to lie thereon, recourse was had to props, for [the feet of] which holes were dug in the ground, each prop having two forking portions [at the head]; then a piece of wood ( xa$abapN , so in the O, in the TA [erroneously] $Ebp ,) is taken, and laid across two props, and this transverse piece of wood is called the misoTaH , [pl. masaATiHu ,] and upon the masaATiH are placed hoops, from the nearest part thereof to the furthest; (O, TA;) and the msATH with the hoops are called msATH . (O.) ― -b4- A smooth piece of rock or hard stone, surrounded with stones, in which water collects: (S, O, K:) or a wide slab of rock or hard stone, bordered round, for the rain-water [ to collect therein ]: and sometimes God creates, at the mouth of the well, a smooth, even, piece of rock or hard stone, [thus called,] which is surrounded with stones, and from which the camels are watered, like the HawoD . (T, TA.) [See also Hawiy~apN .] ― -b5- Also i. q. masoTaHN , q. v. (S, O.) ― -b6- And A mat (S, O, K) woven (O) of xuwS (A, K) or TufoY (O) [i. e. leaves ] of the dawom [or Theban palm ]; (O, K;) as also ↓ misoTaAHN . (A.) ― -b7- A large roasting-pan ( miqolFY ) for wheat, (K, TA,) which is roasted therein. (K, * TA.) ― -b3- Also, aor. as above, (L, K,) and so the inf. n., (L,) (assumed tropical:) He slapped (L, K) it, a man's face, (L,) or him, a man, (K,) with his hand. (L.) And (assumed tropical:) He struck him, or beat him, (K,) with a staff, or stick. (TA.) And (assumed tropical:) He (a bird) slapped it, (S, [in which only the inf. n. is mentioned,] and K,) namely, the object struck by him, (K,) with his wing, (S,) or with his wings. (ElMufradát, TA.) You say, safaEa binaASiyapi Alfarasi liyarokabahu [ He laid hold upon, or seized, the forelock of the horse, to mount him ]. (TA.) And safaEa biyadihi He laid hold upon his hand: (IAar:) or he laid hold upon his hand and raised him: often used in this sense by 'Obeyd-Allah Ibn-Al-Hasan, Kádee of El-Bas- rah. (Sgh.) We will assuredly take by the nASyp (Az, S, TA) to the fire [ of hell ]: (Az, TA:) or we will assuredly lay hold upon his nASyp and drag him thereby with violence to the fire: (Bd:) or we will assuredly drag him thereby to the fire: (O, K:) or we will assuredly blacken his face; the nASyp being put for the face because it is the fore part thereof: (Fr, Az, K:) or we will assuredly mark him with the mark of the people of the fire, (O, K,) making his face black, and his eyes blue: (O:) or we will assuredly abase him: or, render him despicable: (O, K:) or we will assuredly abase him and make him to stand: so in the L and other lexicons; for these, instead of A^wlanuqomiy^an~ahu in the O and K, have walanuqiyman~ahu , and this is shown to be the right reading by the last explanation in the sentence next preceding. (Mgh.) In the face, it is A blackness in the cheeks of a wan, or haggard, woman: (S:) and ↓ safaEN [which is properly the inf. n. of safiEa , q. v.,] a blackness tinged with redness in the cheeks of a wan, or haggard, woman, (O, K,) and of a sheep, or goat. definition: Of a black colour tinged, or intermixed, with redness: (S, Msb:) or black: (Mgh:) applied to a man: (S:) fem safoEaA='u : (Mgh, Msb:) and sufoEN [is the pl.
sourceDefinition: Of a black colour tinged, or intermixed, with redness: (S, Msb:) or black: (Mgh:) applied to a man: (S:) fem safoEaA='u : (Mgh, Msb:) and sufoEN [is the pl., and] signifies blacks inclining to redness. (K.) Applied to an ostrich, i. q. A^arobadu [which is variously explained, as signifying Of a colour inclining to blackness, or of the colour of dust, &c.]. (TA.) And the fem., applied to a ewe, Having black cheeks, the rest of her being white. (TA.) The masc. also signifies A wild bull: (K:) or, applied to a wild bull, it signifies having in his cheeks a blackness inclining a little to redness. (TA.) And The hawk; (K;) because it has spots of black: (Er-Rághib:) all hawks are sufoEN : (S:) and the fem., A pigeon ( HamaAmapN ); because of the sufoEap upon its neck: (S:) or, applied to a pigeon, it signifies of which the sufoEap is upon its neck, (K, TA,) exclusively of the head, (TA,) in the part on each side of the neck above the ring. (K, * TA.) It is also a name for Sheep, or goats; used when they are called to be milked: (K:) so in the O: but in some copies, and in the TS, for the she-goat: (TA:) thus in the phrase, A^a$oli A_ilayoka AlA^asofaEa [ Call thou to thee the sheep, or goats, or the she-goat, to be milked ]: (O, TS, K:) mentioned by Ibn-'Abbád. (TA.) ― -b2- Applied to a garment, or piece of cloth, Black. (K.) ― -b3- ↓ The pl. is also applied to The A^avaAfiY~ , (Lth, S, K,) or three stones upon which the cooking-pot is set up; (TA;) because of their blackness: (Lth, Er-Rághib:) [see HaADinN :] and a single one thereof is called safoEaA='u : (K:) or an iron A^uvofiy~ap [meaning trivet ], (K, TA,) upon which the cooking-pot is set up; and this is said to be the primary application. (TA.) ― -b4- sufoEN also signifies The seeds, or grain, of the colocynth; (Ibn-'Abbád, K;) because of their blackness: (TA:) n. un. with p . (K.)

definition: , (S, M, Mgh,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Mgh,) aor. , (S, M,) inf. n. sal~N ; (S, M, Mgh, K;) and ↓ Astl~hu , (M,) inf. n. AisotilaAlN ; (K; [in the CK, AliAsolAl is put in the place of AliAsotilaAl ;]) He drew the thing out or forth from another thing: (Jel in xxiii. 12:) or he pulled out the thing, or drew it forth, gently: (M, K: *) or he drew, or pulled, the thing out, or forth, as a sword from its scabbard, and a hair from dough. (Mgh.) You say, sal~a Als~ayofa , (S, Msb,) aor. and inf. n. as above; (Msb;) and ↓ Astl~hu , both signifying the same; (S;) [i. e. He drew the sword; ] as also ↓ Asl~hu , inf. n. A_isolaAlN . (TA.) In the saying of El-Farezdak, gadaApa tawal~ayotumo kaAn~a suyuwfakumo ↓ *aA=niynu fiY A^aEonaAqikumo lamo tusalosali [ In the morning when ye turned back, as though your swords were *A=nyn (pl. of *uw^onuwnN a species of fungus) upon your necks, (for the sword was hung upon the shoulder, not by a waist-belt,) not drawn forth ], he has separated the doubled letter: thus the verse is related by IAar: but by Th, ↓ lamo tasal~ali [for tatanasal~ali ]. (M.) It is said in a trad., laA^asul~an~aka minohumo kamaA tusal~u Al$~aEorapu mina AlEajiyni [ I will assuredly draw thee forth from them like as the single hair is drawn forth from dough ]. (TA.) And in another trad., Aall~`hum~a A^osolulo saxiymapa qalobiY (tropical:) [ O God, draw forth the rancour of my heart ]: and hence the saying AlhadaAyaA tasul~u Als~axaAy^ima wataHul~u Al$~akaAy^ima (tropical:) [ Presents draw away feelings of rancour, and loose, or melt, resistances, or incompliances ]. (TA.) And sul~a , said of a colt, means He was drawn forth a saliyl [q. v.]. (M, TA.) ― -b2- Also He took the thing. (Msb.) Hence one says, tusal~u Almay~itu mino qibali raA^osihi A_ilaY Alqabori , i. e. [ The dead body ] is taken [ head-foremost to the grave ]: (Msb:) [or is drawn forth &c.: for] it is said of the Apostle of God, sul~a mino qibal raA^osihi , meaning He was drawn forth [&c.] from the bier. (Mgh.) ― -b3- Also, aor. and inf. n. as above, He stole the thing: (Msb, TA:) or he stole it covertly, secretly, or clandestinely; (TA;) and so ↓ Asl~hu . (TK. [But see 4, below, where Asl~ meaning “ he stole ” is mentioned only as intrans.]) You say, sal~a AlbaEiyra jawofi All~ayoli He drew away the camel from among the other camels in the middle of the night: and in like manner you say of other things. (TA.) -A2- sal~a , aor. , (K,) inf. n. sal~N , (TK,) said of a man; (TA;) or sal~ato , aor. , [whence it would seem that the sec. pers. of the pret. is salilota , and the inf. n. salalN ,] said of a sheep or goat, $Ap ; (M;) He, or it, lost his, or its, teeth: (M, K:) on the authority of Lh. (M.) -A3- sul~a , (M, Msb, K,) in the pass. form, (Msb,) with damm, (K,) He was, or became, affected with the disease termed sil~ [q. v.]. (M, Msb, K.)

definition: It (a thing) became pulled out, or drawn forth, gently;
sourceDefinition: It (a thing) became pulled out, or drawn forth, gently; (M;) it became drawn, or pulled out or forth, as a sword from its scabbard, and a hair from dough. (Mgh.) You say, Ansl~ Als~ayofu mina Algamodi The sword [ became drawn from the scabbard: or] slipped out from the scabbard. (TA.) And Ansl~ qiyaAduAlfarasi mino yadihi [ The leading-rope of the horse slipped out or] came forth [ from his hand ]. (Mgh.) ― -b2- And [hence], as also ↓ tsl~l , (S, M, K,) He slipped away, or stole away; i. e., went away covertly, secretly, or clandestinely: (M, K:) or he went forth, mino bayonihimo [ from among them ]. (S.) And Ainosalalotu mino bayoni yadayohi I went away, and went forth, deliberately, or leisurely, and by degrees, from before him. (TA.) Sb says that Ainosalalotu [used in this or a similar sense] is not a quasi-pass. verb; but is only like [a verb of the measure] faEalotu ; like as Aifotaqara is like DaEufa . (M.) It is said in a prov., ramatoniY bidaAy^ihaAwaA@nosal~ato [ She reproached me with her own fault, and slipped away ]: (S, Meyd, TA:) [originally] said by one of the fellow-wives of Ruhm, daughter of El-Khazraj, wife of Saad Ibn-Zeyd-Menáh, on Ruhm's reproaching her with a fault that was in herself. (Meyd, TA. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. cap. x. no. 2; and another prov. there referred to in cap. ii. no. 78.]) And one says also, bika*aA ↓ Astl~ , meaning He went away with such a thing covertly, secretly, or clandestinely. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: (S, M, Msb, K) and ↓ sulaAlN , (S, M, K,) the former [the more common, and] often occurring in the verses of chaste poets, though El-Hareeree says in the “ Durrat el-Ghowwás ” that it is an erroneous term of the vulgar, and that the latter is the right term, (TA,) signify the same, (S, M, K,) as also ↓ sul~N and ↓ sal~apN , (K,) [ Consumption: or phthisis: ] an emaciating, oppressive, and fatal malady: (T, TA:) a certain disease, well known; said in the medical books to be one of the diseases of girls, because of the abundance of blood in them: (Msb:) accord. to the physicians, (TA,) an ulcer, (K, TA,) or ulcers, (Msb,) [or ulceration, ] in the lungs; (Msb, K, TA;) succeeding ( tuEaq~ibu [grammatically referring to sal~ap ]) either *aAt Alr~iy^ap [i. e. inflammation of the lungs ] or *aAt Aljanob [i. e. pleurisy ]: (in the CK, biEaqabi *At Alr~iy~pi Aw*Ati Aljanobi is [erroneously] put in the place of tuEaq~ibu *aAta Alr~iy^api A^awo *aAta Aljanobi : and in what here follows, the gen. case is put in the place of the nom. in four instances:) or a rheum ( zukaAmN ), and defluxions ( nawaAzilu ), or a long cough, and attended with constant fever. (K, TA.) ― -b2- Hence the saying, in a trad., gubaAru*ayoli AlmaroA^api AlfaAjirapi yuwrvu Als~il~a (assumed tropical:) [ The dust of the skirt of the vitious woman occasions the loss of property ]; meaning that he who follows vitious women and acts vitiously, loses his property, and becomes poor: the diminution and departure of property being likened to the diminution and wasting away of the body when one has the disorder termed sil~ . (TA.)

definition: The drawing of swords;
sourceDefinition: The drawing of swords; (S, M, K;) as also ↓ sil~apN . (K.) So in the saying, A^atayonaAhumo Einoda Als~al~api [ We came to them on the occasion of the drawing of swords ]. (S, M, K.) ― -b2- And Theft: (S, Msb:) or covert, secret, or clandestine, theft; (M, K;) like A_isolaAlN [except that the former is a simple subst., and the latter is an inf. n., i. e. of 4]: (K:) one says, fiY baniY fulaAnK sal~apN [ Among the sons of such a one is theft, or covert theft ]: (S:) and Alxal~apu tadoEuw A_ilaY Als~al~api [ Want invites to theft, or covert theft ]. (TA.) -A2- Also (tropical:) The rush ( dufoEap ) of a horse among other horses, in running: (TA:) or the rush ( dufoEap ) of a horse in striving to outstrip: (S, TA: [I read fiY sibaAqihi , as in a copy of the S; instead of fY siyaAqihi , as in other copies of the S and in the TA:]) so in the saying, farasN $adiydu Als~al~api (tropical:) [ A horse of which the rush &c. is vehement ]: (S, TA:) and xarajato sal~atuhu EalaY Alxayoli (S) or EalaY saAy^iri Alxayoli (TA) (tropical:) [ His rush in striving to outstrip proceeded against the other horses ]. ― -b2- And A revulsion of shortness of breathing ( AirotidaAdu rabowK ) in the chest of a horse, in consequence of his suppressing such shortness of breathing [so I render mino kabowapK yakobuwhaA , but this phrase admits of other renderings, as will be seen in art. kbw ]: (M, K:) when he is inflated thereby, one says, A^axoraja sal~atahu [app. meaning he has manifested his revulsion of shortness of breathing ]; and thereupon he is urged to run with vehemence, and made to sweat, and coverings are thrown upon him, and that shortness of breathing ( *`lika Alr~abowu ) passes forth. (M.) ― -b3- [In a sheep or goat, or a ewe or she-goat, it seems to mean Power, or force, of long continuance: see masoluwlapN , voce masoluwlN .] -A3- See also sil~N . -A4- Also A [ basket of the kind called ] juwnap : (K:) or a thing like the juwnap , (M,) or like the covered juwnap , which is also called saba*apN ; so says Az: (TA:) a receptacle in which fruit is carried: (Msb:) [ sometimes covered with red skin: (see HawarN :) in the present day commonly applied to a basket made of twigs, oblong and deep, generally between a foot and a foot and a half in length: ] and ↓ sal~N signifies the same: (M, K:) what is termed sal~apu Alxubozi [ the bread-basket ] is well known: (S:) sal~apN meaning as expl. above is not thought by IDrd to be an Arabic word: (M:) [the dim. ↓ sulayolapN occurs in the K voce juwnapN , and in the Mgh voce raboEapN , &c.:] the pl. is silaAlN (M, K) and sal~aAtN (Msb) and [coll. gen. n.] ↓ sal~N , of which Abu-l-Hasan says that it is in his opinion a rare kind of pl. [or coll. gen. n.] because it denotes what is made by art, not created, and it should more properly be regarded as of the class of kawokabN and kawokabapN [which are syn.] because this is more common than the class of safiynapN and safiynN . (M.) -A5- Also A fault, or defect, in a water-ing-trough or tank, or in a [ jar of the kind called ] xaAbiyap : (M, K:) or a breach between the A^anoSaAbi , (K,) or [more properly] between the naSaAy^ib , [i. e. the stones set up, and cemented together with kneaded clay, around the interior, ] (M,) of a watering-trough or tank. (M, K.) ― -b2- And Fissures in the ground, that steal [i. e. imbibe ] the water. (TA.) -A6- Also One's sewing [a skin, or hide, with ] two thongs in a single puncture, or stitch-hole. (M, K.)

sourceDefinition: A drawn sword; i. q. ↓ masoluwlN . (M, K.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) A child, or male offspring; [because drawn forth;] (S, M, Msb, K;) as also ↓ sulaAlapN ; (M, Mgh, Msb, K;) metonymically so termed: (Mgh:) or, when it comes forth from the belly of its mother; as also ↓ the latter; the former so called because created from the [sperma genitalis, which is termed] sulaAlap : (Akh, TA:) fem. of the former ↓ saliylapN , (S, M, Msb, K,) applied to a daughter. (AA, K.) ― -b3- A colt; (M, K;) and with p a filly; (S, * M, TA;) the p being affixed, though slyl is of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN , because the word is made a subst.: (Ham p. 102:) or, as some say, (M, in the K “ and ”) the former signifies a colt that is born not in a [ membrane such as is called ] maAsikap nor [ in one such as is called ] salFY : if in either of these, it is termed baqiyrN [not buqayorN as in the CK]. (M, K.) [See also duEomuwSN .] ― -b4- And A young camel when just born, before it is known whether it is a male or a female. (As, S, TA.) -A2- Clear, or pure, beverage or wine; (K, TA;) as though gently drawn away from dust or motes or particles of rubbish or the like: such is said to be the beverage, or wine, of Paradise: or cool beverage or wine: or such as is clear from dust or motes or particles of rubbish or the like, and from turbidness; of the measure faEiylN in the sense of the measure mafoEuwlN : or such as is easy [ in its descent ] in the throat, or fauces. definition: What is, or becomes, drawn forth, or drawn forth gently, from, or of, a thing: (M, K:) or so sulaAlapu $aYo'K : (S:) [ an extract of a thing: and hence,] the clear, or pure, part, or the choice, best, or most excellent, part [of a thing];
sourceDefinition: What is, or becomes, drawn forth, or drawn forth gently, from, or of, a thing: (M, K:) or so sulaAlapu $aYo'K : (S:) [ an extract of a thing: and hence,] the clear, or pure, part, or the choice, best, or most excellent, part [of a thing]; (Mgh; and Ksh and Bd and Jel in xxiii. 12;) because drawn from the thick, or turbid, part. (Mgh.) It is said in the Kur [xxiii. 12], walaqado xalaqonaA A@loA_inosaAna mino sulaAlapK mino TiynK , meaning [ And verily we created man from ] what was drawn forth from every kind of dust, or earth: (Fr, TA:) or from a pure, or choice, or most excellent, sort of earth or clay. (Ksh, Bd, Jel.) ― -b2- And [hence,] The sperma genitalis of a man, or human being; (S, TA;) what is drawn from the Sulob [app. here meaning loins ] of the man and from the taraAy^ib [pl. of tariybap , q. v.,] of the woman: (AHeyth, TA:) the water ( maA=' ) that is drawn from the back. ('Ikrimeh, TA.) ― -b3- See also salylN , second sentence, in two places.

sourceDefinition: , for which one also says safo , (M, Mughnee, K,) rejecting the medial radical letter, (M, Mughnee,) and sawo , (M, Mughnee, K,) rejecting the final radical, (M, Mughnee,) and saYo , (M, Mughnee, K,) rejecting the final radical and changing the medial into Y for the purpose of alleviation [of the utterance], (M, Mughnee,) and accord. to the L saA , (TA,) is a particle, (IJ, M, K,) denoting inception; (K;) or a word denoting tanofiys , (Sb, S, M, K,) i. e. amplification, because it changes the aor. from the strait time, which is the present, to the ample time, which is the future; (Mughnee voce sa [q. v.];) i. e., denoting tnfys with respect to that which has not yet happened; (Sb, S, K;) and postponement; (M;) and is used in terrifying and threatening and promising; (IDrd, K;) or it is a word denoting promising or threatening: (Msb:) it is syn. with sa accord. to some, or has a larger meaning than this latter accord. to others. (Mughnee.) You say, sawofa A^afoEalu [ I will do such a thing]. (Sb, S.) And one may not introduce a separating word between it and its verb, [except in a case mentioned in what follows,] because it occupies the place of the s in sayafoEalu [&c.]. (Sb, S.) [But] it is distinct from sa by its [sometimes] having l prefixed to it; as in [the phrase in the Kur xciii. 5], walasawofa yuEoTiyka rab~uka fataroDaY [ And thy Lord will give thee, and thou wilt be well pleased ]: (Mughnee:) in this phrase, [however,] the l is [considered as] pre- fixed to the verb, not to the particle: (M:) or the phrase is elliptical, for laA^anota sawofa yuEoTiyka . (Bd.) And it is distinct from sa in this, that it is sometimes separated [from its verb] by a verb divested of government both as to the letter and the meaning; as in the saying, wamaA A^adoriY wasawofa A_ixaAlu A^adoriY A^aqawomN A=lu HiSonK A^amo nisaA='u [ And I know not, but I shall, I think, know, whether the family of Hisn be a company of men or women ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b2- When you desire to make it a subst., [i. e. to use it as a subst.,] you make it to have tenween [when it is indeterminate]. (IDrd, K.) IDrd cites as an ex., A_in~a sawofFA waA_in~a layotFA EanaA='N [ Verily sawofa and verily layota are a weariness ]: but one reading is A_in~a law~FA ; and another, A_in~a layotFA wA_in~a law~FA ; and there is no such reading as A_in~a sawofFA . (O, TA.) One says also, fulaAnN yaqotaAtu Als~awofa [lit. Such a one feeds upon the word sawofa ]; meaning (tropical:) Such a one lives by means of things hoped for: (S, K, TA:) and in like manner, maA quwtuhu A_il~aA Als~awofu [lit. His food is not anything but, or other than, the word sawofa ]. (A, TA.) ― -b3- In the following verse of Ibn-Mukbil, cited by Sb, bisawofK mino taHiy~atihaA ↓ lawo saAwafatonaA sawofa AlEayuwfi laraAHa Alr~akobu qado qaniEaA [ Had she put us off with a sawofa as part of her greeting, with the putting off even of such as is affected with dislike, the riders had gone contented ], sawofa is put in the accus. case [for musaAwafapa , i. e.] as an inf. n. with the augmentation [meaning the augmentative letters] rejected. (M.)

definition: [properly A place of smelling: ― -b2- and hence,] (tropical:) Distance;
sourceDefinition: [properly A place of smelling: ― -b2- and hence,] (tropical:) Distance; (S, K, TA;) and ↓ masaAfN and ↓ siyfapN signify the same in this sense [or in others here following]: (K:) [ a space, or tract, or an extent, over which one journeys: ] a far-extending tract that one traverses: originally a place of smelling of the guides, in order that they may know whether it be far or near, out of the way or in the right way: (A, TA:) or a [ desert, or such as is termed ] mafaAzap : (M:) said to be from saAfa Al$~aYo'a meaning “ he smelled the thing; ” for the guide smells the dust of the place wherein he is; and if he smell the odour of urine and dung of camels, he knows that he [or some other] has traversed it; but otherwise, not: (Msb:) or because the guide, when he is in a desert, (S, M, K,) and has lost his way therein, (M,) smells its dust, (S, M, K,) in order that he may know, (S, K,) or and thus knows, (M,) whether he be in the right way, (S, M, K,) or not: (S, K:) then, by reason of frequency of usage of this word [as meaning “ a place of smelling of the guides ”] it became a term for “ distance: ” (S, K:) pl. masaAwifu (A, TA) and masaAfaAtN . (Msb.) One says, kamo masaAfapu h`*ihi AlA^aroDi and ↓ masaAfuhaA and ↓ siyfatuhaA (tropical:) [ How long is the distance, or how much is the extent, of this land? ]. (TA.) And bayonahumo masaAfapN baEiydapN (assumed tropical:) [ Between them is a far-extending distance or space ]. (Msb.) And bayonanaA masaAfapu Ei$oriyna yawomFA (tropical:) [ Between us is the distance, or space, of twenty days ]. (A, TA.)

sourceDefinition: an inf. n. of 1 [q. v.] (S, Msb, K.) ― -b2- And signifying Separation, disunion, or dispersion: so in the saying, AlHamodu lil~`hi Al~a*iY jamaEanaA mino $at~K [ Praise be to God who has brought us together from a state of separation, disunion, or dispersion ]: (TA:) a saying mentioned by AA, as heard by him from an Arab of the desert: (S, TA:) and ↓ $ataAtN is [similar in meaning, being] likewise an inf. n. of 1; (S, A, K;) or it is a subst. from the intrans. verb $at~a , (Msb,) and signifies a state of separation or disunion; as in the saying, A^axaAfu Ealayokumu Al$~ataAta [ I fear for you separation, or disunion ]. (TA.) -A2- Also i. q. mutafar~iqN [meaning Dissolved, broken up, discomposed, deranged, disorganized, disordered, or unsettled; and separated, disunited, dispersed, or scattered ]; as also ↓ $atiytN , (S, A, Msb,) [and ↓ $ataAtN , as will be shown in what follows;] or ↓ $atiytN is syn. with mufar~aqN , [which is virtually the same as mutafar~iqN ,] and mu$at~atN : (K:) the pl. of $at~N is A^a$otaAtN (S) [and $utuwtN also, as will be shown by an ex. in what follows]: and ↓ $at~aY is pl. of ↓ $atiytN , like as maroDaY is of mariyDN ; (Jel in xx. 55, and MF;) or, accord. to some, it is a sing. noun. (MF.) One says A^amorN $at~N i. e. mutafar~iqN [ A state of affairs dissolved, broken up, &c.]; (S;) and [so] ↓ A^amorN $ataAtN , the latter word being an inf. n. used as an epithet. (Ham p. 176.) And ↓ SaAra jamoEuhumo $atiytFA i. e. mutafar~iqFA [ Their company, or congregated body, became separated, disunited, dispersed, or scattered ]. (A.) And jaAw^uwA A^a$otaAtFA They came separated, disunited, dispersed, or scattered; syn. mutafar~iqiyna : (S, Msb, K:) and so ↓ jAw^wA $ataAta $ataAta , (K,) in one copy of the K $ataAta wa$ataAta ; and MF allows ↓ $utaAta , like vulaAva and rubaAEa ; but there is no apparent reason for the repetition; and accord. to the L, the phrase as transmitted from the authorities worthy of confidence is ↓ jaA='a Alqawomu $ataAtFA and $ataAta i. e. The people, or party, came separated, &c. (TA.) And ↓ qawomN $at~aY (S, Msb, K, TA) A people, or party, separated, &c.; syn. mutafar~iquwna : (Msb, TA:) or consisting of sundry, or distinct, bodies; not of one tribe. (K.) And A_in~a Almajolisa layajomaEu $utuwtFA mina Aln~aAsi , (S, TA,) and mina Aln~aAsi ↓ $at~aY , Verily the assembly comprises sundry, or distinct, bodies of men; (TA;) or men not of one tribe. (S TA.) And ↓ A^a$oyaA='u $at~aY [ Things of sundry, or different, or distinct, kinds or sorts ]. (S.) A^azowaAjFA mino nabaAtK ↓ $at~aY , in the Kur xx. 55, means Sorts, of plants, various, or different, in colours, tastes, &c. (Jel.) ↓ A^um~ahaAtuhumo $at~aY see expl. voce A^um~N . And taw^uwbu ↓ $at~aY AlHalabaho , a prov., see expl. voce HaAlibN .

definition: , (K, TA, but omitted in the CK,) with damm to the n of byn , (TA,) [ Different, or distinct, are they two: or widely different or distinct are they two: or how very, or widely, different or distinct, are they two! lit.
sourceDefinition: , (K, TA, but omitted in the CK,) with damm to the n of byn , (TA,) [ Different, or distinct, are they two: or widely different or distinct are they two: or how very, or widely, different or distinct, are they two! lit., the union of them two is severed: or the interval between them two is far-extending, or wide: or how greatly is the union of them two severed! as will be shown below.] AZ quotes, in his “ Nawádir, ” with byn in the nom. case, the following verse: $at~aAna bayonuhumaA fiY kul~i manozilapK h`*aA yaxaAfu wah`*aA yarotajiY A^abadaA [ Different, or widely different, &c., are they two in every predicament: this fears, and this hopes, ever ]. (TA.) The mansoob form, however, is also employed (K, TA, but omitted in the CK) by some of the Arabs in the above-mentioned phrase, so that one says, $at~aAna bayonahumaA , maA being understood, as though one said, $at~a Al~a*iY bayonahumaA [meaning, as above explained, Different, or widely different, &c., are they two: lit., separated, or disunited, or severed, is that which is between them two: or far-extending, or wide, is the interval between them two: or how greatly separated, or severed, is the union between them two! ]: Hassán Ibn-Thábit says, wa$at~aAna bayonakumaA fiY Aln~adaY wafiY AlbaA^osi waAlxubori waAlmanoZari [ And different, or widely different, &c., are ye two in munificence and in valour and internal state and external appearance ]. (TA.) In like manner also, [but with mA ,] one says, $at~aAna maA bayonahumaA , (A, Msb, K,) accord. to Th. (TA.) This [as also, consequently, the same phrase without mA ] is disallowed by As and IKt: IB, however, says that this phrase occurs in the verses of chaste Arabs: for instance, Abu-l-Aswad EdDuälee says, wa$at~aAna maA bayoniY wabayonaka A_in~aniY EalaY kul~i HaAlK A^asotaqiymu wataZolaEu [ And different, or widely different, &c., are I and thou: for I, in every case, go erect, and thou haltest ]: and similar is the saying of El-Ba'eeth, wa$at~aAna maA bayoniY wabayona A@boni xaAlidK A^umay~apa fiY Alr~izoqi Al~a*iY yataqas~amu [ And different, or widely different, &c., are I and Ibn-Khálid Umeiyeh, with respect to the supplies for the wants of life that are divided among mankind ]. (TA.) One says also, $at~aAna maA humaA ; (S, A, K;) and $at~aAna maA EamorNw waA^axuwhu ; (S, K;) Different, or distinct, or widely different, &c., are they two; and 'Amr and his brother: [lit., separate, or distinct, are they two; &c.: or remote are they two, one from the other; &c.:] or how greatly, or widely, are they two separated; &c.! (S, A, K:) here mA is redundant; and in the former phrase, hmA is the agent of $t~An ; as is the former of the two nouns, to which the latter noun is conjoined, in the latter phrase. (TA.) ElAashà says, $at~aAna maA yawomiY EalaY kuwrihaA wayawomu Hay~aAna A^axiYjaAbiri [ Different, or widely different, &c., are (or were ) my day upon her (the camel's) saddle, and the day of Heiyán the brother of Jábir: in which, for yawomiY and yawomu , some read nawomiY and nawomu ]. (S, TA.) And in like manner, [but without mA ,] one says, $at~aAna A^axuwhu waA^abuwhu [ Different, or widely different, &c., are his brother and his father ]. (TA.) [See also an ex. in a verse cited voce daAy^imN , in art. dwm .] ― -b2- $at~aAna , is a preterite verbal noun, signifying Aifotaraqa , [and so expl. above,] accord. to many authorities, [including most of the grammarians,] and therefore they have made it a condition that its agent must be what denotes more than one: [for A$trTwA fY fElh Altrd~d , I read A$trTwA fY fAElhu AltEd~d , which agrees with what is afterwards said in the TA and here; though the former phrase may be so rendered as to convey essentially the same meaning: but this condition is not necessary if we render $t~An by baEuda :] (TA:) or it signifies tabaAEada and Aifotaraqa ; (Ibn-Umm-Kásim;) or baEuda ; [and so expl. above;] (S, A, Msb, K;) and is inflected from $atuta ; (S, K;) [which is a verb not used; in the CK, incorrectly, $atata ;] the fet-hah of the n being the fet-hah originally pertaining to the [final] t [of the verb]; and this fet-hah shows the word to be inflected from the preterite verb, like as saroEaAna is from saruEa , and wa$okaAna from wa$uka : (S:) or, accord. to Er-Radee, it implies wonder, [like several verbs of the measure faEula , as shown in remarks on hayuw^a &c.,] and means how greatly separated, disunited, or severed, &c.! (TA:) or, accord. to El-Marzookee and Hr and Zj and some others, it is an inf. n.: El-Marzookee says, in his Expos. of the Fs, that it is an inf. n. of a verb not used, [namely $atuta ,] and is indecl., with fet-hah for its termination, because it is put in the place of a pret. verb, being equivalent to $at~a , [for $atuta ,] i. e., ta$at~ata A^awo tafar~aqa jid~FA [as expl. above]: and Zj says that it is an inf. n. occupying the place of a verb, of the measure faEolaAn , and therefore indecl., because differing thus from others of its class: Aboo-'Othmán El-Mázinee says that $at~aAn and suboHaAn may receive tenween, whether they be substs, or occupying the place of substs.: upon which AAF observes that if $t~An be in its proper place, it is a verbal noun, meaning $at~a : if with tenween, it is indeterminate; if without tenween, determinate; and if translated from its office of a verbal noun, and made a subst. answering to Alt~a$otiytu , and determinate, it is similar to sbHAn in the phrase suboHaAna mino Ealoqamapa AlfaAxiri , which is a subst. answering to Alt~anoziyhu . (TA.) The n in $at~aAn (sometimes, TA) receives kesreh; (K;) though this is contr. to what is said by AZ and by IDrst: its being sometimes with kesreh is mentioned by Th, on the authority of Fr: and Er-Radee seems to infer that its being so was an opinion of As; and gives two reasons for his disallowal of the expression $t~An mA byn ; first, because $t~An occurs with kesr to the n ; and second, because its agent cannot be otherwise than what denotes more than one: [but see what has been observed above on this point:] IAmb says that one must not say $at~aAni maA bayona A^axiyka waA^abiyka , because, in this case, $t~An [virtually] governs only one noun in the nom. case: but that one may say, $at~aAni A^axuwka waA^abuwka , and $at~aAni maA A^axuwka waA^abuwka , using $at~aAni as the dual of $at~N ; though correctly $t~An is a verbal noun: MF, however, observes that the Expositors of the Fs seem to say that Fr makes $at~aAni to be the dual of $at~N ; but that he only mentions it as a dial. var. of $at~aAna : the following is adduced as an ex. la$at~aAna maA A^anowiY wayanowiY banuw A^abiY [ Different, or widely different, &c., are that which I intend and that which the sons of my father intend ]: in which $t~An is read with both fet-hah and kesreh: and it is said in the O that $at~aAni is a dial. var. of $at~aAna . (TA.) ― -b3- IJ mentions ↓ $at~aY as an accidental syn. of $t~An ; and says that it is not the fem. of the latter: therefore the assertion of some, that it is used by poetical license in the following verse of Jemeel requires consideration: A^uriydu SilaAHahaA waturiydu qatoliY wa$at~aY bayona qatoliY waAlS~ilaAHi [ I desire to make peace with her, but she desires to slay me: and different, or widely different, &c., are slaying me and making peace ]. (TA.)

[See also an ex. in a verse cited voce daAy^imN , in art. dwm .] ― -b2- $at~aAna , is a preterite verbal noun, signifying Aifotaraqa , [and so expl. above,] accord. to many authorities, [including most of the grammarians,] and therefore they have made it a condition that its agent must be what denotes more than one: [for A$trTwA fY fElh Altrd~d , I read A$trTwA fY fAElhu AltEd~d , which agrees with what is afterwards said in the TA and here; though the former phrase may be so rendered as to convey essentially the same meaning: but this condition is not necessary if we render $t~An by baEuda :] (TA:) or it signifies tabaAEada and Aifotaraqa ; (Ibn-Umm-Kásim;) or baEuda ; [and so expl. above;] (S, A, Msb, K;) and is inflected from $atuta ; (S, K;) [which is a verb not used; in the CK, incorrectly, $atata ;] the fet-hah of the n being the fet-hah originally pertaining to the [final] t [of the verb]; and this fet-hah shows the word to be inflected from the preterite verb, like as saroEaAna is from saruEa , and wa$okaAna from wa$uka : (S:) or, accord. to Er-Radee, it implies wonder, [like several verbs of the measure faEula , as shown in remarks on hayuw^a &c.,] and means how greatly separated, disunited, or severed, &c.! (TA:) or, accord. to El-Marzookee and Hr and Zj and some others, it is an inf. n.: El-Marzookee says, in his Expos. of the Fs, that it is an inf. n. of a verb not used, [namely $atuta ,] and is indecl., with fet-hah for its termination, because it is put in the place of a pret. verb, being equivalent to $at~a , [for $atuta ,] i. e., ta$at~ata A^awo tafar~aqa jid~FA [as expl. above]: and Zj says that it is an inf. n. occupying the place of a verb, of the measure faEolaAn , and therefore indecl., because differing thus from others of its class: Aboo-'Othmán El-Mázinee says that $at~aAn and suboHaAn may receive tenween, whether they be substs, or occupying the place of substs.: upon which AAF observes that if $t~An be in its proper place, it is a verbal noun, meaning $at~a : if with tenween, it is indeterminate; if without tenween, determinate; and if translated from its office of a verbal noun, and made a subst. answering to Alt~a$otiytu , and determinate, it is similar to sbHAn in the phrase suboHaAna mino Ealoqamapa AlfaAxiri , which is a subst. answering to Alt~anoziyhu . (TA.) The n in $at~aAn (sometimes, TA) receives kesreh; (K;) though this is contr. to what is said by AZ and by IDrst: its being sometimes with kesreh is mentioned by Th, on the authority of Fr: and Er-Radee seems to infer that its being so was an opinion of As; and gives two reasons for his disallowal of the expression $t~An mA byn ; first, because $t~An occurs with kesr to the n ; and second, because its agent cannot be otherwise than what denotes more than one: [but see what has been observed above on this point:] IAmb says that one must not say $at~aAni maA bayona A^axiyka waA^abiyka , because, in this case, $t~An [virtually] governs only one noun in the nom. case: but that one may say, $at~aAni A^axuwka waA^abuwka , and $at~aAni maA A^axuwka waA^abuwka , using $at~aAni as the dual of $at~N ; though correctly $t~An is a verbal noun: MF, however, observes that the Expositors of the Fs seem to say that Fr makes $at~aAni to be the dual of $at~N ; but that he only mentions it as a dial. var. of $at~aAna : the following is adduced as an ex. la$at~aAna maA A^anowiY wayanowiY banuw A^abiY [ Different, or widely different, &c., are that which I intend and that which the sons of my father intend ]: in which $t~An is read with both fet-hah and kesreh: and it is said in the O that $at~aAni is a dial. var. of $at~aAna . (TA.) ― -b3- IJ mentions ↓ $at~aY as an accidental syn. of $t~An ; and says that it is not the fem. of the latter: therefore the assertion of some, that it is used by poetical license in the following verse of Jemeel requires consideration: A^uriydu SilaAHahaA waturiydu qatoliY wa$at~aY bayona qatoliY waAlS~ilaAHi [ I desire to make peace with her, but she desires to slay me: and different, or widely different, &c., are slaying me and making peace ]. (TA.)

definition: , (S, Msb, K,) of an animal, (Msb,) a word of well known meaning, (S, Msb, K,) Fat;
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) of an animal, (Msb,) a word of well known meaning, (S, Msb, K,) Fat; (MA, KL;) the substance of fatness: (ISd, TA:) $aHomapN is a more special term, (S, Msb,) [i. e. a n. un.,] signifying a piece thereof: (K:) the pl. of the former is $uHuwmN . (Msb, TA.) It is said of the Jews, in a trad., Harumato Ealayohimu Al$~uHuwmu fabaAEuwhaA waA^akaluwA A^avomaAnahaA [ Fats have been forbidden to them; but they have sold them, and have devoured the prices thereof: see Lev. vii. 23]: the fat that is forbidden to them is that of the kidneys and of the stomach and of the intestines into which the food passes from the stomach; but not that of the A^alayop [meaning the “ rump, ” and also the “ tail of a sheep, ”] nor of the back. (TA.) One says, laqiytuhu bi$aHomi kulaAhu [lit. I met him, or found him, with the fat of his kidneys, ] meaning, (tropical:) in his state of briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness. (K, TA.) And of him who is deemed weak, one says, fulaAnN $aHomN lilomubotaliEi (tropical:) [lit. Such a one is fat for the swallower ]. (Ham p. 771.) ― -b2- Also The hump of the camel: (TA:) heard by Az from the Arabs in this sense. (TA in art. Hm .) ― -b3- And The whiteness [app. meaning the white part ] of the belly. (TA.) ― -b4- $aHomapu AlA^u*uni [ The lobe, or lobule, of the ear; ] the part, of the ear, to which the quroT [i. e. ear-ring or ear-drop ] is suspended; (S, Msb, K;) i. e. the soft portion of the lower part of the ear: or the place of the perforation for the quroT . (TA.) ― -b5- $aHomapu AlEayoni The muqolap of the eye; (TA;) i. e., what comprises the white and the black of the eye: (Zj in his “ Khalk el-Insán; ” and S and Msb and K voce muqolapN :) [this is what is generally meant by it; i. e. the globe of the eye: ] in the T it is said to be the Hadaqap [i. e. black, or what is in the middle of the white, ] of the eye: and some say that it is the $aHomap [app. meaning the whole substance ] that is beneath [or behind ] the Hadaqap . (TA.) ― -b6- $aHomapu AlHanoZali [and $aHomuhu , as in the K in art. HnZl ,] The inner part [i. e. the pulp ] of the colocynth, exclusive of its seeds. (K.) ― -b7- $aHomapu Alr~um~aAni The thin yellow [ pulp ] that is amid the seeds of the pomegranate; (K;) or, as in the M, the substance that separates the seeds of the pomegranate. (TA.) ― -b8- $aHomu Aln~axoli The heart pith, or cerebrum, ( jum~aAr ,) of palm-trees: (S in art. j*b :) and $aHomapu Aln~axolapi the heart ( jum~aArap ) of the palm-tree. (M, TA.) ― -b9- $aHomapu Almaroji The xiTomiY~ [or marsh-mallow ]. (K.) ― -b10- $aHomu AlA^aroDi The truffle; as a gen. n.; syn. Alkamo'u : (TA in art. kmA^ :) and $aHomapu AlA^aroDi the truffle; as a n. un.; syn. AlkamoA^apu : (K:) or the white truffle; syn. AlkamoA^apu AlbayoDaA='u . (S.) [It should be observed that Alkamo'u is generally held to be a n. un.; and AlkamoA^apu , to be a coll. gen. n.; contr. to analogy: but they are here evidently used in the reverse manner.] ― -b11- $aHomapu AlA^aroDi also signifies A certain white worm: or is of ( min [which is omitted in some of the copies of the K]) the [ long worms, found in moist earth, and in the mud of rivers, called ] xaraATiyn : (K, TA:) or a white EaZaA='ap [n. un. of EaZaA='N , q. v.], not big: or, as some say, it is not of the [ species called ] EaZaA=' ; it is more pleasant [ to the taste ], and better: and [ because it dwells in the sand-hills, ] they say [i. e. call it ] also $aHomapu Aln~aqaA , like as they say banaAtu Aln~aqaA : (TA:) it is the [ reptile called ] Hulakap , which dives into the sand, and to which the fingers ( banaAn ) of virgins are likened. (TA in art. ArD . [See HulakapN : and see also $abavN .]) ― -b12- A^abuw $aHomK is an appellation of The small species of what is called HimaAru qab~aAna . (TA in art. qb , q. v.) ― -b13- [See also $aHomapN below.]

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. $uruwdN (S, L, Msb, K) and $iraAdN , (S, L, K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Msb,) and $uraAdN (K) and $arodN , (L,) said of a camel, (S, A, L, Msb,) and of a horse or the like, (L,) He took fright, or shied, and fled, or ran away at random; or became refractory, and went away at random, or ran away, or broke loose, and went hither and thither by reason of his sprightliness; syn. nafara , (S, L, Msb, K,) and nad~a : (Msb:) and [simply] he fled, or ran away; said of a camel &c. (Aboo-Bekr, TA.) The saying of the Prophet, A^amaA ya$orudu bika baEiyruka (tropical:) [ Does not thy camel take fright and run away with thee? ], addressed by him to Khowwát, who answered, A^amaA muno*u qay~adahu AlA_isolaAmu falaA [ As to the period since El-Islám shackled him, no ], mentioned in the A, points to a story related of Khowwát Ibn-Jubeyr, (TA,) that, being found by the Prophet sitting by some strange women, he endeavoured to excuse himself by saying that he had a camel which took fright and ran away, and he was seeking for something wherewith to shackle him: the Prophet used afterwards to taunt him by inquiring of him respecting the running-away of his camel: what Kr says, and J in the S [in art. nHY ], is incorrect. (IAth, L.) You say also, $arada Ean~iY fulaAnN Such a one fled, or went away or aside or apart or to a distance, from me; syn. nafara . (A.) [Or] $arada said of a man, inf. n. $uruwdN , means He departed, driven away. (L.) And you say, $arada EalaY A@ll~`hi , meaning He departed from obedience to God, and seceded, or separated himself from the community [ of the faithful ]. (L.)

sourceDefinition: , (A 'Obeyd, O,) aor. , (O,) inf. n. $aSorN , (A 'Obeyd, S, O, K,) He sewed (a garment, or piece of cloth, A 'Obeyd) with wide stitches, or with stitches far apart, (S, O, K,) as in the manner termed ba$okN . (A 'Obeyd.) ― -b2- $aSara Eayona AlbaAziY , (S, O,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (S,) He sewed up the eye of the hawk. (S, O.) ― -b3- $aSara Aln~aAqapa , (M, O, K,) aor. and , (O, K,) inf. n. as above, (S, M, O, K,) He transfixed the sides of the she-camel's vulva with small sharp-pointed pieces of wood, or prickles, (M, O, * K, *) and twisted round behind them sinews, (M,) or a string made of hairs from her tail, (M, O, * K, *) on account of the protruding of her womb on the occasion of her bringing forth; (M, O, K;) syn. of the inf. n. tazoniydN . (S.) See also $iSaArN , below. ― -b4- And $aSara Aln~aAqapa , (K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) signifies also He inserted the piece of wood called $iSaAr between the nostrils of the she-camel; and so ↓ $S~rhA , (K,) inf. n. ta$oSiyrN . (TA.) ― -b5- $aSaratohu $awokapN , (O, K,) inf. n. as above, (K,) A thorn pricked, or pierced, him. (O, K.) ― -b6- $aSarahu biAlr~umoHi , (O,) inf. n. as above, He pierced him (O, K *) with the spear. (O.) ― -b7- $aSorN also signifies A bull's, (O, K,) and a gazelle's, (TA,) smiting (O, K, TA) a man (O, TA) with his horn. (O, K, TA.) -A2- And $aSara , (IAar, O,) inf. n. as above, (K,) He leaped, or leaped upwards; syn. Tafara . (IAar O, K. *) ― -b2- $aSara baSaruhu , aor. , (O, K, in the L ,) inf. n. $uSuwrN , His eye, or eyes, became fixedly open, or raised, or stretched and raised, or his eyelids became raised and he looked intently and became disquieted or disturbed, (syn. $axaSa ,) and the eye became inverted; at the time of death: (O, K:) thus, nearly in the same words, expl. by Lth and IF and Ibn-'Abbád: (O:) or the correct word is $aSaA , or $aTara ; (so accord. to different copies of the K, the latter being the reading in the TA;) or both; for Az says that this explanation of $Sr bSrh is in his opinion a mistake, and that it is correctly $aSaA baSaruhu and $aTara , meaning that he was as though he looked at thee and at another. (O, TA. *)

definition: (A 'Obeyd, S, K) and ↓ $aASirN (Lth, S, K) and ↓ $awoSarN (K) The young one of the gazelle, when he has become strong and active: (A 'Obeyd, S, L, &c.
sourceDefinition: (A 'Obeyd, S, K) and ↓ $aASirN (Lth, S, K) and ↓ $awoSarN (K) The young one of the gazelle, when he has become strong and active: (A 'Obeyd, S, L, &c.:) in the K, when he has become strong, but not active; but this is a mistake: (TA:) or that has become old enough to smite with his horn: or that has become a month old: or that has not yet cropped the herbage [ but only sucked his mother ]; expl. by Al~a*iY lamo yaHotaniko : (K:) A 'Obeyd states that it is said by more than one of the Arabs of the desert that the young one of the gazelle is called TalFA ; then, xi$ofN ; and when his horns come forth, $aAdinN ; and when he has become strong and active, $aSarN , of which the fem. [as is also said in the K] is $aSarapN ; then, ja*aEN ; and then, vaniY~N , which name he continues to have until he dies: (S:) [perhaps correctly corresponding to our six terms which are as follows: a fawn (applied to a buck or doe of the first year), a pricket (to a buck of the second year), a sorel (to a buck of the third year), a sore (to a buck of the fourth year), a buck of the first head (to one of the fifth year), and a great buck (to one of the sixth year):] or ↓ $aASirN is applied to a young gazelle when his horn has come forth: (Lth:) pl. [of $aSarN ,] A^a$oSaArN . (K.) ― -b2- $aSarN also signifies A certain bird, smaller than the EuSofuwr [or sparrow ], (AA, O, K,) of the colour thereof. (AA, O.)

definition: The small sharp-pointed piece of wood, or prickle, (K,) or the small sharp-pointed pieces of wood, or prickles, (IDrd, S,) with which the operation termed tazoniydN [which is that described above in the explanation of $aSara Aln~aAqapa ] is performed;
sourceDefinition: The small sharp-pointed piece of wood, or prickle, (K,) or the small sharp-pointed pieces of wood, or prickles, (IDrd, S,) with which the operation termed tazoniydN [which is that described above in the explanation of $aSara Aln~aAqapa ] is performed; (IDrd, S, K;) as also ↓ $iSorN : (K:) or ↓ $iSoraAni , or $iSaAraAni , is a term applied to two pieces of wood, which are thrust through the edge of the rectum of a she-camel, and then bound with a strong string of the fibres of the palm-tree, behind them: this is done when they desire to make a she-camel affect the young one of another: they take a stuffed durojap [q. v.], and insert it into her rectum, and transfix the rectum with two sharp-pointed pieces of wood, which they bind as above described: this operation is termed ↓ $aSorN and tazoniydN . (ISh.) [See also 1.] ― -b2- Accord. to the T, A piece of wood, which is bound between the two edges of a she-camel's vulva. (TA.) ― -b3- And A piece of wood, which is inserted between the nostrils of a she camel. (K.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. $aEavN , (A, Mgh, Msb,) It (hair) was, or became, shaggy, or dishevelled, (A, Mgh,) and frouzy, or altered in odour, (Mgh,) in consequence of its being seldom dressed: (A, Mgh:) or it was, or became, defiled with dust, and matted, or compacted, in consequence of its being seldom anointed: (Msb:) or, accord. to El-Ghooree, it wanted oil, or ointment: (Har p. 50:) and ↓ t$E~t signifies [the same: or] it was, or became, matted, or compacted, (K, TA,) and dusty. (TA.) And the former verb, [and app. ↓ the latter also,] It (the head) was, or became, dusty, not being renovated [ by dressing or anointing ], nor cleansed. (Msb.) Also the former verb, aor. as above, (L, K, and Ham p. 469,) inf. n. $aEavN (S, L, K, and Ham) and $uEuwvapN , (L and Ham,) He was, or became, shaggy, or dishevelled, in the hair, (JM, PS,) and frouzy, or altered in odour, in consequence of its being seldom dressed: (JM:) or it signifies (or signifies also, JM) he had a dusty head, (S, L, K, JM,) and plucked hair, unanointed; (L;) or he had matted, or compacted, and dusty, hair: (L, and Ham p. 469:) and in like manner ↓ t$E~v . (L.) ― -b2- $aEavN , (Msb,) or ↓ ta$aE~uvN , (S, K, TA,) [or each,] also signifies (tropical:) The being separated, or disunited, (S, Msb, K, TA,) and spread out, (Msb,) and uncompacted, (TA,) like as is the head of the siwaAk [or tooth-stick, by its being bruised, or battered, or mangled by blows ]. (Msb, TA.) You say, raA^osu Als~iwaAki ↓ t$E~v , (Msb, TA,) and Alwatidi , (A, TA,) (tropical:) The head of the tooth-stick, and of the wooden peg or stake, became disintegrated; or separated, disunited, or uncompacted, in its component parts [or its fibres; or rendered brushy; by its being bruised, or battered, or mangled by blows ]. (TA.) And ↓ t$E~vwA (tropical:) They [meaning men] became separated, disunited, dispersed, or scattered. (A.) ― -b3- And $aEiva , aor. as above, (TK,) inf. n. $aEavN , said of the state of affairs, (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, dissolved, broken up, discomposed, deranged, disorganized, disordered, or unsettled. (S, * A, * K, * TA, TK. [In the S and A and K, this is placed as the first of all the meanings in this art.; and in the A, it is mentioned among the meanings that are proper, not tropical; but in my opinion it is tropical. See also $aEavN below.])

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. ta$oEiyvN , He rendered it (i. e. hair) [ shaggy, or dishevelled, and frouzy: (see 1:) or] matte, or compacted, and dusty: or he rendered him [ shaggy, or dishevelled, and frouzy, in his hair: or] matted, or compacted, and dusty, in his hair. (TA.) ― -b2- ta$oEiyvN also signifies (assumed tropical:) The separating, disuniting, dispersing, or scattering, a thing. (S.) And (assumed tropical:) The making to separated like as do rivers and branches. (L.) [Hence,] $E~v raA^osa Als~iwaAki (tropical:) [ He made the head of the tooth-stick to become disintegrated; or separated, disunited, or uncompacted, in its component parts or its fibres; or rendered it brushy; by bruising it, battering it, or mangling it by blows: see 1]. (A.) ― -b3- $E~v Als~anaA (tropical:) He took of the straggling branches, or sprigs, of the senna, without pulling it up by the roots. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b4- See also 5, in two places. ― -b5- $E~v Aln~aAsu fiY AlT~aEoni Ealayohi (assumed tropical:) The people took, or began, to impugn his character, censure him, reproach him, or speak against him, by befouling his reputation ( bita$oEiyvi EiroDihi ). (TA, from a trad.) ― -b6- And $E~v minohu (assumed tropical:) He detracted from his reputation; syn. gaD~a minohu and tanaq~aSahu : from Al$~aEavu [as inf. n. of 1 in the last of the senses assigned to it above,] meaning Ainoti$aAru AlA^amori . (L.) ― -b7- And also, inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) He repelled from him, or defended him: (K:) or he defended his reputation. (TA.) [Thus it has two contr. meanings.]

definition: The point or extremity, verge, brink, or edge, of anything;
sourceDefinition: The point or extremity, verge, brink, or edge, of anything; (S, Msb, K, &c.;) like ↓ $afapN ; for $afaA AlHuforapi (Ksh in iii. 99) or $afaA Albiy^ori (Bd ibid.) and $afatuhaA both signify the same, (Ksh, Bd,) i. e. HarofuhaA (Ksh) or TarafuhaA ; (Bd;) but the final w in the former is changed into A , and in the latter [accord. to those who hold $afapN to be originally $afowapN ] it is elided; (Ksh, Bd;) $afFA being originally $afawN : (Bd:) [but $afFA generally signifies as expl. above; and $afapN almost always signifies the “ lip ” of a human being:] the dual is $afawaAni ; this being known, as Akh says, by the fact that A_imaAlap in the word $afFA is not allowable: (S:) and the pl. is A^a$ofaA='N . (TA.) It is said in the Kur [iii. 99], wakunotumo EalaY $afaA HuforapN mina A@ln~aAri faA^anoqa*akumo minohaA [ And ye were on the verge, or brink, of a pit of the fire of Hell, and He saved, or rescued, you from it ]. (S.) And one says, huwa EalaY $afaA AlhalaAki (tropical:) [ He is on the brink of destruction ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Also (tropical:) A little; (S, A, K, TA;) a small part, or portion; somewhat; (A, TA;) somewhat remaining of the moon when near the change, (K, TA, [ AlhalAk in the CK is erroneously put for AlhilaAl ,]) and of the sight ( AlbaSar ), and of the day, and the like, as in the T. (TA.) One says of a man on the occasion of his dying, and of the moon at [the last period of the month called] its muHaAq , and of the sun at its setting, (S,) maA baqiYa minohu A_il~aA $afFA [and minohaA when said of the sun] (assumed tropical:) There has not remained of him, or it, save a little: (S, K: *) and [in like manner] mina AlEumuri [ of life ]. (S.) And one says, A^atayotuhu bi$afFA mino Dawo'i Al$~amosi (assumed tropical:) [ I came to him in a time when there was little remaining of the light of the sun ]. (TA.) El-'Ajjáj says, A^a$orafotuhu bilaA $afFA A^awo bi$afaA wamirobaA^K EaAlK limanN ta$ar~afaA meaning [ Many an elevated place of observation, high to him who ascends it, I have ascended ] when the sun had set or when there was somewhat of it remaining. (S.) One says also, SaAra fiY $afaA Alqamari meaning (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, in the last part of the night. (TA.) And it is said in a trad., (in relation to [the temporary marriage termed] AlmutoEap ,) falawo laA nahoyuhu EanohaA maA A@HotaAja A_ilaY Alz~inaA A_il~aA $afFA , accord. to the T meaning [ Were it not for his (i. e. God's) forbidding it, none would need having recourse to fornication, ] save a small number of men: (T, TA:) or, accord. to 'Atà, it means, but would be on the brink thereof, without falling into it; $afFA being thus used in the place of the inf. n. A_i$ofaA=' : so says IAth, as from Az. (TA.)

definition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) inf. n. ta$omiyrN , (S, K,) He raised, (S, Msb, K,) or tucked up, or contracted, (A,) his garment, (Msb, K,) or his waist-wrapper, (S,) [or his sleeve,] or his skirts. (A.) One says, $m~r Eano saAqihi [ He raised, or tucked up, his garment, or waist-wrapper, or skirts, from his shank ]. (S.) [And in like manner, ↓ t$m~r signifies He raised, or tucked up, his garment, &c.: for] one says also, t$m~r Eano saAEidayohi [ He tucked up his sleeves from his fore arms ]. (TA.) It is said in a prov., $am~ara *ayolFA waA@d~araEa layolFA i. e. [lit.] He contracted, or drew up, his [or a ] skirt [ and clad himself with night as with a tunic ]: (TA:) or $amiro *ayolFA waA@d~ariEo layolFA , meaning (tropical:) Use thou prudence, or precaution, or good judgment, and journey all the night. (S and K in art. drE .) ― -b2- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) He strove, or laboured, exerted himself or his power or ability, employed himself vigorously or laboriously or with energy, or took extraordinary pains, (AA, Msb, TA,) and was quick, (AA, TA,) fiY AlA^amori [ in the affair ]; as also ↓ $amara , inf. n. $amorN : (TA:) and fiY AlEibaAdapi [ in religious service ]: (Msb:) and fiY sayorihi [ in his pace, or journeying ]; like tajar~ada and Ainojarada . (L and TA in art. jrd .) Also, (K,) inf. n. as above; (TA;) and ↓ $amara , (K,) aor. , inf. n. $amorN ; (TA;) and ↓ An$mr , and ↓ t$m~r ; (K;) (assumed tropical:) He passed along striving, or exerting himself, or vigorously: or he passed along with a proud and self-conceited gait; (K;) [and] ↓ mar~a ya$omuru , inf. n. as above, has the latter meaning. (S.) And $m~r fiY AlA^amori (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, light, or active, (S, Msb, K,) and quick, (Msb,) in, or for, the affair: (S, Msb, K:) and $m~r liloA^amori , and $m~r liloA^amori A^a*oyaAlahu , (A, TA,) and $m~r Eano saAqihi , (TA,) (tropical:) He was, or became, light, or active, and he rose, or hastened, to do the thing, or affair. (A, TA.) And $m~rt AlHarobu and $m~rt Eano saAqihaA (tropical:) [ The war, or battle, became vehement; like ka$afato Eano saAqK ]. (A.) ― -b3- Also He contracted a thing; syn. qal~aSa ; (TA;) [and so, perhaps, ↓ $amara ; for] Al$~amoru signifies taqoliySu Al$~aYo'i , like Alt~a$omiyru : (K:) [or the author of the TA may have misunderstood this explanation in the K, and the meaning may be it (a thing) contracted, or became contracted; for qal~aSa is trans. and also (like qalaSa ) intrans.: that $m~r has this latter meaning, whether it have also, or have not, the former, is shown by the statement that] one says, $am~arati Al$~afapu meaning qalaSat [i. e. The lip became contracted, or became contracted upwards ]: (M in art. qlS :) and ↓ t$m~r [in like manner] signifies it (a thing) contracted, or became contracted; syn. taqal~aSa . (TA.) ― -b4- Also, (inf. n. as above, As, S,) (tropical:) He launched forth a ship, or boat; let it go; let it take its course; (As, IAar, S, A, K;) and in like manner, a hawk; (A;) and he discharged, or shot, an arrow: (As, IAar, S, A, Msb:) and hence, (As, S,) (tropical:) he sent, sent forth, or sent away, (As, S, M, A, K,) a thing. (M, A.) [See also sam~ara .] And $m~r AlA_ibila , inf. n. as above; (TA;) and ↓ A$mrhA ; (K;) (assumed tropical:) He hastened the camels; made them to hasten; syn. A^akoma$ahaA , [which seems to be either syn. with, or a mistranscription for, kam~a$ahaA , (see sam~ara ,)] and A^aEojalahaA . (O, K, TA.) ― -b5- And $am~arotu Aln~axola (tropical:) I cut off the fruit of the palm-trees; syn. Saramotuhu ; (A, TA;) or so ↓ $amarotuhu , (Ibn-'Abbád, O,) [for] Al$~amoru signifies SiraAmu Aln~axoli . (K.)

definition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) aor. ya$iyTu , (Msb, K,) inf. n. $ayoTN and $iyaATapN (K) and $ayoTuwTapN , (Lth, K,) It (a thing, Msb, TA, or, as some say, particularly, olive-oil, and rob, TA) burned, or became burnt; (Msb, K, TA;) as also ↓ t$y~T , (K,) said of flesh-meat: (TA:) or both, said of flesh-meat, signify its upper part became burnt by the contact of fire: (Lth, TA:) the latter is also said of wool; and the former likewise, of wool, and of hair: (TA:) the former also signifies it was near to becoming burnt: (TA:) and, said of clarified butter, and of olive-oil, (S, K,) it became cooked so much that it burned; (S;) because, in that case, it perishes; (O;) [which implies that a signification hereafter to be mentioned is held to be the primary one;] or became thick; or became cooked so much that it almost perished. (K.) You say also, $aATati Alqidoru The cooking-pot burned, and had something sticking in it: (S:) or had something burnt sticking in the bottom of it. (O, K.) ― -b2- $aATa , (S, K,) aor. as above, (S,) also signifies He (a man) perished, or died. (S, K.) [The art. in the S commences with this signification, which, as remarked above, seems to be regarded by some as the primary one.] ― -b3- Also He burned with anger. (TA in art. $Tn .) ― -b4- And It was, or became, null, void, of no account, or of no force. (Msb, TA.) ― -b5- His (a man's) blood, (S,) or it, (his blood,) (Mgh, Msb, K,) went (S, Mgh, Msb, K) for nothing, unretaliated, and uncompensated by a mulct; it was, or became, of no account. (S, Mgh, * Msb.) ― -b6- And It (any- thing ) went away; ― -b7- $aATati Aljazuwru (tropical:) The slaughtered camel became dispensed; syn. tanaf~aqat ; (S, K, TA;) there remained not of it any portion that was not divided and given: (As, S:) and $aATa laHomu Aljazuwri The flesh of the slaughtered camel went away divided and distributed, nothing thereof remaining. (A, TA.) ― -b8- $aATa also signifies (tropical:) He hastened (S, K, TA) in an affair. (K, TA.) -A2- [ $aATahu seems to be dial. var. of saATahu , as signifying He mixed it. ― -b2- And hence,] $aATa Ald~imaA='a (tropical:) He mixed the bloods; as though he shed, or poured forth, the blood of the slayer upon that of the slain. (S, K, TA.) A poet, (S,) namely, El-Mutalemmis, (TA,) uses the expression lawo tu$aATu dimaAw^unaA [ If our bloods were mixed ]; (S, TA;) accord. to one relation; but accord. to another, the verb is with s . (TA.) ― -b3- $aATa bidamihi : see 4.

definition: , (Msb, K,) inf.

A_i$aATapN , (Msb,) He burned it, or made it to burn; (Msb, K;) namely, a thing, (Msb,) as, for instance, olive-oil; (TA;) as also ↓ $y~Thu , (K,) inf. n. ta$oyiyTN . (TA.) ↓ The latter also signifies He burned its wool, namely, that of a sheep, in order to cleanse it; and so $w~Thu : (S, TA:) and each of these, he (a cook) set it on fire, namely the foot of a bull or cow, or of a sheep or goat, and the head, so that what was upon it, of hair, or wool, became burnt. (TA.) You say also, $AT Alqidora He made the cooking-pot to burn, and to have something sticking in it. (S.) And Alqidora ↓ $y~T He made the cooking-pot to boil; as also $w~ThA . (ElKilábee.) And All~aHoma ↓ $y~T He cooked thoroughly the flesh-meat; as also $w~Thu : (Ibn-'Abbád:) or he smoked it, or made it smoky, and did not thoroughly cook it; (S;) and so the latter. (TA in art. $wT .) And AlD~abuEu Aln~abota ↓ $y~T ; and Ald~awaA='u AljuroHa ; (tropical:) The year of drought burned the herbage; and the medicine, the wound. (A, TA:) [See also $aw~aTa .] ― -b2- Also, (K,) inf. n. as above, (S,) He destroyed him, or it. (TA.) You say also, A$AT dama Aljazuwri He shed the blood of the camel that was to be slaughtered. (S, TA.) Also (assumed tropical:) He cut up, or cut in pieces, the flesh of the slaughtered camel before the distribution. (ISh.)

sourceDefinition: [i. e. $ayoTaAnN or $ayoTaAnu , accord. to different authorities, as shown below, A devil; and with the article Al , the devil, Satan; ] is, accord. to some, from $aATa , (Msb, K, TA,) as signifying “ it was, or became, null, void, of no account; ” and the like: (Msb, TA:) or “ he perished: ” (K, TA:) or “ he went away: ” or “ it burned, ” or “ became burnt: ” two reasons given for this derivation are, that among the names of the devil are Almu*ohabu and AlbaATilu : and another is this; that several read, in the Kur xxvi. 210, Al$~ayaATuwna [instead of Al$~ayaATiynu ]: but some say that it is from $aTana , signifying “ he became distant, ” or “ remote: ” Sb gives both of these derivations: respecting the former of which, it should be observed that if from $AT as signifying “ it burned, ” or “ became burnt, ” it is proper; but if from the same in any of the other senses mentioned above, it is tropical: and if belonging to this art., it is imperfectly decl., being of the measure faEolaAn : (S in art. $Tn , in which see it:) [but in the Kur-án it is always perfectly decl.: and SM says that] it is perfectly decl., unless used as a proper name; in the latter case being imperfectly decl. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , for which one says taSad~aY lh , [changing the last d into Y , as in the case of Sad~ada , q. v.,] from AlS~adadu , meaning “ the place, or part, that is before, in front, facing, or opposite; ” (Az, L;) He addressed, or applied, or directed, himself, or his regard, or attention, or mind, to him, or it; [as though he set himself over against the object to which the verb relates:] and he asked him, or petitioned him, for a thing that he wanted: syn. taEar~aDa lahu ; (L and K * in the present art., and S and M and K in art. SdY ;) and A^aqobala Ealayohi ; (L;) and taDar~aEa lahu : (M in art. SdY :) he inclined to him, or it: (L:) he raised his head towards it: (M in art. SdY , in explanation of tSd~Y :) he raised his head and breast towards it, looking towards it, or regarding it: (TA in art. SdY , in explanation of tSd~Y :) the object is one at which you raise your eyes, looking at it: (S in art. SdY , in explanation of tSd~Y :) he applied, or gave, his whole attention to it, (meaning an affair,) having his mind unoccupied by other things; syn. tafar~aga lahu watabat~ala . (Msb.) One says also, tSd~Y lilr~ad~i EalaY AlmuSan~ifi [ He addressed, or applied, himself to reply against the author ]. (TA in art. Hzb , &c.) And tSd~Y lilomaEoruwfi waTalabahu He addressed himself, or applied himself, to obtain favour, or bounty; and sought it; syn. taEar~aDa lahu [and tabar~aY lh ]. (Msb in art. ErD .) And A^anota lahu taSad~aY , [in the Kur, lxxx., 6,] originally tataSad~adu , (L,) and accord. to one reading taS~ad~aY , (Jel,) means To him thou addressest thyself, or directest thine attention, and inclinest; syn. tataEar~aDu lahu , (L,) and tuqobilu Ealayohi , (Zj,) and tamiylu A_ilayohi ; (L;) or tataEar~aDu lahu biA@loA_iqobaAli Ealayohi : (Bd:) or addressest thyself, &c., and humblest thyself: (M in art. SdY : [in which, however, this explanation is not given with express reference to the above-cited phrase in the Kur:]) or it may signify thou seekest to bring thyself near to him, or to advance thyself in his favour; from AlS~adadu as signifying Alqurobu . (T.) [See also art. SdY .]

definition: (M, A, L, Msb, K) and ↓ Sad~N (K) The side of a valley, (M, A, Msb, K,) or of a $iEob [i.
sourceDefinition: (M, A, L, Msb, K) and ↓ Sad~N (K) The side of a valley, (M, A, Msb, K,) or of a $iEob [i. e. the kind of water-course so called, or a ravine], and of a mountain where it forms a ravine, (M, L,) and (tropical:) of a road: (A:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aSodaAdN and [of mult.] SuduwdN . (TA.) And ↓ Sad~N (L) and ↓ SadadN (M, L) signify [in like manner] A side; a lateral, or an adjacent, part, quarter, tract, or the like; syn. of the former jaAnibN , (L,) and of the latter naAHiyapN . (M, L.) AinoDam~a Ealayohimu AlS~ud~aAni [lit. The two sides of the road confined them ] means (tropical:) they occupied the middle of the road. (A.) And AlS~ud~aAni signifies also (tropical:) The two edges, or extremities, or cusps, of the notch of an arrow, between which is the place of the bow-string; syn. $aroxaA Alfuwqi . (O. [In the K, erroneously, $aroxaA Alfaroqi .]) ― -b2- Also Sud~N and ↓ Sad~N A mountain: (AA, S, M, L, Msb, K:) and so sud~N and sad~N : (AA, S, M:) pl. A^aSodaAdN and SuduwdN . (M, L.) ― -b3- And ↓ Sad~N [or Sud~N ] A cloud, or collection of clouds, rising high, and appearing like a mountain: and so sad~N [or sud~N (q. v.)], which is the more approved word. (M, L.)

(ISk, * T, S, * M, A, * L, K. *) One says, daAruhu biSadadi Almasojidi [ His house is in the vicinity of, i. e. near to, the mosque; or his house is opposite to the mosque ]. (Msb. [The former meaning is there indicated; but no meaning is expressed.]) And A^axa*otuhu mino SadadK i. e. mino qurobK [ I took it from a near place or spot ]. (A.) And daAriY Sadada daArihi , (ISk, S, A, K,) in which Sdd is in the accus. case as an adv. n. of place, (S, K,) and biSadadihi , (ISk, A,) and EalaY Sadadihi , (Lth, ISk,) My house is opposite to, i. e. in the place, or part, that is in front of, his house: (ISk, S, A, K:) and in the vicinity of, or near to, his house. (K.) And h`*aA Sadada h`*aA , and biSadadihi , This is in front of, or opposite to, this. (M.) ― -b3- [Hence, app.,] laA Hadada liY duwnahu walaA Sadada There is no impediment to me in the way of it, nor any obstacle. (A.) ― -b4- And huwa Sadadaka i. q. qaSodaka [i. e. He, or it, is tending, or looking, in the direction of thee; or is before thee, or before thy face: see art. qSd ]. (Sb, M.) ― -b5- And A^anaA biSadadK mino h`*aA AlA^amori [ I am directing myself, or my attention, to this affair ]. (A.) [ narojiEu A_ilaY maA naHonu biSadadihi , meaning We will return to that subject to which our attention is directed, is a phrase of frequent occurrence after a digression.]

sourceDefinition: : see 1. ― -b2- [Hence,] ASEd fiY AlA^aroDi He went through the land towards a land higher than the other [ from which he came ]: (A, TA:) taken from the saying of Lth, that ASEd , inf. n. A_iSoEaAdN , signifies He went towards a declivity, or a river, or a valley, higher than the other [ from which he came ]. (TA.) And ASEd fiY AlbilaAdi He went up, or upwards, through the countries, or lands. (AA, Msb.) And ASEd mino baladi ka*aA A_ilaY baladi ka*aA He journeyed [ upwards ] from such a region, or town, to such another region, or town; from one that was lower to one that was higher. (Msb.) [And hence,] ASEd , inf. n. A_iSoEaAdN , He journeyed, or went, towards Nejd, and El-Hijáz, and El-Yemen: [or towards a higher region: ] and AinoHadara signifies “ he journeyed, or went, towards El-'Irák, and Syria, and 'Omán: ” (ISk, on the authority of 'Omárah:) or the former, he journeyed, or went, towards the Kibleh: and the latter, “ he journeyed, or went, towards El-'Irák: ” (Aboo- Sakhr, T:) or the former, he came to Mekkeh; (K;) but this is a defective explanation: (TA:) and muSoEadN , also, is used as an inf. n. of this verb; and munoHadarN , as an inf. n. of AnHdr : (T, TA:) or ASEd , inf. n. A_iSoEaAdN , he commenced a journey, or went forth; as from Mekkeh, and from ElKoofeh to Khurásán, and the like: (Fr:) or he commenced a journey, or the like, in any direction: and AnHdr signifies “ he returned, from any town or country. ” (Ibn-'Arafeh.) And ASEd fiY AlA^aroDi , (Akh, S, K,) or fY AlbilaAdi , (Akh accord. to the T,) He went away, and journeyed, through the land, (Akh, S, K,) or through the countries, (Akh, T,) in any direction. (L.) And ASEdt Als~afiynapu , inf. n. A_iSoEaAdN ; (L;) or ↓ SE~dt ; (A;) The ship spread her sail, and was borne along by the wind, (A, L,) upwards [app. meaning up a river or the like ]. (L.) ― -b3- ASEd fiY AlwaAdiY ; (Akh, S, L, K;) and fiyhi ↓ SE~d , inf. n. taSoEiydN ; (Akh, S, Msb, K;) and ↓ AiS~aE~ada , (Lth,) but this last is disapproved by Az; (TA;) He descended, or went down, into the valley, (Akh, S, L, Msb, K,) from the part whence the torrent comes; not going to the bottom of the valley: and in like manner, ASEd fiY AlA^aroDi He descended, or went down, into the land: (L:) and fiY Aljabali ↓ SE~d He descended the mountain; as well as he ascended it. (IB, L.) Akh cites the following words of 'Abd-Allah Ibn-Hemmám Es-Saloolee, TaworFA fiY AlbilaAdi waA^uforiEu ↓ A^uSaE~idu (S, L,) as meaning I descending, or going down, at one time, through the countries, and [another time] ascending, or going up: this, says IB, is what induced Akh to explain SE~d as he has done; but it presents no proof, because A_iforaAEN has two contr. significations, that of A_iSoEaAdN and that of AinoHidaArN : and accord. to AZ, by A^uSaE~idu the poet means I ascending, or going up, to high places; and by A^uforiEu , the contrary. (L.) ― -b4- ASEd also signifies He advanced towards another. (L.) ― -b5- And He went far; syn. A^aboEada . (Ham p. 22.) ― -b6- And ASEd fiY AlEadowi He exerted himself vehemently in running. (L.) -A2- ASEd as trans.: see 2, in two places. -A3- ASEdt She (a camel) became such as is termed SaEuwd [q. v.]. (S, L, K.) ― -b2- And A^aSoEadotu Aln~aAqapa , (S, L, K,) and ↓ SaEadotuhaA , [probably imperfectly transcribed for ↓ SaE~adotuhaA ,] (L,) I made the she-camel to be, or became, such as is termed SaEuwd . (IAar, S, L, K.)

definition: A sigh, or sighing;
sourceDefinition: A sigh, or sighing; a breathing with an expression of pain, grief, or sorrow: or with difficulty: (L:) a long breathing: (K:) or a prolonged breathing: (S:) or a loud breathing: (A:) accord. to some, a breathing emitted upwards. (L.) You say, tanaf~asa AlS~uEadaA='a , (L,) or tnf~s SuEadaA='a , (A,) and ↓ tnf~s SuEudFA , (L,) He sighed; uttered a sigh or sighing; or breathed with an expression of pain, grief, or sorrow: (L:) [or uttered a prolonged breathing: ] or breathed loudly. (A.) ― -b2- [Hence,] fulaAnN yatobaEu SuEadaA='ahu , (A,) or yatatab~aEu SuEudaA='ahu , (L, [in which the noun is evidently mistranscribed,]) (tropical:) Such a one raises his head, and does not stoop it, by reason of pride: (A:) or does not raise his head nor stoop it. (L. [The former explanation seems to be the right.]) ― -b3- See also SaEuwdN , in four places.

definition: An acclivity; contr. of habuwTN , (S, L, K,) or of HaduwrN ; (Msb;) and ↓ SaEadN is [syn. therewith, being] contr. of SababN : (L:) pl. SaEaAy^idu and SuEudN . (S, K.) An ascending road: of the fem....
sourceDefinition: An acclivity; contr. of habuwTN , (S, L, K,) or of HaduwrN ; (Msb;) and ↓ SaEadN is [syn. therewith, being] contr. of SababN : (L:) pl. SaEaAy^idu and SuEudN . (S, K.) An ascending road: of the fem. gender: pl. [of pauc.] A^aSoEidapN and [of mult.] SuEudN . (L.) A mountain-road difficult of ascent; (S, A, L, K;) as also ↓ SaEuwdaA='u , (L, K,) and ↓ SuEadaA='u : (L in art. kA^d :) a difficult place of ascent. (L in that art.) [Hence,] AlS~aEuwdu A certain mountain in Hell, (L, K, MF,) consisting of fire, which the unbeliever will ascend during a period of seventy years, after which he will fall down it, and thus he will do for ever: (MF:) it is of one live coal; the unbeliever will be compelled to ascend it, and will be beaten with maqaAmiE [pl. of miqomaEapN , q. v.]; and whenever he puts his leg upon it, it will dissolve as high as the lower part of his hip, and will then become replaced whole and sound. (L.) ― -b2- [Hence also,] (tropical:) Difficulty, grievousness, distress, affliction, or trouble; (A, L, Msb;) as also ↓ SaEadN (L) and ↓ SaEodaA='u , (K,) or ↓ SuEadaA='u , (L,) and ↓ SuEodudN . (K.) You say, A^arohaqotuhu SaEuwdFA (tropical:) I made him, or constrained him, to do a difficult, grievous, distressing, afflicting, or troublesome, thing: (A:) or I imposed upon him such a punishment. (L.) And ↓ lils~iyaAdapi SaEodaA='u [or ↓ SuEadaA='u ? (see above)] (tropical:) There is a difficult, or distressing, ascent to lordship, or mastery. (A.) And A^akamapN ↓ *aAtu SuEadaA='a (assumed tropical:) A hill difficult to ascend. (L.) ― -b3- Also A she-camel that brings forth a young one imperfectly formed, (As, S, K,) after six or seven months, (As,) and is made to take an affection to the young one of the preceding year, (As, S,) or and takes an affection to the young one of the preceding year: (K:) or a she-camel whose young one dies, and which returns to her former young one, and yields it milk: when she does this, her milk is the sweeter: (Lth:) or a she-camel that brings forth her young one after its hair has grown, and then takes an affection to her former young one, or to the young one of another: pl. SaEaAy^idu and SuEudN ; but this latter pl. is disapproved by Sb. (L.)

definition: High, or elevated, land or ground: or high, or elevated, land or ground, above such as is low, or depressed: or even land or ground: (L:) or even land or ground, without any trees: (Lth, L:) or a [...
sourceDefinition: High, or elevated, land or ground: or high, or elevated, land or ground, above such as is low, or depressed: or even land or ground: (L:) or even land or ground, without any trees: (Lth, L:) or a [ desert such as is termed ] SaHoraA=' : (A:) or the surface of the earth; (Th, Zj, S, A, Msb, K;) whether it be dust or earth, or otherwise: Zj says, I know not any difference of opinion among the lexicologists on this point: (Msb:) [such is said to be its meaning in the Kur iv. 46 and v. 9; and therefore in performing the act termed Alt~ayam~am ,] a man should strike his hands upon the surface of the earth, and not care whether there be in chat place dust or not: (Zj:) [hence] one says, TaAra Siytuka fiY Alqariybi waAlbaEiydi wabalaga munotahaY AlS~aEiydi [ Thy fame has flown through the near and the distant regions, and reached the extremity of the surface of the earth ]: (A:) or SaEiydN signifies the earth, or ground, itself; (IAar, A, L;) as in the saying Ealayoka biAlS~aEiydi , meaning Sit thou upon the earth, or ground: (A:) or good earth or land: or earth, or land, not mixed with sand nor with salt soil: (L:) or dust, or earth, (Fr, S, L, Msb, K,) such as is pure, upon the surface of the ground or that has come forth from within it; thus accord. to Az in the Kur iv. 46 and v. 9, in the opinion of most of the learned: (Msb:) or only earth containing dust; not applied to a coarse, nor to a fine, baToHaA=' ; nor to a coarse kaviyb ; although it be mixed with dust: (Esh-Sháfi'ee, L:) pl. SuEudN and SuEudaAtN , (S, L, K,) the latter a pl. pl. (Msb, TA.) ― -b2- And A wide, or an ample, place. (L.) ― -b3- And A road, (L, Msb, K,) whether wide or narrow: (L:) pls. as above (L, Msb) and SuEodaAnN . (L.) It is said in a trad., A_iy~aAkumo waAlquEuwda biAlS~uEudaAti A_il~aAmano A^ad~aY Haq~ahaA , i. e. Beware ye of sitting in, or by, the roads, save he who performs the duty relating thereto: [respecting which duty see TariyqN :] SuEudaAt is here the pl. of SuEudN , which is pl. of SaEiydN : or, as some say, it is pl. of ↓ SuEodapN , which signifies A court, or an open space, before the door of a house, and the place through which men pass in front of it. (L.) ― -b4- Also A grave. (AA, Mtr, L, K.)

definition: The woman, being taken with the pains of parturition, screamed, or cried out vehemently: (S, O, K:) or threw herself upon her sides, one time thus and another time thus.

sourceDefinition: , (M, K,) inf. n. taSoniyfN , (S, M, O, K,) He assorted it; i. e. made it into, or disposed it in, sorts, or species; (S, O, K;) and separated, or distinguished, its several parts or portions or constituents, one from another: (S, M, O, K:) Alt~aSoniyfu is the separating, or distinguishing, of things, one from another. (Msb.) ― -b2- And hence, (Z, Msb, * TA,) taSoniyfu Alkutubi (Z, TA) or AlkitaAbi : (Msb:) you say, Sn~f AlkitaAba , inf. n. as above, He composed the book. (MA.) -A2- Sn~ft AlEiDaAhu The [ trees called ] EDAh became green: (M:) and Sn~f Al$~ajaru the trees put forth their leaves: (O, K: [and the like is said in the Msb:]) AHn says that this signifies the trees began to leaf, so that they were of two sorts, one sort that had leaved and one sort that had not leaved; but this is not a valid saying; and in like manner ↓ tSn~f : (M:) accord. to the A, both signify the trees became of different sorts; and in like manner Aln~abaAtu [ the plants, or herbage ]: (TA:) and Sn~f Alv~amaru , inf. n. as above, signifies the fruits became so that some of them were ripe exclusively of others, and some of them coloured exclusively of others: (Msb:) and AlA^aroTaY ↓ tSn~f , and Aln~abotu , the [ trees called ] ArTY , and the plants, or herbage, broke forth to leaf. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) 'ObeydAlláh Ibn-Keys-er-Rukeiyát says, saqoyFA liHulowaAna *iY Alkuruwmi wamaA San~afa mino tiynihi wamino Einabiho [ May there be a sending down of rain to Hulwán, the possessor of vines, and of such as have put forth their leaves, of the fig-trees and the grape-vines thereof ]: (O, K:) it is said in the K that the verb in this verse is thus, from Sn~f Al$~ajaru , not from Sn~fhu ; and that J has erred in the reading that he has given; for the reading given by J, who ascribes this verse to Ibn-Ahmar, is Sun~ifa ; but this is the reading of Fr, [as is said in the O,] and both readings are correct; and of the latter, [accord. to which the meaning is, and of such as have been made to consist of various sorts or species, of the fig-trees and the grape-vines thereof, ] MF says, it is that which the case requires, the commendation being for the abundance and variety of the fruits of the trees, rather than for the trees putting forth their leaves. (TA.)
