SayoruwrapN (S, Msb) and SayorN , (S,) He, or it, attained to the state, or condition, of such a thing; (T;) became such a thing; (T, Msb;) in which sense the verb is like kaAna [in meaning, when the latter is non-attributive, and in having its subject in the nom. case and its predicate in the accus.]. (T.) You say, SaAra zayodN rajulFA Zeyd became a man; or attained to the state, or condition, of a man. (TA.) And SaAra zayodN ganiy~FA Zeyd became rich, not having been so. (Msb.) And SaAra AlEaSiyru xamorFA The expressed juice became wine. (Msb.) [And SaAra laA $aYo'a Einodahu He became in a state, or condition, in which there was not anything in his possession. And SaAra yafoEalu ka*aA He became in the state, or condition, of doing such a thing; i. e. he became occupied, or engaged, in doing such a thing; or he set about, began, commenced, took to, or betook himself to, doing such a thing; like jaEala . And SaAra laA yafoEalu $ayoy^FA He became in the state, or condition, of not doing anything; or he became unoccupied in doing anything. And SaAra laA yatakal~amu He became in the state of not speaking; he became speechless. And SaAra yatafak~aru fiY ka*aA He became in a state of reflection upon such a thing; he began to reflect upon such a thing. ] ― -b2- One says also, SaAra AlA^amoru A_ilaY ka*aA , (M, A, Msb, K,) aor. as above, (TA,) inf. n. maSiyrN , (S, M, A, Msb, K,) which is anomalous, being regularly maSaArN , like maEaA$N , (S,) and SayorN and SayoruwrapN , (M, A, K,) i. e. rajaEa A_ilayohi : (Msb:) [but this is a loose explanation; the meaning being, The thing, or affair, or case, came eventually (see SiyrN ) to such a state, or condition: ] the difference between maSiyrN and marojiEN is, that the former word necessarily implies a difference [of the latter state or condition] from the former state or condition; but the latter word does not. (Bd in iii. 156.) [In this case, the ulterior state or condition is likened to a place: for] ― -b3- SaAra also signifies He, or it, attained in respect of place: so in the saying, SaAra zayodN A_ilaY EamorKw [ Zeyd came, or went, or pursued a course that brought him, to 'Amr ]. (TA.) Sirotu A_ilaY fulaAnK [ I came, &c., to such a one ] is similar to the phrase in the Kur [iii. 27] waA_ilaY A@ll~`hi A@lomaSiyru [ And to God, as the ultimate object, is the transition, or course, of every human being]. (S.) [Hence, A^FlaA A_ilaY A@ll~`hi taSiyru A@loA^umuwru , in the Kur xlii. last verse, which Bd explains by adding the words biA@rotifaAEi AlwasaAy^iTi waAlt~aEal~uqaAti ; the meaning being, Verily to God are things, or events, referrible, mediately and dependently: in the Expos. of the Jel expl. as meaning tarojiEu .] ― -b4- [And in like manner one says, SaAra lahu ka*aA Such a thing came to, betided, or befell, him, or it: and hence, he, or it, came to have, or became possessed of, such a thing. ] ― -b5- And SaAra fiY A^aroDi falaApK [ He became, or came to be, meaning he found himself, in a desert, or waterless, land ]; i. q. waqaEa fiyhaA . (Msb in art. wqE .) And SaAra fiY Alr~abiyEi [ He entered, lit. became in, the season called rbyE ]; i. q. A^arobaEa [which is expl. in the S as signifying daxala fiY Alr~abiyEi ]. (K in art. rbE .) -A2- SayorN signifies also The returning of seekers after herbage to the watering-places. (O, K.) And one says, SaAra Alr~ajulu , aor. yaSiyru , [inf. n. SayorN ,] The man stayed, or abode, at the water. (TA.) And SaAra Aln~aAsu AlmaA='a The people stayed, or abode, at the water. (M, K, TA.) -A3- SaArahu , (S,) first pers. Sirotuhu , (M,) aor. as above, (S,) inf. n. SayorN , (K,) a dial. var. of SaArahu having for its aor. yaSuwruhu , [q. v.,] (S,) He cut it; (S, M, K;) and clave it, or split it. definition: He made him, or it, to be in such a state, or condition;
sourceDefinition: He made him, or it, to be in such a state, or condition; or he made him, or it, to be such a thing; [as also ↓ A^aSaArahu ;] syn. jaEalahu . (S.) You say, Say~araniY lahu EabodFA and ↓ A^FSaAraniY [ He made me to be to him a slave ]. (A.) ― -b2- [And Say~arahu A_ilaY ka*aA and ↓ A^aSaArahu He, or it, made, or caused, him, or it, to come, or to pursue a course that led, to such a state, or condition; brought, or reduced, him, or it, thereto. ] 'Omeyleh El-Fezáree said to his paternal uncle Ibn-'Ankà, ↓ maA Al~a*iY A^aSaAraka A_ilaY maA A^araY yaA Eam~i [ What hath made thee to come, or brought thee, or reduced thee, to the state, or condition, that I see, O my paternal uncle? ]. (M.) [In this case, the ulterior state or condition is likened to a place: for] you say, Say~arahu A_ilayohi and ↓ A^aSaArahu [meaning He, or it, made him to come, or brought him, to him, or it; i. e., to a person, or place, or to a state, or condition:] (M, K:) and Say~aratoniY A_ilayohi AlHaAjapu and ↓ A^aSaAratoniY [ Want, or need, or necessity, made me to come, or brought me, to him, or it ]. (A.) And [hence,] Say~ara A_ilayohi AlA^amora He committed to him the thing, or affair; syn. faw~aDahu Alyh . (M in art. fwD .) [And Say~ara lahu ka*aA He made such a thing to come to, betide, or befall, him, or it: and consequently, he made him, or it, to have, or become possessed of, such a thing. ] ― -b3- taSoyiyrN is also by word, or covenant, as well as by deed. (Bd in ii. 20.) [You say, Say~arahu ka*aA meaning He asserted, or pronounced, him, or it, to be in such a state, or condition; or to be such a thing: in which case, also, it is syn. with jaEalahu , whereby it is expl. in the S. And Say~ara lahu ka*aA He asserted, or pronounced, such a thing to belong to him, or it; asserted, or pronounced, him, or it, to have such a thing; attributed to him, or it, such a thing: and appointed or assigned, to him, or it, such a thing. ]

definition: The ulterior or ultimate, latter or last, state, or condition;
sourceDefinition: The ulterior or ultimate, latter or last, state, or condition; the end, conclusion, event, issue, or result; of a thing, an affair, or a case; (S, M, O, Msb, K;) as also ↓ SayorN (O, K) and ↓ maSiyrN (S, O, Msb, TA) and ↓ maSiyrapN (TA) and ↓ Say~uwrN , (S, M, K,) of the measure fayoEuwlN , (S,) and ↓ Say~uwrapN . (K.) ― -b2- The verge, brink, or point, of an affair, or event. (M, K.) You say, A^anaA EalaY SiyrK mino A^amori ka*aA I am on the verge of such an affair, or event. (M.) And A^anaA EalaY SiyrK mino HaAjatiY I am at the point of [attaining] the object of my want. (M.) And A^anaA EalaY SiyrK mino qaDaA='i HaAjatiY I am at the point of accomplishing my want. (A.) And fulaAnN EalaY Siyri A^amorK Such a one is at the point of accomplishing an affair. (S.) -A2- A water at which people stay, or abide; (M, O, K;) as also ↓ SiyrapN . (TA.) -A3- A crevice of a door. (S, M, A, Msb, K.) It is said in a trad., mano naZara fiY Siyri baAbK fafuqiy^ato Eayonuhu fahiYa hadarN [ Whosoever looks into the crevice of a door and has his eye put out, it is a thing for which no mulct is to be exacted ]: (S, M:) A'Obeyd says that this is the only instance in which the word [in this sense] has been heard. (S.) -A4- [The condiment, made of small fish, called ] SiHonaAp : (S, M, K:) or [ a condiment, or the like, ] resembling SHnAp : (M, K:) or what is called in Pers. maAhiY A=waho [ jelly of salted fish ]; as also SiHonaApN : (Mgh voce SHnAp :) and the small salted fish of which SHnAp is made: (Kr, M, K:) or the young ones of fish: [a coll. gen. n.:] n. un. with p : (Msb:) thought by IDrd to be Syriac; (TA;) by IAth, to be Pers., as also SHnAp . (TA in art. SHn .) -A5- Also The A^usofuf~ [properly bishop ] of the Jews. (O, K.) -A6- See also the next paragraph.

definition: Tar: and anything (S, Mgh, Msb, K) of the like kind (Mgh, Msb) with which one daubs or smears or the like;
sourceDefinition: Tar: and anything (S, Mgh, Msb, K) of the like kind (Mgh, Msb) with which one daubs or smears or the like; [i. e. any fluid, semifluid, liniment, unguent, oil, varnish, plaster, or the like, with which a thing is daubed, smeared, rubbed or done over, anointed, painted, varnished, plastered, coated, overspread, or overlaid; ] (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ TulaAwapN , which by rule should be ↓ TulaAyapN , for it is from Talayotu . (TA, in which TulaAyapN is afterwards mentioned as having the same meaning.) ― -b2- And, as being likened thereto, (assumed tropical:) Any thick beverage or wine: (Mgh:) expressed juice of grapes cooked until the quantity of two thirds has gone by evaporation; (S, A, Mgh;) called by the Persians mayobuxotaj [or maYo Puxotah ]; called by the Arabs TilaA=' as being likened to tar: (A, Mgh: *) or thick expressed juice, or wine, cooked until half of it has gone: (K:) in a verse of Ibn-Sukkarah, shortened to ↓ TilFA , for the sake of the metre. (Har p. 302.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) Wine [in an absolute sense] (S, K) is thus called by some of the Arabs, for the purpose of euphemism. (S.) 'Obeyd Ibn-El-Abras said to El-Mundhir when he [the latter] desired to slay him, hiYa Alxamoru tukonaY AlT~ilaA='a kamaA Al*~iy^obu yukonaY A^abaA jEodapa [ It is wine: it is surnamed AlTlA=' like as the wolf is surnamed Abw jEdp ]: i. e. thou pretendest to show honour to me while desiring to slay me; like the wolf, whose acting is not good though his surname is good: (S:) or, as cited by IKt, Eani Alxamori takoniY AlT~ilaA='a : and in the M, haYi Alxamoru yakonuwnahaA biAl`T~ilaA='i [forming a hemistich; the words kamaA Al*~iy^obu Alx , cited above, completing the verse]. (TA.) ― -b4- And (assumed tropical:) The ashes between the three stones upon which the cooking-pot is placed: so called by way of comparison [to tar]. (TA.) ― -b5- And Pure silver. (TA.) ― -b6- And (assumed tropical:) Revilement, or reproach. (K.) -A2- Also The cord with which the leg of the lamb, or kid, is tied (S, K) to a peg, or stake; (S;) and so ↓ TilowN and ↓ TilowapN : (TA:) or the string with which the leg of the kid is tied as long as he is little; (Lh, TA;) and so ↓ TuloyapN and ↓ TaloyapN and ↓ TalFY [or TalFA ]. (TA.)

definition: The edge of the shin: (K:) or the tough edge of the shin: or the external part of the shank: (M, TA:) or the shin-bone: or the edge of the shin-bone: (M, K:) or the tough bone in the fore part of the shank: (S:) but accord.
sourceDefinition: The edge of the shin: (K:) or the tough edge of the shin: or the external part of the shank: (M, TA:) or the shin-bone: or the edge of the shin-bone: (M, K:) or the tough bone in the fore part of the shank: (S:) but accord. to AZ, this term is not used in relation to animals that have A^awoZifap : [see waZiyfN :] (T, TA:) pl. ZanaAbiybu . (S, M, K.) EaAriY AlZ~anaAbiybi Without flesh upon the shins (TA) is an epithet applied to a male ostrich. (S, TA.) qaraEa Zunobuwba AlbaEiyri means He knocked, or struck, the shin of the camel, that he might lie down, and he might mount him: or qaroEu AlZ~unobuwbi signifies a man's knocking, or striking, the shin of his camel with his stick when he makes him lie down that he may mount him, as one in haste to betake himself to a thing: or striking the shin of his beast with his whip, [in the TA is here added lytrqh , which I can only suppose to be put for liyuborikahu , to make him lie down,] when he desires to mount him. (TA.) [See an ex. voce EuroquwbN . Hence,] qaraEa fulaAnN liA^amorihi Zunobuwbahu (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one struck his shin to betake himself to his affair ] means such a one applied himself to his affair with diligence, or energy. (T, L, TA.) Selámeh Ibn-Jendel says, kun~aA A_i*aA maA A^ataAnaA SaArixN faziEN kaAna AlS~uraAxu lahu qaroEa AlZ~anaAbiybi [ We were ( such that ), when there came to us one crying aloud, in terror, the clamour ( returned ) to him was the striking of the shins; ] by which he is said to mean that a quick reply was given; calling the striking of the whip upon the leg of the boot, in urging on the horse, “ the striking of the shin. ” (S.) You also say, qaraEa li*`lika AlA^amori Zunobuwbahu meaning (assumed tropical:) He prepared himself for that affair, or thing: and agreeably with this signification the verse of Selámeh cited above has been explained. (M, TA.) And qaraEa ZanaAbiyba AlA^amori (tropical:) He made, or rendered, the affair manageable. (M, K, TA.) A poet, cited by IAar, says, qaraEotu ZanaAbiyba AlohawaY yawoma EaAlijK (tropical:) I subdued love, or subjected it to my will, on the day of 'Álij;. as though I struck it on the shins; as a camel's shin is struck when one desires him to lie down, that he may mount him. (M, TA.) ― -b2- ZunobuwbN also signifies A nail that is in the jub~ap of a spear-head, [i. e., in the part into which the shaft enters, ] (M, K,) where it is fixed upon the upper extremity of the shaft: and ZanaAbiyb has been said to be the pl. of the word in this sense in the verse of Selámeh cited above. (M, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) inf. n. Eab~N , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) He (a man, Msb) drank water without taking breath: (O, Msb, TA; and T in art. Env : [this is the sense in which it is generally used:]) or he drank water without sipping or sucking in ( mino gayori maS~K ): (S, O:) thus, (S, O, Msb,) in the manner termed Eab~N , (S, O,) i. e. mino gayori maS~K , (Msb,) the pigeon drinks water, like horses and similar beasts; (S, O, Msb;) whereas other birds take it sip after sip: (Msb:) or he drank water at once, without interrupting the swallowing: AA says, the pigeon drinks thus; differing from the other birds; for these drink by little and little: (Mgh:) [in like manner also] Esh-Sháfi'ee says, the pigeon is a bird that drinks in the manner termed Eab~N , and cooes; for it does not drink like other birds, by little and little: (TA:) and it is said in a trad. that the livercomplaint ( AlkubaAd ) is occasioned by drinking in the manner termed Eab~N : (S, O, TA:) or Eab~N signifies [simply] the drinking water: or the gulping, or swallowing down: or the doing so uninterruptedly: (K, TA:) or the drinking water in a single stream, without interruption: (TA:) and the drinking with the mouth from a place, or vessel, containing water, not with the hands nor with a vessel: (K, TA:) you say, Eab~a fiY AlmaA='i , and fiY AlA_inaA='i , he so drank of the water, and from the vessel: and [accord. to some] one says of a bird, Eab~a ; not $ariba : (TA:) [but] Es-Sarakustee says, one does not say of a bird $ariba AlmaA='a , but HasaAhu . (Msb in art. $rb .) ― -b2- yaEub~u fiyhi miyzaAbaAni , in a trad. respecting the HawoD [i. e. Mohammad's pool], as some relate it, means [ Two spouts ] were pouring forth into it with an uninterrupted pouring: but accord. to the relation commonly known, the verb is ygt~ , [i. e. yagut~u in this sense, but yagit~u in another sense, as meaning the making a murmuring sound,] with g and t . definition: The berries ( Hab~ ) of the kaAkanaj or kaAkanoj [thus differently written, from the Pers.
sourceDefinition: The berries ( Hab~ ) of the kaAkanaj or kaAkanoj [thus differently written, from the Pers. kaAkonajo ], (K,) which, accord. to more than one of the leading authorities, is a tree, but is expl. by the author of the K [in its proper art.] as meaning a gum: (TA:) [what is here meant by it is the physalis alkekengi, or common wintercherry: accord. to Forskål (Flora Aegypt. Arab p. cvi.) the name Eubab is applied to the physalis somnifera: and also (pp. cxxi. and cxxii. and 163) to the croton lobatum and croton villosum: ] or it is applied by the physicians to the [ plant itself called ] kAknj : (O:) or i. q. Einabu Alv~aEolabi ; (IAar, O, K;) which is said by Ibn-Habeeb to be an incorrect appellation, (O, TA,) being correctly Eubab , but AM denies that the former is incorrect: (TA:) or i. q. raA='N ; (K;) i. e. the tree called raA=' : (TA:) or a tree, or plant, ( $ajarapN ,) of the [ kind called ] A^agolaAv : (K:) AHn says, on the authority of Aboo-Ziyád, it is of the A^agolaAv , and is a tree, or plant, ( $ajarapN ,) resembling the Haromal [ peganum harmala of Linn.], except that it is taller, coming forth in the form of strings, and having pods ( sinafap ) like those of the Haromal , and sometimes the goats nibble from its leaves and from its pods when they dry up; it has also berries, intensely red, like beads of carnelian, smaller than the nabiq [or fruit of the lote tree ], and larger than the grape; and people seek out the leaves thereof that have not been rendered foraminous, which leaves are then bruised, and used beneficially as a dressing for maladies attended with pain: the people assert that the jinn, or genii, perforate them in envy of mankind. (O.)

definition: A certain food, (K,) or sort of food, (TA,) and a beverage, (K, TA,) obtained (TA) from the [ species of mimosa called ] EurofuT , of sweet flavour: (K, TA:) or the exudation [or matter exuded in the form of drops ] of gum;
sourceDefinition: A certain food, (K,) or sort of food, (TA,) and a beverage, (K, TA,) obtained (TA) from the [ species of mimosa called ] EurofuT , of sweet flavour: (K, TA:) or the exudation [or matter exuded in the form of drops ] of gum; ( Erqu AlS~amogi ; [written in the TA without any syll. signs; in the CK Eiroqu AlS~amogi , and so in my MS. copy of the K; but in the latter, the former word has been altered, app. from Earaqu , which is evidently the right reading;]) it is of sweet flavour, and is beaten with [ the implement called ] a mijodaH until it becomes thoroughly fit for use ( Hat~aY yanoDaja ), [app., from what here follows, over a fire, ] and is then drunk: (TA:) or what drops, or distils, of the exudations ( magaAfiyr ) of the EurofuT : or Eabiybapu All~avaY , accord. to ISk, is the infusion ( gusaAlap ) of lavFY ; (S, TA;) lavFY being a substance which the [ plant called ] vumaAm exudes, of sweet flavour; what falls thereof upon the ground is taken, and put into a garment, or piece of cloth, and water is poured upon it, and when it flows from the garment, or piece of cloth, it is drunk, in a sweet state, and sometimes it is made thick; (S;) or lavFY is a substance which the vumaAm exudes, sweet like naATif [q. v.]; and when any of it flows upon the ground, it is taken, and put into a vessel, or sometimes it is poured upon water, and then drunk, in a sweet state, and sometimes it is made thick: (TA:) [or Eabiybapu All~avaY is a decoction of the matter exuded by a species of vumaAm ; for] AM says, I have seen, in the desert, a species of vumaAm that exudes a sweet gum, which is gathered from its shoots, and eaten, and is called lavaY Alv~umaAmi : when it has remained for some time, it is found scattered at the foot of the vumaAm , and is taken with its dust, and put into a garment, or piece of cloth, and cleansed by water poured upon it; then it is boiled over a fire until it thickens; when it is eaten: what flows from it [or the fluid part of it] is called EabiybapN : and taEab~abotu EabiybapF means “ I drank Eabiybap . ” (L, TA.) It is stated in a marginal note in the L, that A'Obeyd [is related to have] said that Eabiybap is “ milk such as is termed raAy^ib : ” but AM observes that this is a disgraceful mistake, and that A'Obeyd is related on the authority of Sh to have assigned this meaning to gabiybapN . (TA.) ― -b2- Also The [ shrub called ] rimov , (K, TA,) on which camels feed, (TA,) when it is in a depressed tract of land. (K, TA.)

(S, TA;) lavFY being a substance which the [ plant called ] vumaAm exudes, of sweet flavour; what falls thereof upon the ground is taken, and put into a garment, or piece of cloth, and water is poured upon it, and when it flows from the garment, or piece of cloth, it is drunk, in a sweet state, and sometimes it is made thick; (S;) or lavFY is a substance which the vumaAm exudes, sweet like naATif [q. v.]; and when any of it flows upon the ground, it is taken, and put into a vessel, or sometimes it is poured upon water, and then drunk, in a sweet state, and sometimes it is made thick: (TA:) [or Eabiybapu All~avaY is a decoction of the matter exuded by a species of vumaAm ; for] AM says, I have seen, in the desert, a species of vumaAm that exudes a sweet gum, which is gathered from its shoots, and eaten, and is called lavaY Alv~umaAmi : when it has remained for some time, it is found scattered at the foot of the vumaAm , and is taken with its dust, and put into a garment, or piece of cloth, and cleansed by water poured upon it; then it is boiled over a fire until it thickens; when it is eaten: what flows from it [or the fluid part of it] is called EabiybapN : and taEab~abotu EabiybapF means “ I drank Eabiybap . ” (L, TA.) It is stated in a marginal note in the L, that A'Obeyd [is related to have] said that Eabiybap is “ milk such as is termed raAy^ib : ” but AM observes that this is a disgraceful mistake, and that A'Obeyd is related on the authority of Sh to have assigned this meaning to gabiybapN . (TA.) ― -b2- Also The [ shrub called ] rimov , (K, TA,) on which camels feed, (TA,) when it is in a depressed tract of land. (K, TA.)

EajabN ; (Msb, TA;) and mnh ↓ tEj~b , and ↓ AstEjb mnh , (S, O, Msb, K,) which two are syn. each with the other, (S, O, K,) and with the first also; (S, K;) all signify He wondered at it; i. e. he deemed it strange, extraordinary, or improbable, said of a thing occurring, or presenting itself, to him; (K, TA;) on account of his being little accustomed to it: (TA:) or the first signifies [as above, i. e.] he deemed it strange, extraordinary, or improbable: and ↓ taEaj~ubN is of two kinds; one is [the wondering ] at a thing which one commends, and it means the accounting (a thing) good or goodly, or approving [it], and expressing one's approval of a thing; and the other is at a thing that one dislikes, and it means the deeming [a thing] strange, extraordinary, or improbable, and discommending [it]: (Msb:) or, accord. to some of the grammarians, it signifies the mind's becoming affected, or acted upon, by some excessive quality in the thing by which it is so affected; [so that it may be rendered the becoming affected with wonder; ] as when one says maA A^a$ojaEahu [“ how courageous is he! ”] and A^asomiEo bihimo waA^aboSiro [“ how clearly shall they hear! and how clearly shall they see! ”]: (Msb, MF, TA:) or it is [the wondering ] at a thing of which the cause, or reason, is hidden, and not known: or it is when one sees a thing that pleases him, and thinks that he has not seen the like of it: (L, TA:) [therefore taEaj~aba minohu may be rendered he wondered at it, and he admired it: ] accord. to some, it peculiarly relates to what is deemed good or goodly, or approved; [though this is inconsistent with the application of the grammatical term fiEolu Alt~aEaj~ubi the verb of wonder; ] and the subst. derived from it is ↓ EajobN : and ↓ AstEjb relates to what is good or goodly or approved, and to what is otherwise; and the subst. is ↓ EajabN [which is also the inf. n. of Eajiba ]: or accord. to the A and L, ↓ AstEjb signifies he wondered at a thing intensely; or became affected with intense wonder. ”] and A^asomiEo bihimo waA^aboSiro [“ how clearly shall they hear! and how clearly shall they see! ”]: (Msb, MF, TA:) or it is [the wondering ] at a thing of which the cause, or reason, is hidden, and not known: or it is when one sees a thing that pleases him, and thinks that he has not seen the like of it: (L, TA:) [therefore taEaj~aba minohu may be rendered he wondered at it, and he admired it: ] accord. to some, it peculiarly relates to what is deemed good or goodly, or approved; [though this is inconsistent with the application of the grammatical term fiEolu Alt~aEaj~ubi the verb of wonder; ] and the subst. derived from it is ↓ EajobN : and ↓ AstEjb relates to what is good or goodly or approved, and to what is otherwise; and the subst. is ↓ EajabN [which is also the inf. n. of Eajiba ]: or accord. to the A and L, ↓ AstEjb signifies he wondered at a thing intensely; or became affected with intense wonder. (TA.) ― -b2- [ EajabFA lih`*aA , a phrase of common occurrence, (mentioned in the K voce wayobN , &c.,) is for A^aEojabu EajabFA lih`*aA I wonder greatly, lit. with wondering, at this. See also an ex. voce EajabN , last sentence but two.] ― -b3- Of the words in the Kur xxxvii. 12, there are two readings, balo Eajibota wayasoxaruwna and bl Eajibotu wysxrwn : accord. to the former, the meaning is, Nay, thou wonderest at their conduct, or deemest it extraordinary, [O Mohammad,] and they mock: respecting the latter reading, [which may be rendered Nay, I wonder, &c.,] it is observed that EajabN when attributed to God has a meaning different from that which it has when attributed to men: IAth says that, when attributed to God, it is used in a tropical manner, as the causes of things are not hidden from Him: or, accord. to IAmb, the verb here meams I have recompensed them for their wondering at the truth, or their deeming it strange or improbable: and in like manner it is said [in the Kur viii. 30], yamokuruwna wayamokuru A@ll~`hu [lit. “ They plot and God plotteth ”], meaning, “ God recompenseth them for their plotting. ” (L, TA.) ― -b4- It is also said that EajabN when attributed to God [sometimes] means The being well pleased, content, or satisfied. (K, TA.) The saying, in a trad., Eajiba rab~uka mino qawomK yuqaAduwna A_ilaY Aljan~ap fiY Als~alaAsili means Thy Lord wonders at a people who will be led to Paradise in chains [because of their deeming themselves unworthy thereof]; the verb Ejb being here used in a tropical sense: or the meaning is, thy Lord is well pleased with, and will reward, a people &c.: and there are other trads. of the same kind. (L, TA.) ― -b5- Eajiba A_ilayohi means He loved, or liked, him, or it. (L, TA.) [See a verse cited voce EajiybN ; from which it seems to signify lit. He, or it, was an object of love to him. ] -A2- Eajibato , inf. n. EajabN ; and Eajubato ; said of a she-camel, She was, or became, such as is termed EajobaA=' (TA.)

definition: It (a thing, or an affair, or event, TA) induced, or excited, him to wonder.
sourceDefinition: It (a thing, or an affair, or event, TA) induced, or excited, him to wonder. (K, TA. [See also 2.]) In the following saying of Ibn- Keys-er-Rukeiyát, raA^ato fiY Alr~aA^osi min~iY $ayobapF lasotu A^ugay~ibuhaA faqaAlato liY A@bonu qayosK *aA wabaEoDu Al$~ayobi yuEojibuhaA the meaning is, [ She saw upon my head some hoariness, which I did not hide; and she said to me, “ Is this Ibn-Keys? ” somewhat of hoariness ] causing her to have wonder. (TA.) ― -b2- And It (a thing, or an affair, or event, TA) induced in him wonder, or admiration, and pleasure, or joy: (K:) or it excited his admiration, or approval: (Msb:) or it pleased, or rejoiced, him. (TA.) You say, A^aEojabaniY h`*aA Al$~aYo'u liHusonihi [ This thing has excited my admiration, or approval, or has pleased me, for its goodness, or goodliness, or beauty ]. (S, O.) And A^aEojabaniY Husonuhu [ Its goodness, or goodliness, or beauty, excited my admiration, &c.]. (Msb.) ― -b3- And A^uEojiba bihi He was excited to wonder, or admiration, and pleasure, or joy, by it; he admired it, and was pleased with it, or rejoiced by it. (K.) You say, A^uEojiba binafosihi , (S, O, Msb,) inf. n. A_iEojaAbN , [which is often used as syn. with EujobN , the corresponding subst.,] (O,) [ He admired himself, (lit. was excited to admiration by himself, ) was pleased with himself, or was self-conceited, or vain; or] he exalted, and magnified, himself; was haughty, and proud. (Msb.) ― -b4- [ maA A^aEojabahu generally signifies How wonderful is it! ] ― -b5- maA A^aEojabahu biraA^oyihi [ How greatly does he admire his opinion or judgment! or how greatly is he pleased with it! or how conceited, or vain, or proud, is he of it! ] is anomalous [in two respects], (S, O, K,) not to be taken as an example to be imitated; (S, O;) for the verb here is formed from a passive [and augmented] verb [ A^uEojiba ], like as is the case in maA A^a$ogalahu ; whereas it is the primary rule with respect to the verb of wonder that it shall not be formed from any but an active [and unaugmented] verb. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: : see EajabN , in two places: -A2- and see also EujobN . -A3- Also The root, or base, of the tail: (S, O, K:) or the part of the root, or base, of the tail, of any beast, which the haunch encloses, (Msb, TA,) and which is inserted in the hinder part of the rump: (TA:) or the root, or base, and bone, of the tail: (Lh, TA:) also called the EuSoEuS [q. v.]: (Msb, TA:) or it is the head of the EuSoEuS : (TA:) or the upper part of the EuSoEuS : or the external extremity of the spine; and the EuSoEuS is its internal extremity: (Az, L voce quHoquHN :) it is said in a trad., that every part of a man will become consumed, except the Eajob , (TA,) or the Eajob of the tail, (O, TA,) accord. to different relations; (TA;) from which [as a rudiment] he was created, and upon which he will [at the resurrection] be put together: (O:) i. e. the bone at the lower, or lowest, part of the spine, at the rump; which is the Easiyb of beasts: it is said to be like a grain of mustard-seed: or, as Z says in the “ Fáïk, ” it is the bone that is between the buttocks: it is also pronounced ↓ EujobN ; and accord. to MF, ↓ EijobN , but no one else says this: and, as El-Khafájee says, it is also called EajomN and EujomN and EijomN , in this case with the three vowel-sounds. (TA.) ― -b2- Also (tropical:) The hinder part (S, O, K, TA) of a tract of sand, (S, O,) or of anything: (K, TA:) and hence, Eajobu kaviybK i. e. the thin hinder portion [ of a sand-hill, or of an extended and gibbous sand-hill, or of a collection of sand that has poured down ]: (TA:) pl. EujuwbN , (S, O,) and perhaps A^aEojaAbN also in the former sense [and therefore in this likewise]. (TA.)

definition: [originally an int.
sourceDefinition: [originally an int. n.] (S, O, K) and ↓ EujobN , (accord. to the K,) or ↓ EajobN , (accord. to the TA,) Wonder; i. e. a deeming strange, extraordinary, or improbable, what occurs, or presents itself, to one, (K, TA,) on account of being little accustomed to it; (TA;) or [the effect, upon the mind, of ] the consideration of a thing with which one is not familiar, and to which one is not accustomed: (IAar, TA:) for a distinction between EajabN and ↓ EajobN , see 1, in the middle of the paragraph: the pl. of EajabN [in this sense] is [said to be] A^aEojaAbN ; (K;) or it has no pl.: (S, O, K:) [this statement correctly applies to EajabN as an epithet; for as such it is app. used as sing. and pl., being originally an inf. n.:] but El-'Ajjáj has pluralized it, [regarding it in the sense expl. above,] saying, *akarona A^a$ojaAbFA limano ta$aj~abaA wahijona A^aEojaAbFA limano taEaj~abaA [ They mentioned griefs to him who grieved, and they excited wonder to him who wondered ]. (O.) yaA laloEajabi [may be rendered O case of wonder! but properly] means O wonder come, for this is thy time: and yaA liloEajabi [may also be rendered O case of wonder! but properly] means O [people, or the like, come] to wonder; the noun signifying the invoked being suppressed. (Har p. 27.) -A2- It is also an epithet applied to a thing, an affair, an event, or a case; one says A^amorN EajabN [ A wonderful thing or affair &c.]; and so ↓ EajiybN [which is more common in this sense], and ↓ EujaAbN , and ↓ Euj~aAbN : or ↓ EajiybN is syn. with EajabN ; but ↓ EujaAbN signifies more than EajabN : (K:) or ↓ EujaAbN is syn. with ↓ EajiybN , (S, O,) which signifies a thing, (S, O, Msb,) or an affair, or event, or a case, (S, O,) wondered at; (S, O, Msb, TA;) or inducing wonder, or admiration, and pleasure, or joy; or pleasing, or rejoicing; syn. ↓ muEojibN ; (TA;) and ↓ Euj~aAbN ; signifies more than EajabN : (S, O, TA:) [it is said that] EajabN has no pl.; [app. meaning when it is used as an epithet, as observed above;] nor has ↓ EajiybN ; (S, O, K;) or the pl. of this is EajaAy^ibu [respecting which see EajiybapN ]; (S, O, K;) like as A^afaAy^ilu is pl. of A^afiylN ; and tabaAy^iEu , of tabiyEN . (S, O.) [Being originally an inf. n., it is used alike as masc. and fem.:] one says qiS~apN EajabN [meaning A wonderful story: and for the same reason, it may, as an epithet, be also used alike as sing. and pl.: like EadolN &c.]. (O.) ― -b2- [It is also used as a subst. in a pl. sense, signifying Wonders, as meaning wonderful things; like the pl. EajaAy^ibu , &c.; and it may be similarly used in a sing. sense for $aYo'N EajabN or A^amorN EajabN : but when used as a subst. in the pl. sense expl. above, it seems to be regarded by some as a coll. gen. n., of which ↓ EajabapN is the n. un.; for] one says, maA fulaAnN A_il~aA EajabapN mina AlEajabi [ Such a one is none other than a wonder of wonders ]. (A, TA.) [Hence, also,] A^abuw AlEajabi [lit. The father of wonders ] is a surname of Fortune. (TA.) And it signifies also The practiser of legerdemain, or sleight-of-hand; syn. Al$~aEowa*iY~u , (A, TA,) or Almu$aEowi*u : (Eth-Tha'álibee, TA in $E* :) and any one who does wonderful things. (A, TA.) Prov. ii. 112, where another reading is mentioned, which, by what he says, is shown to be A^aEoraDota Alqirofapa Thou hast made suspicion wide. ] In another prov. it is said, vawobu Almalobasi ↓ A^aEoraDa (IAar, A, TA, and K in art. lbs ,) and Almilobasi and Almulobisi (IAar, and K in art. lbs ,) and Almulotabisi (TA in art. lbs ) i. e. (TA in that art.) [See, again, Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 100, where it is said that A^aEoraDa vawobu Almulobisi app. means The garment of the suspected appeared, or has appeared: but that another reading is EaruDa , meaning became, or has become, wide. ] -A2- EaraDa , aor. , (Fr, S, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. EaroDN ; (TA:) and EariDa , (As, TS, K,) aor. , (Fr, K,) or , like Hasiba , aor. , deviating from the general rule; (As, TS;) It (a thing) appeared, or became apparent, lahu to him; (S, O, Msb, K; [but in some copies of the K, instead of the explanation Zahara wabadaA , we find Zahara Ealayohi wabadaA , which is a mistake;]) as also ↓ AErD , (Fr, S, O, Msb, K,) which is a deviation from a general rule, being quasi pass. of EaraDahu , which see below; (S, * O, * Msb, K;) [lit.] it showed its breadth, or width. (O, * TA.) You say, laka Al$~aYo'u ↓ AErD mino baEiydK The thing appeared to thee from afar. (TA.) And EaraDato lahu Alguwlu , and EariDato , (AZ, S, O, K,) The ghool appeared to him. (K.) The Arabs say, of a thing, EaraDa and ↓ AErD and ↓ tEr~D and ↓ AEtrD , using these verbs as syn.; (Sh;) [app. as meaning It showed, presented, or offered, itself, (lit. its breadth, or width, or its side, see 5,) to a person: the first and last also often signify, and the others sometimes, he obtruded himself in an affair; interfered therein:] IKt disallows ↓ AErD in the sense of AEtrD , as not having been found by him: (TA:) [but] an instance of the former of these two verbs used in the sense of the latter of them occurs in the phrase liln~aAZiriyna ↓ A_i*aA A^uEoraDato [app. meaning When she shows, or presents, herself to the lookers ], in a poem by one of the tribe of Teiyi. (Sh.) ― -b2- EaraDa laka Alxayoru , [in one place in the TA Alxabara , and Alxbr in a copy of the Msb,] inf. n. EaroDN ; (TA; [in one place in the TA EuruwDN there referring to Alxabaru , which is app. a mistranscription;]) and ↓ AErD ; (S, O, K, TA;) Good [i. e. the doing of good ] hath become within thy power, or practicable to thee, or easy to thee. (S, O, K, TA.) And laka AlZ~aboYu ↓ AErD The gazelle hath exposed to thee its side; (TA;) or hath put its side in thy power, (S, O, K, TA,) by turning it towards thee: (O, TA:) said to incite one to shoot it, or cast at it. (S, O.) Or laka ↓ AErD , said of an animal of the chase, or other thing, signifies It hath put in thy power, [or exposed to thee, ] its breadth, or width: (A:) or lahu ↓ AErD signifies it (a thing) became within his power, or practicable to him, or easy to him; lit., it showed its side [ to him ]. (Mgh.) [In the TA, I find A^aEoraDa fiY Al$~aYo'i expl. as signifying He had the width of the thing in his power: but fY , here, seems to be a mistake for lahu .] A poet, also, says ↓ A^aEoriDiY addressing a woman; meaning A^amokiniY [ Empower thou; i. e. grant thou access ]. (S.) ― -b3- EaraDa lahu , aor. ; (As, S, K, TA;) and EariDa , aor. ; (TA;) are also said of an event, (As, TA,) or of a disease, and the like, (S, K, TA,) such as disquietude of mind, and a state of distraction of the mind or attention; (TA;) [meaning It happened to him; it befell him; it occurred to him; was incident to him; ] and also of doubt, and the like. (TA.) [So, too, is ↓ AEtrD .] You also say, EaraDahu EaAriDN mina AlHum~aY wanaHowihaA [ An occurrence of fever, and the like, happened to him, or befell him ]. (S.) And Albadana ↓ AEtrD [ It befell the body ] is said of [a disease, as, for instance,] the mange, or scab. (B, in TA in art. Er .) ― -b4- EaraDa lahu , aor. ; (Msb, TA;) and EariDa lh , aor, ; (Msb;) He intervened as an obstacle to him, preventing him from attaining his desire, (Msb, TA, *) or from seeking to attain his desire, and from going his way; (TA;) as also lh ↓ AEtrD . (Msb.) You say also, EaraDa lahu A^a$ad~a AlEaroDi , and ↓ AEtrD , He opposed himself to him ( qaAbalahu binafosihi ) with the most vehement opposition of himself. (TA.) See also 5, second sentence. One should not say, Er~Dtu lahu , with teshdeed, in the sense of AiEotaraDotu . (Msb.) You also say, EaraDa EaAriDN , meaning [ An obstacle intervened, or prevented; lit.] an intervening thing intervened; a preventing thing prevented. (TA.) And sirotu faEaraDa liY fiY AlT~ariyqi EaAriDN mino jabalK wanaHowihi I journeyed, and there opposed itself to me, so as to prevent my going on, an obstacle consisting in a mountain, and the like; as also ↓ AEtrD : whence the AiEotiraADaAt [or objections ] of the lawyers; because they prevent one's laying hold upon the evidence. (Msb.) And EaraDa lahu Al$~aYo'u fiY AlT~ariyqi The thing intervened as an obstacle to him in the way, preventing him from going on. (TA.) And EaraDa Al$~aYo'u The thing stood up and prevented; [or stood in the way, or presented itself as an obstacle; or opposed itself; ] as also ↓ AEtrD . (TA.) [And The thing lay, or extended, breadthwise, or across, or athwart; like AEtrD , q. v.] And Al$~aYo'u duwna Al$~aYo'i ↓ AEtrD The thing intervened as an obstacle in the way to the thing; syn. HaAla . (S, O.) ― -b5- maA EaraDotu lahu bisuwo'K , aor. ; and mA EariDotu , aor. ; signify mA taEar~aDotu : see 5: or, as some say, I did not, or have not, become exposed to his reviling, or evilspeaking, by reviling, or speaking evil, of him. (Msb.) [See also EaraDa EiroDahu , below.] ― -b6- EaraDa lahu also signifies He went towards him; (TA in art. nHw ;) and EaraDa EaroDahu and EuroDahu [the same, i. e.] naHaA naHowahu ; (K;) as also ErDh ↓ AEtrD (TA.) ― -b7- In the saying of El-Kumeyt, faA^aboligo yaziyda A_ino EaraDota wamuno*irFA he means [ And convey thou to Yezeed, ] if thou pass by him, [ and to Mundhir: or perhaps, if thou go to him: or if thou present thyself to him.] (S.) ― -b8- EaraDa Alfarasu , (L, K,) aor. , inf. n. EaroDN , (L, TA,) The horse went along inclining towards one side: (K, TA:) or ran inclining his breast and head: (L, TA:) and ran inclining his head and neck; (K; [in which only the inf. n. of the verb in this last sense is mentioned;]) the doing of which is approved in horses, but disapproved in camels. (TA.) [See also 3, and 5.] ― -b9- EaraDa AlbaEiyru , (K,) inf. n. EaroDN , (TA,) The camel ate of the A^aEoraAD , i. e. of the upper parts of the trees [or shrubs ]. (K.) ― -b10- EaraDato , said of a she-camel, A fracture, (S, O, K,) or some injurious accident, (S, O,) befell her; (S, O, K;) as also EariDato ; (O, K;) but the former is the more approved: (TA:) and EaraDa lahaA a disease, or a fracture, befell her. (TA, from a trad.) Also, said of a sheep, or goat, ( $Ap ,) It died by disease. (K.) And EariDa Al$~aA='u The sheep, or goats, burst, or became rent, from abundance of herbage. (K.) And EaraDa , (IKtt,) inf. n. EaroDN , (K,) He (an animal, IKtt, or a man, K, [but it is said in the TA that there is no reason for this restriction,]) died without disease. (IKtt, K.) ― -b11- EaraDa bisiloEatihi i. q. EaAraDa bihaA . (K.) See 3, in two places. [And under the same, see a similar phrase.] ― -b12- EaraDa He (a man, S, O) came to AlEaruwD , i. e. Mekkeh and El-Medeeneh, (S, O, K, TA,) and El-Yemen, (TA,) and what is around them. (S, O, K, TA.) -A3- EaraDa Al$~aYo'a , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. EaroDN , (Msb,) He made the thing apparent; showed it; exhibited it; manifested it; exposed it to view; presented it; (S, O, Msb, K;) unfolded it; laid it open: and also he mentioned it: (Msb:) [lit. he showed its breadth, or width, or its side: and hence it also signifies he made the thing to stand as an obstacle, duwna $aYo'K in the way to, or of, a thing. ] You say, EaraDa lahu Al$~aYo'a He made apparent, showed, exhibited, manifested, or exposed to view, to him the thing; (S, O, K;) unfolded it, or laid it open, to him. (S, TA.) And EaraDa Ealayohi A^amora ka*aA (S, O, K *) He showed, propounded, or proposed, to him, such a thing, or such a case: (K, * TA:) [and he asked, or required, of him, with gentleness, the doing of such a thing; for] AlEaroDu signifies TalabN biliynK , (Mughnee and K, voce A^alaA ,) or TalabN biliynK wataA^ad~ubK . (Mughnee voce lawolaA .) And EaraDotu AlmataAEa lilobayoEi [ I showed, exposed, presented, or offered, the commodity for sale; or] I showed the commodity to those desirous of purchasing it. (Msb.) The phrase EaraDa Ealayohi AlmataAEa [ He showed, or offered, to him the commodity ] is used because the person shows to the other the length and breadth of the thing ( Tuwlahu waEaroDahu ), or because he shows him one of its sides ( EuroDFA mino A^aEoraADihi ). (Mgh.) [Hence,] it is said in a trad. of Hodheyfeh, tuEoraDu Alfitanu EalaY Alquluwbi EaroDa AlHaSiyri , which means, accord. to some, that fitan [ Temptations, &c.,] will be [ displayed and ] embellished to the hearts of men like [ as ] the ornamented and variegated garment called HSyr [ is displayed and embellished ]: (B, TA in art. HSr :) or the meaning is, that they will be laid and spread upon the hearts like the HSyr : (IAth, TA in the present art.:) and some say that by this last word is here meant a certain vein extending across upon the side of a beast, towards the belly. (TA in art. HSr .) [Hence also,] EaroDN saAbiriY~N [ A slight exhibition: (see art. sbr :)] so in the proverbs by A'Obeyd, in the handwriting of Ibn-El-Jawáleekee: (TA:) or EaroDu saAbiriY~K : (TA, and so in a copy of the S in this art.:) or EaroDa saAbiriY~K . (O, TA, and so in a copy of the S in this art.) With this agrees in meaning the saying EaraDa EalaY~a sawoma EaAl~apK [ He offered to me in the manner of offering water to camels taking a second draught: see also arts. swm and El ; and see Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 84]. (TA.) You say also, EaraDotu AljaAriyapa EalaY AlbayoEi [ I showed, or displayed, or exposed, or offered, the girl for sale ]: (S, O, TA:) and in like manner AlmataAEa [ the commodity ]. (TA.) And EaraDotu lahu vawobFA makaAna Haq~ihi ; (S, O;) and EaraDotu lahu mino Haq~ihi vawobFA , (S, O, K,) or mataAEFA , (TA,) this meaning, [as also the former phrase,] I gave to him a garment, or piece of cloth, [or a commodity, ] in place of his due: (S, O, K:) and in like manner, ErDt bihi . (El-Umawee, TA.) And EaraDotu AlbaEiyra EalaY AlHawoDi , which is an instance of inversion, meaning EaraDotu AlHawoDa EalaY AlbaEiyri [ I showed the watering-trough to the camel ]: (S, O, Msb:) [or it agrees in meaning with the phrase] EaraDa Aln~aAqapa EalaY AlHawoDi , and ↓ A^aEoraDahaA , [as rendered] He offered to the she-camel to drink [ at the wateringtrough ]. (L, TA.) And EaraDahumo EalaY Als~ayofi [lit. He exposed them to the sword; (see also 2;) meaning] he slew them (S, A, O, Msb, K) with the sword. (Msb.) And EaraDahumo EalaY Als~awoTi He beat them with the whip; he flogged them. (K, * TA.) And EaraDahumo EalaY Aln~aAri He burned them. (A, TA.) And EaraDotu AlEasala EalaY Aln~aAri I cooked the honey [ upon the fire ] to separate it from the wax. (Msb.) [And EaraDa nafosahu lilohalaAki He exposed himself to destruction. ] ― -b2- EaroDN also signifies The bringing a man before a judge, and accusing him. (IAar, in TA, art. Eqb .) [And The presenting, or addressing, a petition, &c., with EalaY or li before the word signifying the person to whom it is presented or addressed.] ― -b3- One says also, maA yaEoriDuka lifulaAnK , (S, [so in two copies,] and O,) or maA yaEoruDaka , (L, TA,) with fet-h to the Y and damm to the r , (L,) the verb being coordinate to naSara : (TA:) [app. meaning What causeth thee to present thyself to such a one? ]: Yaakoob disallows one's saying ↓ maA yuEar~iDuka lifulaAnK , with teshdeed. (S, O, TA.) [But the latter of these two verbs has a signification nearly allied to that which is here assigned to the former, and exactly agreeing with one mentioned before. See 2.] ― -b4- EaraDa Aljunoda , (S, Msb,) and EaraDa Aljunoda EaroDa AlEayoni , (S, O,) or EaroDa EayonK , (A, K, B, except that in the A and B we find Aljayo$a instead of Aljnd ,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. EaroDN , (Yoo, S,) He made the army, or body of soldiers, to pass by him, and examined their state, (S, O, K,) what it was: (S, O:) [i. e. he reviewed them: ] or he made them to pass before him in review, that he might know who was absent and who was present: (A, B:) or he caused them to come forth, and examined them, that he might know them: (Msb:) and you say also, ↓ AEtrDhumo , (S, O, K,) meaning [the same, or] he made them to pass by him, or before him, and examined them, one by one, (K, TA,) to see who were absent from those who were present. (TA.) You say also, ↓ AEtrD AlmataAEa wanaHowahu and EalaY Eayonihi ↓ AEtrDhu [ He examined the commodity, and the like thereof, having it displayed before his eye ]. (Th.) [See also EaroDN .] ― -b5- EaraDotu AlkitaAba , (S, O, Msb,) aor. , inf. n. EaroDN , (Msb,) I read, or recited, the writing, or book: (O, TA: [in the S it is unexplained, but immediately followed by EaraDotu Aljunoda EaroDa AlEayoni :]) or I recited it by heart, or memory. (Msb.) -A4- EaraDa EiroDahu , aor. ; (TA;) and ↓ AEtrDhu ; (A, TA;) [perhaps originally signified He examined his grounds of pretension to respect, or the like: and then became used to express a frequent consequence of doing so; i. e.] he spoke evil of him; reviled him; detracted from his reputation: (A, TA:) or he corresponded to him, or equalled him, in grounds of pretension to respect: (TA:) [the former seems to be the more probable of the two meanings; for it is said that] fulaAnFA ↓ AEtrD signifies he spoke evil of such a one; reviled him; detracted from his reputation; (Lth, S, O, K;) and annoyed him. (Lth, TA.) -A5- EaraDa Al$~aYo'a , (K,) aor. , inf. n. EaroDN , (TA,) He hit the side ( EuroD ) of the thing. (K.) -A6- EaraDa AlEuwda EalaY AlA_inaA='i , (S, O, Msb, K,) and Als~ayofa EalaY faxi*ihi , (S, O, K,) aor. and , (S, O, Msb, K,) in both phrases, (O, K,) [J says, in the S, app. referring, not, as SM thinks, to the latter of the two phrases, but to the meaning, “ this, only, with damm, ”] He put the stick breadthwise, across, athwart, or crosswise, ( maEoruwDFA , TA, or biAlEaroDi , Msb, TA, both meaning the same, TA,) upon the vessel, (Msb, TA,) [and so the sword upon his thigh: and ↓ Er~Dhu signifies the same.] ― -b2- EaraDa Alr~umoHa , aor. , [and probably also,] inf. n. EaroDN ; and ↓ Er~Dhu , inf. n. taEoriyDN ; (TA:) He turned, or placed, the spear sideways; contr. of sad~adahu . (S, in art. sd , relating to the former verb; and L, in the same art., relating to the latter verb.) ― -b3- EaraDa Alr~aAmiY Alqawosa , inf. n. EaroDN , The archer laid the bow upon its side on the ground, and then shot with it. (TA.) ― -b4- The saying of Aboo-Kebeer El-Hudhalee, cited, but not expl., by Th, faEaraDotuhu fiY saAqi A^asomanihaA is thought by ISd to mean And I made its (the sword's) breadth to become concealed in the thigh of the fattest of them. (TA.) -A7- EaraDahu He fed him: (Fr, TA:) [or he offered, or presented, to him food: for] EuriDuwA signifies They were fed: and they had food offered, or presented, to them. (L, TA.) [See also 2, in the last quarter.] ― -b2- EaraDa AlHawoDa and Alqirobapa He filled the wateringtrough and the water-skin. (K.) -A8- EaraDa Al$~awoka : see 8, near the end. -A9- EaraDa baEiyrahu , inf. n. EaroDN , He branded his camel with the mark called EiraAD ; (S;) and so ↓ Er~Dhu : (S, TA:) and EuriDa AlbaEiyru , inf. n. as above, The camel was branded with that mark. (K.) -A10- EaraDotuhu , (K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. EaroDN , (K, TA,) I defrauded, or deceived, him in selling. (K.) -A11- EuriDa , (K,) or EuriDa lahu , (A, TA,) inf. n. EaroDN , (K,) He was, or became, mad, or insane, or possessed by jinn or by a jinnee: (A, K:) or he was, or became, affected, by a touch, or stroke, from the jinn. (TA.)

EiraDN , [instead of which, as a simple subst., EaroDN is generally used,] and EaraADapN , It was, or became, broad, or wide; (S, O, * Msb, K, TA;) as also ↓ AErD , (A, TA,) which occurs in this sense in two exs. following. (TA.) [And in like manner, ↓ AstErD It grew, or spread, wide; said of a tree; opposed to TaAla ; occurring in the TA in art. bhl .] It is said in a prov., Alqirofapu ↓ A^aEoraDati (S, O, * TA [but in two copies of the S, I find the verb in this instance written AErDtu , and in the O AErDta , and I do not know that the reading in the TA, which seems to be the common one, is found in any copy of the S,]) Suspicion became, or has become, wide; syn. Ait~asaEat : (TA:) used when it is said to a man, “ Whom dost thou suspect ? ” and he answers, “ The sons of such a one, ” referring to the whole tribe. (S, O, TA.) [See Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 112, where another reading is mentioned, which, by what he says, is shown to be A^aEoraDota Alqirofapa Thou hast made suspicion wide. ] In another prov. it is said, vawobu Almalobasi ↓ A^aEoraDa (IAar, A, TA, and K in art. lbs ,) and Almilobasi and Almulobisi (IAar, and K in art. lbs ,) and Almulotabisi (TA in art. lbs ) i. e. SaAra *aA EaroDK , (A, TA,) and EaruDa , and Ait~asaEa ; (Sh;) [meaning the same as the prov. before mentioned;] used with reference to him whose suspicion has become wide; (IAar, and TA in art. lbs ;) i. e. with reference to him who suspects many persons (IAar, Az, and K in art. lbs ,) of a theft; (IAar, Az, and TA in that art.;) or of saying a thing: (TS, and TA in that art.:) or when thou askest a person respecting a thing and he does not explain it to thee. (TA in that art.) [See, again, Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 100, where it is said that A^aEoraDa vawobu Almulobisi app. means The garment of the suspected appeared, or has appeared: but that another reading is EaruDa , meaning became, or has become, wide. ] -A2- EaraDa , aor. , (Fr, S, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. EaroDN ; (TA:) and EariDa , (As, TS, K,) aor. , (Fr, K,) or , like Hasiba , aor. , deviating from the general rule; (As, TS;) It (a thing) appeared, or became apparent, lahu to him; (S, O, Msb, K; [but in some copies of the K, instead of the explanation Zahara wabadaA , we find Zahara Ealayohi wabadaA , which is a mistake;]) as also ↓ AErD , (Fr, S, O, Msb, K,) which is a deviation from a general rule, being quasi pass. of EaraDahu , which see below; (S, * O, * Msb, K;) [lit.] it showed its breadth, or width. (O, * TA.) You say, laka Al$~aYo'u ↓ AErD mino baEiydK The thing appeared to thee from afar. (TA.) And EaraDato lahu Alguwlu , and EariDato , (AZ, S, O, K,) The ghool appeared to him. (K.) The Arabs say, of a thing, EaraDa and ↓ AErD and ↓ tEr~D and ↓ AEtrD , using these verbs as syn.; (Sh;) [app. as meaning It showed, presented, or offered, itself, (lit. its breadth, or width, or its side, see 5,) to a person: the first and last also often signify, and the others sometimes, he obtruded himself in an affair; interfered therein:] IKt disallows ↓ AErD in the sense of AEtrD , as not having been found by him: (TA:) [but] an instance of the former of these two verbs used in the sense of the latter of them occurs in the phrase liln~aAZiriyna ↓ A_i*aA A^uEoraDato [app. meaning When she shows, or presents, herself to the lookers ], in a poem by one of the tribe of Teiyi. (Sh.) ― -b2- EaraDa laka Alxayoru , [in one place in the TA Alxabara , and Alxbr in a copy of the Msb,] inf. n. EaroDN ; (TA; [in one place in the TA EuruwDN there referring to Alxabaru , which is app. a mistranscription;]) and ↓ AErD ; (S, O, K, TA;) Good [i. e. the doing of good ] hath become within thy power, or practicable to thee, or easy to thee. (S, O, K, TA.) And laka AlZ~aboYu ↓ AErD The gazelle hath exposed to thee its side; (TA;) or hath put its side in thy power, (S, O, K, TA,) by turning it towards thee: (O, TA:) said to incite one to shoot it, or cast at it. (S, O.) Or laka ↓ AErD , said of an animal of the chase, or other thing, signifies It hath put in thy power, [or exposed to thee, ] its breadth, or width: (A:) or lahu ↓ AErD signifies it (a thing) became within his power, or practicable to him, or easy to him; lit., it showed its side [ to him ]. (Mgh.) [In the TA, I find A^aEoraDa fiY Al$~aYo'i expl. as signifying He had the width of the thing in his power: but fY , here, seems to be a mistake for lahu .] A poet, also, says ↓ A^aEoriDiY addressing a woman; meaning A^amokiniY [ Empower thou; i. e. grant thou access ]. (S.) ― -b3- EaraDa lahu , aor. ; (As, S, K, TA;) and EariDa , aor. ; (TA;) are also said of an event, (As, TA,) or of a disease, and the like, (S, K, TA,) such as disquietude of mind, and a state of distraction of the mind or attention; (TA;) [meaning It happened to him; it befell him; it occurred to him; was incident to him; ] and also of doubt, and the like. (TA.) [So, too, is ↓ AEtrD .] You also say, EaraDahu EaAriDN mina AlHum~aY wanaHowihaA [ An occurrence of fever, and the like, happened to him, or befell him ]. (S.) And Albadana ↓ AEtrD [ It befell the body ] is said of [a disease, as, for instance,] the mange, or scab. (B, in TA in art. Er .) ― -b4- EaraDa lahu , aor. ; (Msb, TA;) and EariDa lh , aor, ; (Msb;) He intervened as an obstacle to him, preventing him from attaining his desire, (Msb, TA, *) or from seeking to attain his desire, and from going his way; (TA;) as also lh ↓ AEtrD . (Msb.) You say also, EaraDa lahu A^a$ad~a AlEaroDi , and ↓ AEtrD , He opposed himself to him ( qaAbalahu binafosihi ) with the most vehement opposition of himself. (TA.) See also 5, second sentence. One should not say, Er~Dtu lahu , with teshdeed, in the sense of AiEotaraDotu . (Msb.) You also say, EaraDa EaAriDN , meaning [ An obstacle intervened, or prevented; lit.] an intervening thing intervened; a preventing thing prevented. (TA.) And sirotu faEaraDa liY fiY AlT~ariyqi EaAriDN mino jabalK wanaHowihi I journeyed, and there opposed itself to me, so as to prevent my going on, an obstacle consisting in a mountain, and the like; as also ↓ AEtrD : whence the AiEotiraADaAt [or objections ] of the lawyers; because they prevent one's laying hold upon the evidence. (Msb.) And EaraDa lahu Al$~aYo'u fiY AlT~ariyqi The thing intervened as an obstacle to him in the way, preventing him from going on. (TA.) And EaraDa Al$~aYo'u The thing stood up and prevented; [or stood in the way, or presented itself as an obstacle; or opposed itself; ] as also ↓ AEtrD . (TA.) [And The thing lay, or extended, breadthwise, or across, or athwart; like AEtrD , q. v.] And Al$~aYo'u duwna Al$~aYo'i ↓ AEtrD The thing intervened as an obstacle in the way to the thing; syn. HaAla . (S, O.) ― -b5- maA EaraDotu lahu bisuwo'K , aor. ; and mA EariDotu , aor. ; signify mA taEar~aDotu : see 5: or, as some say, I did not, or have not, become exposed to his reviling, or evilspeaking, by reviling, or speaking evil, of him. (Msb.) [See also EaraDa EiroDahu , below.] ― -b6- EaraDa lahu also signifies He went towards him; (TA in art. nHw ;) and EaraDa EaroDahu and EuroDahu [the same, i. e.] naHaA naHowahu ; (K;) as also ErDh ↓ AEtrD (TA.) ― -b7- In the saying of El-Kumeyt, faA^aboligo yaziyda A_ino EaraDota wamuno*irFA he means [ And convey thou to Yezeed, ] if thou pass by him, [ and to Mundhir: or perhaps, if thou go to him: or if thou present thyself to him.] (S.) ― -b8- EaraDa Alfarasu , (L, K,) aor. , inf. n. EaroDN , (L, TA,) The horse went along inclining towards one side: (K, TA:) or ran inclining his breast and head: (L, TA:) and ran inclining his head and neck; (K; [in which only the inf. n. of the verb in this last sense is mentioned;]) the doing of which is approved in horses, but disapproved in camels. (TA.) [See also 3, and 5.] ― -b9- EaraDa AlbaEiyru , (K,) inf. n. EaroDN , (TA,) The camel ate of the A^aEoraAD , i. e. of the upper parts of the trees [or shrubs ]. (K.) ― -b10- EaraDato , said of a she-camel, A fracture, (S, O, K,) or some injurious accident, (S, O,) befell her; (S, O, K;) as also EariDato ; (O, K;) but the former is the more approved: (TA:) and EaraDa lahaA a disease, or a fracture, befell her. (TA, from a trad.) Also, said of a sheep, or goat, ( $Ap ,) It died by disease. (K.) And EariDa Al$~aA='u The sheep, or goats, burst, or became rent, from abundance of herbage. (K.) And EaraDa , (IKtt,) inf. n. EaroDN , (K,) He (an animal, IKtt, or a man, K, [but it is said in the TA that there is no reason for this restriction,]) died without disease. (IKtt, K.) ― -b11- EaraDa bisiloEatihi i. q. EaAraDa bihaA . (K.) See 3, in two places. [And under the same, see a similar phrase.] ― -b12- EaraDa He (a man, S, O) came to AlEaruwD , i. e. Mekkeh and El-Medeeneh, (S, O, K, TA,) and El-Yemen, (TA,) and what is around them. (S, O, K, TA.) -A3- EaraDa Al$~aYo'a , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. EaroDN , (Msb,) He made the thing apparent; showed it; exhibited it; manifested it; exposed it to view; presented it; (S, O, Msb, K;) unfolded it; laid it open: and also he mentioned it: (Msb:) [lit. he showed its breadth, or width, or its side: and hence it also signifies he made the thing to stand as an obstacle, duwna $aYo'K in the way to, or of, a thing. ] You say, EaraDa lahu Al$~aYo'a He made apparent, showed, exhibited, manifested, or exposed to view, to him the thing; (S, O, K;) unfolded it, or laid it open, to him. (S, TA.) And EaraDa Ealayohi A^amora ka*aA (S, O, K *) He showed, propounded, or proposed, to him, such a thing, or such a case: (K, * TA:) [and he asked, or required, of him, with gentleness, the doing of such a thing; for] AlEaroDu signifies TalabN biliynK , (Mughnee and K, voce A^alaA ,) or TalabN biliynK wataA^ad~ubK . (Mughnee voce lawolaA .) And EaraDotu AlmataAEa lilobayoEi [ I showed, exposed, presented, or offered, the commodity for sale; or] I showed the commodity to those desirous of purchasing it. (Msb.) The phrase EaraDa Ealayohi AlmataAEa [ He showed, or offered, to him the commodity ] is used because the person shows to the other the length and breadth of the thing ( Tuwlahu waEaroDahu ), or because he shows him one of its sides ( EuroDFA mino A^aEoraADihi ). (Mgh.) [Hence,] it is said in a trad. of Hodheyfeh, tuEoraDu Alfitanu EalaY Alquluwbi EaroDa AlHaSiyri , which means, accord. to some, that fitan [ Temptations, &c.,] will be [ displayed and ] embellished to the hearts of men like [ as ] the ornamented and variegated garment called HSyr [ is displayed and embellished ]: (B, TA in art. HSr :) or the meaning is, that they will be laid and spread upon the hearts like the HSyr : (IAth, TA in the present art.:) and some say that by this last word is here meant a certain vein extending across upon the side of a beast, towards the belly. (TA in art. HSr .) [Hence also,] EaroDN saAbiriY~N [ A slight exhibition: (see art. sbr :)] so in the proverbs by A'Obeyd, in the handwriting of Ibn-El-Jawáleekee: (TA:) or EaroDu saAbiriY~K : (TA, and so in a copy of the S in this art.:) or EaroDa saAbiriY~K . (O, TA, and so in a copy of the S in this art.) With this agrees in meaning the saying EaraDa EalaY~a sawoma EaAl~apK [ He offered to me in the manner of offering water to camels taking a second draught: see also arts. swm and El ; and see Freytag's Arab. Prov. ii. 84]. (TA.) You say also, EaraDotu AljaAriyapa EalaY AlbayoEi [ I showed, or displayed, or exposed, or offered, the girl for sale ]: (S, O, TA:) and in like manner AlmataAEa [ the commodity ]. (TA.) And EaraDotu lahu vawobFA makaAna Haq~ihi ; (S, O;) and EaraDotu lahu mino Haq~ihi vawobFA , (S, O, K,) or mataAEFA , (TA,) this meaning, [as also the former phrase,] I gave to him a garment, or piece of cloth, [or a commodity, ] in place of his due: (S, O, K:) and in like manner, ErDt bihi . (El-Umawee, TA.) And EaraDotu AlbaEiyra EalaY AlHawoDi , which is an instance of inversion, meaning EaraDotu AlHawoDa EalaY AlbaEiyri [ I showed the watering-trough to the camel ]: (S, O, Msb:) [or it agrees in meaning with the phrase] EaraDa Aln~aAqapa EalaY AlHawoDi , and ↓ A^aEoraDahaA , [as rendered] He offered to the she-camel to drink [ at the wateringtrough ]. (L, TA.) And EaraDahumo EalaY Als~ayofi [lit. He exposed them to the sword; (see also 2;) meaning] he slew them (S, A, O, Msb, K) with the sword. (Msb.) And EaraDahumo EalaY Als~awoTi He beat them with the whip; he flogged them. (K, * TA.) And EaraDahumo EalaY Aln~aAri He burned them. (A, TA.) And EaraDotu AlEasala EalaY Aln~aAri I cooked the honey [ upon the fire ] to separate it from the wax. (Msb.) [And EaraDa nafosahu lilohalaAki He exposed himself to destruction. ] ― -b2- EaroDN also signifies The bringing a man before a judge, and accusing him. (IAar, in TA, art. Eqb .) [And The presenting, or addressing, a petition, &c., with EalaY or li before the word signifying the person to whom it is presented or addressed.] ― -b3- One says also, maA yaEoriDuka lifulaAnK , (S, [so in two copies,] and O,) or maA yaEoruDaka , (L, TA,) with fet-h to the Y and damm to the r , (L,) the verb being coordinate to naSara : (TA:) [app. meaning What causeth thee to present thyself to such a one? ]: Yaakoob disallows one's saying ↓ maA yuEar~iDuka lifulaAnK , with teshdeed. (S, O, TA.) [But the latter of these two verbs has a signification nearly allied to that which is here assigned to the former, and exactly agreeing with one mentioned before. See 2.] ― -b4- EaraDa Aljunoda , (S, Msb,) and EaraDa Aljunoda EaroDa AlEayoni , (S, O,) or EaroDa EayonK , (A, K, B, except that in the A and B we find Aljayo$a instead of Aljnd ,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. EaroDN , (Yoo, S,) He made the army, or body of soldiers, to pass by him, and examined their state, (S, O, K,) what it was: (S, O:) [i. e. he reviewed them: ] or he made them to pass before him in review, that he might know who was absent and who was present: (A, B:) or he caused them to come forth, and examined them, that he might know them: (Msb:) and you say also, ↓ AEtrDhumo , (S, O, K,) meaning [the same, or] he made them to pass by him, or before him, and examined them, one by one, (K, TA,) to see who were absent from those who were present. (TA.) You say also, ↓ AEtrD AlmataAEa wanaHowahu and EalaY Eayonihi ↓ AEtrDhu [ He examined the commodity, and the like thereof, having it displayed before his eye ]. (Th.) [See also EaroDN .] ― -b5- EaraDotu AlkitaAba , (S, O, Msb,) aor. , inf. n. EaroDN , (Msb,) I read, or recited, the writing, or book: (O, TA: [in the S it is unexplained, but immediately followed by EaraDotu Aljunoda EaroDa AlEayoni :]) or I recited it by heart, or memory. (Msb.) -A4- EaraDa EiroDahu , aor. ; (TA;) and ↓ AEtrDhu ; (A, TA;) [perhaps originally signified He examined his grounds of pretension to respect, or the like: and then became used to express a frequent consequence of doing so; i. e.] he spoke evil of him; reviled him; detracted from his reputation: (A, TA:) or he corresponded to him, or equalled him, in grounds of pretension to respect: (TA:) [the former seems to be the more probable of the two meanings; for it is said that] fulaAnFA ↓ AEtrD signifies he spoke evil of such a one; reviled him; detracted from his reputation; (Lth, S, O, K;) and annoyed him. (Lth, TA.) -A5- EaraDa Al$~aYo'a , (K,) aor. , inf. n. EaroDN , (TA,) He hit the side ( EuroD ) of the thing. (K.) -A6- EaraDa AlEuwda EalaY AlA_inaA='i , (S, O, Msb, K,) and Als~ayofa EalaY faxi*ihi , (S, O, K,) aor. and , (S, O, Msb, K,) in both phrases, (O, K,) [J says, in the S, app. referring, not, as SM thinks, to the latter of the two phrases, but to the meaning, “ this, only, with damm, ”] He put the stick breadthwise, across, athwart, or crosswise, ( maEoruwDFA , TA, or biAlEaroDi , Msb, TA, both meaning the same, TA,) upon the vessel, (Msb, TA,) [and so the sword upon his thigh: and ↓ Er~Dhu signifies the same.] ― -b2- EaraDa Alr~umoHa , aor. , [and probably also,] inf. n. EaroDN ; and ↓ Er~Dhu , inf. n. taEoriyDN ; (TA:) He turned, or placed, the spear sideways; contr. of sad~adahu . (S, in art. sd , relating to the former verb; and L, in the same art., relating to the latter verb.) ― -b3- EaraDa Alr~aAmiY Alqawosa , inf. n. EaroDN , The archer laid the bow upon its side on the ground, and then shot with it. (TA.) ― -b4- The saying of Aboo-Kebeer El-Hudhalee, cited, but not expl., by Th, faEaraDotuhu fiY saAqi A^asomanihaA is thought by ISd to mean And I made its (the sword's) breadth to become concealed in the thigh of the fattest of them. (TA.) -A7- EaraDahu He fed him: (Fr, TA:) [or he offered, or presented, to him food: for] EuriDuwA signifies They were fed: and they had food offered, or presented, to them. (L, TA.) [See also 2, in the last quarter.] ― -b2- EaraDa AlHawoDa and Alqirobapa He filled the wateringtrough and the water-skin. (K.) -A8- EaraDa Al$~awoka : see 8, near the end. -A9- EaraDa baEiyrahu , inf. n. EaroDN , He branded his camel with the mark called EiraAD ; (S;) and so ↓ Er~Dhu : (S, TA:) and EuriDa AlbaEiyru , inf. n. as above, The camel was branded with that mark. (K.) -A10- EaraDotuhu , (K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. EaroDN , (K, TA,) I defrauded, or deceived, him in selling. (K.) -A11- EuriDa , (K,) or EuriDa lahu , (A, TA,) inf. n. EaroDN , (K,) He was, or became, mad, or insane, or possessed by jinn or by a jinnee: (A, K:) or he was, or became, affected, by a touch, or stroke, from the jinn. (TA.)

definition: , inf. n. taEoriyDN , He made it (a thing) broad, or wide; (S, K;) as also ↓ AErDhu , (Lth, S, K,) inf. n. A_iEoraADN . (TA.) ― -b2- See also 1, near the end, in three places. ― -b3- taEariyDN also...
sourceDefinition: , inf. n. taEoriyDN , He made it (a thing) broad, or wide; (S, K;) as also ↓ AErDhu , (Lth, S, K,) inf. n. A_iEoraADN . (TA.) ― -b2- See also 1, near the end, in three places. ― -b3- taEariyDN also signifies The speaking obliquely, indirectly, obscurely, ambiguously, or equivocally; contr. of taSoriyHN ; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as when thou askest a man, “ Hast thou seen such a one? ” and he, having seen him, and disliking to lie, answers, “ Verily such a one is seen: ” (Msb:) or the making a phrase, or the like, to convey an allusion, or an indication not expressly mentioned therein; as when you say “ How foul is niggardliness! ” alluding to such a one's being a niggard ( tuEar~iDu biA^an~ahu baxiylN ): differing from kinaAyapN , which is the mentioning of the consequence and meaning that of which it is the consequence; as when you say “ Such a one has a long suspensory cord to his sword, and has many ashes of the cooking-pot; ” meaning that he is tall of stature, and one who entertains many guests: (Mgh:) [but many hold these two words to be identical in meaning.] You say, Ear~aDotu lifulaAnK and bifulaAnK , i. e. I said something [ in the manner explained above ], meaning such a one. (S, Msb.) [See also an ex. voce kal~aA='N .] 'Omar defined [or rather explained] Alt~aEoriyDu biAlfaAHi$api [ The making an allusion to that which is foul, or obscene ] by the instance of a man saying to another “ My father is not an adulterer, nor is my mother an adulteress. ” (O, TA.) Or, accord. to the early authorities, Er~D signifies He used a phrase susceptible of different meanings, or an equivocal phrase, by which the hearer understood a meaning different from that which he ( the speaker ) intended: or, accord. to the later authorities, as Et-Teftezánee, he mentioned a thing by a proper or tropical or metonymical expression, to signify some other thing, which he did not mention; as when one says, “ I heard him whom thou hatest praying for thee, and making good mention of thee; ” meaning in his praying for the Muslims in general. (El-Munáwee, in explaining the trad. A_in~a fiY AlmaEaAriyDi Alx , which see below, voce miEoraADN .) tEryD with respect to the demanding of a woman in marriage in [the period of] her Eid~ap , [during which she may not contract a new marriage,] is the using language which resembles a demand of her in marriage, but does not plainly express it; as the saying to her “ Verily thou art beautiful, ” or “ Verily there is a desire for thee, ” or “ Verily women are of the things that I need: ” and tEryD is sometimes made by the quoting of proverbs, and by the introducing of enigmas in one's speech. (TA.) [When followed by EalaY , it signifies The making an indirect objection against a person or saying &c.] ― -b4- Also Er~D , (S, O,) inf. n. as above, (K,) He wrote indistinctly; (S, O, K;) not making the letters distinct, nor the handwriting rightly formed or disposed. (TA.) -A2- taEoriyDN also sigsifies The making a thing to be exposed [or liable ] to another thing. (K, [It is there expl., with the article Al prefixed to it, by the words A^ano yajoEala lil$~aYo'i ↓ Al$~aYo'a EaroDFA , or ↓ EaraDFA , accord. to different copies; the latter (which see, last sentence but one,) app. the right reading; meaning maEoruwDFA , whichever be the right; for an inf. n. may be used in the sense of a pass. part. n.; and many a word of the measure faEalN is used in that sense, as, for instance, xabaTN and nafaDN and hadamN . That I have rightly rendered the above-mentioned explanation in the K is indicated by what here immediately follows.]) Hence the trad. maA EaZumato niEomapu A@ll~`hi EalaY EabodK A_il~aA EaZumato maw^uwnapu Aln~aAsi Ealayohi famano lamo yaHotamilo tiloka Almaw^uwnapa faqado Ear~aDa tiloka Aln~iEomapa lilz~awaAli [ The blessing of God upon a servant, or man, hath not become great but the burden of other men upon him hath become great; and he who doth not take upon himself that burden causeth that blessing to be exposed to cessation ]. (O, TA.) You also say, huwa lahu ↓ Ear~aDotu fulaAnFA lika*aA fataEar~aDa [ I caused such a one to expose himself, or I exposed him, to such a thing, and he exposed himself, or became exposed, to it ], (S, O, *) i. e. ↓ jaEalotuhu EaraDFA lika*aA . (O.) See also 1, last quarter. ― -b2- Also The giving a thing in exchange for, as an equivalent for, or in the place of, another thing. (TA.) ― -b3- And The act of bartering, or selling, a commodity for a like commodity. (K, * TA.) See 3, in two places. ― -b4- And The giving what is termed an EuraADap : (TA:) and the feeding with what is so termed: (K:) or the giving food of what is so termed. (S.) [See also 1, near the end.] It is said in a trad., respecting a company of travelling merchants making presents to Mohammad and Aboo-Bekr, Ear~aDuwhumaA viyaAbFA biyDFA They gave to both of them white garments, or pieces of cloth. (L.) And you say, Ear~aDuwhumo maHoDFA They gave them to drink [ unmixed ] milk. (TA.) And Ear~iDuwnaA Give ye to us food of your EuraADap ; your wheat, or corn, which ye have brought. (S, TA.) ― -b5- Er~D AlmaA$iyapa , inf. n. taEoriyDN , He made the cattle to have such pasturage as rendered them in no need of being fed with fodder. (TA.) -A3- Er~D , (IAar, O,) inf. n. taEoriyDN (K,) also signifies He became possessed of EaAriDap [i. e. courage, or courage and energy ], (IAar, O, K,) and strength, or power, (IAar, O,) and a faculty of speech, (IAar, O, K,) or, as in the Tekmileh, and power of speech. (TA.) -A4- And He kept continually to the eating of EiroDaAn , (O, * K, TA, [in the O EiraAD ,]) pl. of EariyDN . (TA.) -A5- See also 4, last sentence.

(L.) And you say, Ear~aDuwhumo maHoDFA They gave them to drink [ unmixed ] milk. (TA.) And Ear~iDuwnaA Give ye to us food of your EuraADap ; your wheat, or corn, which ye have brought. (S, TA.) ― -b5- Er~D AlmaA$iyapa , inf. n. taEoriyDN , He made the cattle to have such pasturage as rendered them in no need of being fed with fodder. (TA.) -A3- Er~D , (IAar, O,) inf. n. taEoriyDN (K,) also signifies He became possessed of EaAriDap [i. e. courage, or courage and energy ], (IAar, O, K,) and strength, or power, (IAar, O,) and a faculty of speech, (IAar, O, K,) or, as in the Tekmileh, and power of speech. (TA.) -A4- And He kept continually to the eating of EiroDaAn , (O, * K, TA, [in the O EiraAD ,]) pl. of EariyDN . (TA.) -A5- See also 4, last sentence.

definition: [ EaArDhu has two contr.
sourceDefinition: [ EaArDhu has two contr. significations, which are unequivocally expressed by saying EArDhu biAlxilaAfi and EArDhu biAlwifaAqi . (See EaAnadahu .) Thus one says,] EArDhu , (Msb,) inf. n. muEaAraDapN , (TA,) He opposed him [ being opposed by him ]. (Kull p. 342.) ― -b2- And [ He vied, competed, or contended for superiority, with him; emulated, rivalled, or imitated, him; ] he did like as he (the latter) did. (Msb, TA.) You say also, EaAraDotuhu bimivoli maA SanaEa , (S, O,) or bimivoli SaniyEihi , (K,) I did to him like as he did: (S, O, K:) whence AlmuEaAraDap [in trafficking, as will be seen below]: as though the breadth ( EaroD ) of the action of the one were like the breadth of the action of the other. (O, K.) And EArDhu bimaA SanaEahu He requited him for that which he did. (L.) ― -b3- [Hence] muEaAraDapN also signifies The selling a commodity for another commodity; exchanging it for another; as also EaroDN : (TA:) and [in like manner] ↓ taEoriyDN , the act of bartering, or selling a commodity for a like commodity. (K, * TA.) You say, EArD bisiloEatihi ; and bihaA ↓ EaraDa , (K, TA,) aor , inf. n. EaroDN ; (TA;) He exchanged his commodity; giving one commodity and taking another; (TA:) and mataAEahu ↓ Er~D he sold his commodity for another commodity. (TK.) Also EArDhu biAlbayoEi (M and L in art. bd ) and baAEahu muEaAraDapF (S and K in that art.) [ He bartered, or exchanged commodities, with him ]. And ↓ A^axa*otu h`*ihi Als~iloEapa EaroDFA I took this commodity giving another in exchange for it. (TA.) And when persons demand blood of other persons, and they [the latter] do not retaliate for them, they [the latter] say, naHonu naEoriDu minohu [ We will give a compensation for it ]: and they [the former] accept ( AEtrDwA ) the bloodwit. (L.) ― -b4- You say also, EaAraDotuhu fiY AlbayoEi faEaraDotuhu [ I vied with him in endeavouring to defraud, or deceive, in selling, or buying, ] and I defrauded, or deceived, him therein. (K, * TA.) And EArDhu biAlmajodi [ He vied, or competed, or contended, with him, or emulated him, or rivalled him, in glory, or honour, &c.]: (L and K in art. mjd :) and in like manner EArDhu biAlfaxori . (K in art. fxr .) See 6. ― -b5- EArDhu , (O, K,) or EArDhu fiY Almasiyri (S,) or fY Als~ayori , (A,) He went along over against him; or on the opposite side to him; (S, A, O, K;) in a corresponding manner; (TA;) [ each taking the side opposite to the other. ] ― -b6- [Hence. EArDhu as signifying It (a tract &c.) lay over against him. Also as syn. with AErD Eanohu .] See 4. ― -b7- [Hence also,] EArD , (S, O, K,) inf. n. muEaAraDapN , (TA,) He took to one side (S, O, K *) of the way, or ways, (accord. to different copies of the K,) while another took to another way, so that they both met. (TA. [See 3 in arts. xzm and zm .]) El-Ba'eeth says, madaHonaA lahaA rawoqa Al$~abaAbi faEaAraDato janaAba AlS~ibaA fiY kaAtimi Als~ir~i A^aEojamaA [cited in the S, voce ray~iq , but with rayoqa , in the place of rawoqa , and there ascribed to Lebeed,] meaning, accord. to ISk, [ We praised to her the first part of youth, and thereupon ] she took to the side of AlSbA [or youthful foolishness, and amorous dalliance ], or, as another says, she entered with us into it, in a manner not open, but making it appear to us that she was entering with us; jnAb AlSbA meaning janobahu . (TA.) ― -b8- EArD AljinaAzapa He came to the bier, or the bier conveying the corpse, intermediately ( muEotariDFA ), in a part of the way, not following it from the abode of the deceased: (O, K, TA:) said of Mohammad, in a trad. respecting the funeral of Aboo-Tálib. (O, TA.) ― -b9- EArD AlmaroA^apa , inf. n. EiraADN and muEaAraDapN , He came in to the woman [ indirectly, or] unlawfully; (Sgh, K, TA;) i. e. without marriage and without possession [ of her as his slave ]. (Sgh, TA.) Hence the saying, jaA='ato biwaladK Eano EiraADK and muEaAraDapK She brought forth a child in consequence of a man's having so come in to her: (K:) or a child whose father was unknown. (A, O, TA.) [Hence also,] Aibonu muEaAraDapK i. q. safiyHN ; (O, K;) i. e. A son the offspring of fornication. (O, TA.) ― -b10- AljawozaA='u tamur~u EalaY janobK watuEaAriDu Aln~ujuwma , inf. n. muEaAraDapN , [ Orion passes along towards one side, and is oblique in its course with respect to the other stars; ] i. e. it is not direct [in the disposition of its stars, particularly of the three conspicuous stars of the belt, with respect to its course] in the sky. (As, S, O.) [See also 5.] ― -b11- EArD Alr~iyHa , said of a camel, (TA,) [ He turned his side to the wind; ] he did not face the wind nor turn his back to it. (A, TA.) ― -b12- naZara A_ilayohi muEaAraDapF He looked at him, or towards him, sideways, or obliquely. (A, TA.) You say also, naZara Eano muEaAraDapK [ He looked sideways, or obliquely ]. (TA in art. xzr .) And you say of a she-camel, tamo$iY muEaAraDapF liln~a$aATi [ She goes obliquely by reason of briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness ]. (S, K. * [See again 5, latter half.]) ― -b13- EArD Al$~aYo'a biAl$~aYo'i He compared the thing with the thing. (Msb.) You say, EArD AlkitaAba , (S, O, K,) inf. n. muEaAraDapN and EiraADN , (TA,) He compared, or collated, the writing, or book, (S, O, K,) bikitaAbK A=xara with another writing, or book. (S, * O, * TA.) And kataba kitaAbFA Eano muEaAraDapK [ He copied, or transcribed, the writing, or book ]. (K in art. nsx .) ― -b14- And AlmuEaAraDapu is syn. with AlmudaArasapu [probably as meaning The reading, or studying, with another ]. (TA.) -A2- Daraba Aln~aAqapa Eir~ADFA [ He covered the she-camel agreeably with her desire ] is said when the stallion is offered to her, and if she desire he covers her, but otherwise he does not: (S, O, TA:) in the K it is said, if he desire her; which is wrong: (TA:) this is because of her generous quality. (S, O, TA.) ― -b2- And laqiHato EiraADFA She (a camel) conceived by a stallion, she not being of the camels among which he was sent. (AO, TA.) ― -b3- See also 8, near the end.
