definition: ; [app. as meaning It showed, presented, or offered, itself, to a person; lit. it showed, or presented, its breadth, or width; or, as tEr~D is expl. in the EM p. 19, it showed its EuroD , i. e. side:...
sourceDefinition: : see EaraDa , near the beginning, where these two verbs, and AErD and AEtrD , are said to be used as syn.; [app. as meaning It showed, presented, or offered, itself, to a person; lit. it showed, or presented, its breadth, or width; or, as tEr~D is expl. in the EM p. 19, it showed its EuroD , i. e. side: this, or it, or he, presented, or offered, or exposed, its, or his, side, seems to be the primary signification of tEr~D , and of AEtrD , as well as of EaraDa ; and is of frequent occurrence: and all (as mentioned voce EaraDa ) signify also he obtruded himself in an affair; interfered therein.] ― -b2- [Hence,] tEr~D lahu He opposed himself to him; he offered opposition to him; or he attacked him; said of a man, and of a beast of prey, or noxious reptile, and the like; as also ↓ EaraDa and ↓ AEtrD : this signification also is of frequent occurrence. (The lexicons passim.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] He addressed, or applied, or directed, himself, or his regard, or attention, or mind, to him, or it; [as though he set himself over against the object to which the verb relates;] syn. taSad~aY . (Lth, Lh, S, O, Msb, K.) So in the saying, tEr~D limaEoruwfihimo and maEoruwfahumo [ He addressed himself, &c., presented himself, betook himself, advanced, came forward, or went forward, or attempted, to obtain their favour, or bounty ]: and tEr~D lilomaEoruwfi and AlmaEoruwfa [ He addressed himself, &c., to obtain favour, or bounty; and] he sought, or demanded, it: (Az, Msb:) and [so] llmErwf ↓ AEtrD (Msb in art. Er . [See also AEtrD lahu .]) So too in the saying, taEar~aDuwA linafaHaAti raHomapi A@ll~`hi [ Address ye yourselves, &c., to become objects of the effusions of the mercy of God ]; (O, K, TA;) occurring in a trad. (TA.) And hence the saying, tEr~D fiY $ahaAdatihi lika*aA He addressed himself, &c., ( tSd~Y ,) in his testimony, to the mention of such a thing. (Msb.) It is likewise syn. with tSd~Y in the saying, tEr~D liY fulaAnN bimakoruwhK [ Such a one addressed himself, &c., or attempted, to do me an abominable, or evil, action; or opposed himself to me with an abominable, or evil, action ]. (Lth.) [In like manner also you say,] yataEar~aDu liln~aAsi biAl$~ar~i [ He addresses himself, &c., to do to men evil; or he opposes himself to men with evil or mischief ]. (S, K.) And maA taEar~aDotu lahu bisuwo'K [ I did not address myself, or have not addressed myself, &c., to do to him evil ]: and ↓ maA EaraDotu and ↓ maA EariDotu are said to signify the same. (Msb.) AEtrD signifies [ It lay, or extended, breadthwise, across, transversely, athwart, sideways, obliquely, or horizontally: or so as to present an obstacle: or so intervened in any manner; as shown in the part last referred to, above: or rather it has both of these meanings; and in the former sense it is used, in the TA, art. Hr , in describing the direction of an asterism, opposed to AinotaSaba : or, in other words,] it (a thing, S) became, (K,) or became an obstacle, ( SaAra EaAriDFA , S, O,) like a piece of wood lying across, or athwart, or obliquely, ( muEotariDapF ,) in a channel of running water, (S, O, K,) or a road, (O, L,) and the like, preventing persons from passing along it. (L.) It is also said [of a collection of clouds appearing, or presenting itself, or extending sideways, or stretching along in the horizon like a mountain; see EaAriDN : and] of a building, or other thing, such as a trunk of a palm-tree, or a mountain, lying in a road: and as this prevents the passengers from passing along the road, it is used as signifying He, or it, prevented, or hindered: (O, K:) it is quasi-pass. of EaraDahu . (K, * TA.) [respecting horseracing] signifies A man's coming intermediately with his horse, in a part of the course, and so entering among the [ other ] horses. (O, L, K.) sourceDefinition: Breadth; width; contr. of TuwlN ; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) and i. q. saEapN ; (K;) the mutual distance of the edges or sides of a thing: (Msb:) primarily relating to corporeal things, but afterwards used in relation to other things: [see EariyDN :] (TA:) this word as signifying the contr. of Twl is the common source of derivation of the other words of this art., not withstanding their multitude: (O:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aEoraADN (IAar, TA) and of mult. EuruwDN and EiraADN . (TA.) It is said in the Kur [lvii. 21, wajan~apK EaroDuhaA kaEaroDi Als~amaA='i wAlA^aroDi And a paradise whereof the breadth, or width, is like the breadth, or width, of the heaven and the earth: and in iii. 127,] EaroDuhaA Als~am`waAtu wAlA^aroDu [ the breadth, or width, whereof is as the heavens and the earth ]: and Ibn-'Arafeh observes that when the EaroD is described as being much, it indicates that the Tuwl is much, for the latter is more than the former. (O, TA.) You say also, EaraDa EaroDahu , and ↓ EuroDahu , He went towards him: [lit. towards his breadth, and his side. ] (K.) And *ahaba EaroDFA waTuwlFA [ He went wide and long ]; (S, Msb, * K;) fiY Al$~aYo'i [ in the thing ]; (Msb;) and fiY AlmakaArimi (tropical:) [ in generous actions ]. (TA.) And qaTaEahu EaroDFA [ He cut it breadthwise, or across, or crosswise ]. (S in art. qT , &c.) And qaTaEa AlwaAdiY EaroDFA [ He crossed the valley ]; (S and K in art. jzE &c.;) and in like manner, AlA^aroDa [ the land ]. (K in that art.) And waDaEa AlEuwda EalaY AlA_inaA='i biAlEaroDi [ He put the stick upon the vessel breadthwise, or across, or crosswise ]; (Msb;) i. q. maEoruwDFA . (TA.) ― -b2- [In geography, The latitude of a place.] ― -b3- The middle, or midst, of a thing: or EaroDu Al$~aYo'i signifies the thing itself. (TA.) See also EuroDF , former half, and in three places towards the end. -A2- A mountain; (S, K;) as also ↓ EaAriDN : (S, O, K:) or the former, the lowest part, or base, ( safoH ,) thereof; (S, K;) as also ↓ EuroDN : (O, K:) and (so in the S, but in the K “ or ”) the side thereof; (S, K;) as also ↓ EuroDN : (TA:) or the place whence, or whereby, ( minohu ,) a mountain is ascended: (K:) and ↓ EaAriDN , a lofty mountain: (TA:) pl. of the first, A^aEoraADN and EuruwDN . (S, TA.) -A3- A collection of clouds: (K:) or a collection of clouds that obstructs the horizon: (S, K:) [see also EiroDN and EaAriDN :] pl. EuruwDN . (TA.) -A4- (assumed tropical:) An army: (O, K:) or a great army: (S, TA:) and ↓ EiroDN also has the former signification: (K:) or the latter: (TA:) so called as being likened to a mountain; or to the clouds that obstruct the horizon: (S, TA:) pl. A^aEoraADN . (TA.) ― -b2- jaraAdN EaroDN (assumed tropical:) Numerous locusts; (S, O, K; *) likened to the clouds that obstruct the horizon; (TA;) as also ↓ EiroDN : (K:) pl. of the former, EuruwDN : (TA:) and ↓ EaAriDN also signifies a multitude of locusts; (S, O, TA;) and of bees: (TA:) as in the saying, mar~a binaA EaAriDN qado malaA^a AlA^ufuqa [ There passed by us a multitude of locusts, or of bees, which had filled the horizon ]: (S, O, TA:) so says Aboo-Nasr Ahmad Ibn-Hátim. (S, O.) -A5- A valley. (IDrd, K.) See also EiroDN . -A6- [As inf. n. of EaraDa , it occurs in the phrases EaroDa EayonK and EaroDa AlEayoni : see EaraDa Aljunoda .] You say also, naZara A_ilayohi EaroDa EayonK (Th, A) He looked at, or examined, him, or it, having him, or it, before his eye; i. q. AiEotaraDahu EalaY Eayonihi . (TA.) And raA^ayotuhu EaroDa EayonK I saw him, or it, obviously; nearly. (TA.) [See also an ex. voce EayonN .] ― -b2- [ yawomu AlEaroDi is an appellation of The day of the last judgment. ] -A7- A compensation; a substitute; a thing that is given or received or put instead of another thing: so, accord. to some, in the Kur iii. 127, quoted above: [but this is strange:] and so in the phrase EaroDu h`*aA Alv~awobi ka*aA waka*aA [ The compensation, or substitute, for this garment, or piece of cloth, is such a thing, and such a thing: but not necessarily; for ErD in this phrase may have the meaning first assigned to it above]. (TA.) See also what next follows. ― -b2- A commodity; or commodities, or goods; syn. mataAEN ; (S, O, Msb, K;) as also ↓ EaraDN ; accord. to Kz; (K;) which is the contr. of EayonN : (Mgh:) and the former, anything except silver and gold money, or dirhems and deenárs, (S, Msb, K,) which are termed EayonN : (S, Msb:) or any worldly goods or commodities except silver and gold money: (Mgh, * O, TA:) but ↓ EaraDN , which see below, has a more comprehensive signification; everything that is termed EaroDN being included in EaraDN , whereas everything that is termed EaraDN is not EaroDN : (TA:) the pl. of EaroDN is EuruwDN , (Msb,) which A'Obeyd explains as signifying the commodities, or goods, whereof none are meted in a measure nor weighed, and which are not animals, and do not consist in EaqaAr [or immoveable property ]. (S, O, Msb.) You say, Ai$otarayotu AlmataAEa biEaroDK I bought the commodity for a commodity like it. (S, O.) -A8- jaEala Al$~aYo'a EaroDFA lil$~aYo'i , or EaraDFA , accord. to different copies of the K: see 2, in the latter half of the paragraph. -A9- saA^alotuhu EaroDa maAlK : see EuraADapN . -A10- EaroDN also signifies Madness; insanity; or possession by jinn, or by a jinnee. (K, TA.) [See 1, last sentence.] -A11- maDaY EaroDN mina All~ayoli An hour, or a portion, of the night passed; syn. saAEapN . (K, * TA.) -A12- See also EaroDN , with the unpointed S .

sourceDefinition: A side; a lateral, or an outward, part, or portion; syn. jaAnibN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) and naAHiyapN , (S, O, Msb, K,) from whatever direction one comes to it, (S, O,) and $iq~N : (S, Mgh:) and so ↓ EiroDN ; syn. naAHiyapN ; of anything: (TA:) and ↓ EaAriDN , or ↓ EaAriDapN , (accord. to different copies of the K,) or both; (TA;) syn. naAHiyapN : (K, TA:) and ↓ EaruwDN ; syn. EaAriDapN : (S, A, O, K:) and ↓ EiraADN ; syn. naAHiyapN , and $iq~N : (S, O, K:) [or] this last is pl. of EaroDN ; (Sgh, K;) or, accord. to the M, of EaroDN as signifying the contr. of TuwlN : and A^aEoraADN is pl. [or is another pl.] of EuroDN ; and is also pl. of EiroDN in the sense expl. above. (TA.) You say, EuroDu Als~ayofi The side, or flat, ( SafoH ,) of the sword. (K.) And EuroDu AlEunuqi The two sides of the neck: (K:) or each side of the neck. (TA.) [See also EaAriDN .] And EuroDaA A^anofi AlbaEiyri The beginning of the part of the bone of the camel's nose which slopes downwards, in both its edges. (Az, TA.) And naZara A_ilayohi biEuroDi wajohihi He looked at him with the side of his face [ turned towards him ]. (S, O.) And naZara A_ilayohi Eano EuroDK and ↓ EuruDK He looked at him from one side. (S, O, K. *) And xarajuwA yaDoribuwna Eano EuroDK (S, O, K *) They went forth smiting the people from one side, in whatever manner suited, (S, O,) not caring whom they smote. (S, O, K.) And AiDoribo bihi EuroDa AlHaAy^iTi Strike thou with it indiscriminately any part that thou findest of the wall: (S, O, Msb, TA:) or the side thereof. (TA.) And A^aloqihi fiY A^aY~i A^aEoraADi Ald~aAri $iy^ota Throw thou it in any side, or quarter, of the house which thou wilt. (TA.) And xu*ohu mino EuroDi Aln~aAsi , and ↓ EaroDihimo , Take thou him from any side of the people which thou wilt. (TA.) And A^awoSaY A^ano yunofiqa Ealayohi mino EuroDi maAlihi He enjoined that he should expend upon him, or it, of any part of his property indiscriminately. (Mgh.) And fulaAnN mino EuroDi AlEa$iyrapi Such a one is of the collateral class of the kinsfolk, or tribe; not of the main stock thereof. (Mgh.) And EaraDa EuroDaha , He went towards him: [lit. towards his side. ] (K.) See also EaroDN , near the beginning. And mina AlT~ariyqi ↓ A^axa*a fiY EaruwDK (S, * K) He took to one side of the way. (S, * TA.) And siwaY h`*ihi ↓ xu*o fiY EaruwDK Take thou to a side other than this. (A.) And A^axa*a maA tuEojibuniY ↓ fulaAnN fiY EaruwDK (S, A) Such a one took to a way and side not pleasing to me. (S.) [ EaruwDN , it will be observed, is fem.] And sirotu ↓ fiY EiraADihi I went along over against him. (A.) And Alqawomi ↓ sironaA fiY EiraADi We went along not facing the people, or company of men, but coming to them from their side. (TA.) And Aboo-Dhueyb says, A^aminoki baroqN A^abiytu All~ayola A^aroqubuhu Al$~aAmi miSobaAHu ↓ kaA^an~ahu fiY EiraADi (S, * TA,) i. e. [ Is there lightning proceeding from thee, which I pass the night watching, as though it were a lamp ] in the side, or region, of Syria? (S.) ― -b2- See also EaroDN , as signifying the “ lowest part, or base, of a mountain; ” and the “ side thereof. ” [And see $afaqN , last sentence but one.] ― -b3- The middle, or midst, of a river or rivulet or the like, (O, K,) and of the sea, (K,) and of men or people, and of a story or tradition; and ↓ EaroDN signifies the same, of men or people, &c.: (TA:) and the former, the main part of men or people; as also ↓ the latter; and of a story or tradition; (K;) as also ↓ EiraADN , (TA, and so in some copies of the K,) and ↓ EuraADN . (TA, and so in some copies of the K.) You say, raA^ayotuhu fiY EuroDi Aln~aAsi I saw him among the people: (S, O:) and some of the Arabs say, Aln~aAsi ↓ raA^ayotuhu fiY EaroDi , meaning fiY EuroDK ; (Yoo, S, O, TA;) or meaning I saw him in the midst of the people; (TA;) or, as also Aln~aAsi ↓ fiY EuruDi , in the middle portions of the people; or, as some say, in the surrounding portions of the people. (Msb.) And fulaAnN mino EuroDi Aln~aAsi Such a one is of the common people, or vulgar. (S, K. *) ― -b4- kuli Aljubona EuroDFA [ Eat thou cheese indiscriminately; or] take thou cheese at random, or indiscriminately, and buy it of him whom thou findest, not asking respecting him who made it, (As, S, O, K,) whether it be of the making of the people of the Scriptures, or of the making of the Magians. (As, S, O.) -A2- naAqapN EuroDu A^asofaArK : and EuroDu h`*aA AlbaEiyri Als~afaru waAlHajaru : see EuroDapN , last two sentences but one. -A3- A^aEoraADu AlkalaAmi : see miEoraADN . [But whether AErAD in this phrase be pl. of EuroDN , or whether it have any sing., I know not.] ― -b2- See also EuruDN .

rawSourceText: A side; a lateral, or an outward, part, or portion; syn. jaAnibN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) and naAHiyapN , (S, O, Msb, K,) from whatever direction one comes to it, (S, O,) and $iq~N : (S, Mgh:) and so ↓ EiroDN ; syn. naAHiyapN ; of anything: (TA:) and ↓ EaAriDN , or ↓ EaAriDapN , (accord. to different copies of the K,) or both; (TA;) syn. naAHiyapN : (K, TA:) and ↓ EaruwDN ; syn. EaAriDapN : (S, A, O, K:) and ↓ EiraADN ; syn. naAHiyapN , and $iq~N : (S, O, K:) [or] this last is pl. of EaroDN ; (Sgh, K;) or, accord. to the M, of EaroDN as signifying the contr. of TuwlN : and A^aEoraADN is pl. [or is another pl.] of EuroDN ; and is also pl. of EiroDN in the sense expl. above. (TA.) You say, EuroDu Als~ayofi The side, or flat, ( SafoH ,) of the sword. (K.) And EuroDu AlEunuqi The two sides of the neck: (K:) or each side of the neck. (TA.) [See also EaAriDN .] And EuroDaA A^anofi AlbaEiyri The beginning of the part of the bone of the camel's nose which slopes downwards, in both its edges. (Az, TA.) And naZara A_ilayohi biEuroDi wajohihi He looked at him with the side of his face [ turned towards him ]. (S, O.) And naZara A_ilayohi Eano EuroDK and ↓ EuruDK He looked at him from one side. (S, O, K. *) And xarajuwA yaDoribuwna Eano EuroDK (S, O, K *) They went forth smiting the people from one side, in whatever manner suited, (S, O,) not caring whom they smote. (S, O, K.) And AiDoribo bihi EuroDa AlHaAy^iTi Strike thou with it indiscriminately any part that thou findest of the wall: (S, O, Msb, TA:) or the side thereof. (TA.) And A^aloqihi fiY A^aY~i A^aEoraADi Ald~aAri $iy^ota Throw thou it in any side, or quarter, of the house which thou wilt. (TA.) And xu*ohu mino EuroDi Aln~aAsi , and ↓ EaroDihimo , Take thou him from any side of the people which thou wilt. (TA.) And A^awoSaY A^ano yunofiqa Ealayohi mino EuroDi maAlihi He enjoined that he should expend upon him, or it, of any part of his property indiscriminately. (Mgh.) And fulaAnN mino EuroDi AlEa$iyrapi Such a one is of the collateral class of the kinsfolk, or tribe; not of the main stock thereof. (Mgh.) And EaraDa EuroDaha , He went towards him: [lit. towards his side. ] (K.) See also EaroDN , near the beginning. And mina AlT~ariyqi ↓ A^axa*a fiY EaruwDK (S, * K) He took to one side of the way. (S, * TA.) And siwaY h`*ihi ↓ xu*o fiY EaruwDK Take thou to a side other than this. (A.) And A^axa*a maA tuEojibuniY ↓ fulaAnN fiY EaruwDK (S, A) Such a one took to a way and side not pleasing to me. (S.) [ EaruwDN , it will be observed, is fem.] And sirotu ↓ fiY EiraADihi I went along over against him. (A.) And Alqawomi ↓ sironaA fiY EiraADi We went along not facing the people, or company of men, but coming to them from their side. (TA.) And Aboo-Dhueyb says, A^aminoki baroqN A^abiytu All~ayola A^aroqubuhu Al$~aAmi miSobaAHu ↓ kaA^an~ahu fiY EiraADi (S, * TA,) i. e. [ Is there lightning proceeding from thee, which I pass the night watching, as though it were a lamp ] in the side, or region, of Syria? (S.) ― -b2- See also EaroDN , as signifying the “ lowest part, or base, of a mountain; ” and the “ side thereof. ” [And see $afaqN , last sentence but one.] ― -b3- The middle, or midst, of a river or rivulet or the like, (O, K,) and of the sea, (K,) and of men or people, and of a story or tradition; and ↓ EaroDN signifies the same, of men or people, &c.: (TA:) and the former, the main part of men or people; as also ↓ the latter; and of a story or tradition; (K;) as also ↓ EiraADN , (TA, and so in some copies of the K,) and ↓ EuraADN . (TA, and so in some copies of the K.) You say, raA^ayotuhu fiY EuroDi Aln~aAsi I saw him among the people: (S, O:) and some of the Arabs say, Aln~aAsi ↓ raA^ayotuhu fiY EaroDi , meaning fiY EuroDK ; (Yoo, S, O, TA;) or meaning I saw him in the midst of the people; (TA;) or, as also Aln~aAsi ↓ fiY EuruDi , in the middle portions of the people; or, as some say, in the surrounding portions of the people. (Msb.) And fulaAnN mino EuroDi Aln~aAsi Such a one is of the common people, or vulgar. (S, K. *) ― -b4- kuli Aljubona EuroDFA [ Eat thou cheese indiscriminately; or] take thou cheese at random, or indiscriminately, and buy it of him whom thou findest, not asking respecting him who made it, (As, S, O, K,) whether it be of the making of the people of the Scriptures, or of the making of the Magians. (As, S, O.) -A2- naAqapN EuroDu A^asofaArK : and EuroDu h`*aA AlbaEiyri Als~afaru waAlHajaru : see EuroDapN , last two sentences but one. -A3- A^aEoraADu AlkalaAmi : see miEoraADN . [But whether AErAD in this phrase be pl. of EuroDN , or whether it have any sing., I know not.] ― -b2- See also EuruDN .

definition: ― -b2- Also The side of a valley, and of a balad [i.
sourceDefinition: : see EuroDN , first signification. ― -b2- Also The side of a valley, and of a balad [i. e. country or the like, or town or the like ]: (K: [in the CK, bld is in the nom. case, which I think a mistake:]) or (as some say, TA) a part, region, quarter, or tract, (K, TA,) and the low ground or land, (TA,) of, or pertaining to, either of these: (K, TA:) pl. A^aEoraADN . (TA.) ― -b3- A valley in which are towns, or villages, and waters: (O, K:) or in which are palm-trees: (K:) or a valley containing many palms and other trees: (TA:) or any valley in which are trees: (S, O:) [see also EaroDN , explained as applied to a valley:] pl. as above, (S,) and EuroDaAnN . (TA.) ― -b4- A^aEorADu AlHijaAzi The towns, or villages, of El-Hijáz: (K:) or these, (TA,) or the A^aEoraAD , (S, O,) are certain towns, or villages, [ with their territories; i. e. certain provinces, or districts; ] between El-Hijáz and El-Yemen: (S, O, TA:) and some say that A^aEoraADu Almadiynapi is applied to the towns, or villages, that are in the valleys of El-Medeeneh: (TA:) or the low lands of its towns, or villages, where are seed-produce and palm-trees: so says Sh: (O, TA:) the sing. is EiroDN . (K.) ― -b5- And EiroDN , (S, O,) or A^aEoraADN , (K,) which is its pl., (TA,) signifies [The trees called ] A^araAk (S, O, K) and A^avol (S, O) and HamoD . (S, O, K.) -A2- Also A great cloud, (K, TA,) appearing, or presenting itself, or intervening, ( yaEotariDu ,) in the horizon. (TA.) [See EaroDN and EaAriDN , which signify nearly the same.] -A3- I. q. EaroDN , q. v., as signifying (assumed tropical:) An army: (K:) or a great army: (TA:) ― -b2- and as signifying (assumed tropical:) Numerous locusts. (K.) -A4- One's self; syn. nafosN ; (S, O, Msb, K;) i. e. nafosu rajulK . (IKt.) You say, A^akoramotu Eanohu EiroDiY I preserved myself from it. (S, O.) And fulaAnN naqiY~u AlEiroDi Such a one is [ pure in respect of himself; or] free from reproach; (S, O;) or from fault, or vice, or the like. (S, Msb.) And in the same sense it occurs in the saying of Abu-d-Dardà, A^aqoriDo mino EiroDika liyawomi faqorika [ Lend thou from thyself for the day of thy poverty: but see art. qrD ]: and in other instances. (TA.) ― -b2- The body; syn. jasadN , (IAar, S, O, K,) or badanN : (IKt, Az:) pl. A^aEoraADN . (Az, S.) So in the description of the people of Paradise, (Az, S,) in a trad., (Az,) A_in~amaA huwa EaraqN yajoriY mino A^aEoraADihimo [ It is only sweat which flows from their bodies ]. (Az, S, O.) ― -b3- The skin. (Ibráheem El-Harbee, O, K.) ― -b4- Any place of the body that sweats: (O, K:) so in the trad. cited above: (TA:) or any part of the body such as the arm-pit and the groin and the like. (A'Obeyd.) ― -b5- The odour of the body, (S, O, K,) and of other things, (S, O,) whether sweet or foul. (S, O, K.) You say, fulaAnN Tay~ibu AlEiroDi [ Such a one is sweet in respect of odour ], and munotinu AlEiroDi [ foul in respect of odour ]; and siqaA='N xabiyvu AlEiroDi a stinking water-skin, or milk-skin; from A'Obeyd. (S, O.) ― -b6- A man's honour, or reputation, ( jaAnibuhu ,) which he preserves from impairment and blame, both as it relates to himself and to his Hasab [or grounds of pretension to respect on account of the honourable deeds or qualities of his ancestors, &c.]: (IAth, O, K:) or whether it relate to himself or to his ancestors or to those of whose affairs the management is incumbent on him: (K:) or a subject of praise, and of blame, of a man, (Abu-l-'Abbás, IAth, O, K,) whether it be in himself or in his ancestors or in those of whose affairs the management is incumbent on him: (IAth:) or those things by the mention whereof with praise or dispraise a man rises or falls; which may be things whereby he is characterized exclusively of his ancestors; and it may be that his ancestors are mentioned in such a manner that imperfection shall attach to him by reason of the blaming of them. respecting this there is no disagreement among the lexicologists, except IKt [whose objection see in what follows]: (Abu-l-'Abbás, O:) or (accord. to some, S) grounds of pretension to respect on account of the honourable deeds or qualities of one's ancestors, &c., ( HasabN , S, Msb, K,) and eminence, or nobility, ( $arafN ,) in which one glories. (K.) You say, fulaAnN kariymu AlEiroDi Such a one is generous, or noble, in respect of Hasab : and huwa *uw EiroDK he is a possessor of Hasab ; and of $araf . (TA.) ― -b7- Sometimes, Ancestors are meant by it. (A'Obeyd, K.) Thus you say, $atama fulaAnN EiroDa fulaAnK , meaning Such a one spoke evil of the ancestors of such a one. (A'Obeyd.) And fulaAnN jaribu AlEiroDi Such a one is base, or ignoble, in respect of ancestry. (TA.) IKt disallows this signification, asserting EiroDN to have no other signification than those of a man's nafos and his badan : (O, * TA:) but I Amb says that this is an error; as is shown by the saying of Aboo-Miskeen Ed-Dárimee, rub~a mahozuwlK samiynN EiroDuhu wasamiyni Aljisomi mahozuwlu AlHasabo in which EiroD cannot be syn. with badan and jisom , for, were it so, it would involve a contradiction; the meaning being only Many a person meagre in respect of his body is noble [or great ] in respect of his ancestry; [ and fat in respect of the body, meagre in respect of grounds of pretension to honour on account of the honourable deeds or qualities of his ancestors, &c.:] and by Mohammad's using the expression damuhu waEiroDuhu ; for if EiroD were [here] syn. with nafos , it had sufficed to say dmh without ErDh . (O, TA.) ― -b8- Also A natural disposition that is commended. (IAth, K.) ― -b9- And A good action. (TA.) -A5- Also One who speaks evil of men ( yaEotariDuhumo ) falsely; (O, K;) applied to a man: and so with EiroDanN applied to a woman: (O, K: *) so too ↓ p applied to a man, and with EaroDanN to a woman. (TA.)

definition: A thing that happens to, befalls, or occurs to, a man;
sourceDefinition: A thing that happens to, befalls, or occurs to, a man; such as disease, and the like; (S, O, K;) as disquietude of mind, and a state of distraction of the mind or attention: or a misfortune, such as death, and disease, and the like: (TA:) or an event that happens to a man, whereby he is tried: (As:) or a thing that happens to a man, whereby he is impeded; such as disease, or a theft: (Lh:) or a bane, or cause of mischief, that occurs in a thing; as also ↓ EaAriDN : (TA:) [both signify also an accident of any kind: ] pl. A^aEoraADN . (TA.) ― -b2- A thing's befalling, or hitting, unexpectedly. (O, K. [I follow the reading of the O, which is that of the K as given in the TA, and of my MS. copy of the K, A^ano yuSiyba Al$~aYo'u EalaY gir~apK ; in preference to that in the CK, A^ano tuSiyba Al$~aYo'a EalaY gir~apK .]) You say, A^aSaAbahu sahomu EaraDK (S, A, O, K *) and sahomN EaraDN , (A, TA,) and Hajaru EaraDK (S, O) and HajarN EaraDN , (TA,) [ A random arrow, and a random stone, or] an arrow, and a stone, aimed at another, hit him: (S, O, K:) such as hits, or falls upon, a man without any one's shooting it, or casting it, is not thus termed. (L.) And maA jaA='aka mina Alr~aA^oYi EaraDFA xayorN mim~aA jaA='aka musotakorahFA , i. e. [ The opinion ] that comes to thee without consideration, or thought, [ is better than that which comes to thee forced. ] (TA.) And Eul~iqotuhaA EaraDFA I became attached to her (S, O, K) accidentally, or unintentionally, (S, O,) in consequence of her presenting herself to me (ISk, S, O, K) as a thing occurring without my seeking it. (ISk.) [See an ex., in a verse of Antarah, cited in the first paragraph of art. zEm ; and another, in a verse of El-Aashà, cited in the first paragraph of art. Elq .] ― -b3- A thing that is not permanent: (Mgh, O, B, K.) so in the conventional language of the Muslim theologians: (Mgh:) opposed to jawoharN : (TA:) or hence metaphorically applied by the Muslim theologians to (tropical:) a thing that has not permanence unless in, or by, the substance; [i. e., in the language of old logicians, an accident; an essential, and an accidental (as meaning a non-essential ), property, or quality; or what modern logicians call a mode; whether it be, in their language, an essential mode or an accidental mode; which latter only they term “ an accident; ”] as colour, and taste: (B:) or, in the conventional language of the Muslim theologians ( Almutakal~imuwn [expl. in the TA as signifying “ the philosophers, ” from whom, however, they are generally distinguished]), a thing that subsists in, or by, another thing; (O, K;) as colours, and tastes, and smells, and sounds, and powers, and wills: (O: [and the like is said in the Msb:]) or, in philosophy, a thing that exists in its subject, or substance, and ceases therefrom without the latter's becoming impaired or annihilated; and also such as does not cease therefrom: the former kind being such as tawniness occasioned by an altered state of the body, and yellowness of complexion, and motion of a thing moving; and the latter kind, such as the blackness of pitch, and of [ the beads called ] sabaj , and of the crow. (L.) ― -b4- [Hence, An appertenance of any kind. ― -b5- Hence also,] The frail goods ( HuTaAm ) of the present world or state; (As, O, K;) and what a man acquires thereof: (As, O:) [so called as being not permanent:] or worldly goods or commodities, (AO, Msb,) of whatever kind, are thus called, with fet-h to the r : (AO:) and any property or wealth, little or much, (S, O, K,) is thus called, (K,) or is called EaraDu Ald~unoyaA . (S, O.) See also EaroDN , expl. as signifying “ a commodity, ” or “ commodities ” or “ goods. ” One says, Ald~unoyaA EaraDN HaADirN yaA^okulu minohaA Albar~u waAlfaAjiru [ The world is a present frail good: the righteous and the unrighteous eat thereof ]: (S, O, TA:) i. e. it has no permanence: a trad. related by Sheddád Ibn-Ows. (TA.) And in another trad. related by the same, it is said, layosa AlginaY Eano kavorapi AlEaraDi A_in~amaA AlginaY ginaY Aln~afosi [ Richness is not from the abundance of worldly goods: richness is only richness of the soul ]. (O, TA.) One says also, qado faAtahu AlEaraDu , (Yoo, S, L,) and ↓ AlEaroDu , but the former is the more approved, (L,) [ The property, &c., (but see another meaning below,) had escaped him ], which is from EaroDu Aljunodi , [see EaraDa ,] like as one says qabaDa qaboDFA and qado A^aloqaAhu fiY AlqabaDi : (Yoo, S:) [which seems to indicate that EaraDN properly signifies maEoruwDN , like as qabaDN signifies maqobuwDN .] ― -b6- Booty; spoil. (O, K.) So in the Kur ix. 42: (O:) or it there signifies ― -b7- i. q. maTolabN [app. meaning A thing sought, or desired; and object of desire; rather than a place where a thing is sought ]. (TA.) ― -b8- I. q. TamaEN [app. meaning A thing that is eagerly desired, or coveted: and also eager desire; or covetousness ]. (AO, O, K.) So explained by some as occurring in the saying qado faAtahu AlEaraDu , mentioned above. (TA.) And the following verse is also cited as an ex., mano kaAna yarojuw baqaA='F laA nafaAda lahu falaA yakuno EaraDu Ald~unoyaA lahu $ajanaA [ Whoso hopeth for continuance without cessation, let not the eager desire of worldly goods be to him a cause of anxiety ]. (O, TA.) ― -b9- A gift. (TA.) (Mgh.) And one says, huwa biEaraDK A^ano yaDiyEa [ He is exposed, or liable, to perish ]. definition: is of the measure fuEolapN in the sense of the measure mafoEwlN , like quboDapN ;
sourceDefinition: is of the measure fuEolapN in the sense of the measure mafoEwlN , like quboDapN ; (Bd, ii. 224;) and is applied to A thing that is set as an obstacle in the way of a thing: (Bd, TA:) and also to a thing that is exposed to a thing: (Bd:) or that is set as a butt, like the butt of archers. (TA.) You say, jaEalotu fulaAnFA EuroDapF lika*aA , meaning naSabotuhu lahu ; (S, O, K; *) i. e. I set such a one as an obstacle to such a thing: or as a butt for such a thing. (TA.) And huwa lahu duwnahu EuroDapN He is an obstacle to him intervening in the way of it. (S, O.) And fulaAnN EuroDapN liln~aAsi Such a one is [ a butt to men; i. e.] a person whom men cease not to revile: (S, O, Msb, K:) or a person to whom men address themselves to do evil, and whom they revile. (Az, TA.) And humo DuEafaA='u EuroDapN likul~i mutanaAwilK They are weak persons; persons who offer themselves as a prey to any one who would take them. (TA.) And it is said in the Kur [ii. 224], walaA tajoEaluwA A@ll~`hu EuroDapF liA^ayomaAnikumo A^ano tabar~uwA watat~aquwA watuSoliHuwA bayona Aln~aAsi , (S, * &c.,) meaning naSobFA ; (S, TA;) admitting the two significations of an obstacle and a butt: (TA:) i. e. And make not God an obstacle between you and that which may bring you near unto God, &c.: (O, K:) or make not God an obstacle to the performance of your oaths to be pious (O, Bd) and to fear God and to make reconciliation between men: or make not God an obstacle, because of your oaths, to your being pious &c.: (Bd:) or make not the swearing by God an obstacle to your being pious [&c.]: (Fr:) and Zj says the like of this: (L:) or EuroDapN signifies intervention with respect to good and evil; (Abu-l- 'Abbás, O, K;) and the meaning is, do not intervene by swearing by God every little while so as not to be pious &c.: (O, K, * TA:) or make not God an object of your oaths, by ordinary and frequent swearing by Him, (Bd,) or a butt for your oaths, like the butt of archers, (TA,) in order that ye may be pious &c.; for the habitual swearer emboldens himself against God, and is not pious &c.: (Bd:) or, as some say, the meaning is make not the mention of God a means of strengthening your oaths. (TA.) You say also, h`*aA EuroDapN laka as meaning This is a thing prepared for thy common, or ordinary, use. (O, TA.) ― -b2- A purpose; an intention; or an object of desire, or of endeavour; [as though it were a butt;] syn. him~apN . (S, O, K.) Hassán says, (S, O,) i. e. Ibn-Thábit, (O, TA,) waqaAla A@ll~`hu qado yas~arotu junodFA humu AlA^anoSaAru EuroDatuhaA All~iqaA='u [ And God said I have prepared an army: they are the Ansár; whose purpose, or the object of whose desire, is conflict with the unbelievers]. (S, O, TA. [In one copy of the S, in the place of yas~arotu , I find A^aEodadotu , which signifies the same.]) ― -b3- A pretext; an excuse. (MA.) ― -b4- One says also, fulaAnN EuroDapu *aAka , (S, O,) or EuroDapN li*aAka , (S, O, K,) Such a one is possessed of the requisite ability and strength for that: (S, O, K:) and EuroDapN lil$~ar~i possessed of strength to do evil, or mischief: and in like manner EuroDapN is applied to two things, and to more. (TA.) And fulaAnapu EuroDapN lilz~awoji (S, O, K) Such a female is possessed of sufficient strength for the husband; [i. e., to be married;] (TA;) or liln~ikaAHi for marriage. (A.) And naAqapN EuroDapN liloHijaArapi A she-camel having strength enough for [going upon] the stones. (S, O, K.) And [in like manner] A^asofaArK ↓ naAqapN EuroDu A she-camel having strength sufficient for journeys. (S, O, K. *) And h`*aA AlbaEiyri Als~afaru waAlHajaru ↓ EuroDu (S, O, K) The strength of this camel is sufficient for journeying and for going over stone. (IB.) -A2- EuroDapN also signifies A kind of trick, or artifice, in wrestling, (S, O, K,) by which one throws down men. (S, O.)

definition: An oblique course or motion: (A'Obeyd, L, TA:) and briskness, liveliness, sprightliness: and EiriDonapN signifies the same.
sourceDefinition: An oblique course or motion: (A'Obeyd, L, TA:) and briskness, liveliness, sprightliness: and EiriDonapN signifies the same. (TA. [See also EiriaD~aY .]) One says, yamo$iY AlEiraDonapa and ↓ AlEiraDonaY He goes along with a proud gait, (S, O, K,) inclining towards one side, (S, O,) by reason of his briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness. (S, O, K.) And ↓ taEoduw AlEiraDonaY and AlEiraDonapa and AlEiraDonaApa [perhaps correctly AlEiraDonaAta ] She (a mare) runs in a sidelong manner, one time in one direction and another time in another. (O, TA.) And yaEoduw AlEiraDonapa He (a man) runs so that he outstrips. (L, TA.) And naZarotu A_ilaY fulaAnK EiraDonapF I looked towards such a one from the outer angle of my eye. (S, O, K. *) The dim. of ↓ EiraDonaY is ↓ EurayoDinN ; the n being retained because it is a letter of quasi-coordination, and the Y suppressed because it is not such. (S, O.) ― -b2- Also, [app. for *aAtu EiraDonapK ,] A she-camel that goes along obliquely, (S, O, K,) by reason of briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness: pl. EiraDonaAtN . (S, O. [See, again, EiraD~aY .] But A'Obeyd disallows the application of this epithet to a she-camel. (TA in art. ErDn .) ― -b3- And A woman that has become broad by reason of her fatness and plumpness. (TA.)

EuruDN (TA) and A^aEaAriyDu . (Ham ubi suprà.) Hence the phrase in a trad. of Aboo-Hureyreh, faA^axa*a fiY EaruwDK A=xara (assumed tropical:) And he took another way of speech. (TA.) ― -b4- The place that is over against one, or on the opposite side to one, as he goes along. (S, O, K.) -A2- A she-camel that takes to a side, or tract, different from that which her rider would traverse; for which reason this epithet is applied to her: (O:) or that goes to the right and left, and does not keep to the road: (IAth:) or that has not been trained: (S, O, K:) or that has received some training, but is not thoroughly trained: (ISk:) or such as is termed ↓ EuroDiy~ap , stubborn in the head, but submissive in her middle part; that is loaded; and then the other loaded camels are driven on; and if a man ride her, she goes straight forward, and her rider has not the power of exercising his own free will [ in managing her ]. (Sh.) To such a camel, 'Omar likened a class of his subjects. (TA.) And 'Amr Ibn-Ahmar El-Báhilee says, A^uxib~u *aluwlFA A^awo EaruwDFA A^aruwDuhaA [ I make a submissive one to go the pace termed xabab , or an untrained one I train ]; meaning that he recites two poems; one of which he has made easy, and the other whereof is difficult: J gives a different reading, A^usiyru EasiyrFA , meaning A^usay~iru ; with the same explanation that is given above, of the former reading. (IB, O.) ― -b2- A camel, (S, O, TA,) in the K, erroneously, a sheep or goat, (TA,) that eats the thorns (S, O, K, TA) when herbage is unattainable by him. (S, O.) ― -b3- And i. q. EatuwdN [ A yearling goat, &c.]. (TA [See also EariyDN .]) -A3- Also i. q. kaviyrN , (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K,) [as meaning A large quantity or number ] of a thing [or of things], (K.) [or large in number, ] as in the phrase HaY~N EaruwDN [ A tribe large in number ]. (Ibn-'Abbád, O.) -A4- And Clouds; syn. saHaAbN ; (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K;) and gayomN . (K.) -A5- And Food. (Fr, O, K.) -A6- EaruwDu kalaAmK The meaning, or intended sense, of speech; syn. faHowaAhu , (ISk, S, O, K,) and maEonaAhu : (ISk, S, O:) as also kalaAmK ↓ miEoraADu , (K,) of which the pl. is maEaAriyDu and maEaAriDu . (TA.) One says Earafotu *a`lika fiY EaruwDi kalaAmihi [ I knew that in the intended sense of his speech ]; (ISk, S, O;) and kalaAmihi ↓ fiY miEoraADi ; (A, O;) and in like manner, maEaAriDi kalaAmihi : (L, TA:) and Earafotuhu fiY kalaAmihi ↓ miEoraADi and fY laHoni klAm and fY naHowi klAmh signify the same. (Msb.) [See also miEoraADN .] -A7- h`*ihi AlmasoA^alap EaruwDu h`*ihi This question is the like of this. (TA.) [See also EiraADN .] -A8- EaruwDN also signifies The transverse pole or piece of wood ( EaArDap ) which is in the middle of a tent, and which is its main support. (Aboo-Is-hák.) ― -b2- And hence, (Aboo-Is-hák,) The middle portion [or foot ] of a verse; (Aboo-Is-hák, O;) for the bayot of poetry is constructed after the manner of the bayot inhabited by the Arabs, which is of pieces of cloth; and as the ErwD of the latter is the strongest part, so should that of the former be; and accordingly we see that a deficiency in the Darob is more frequent than it is in the ErwD : (Aboo-Is-hák:) the last foot of the first half or hemistich (S, K) of a verse; (S;) whether perfect or altered: (K:) some make it to be the TaraAy^iq of poetry, and its Eamuwd : (TA:) [i. e. they liken it to these parts of the tents:] it is fem.: (K:) or sometimes masc.: (L:) the pl. is A^aEaAriyDu ; (S, O, K;) contr. to rule, as though pl. of A_iEoriyDN ; and one may use as its pl. A^aEaAriDu . (S, O.) ― -b3- Also [The science of prosody, or versification; ] the science of the rules whereby the perfect measures of Arabic verse are known from those which are broken; (Msb;) the standard whereby verse is measured: (S, O, K:) because it is compared ( yuEaAraDu ) therewith: (S, O:) or because what is correct in measure is thereby distinguished from what is broken: (K: [in which some other reasons are added, too futile, in my opinion, to deserve mention: I think it more probable that ErwD is used by a synecdoche for $iEorN , as being the most essential part thereof; and then, elliptically, for Eilomu AlEaruwDi , which is the more common term for the science:]) it is fem.; and has no pl., because it is a gen. n. (S, O.) -A9- See also EaAriDapN ; second and two following sentences. -A10- AlEaruwDu is a name of Mekkeh and El-Medeeneh, (S, O, Msb, K, TA,) and El-Yemen, (Msb, TA,) with what is around them. (S, O, K, TA.)

(Msb.) You say, EuraADapN and ↓ EuraADapN [ A broad, or wide, bow ]. (S.) And ↓ EuraADaAtN , (TA,) or A^avarFA ↓ EuraADaAtN , in which the latter word is in the accus. case as a specificative, (S, O, TA,) meaning Camels whose foot-marks are broad. (S, O, TA.) And fulaAnN EariyDu AlbiTaAni (assumed tropical:) Such a one is rich; or in a state of competence: (A, TA:) or possessed of much property. (S, * O, K, * TA. [See also art. bTn .]) And EariyDu AlqafaA (tropical:) Fat: (TA:) or (assumed tropical:) stupid. (Mgh.) And EariyDu AlwisaAdi (tropical:) Sleepy: (TA:) or (assumed tropical:) stupid, dull, or wanting in intelligence. (Msb in art. wsd .) duEaA='N EariyDN , occurring in the Kur [xli. 51], means (assumed tropical:) Large, or much, prayer, or supplication: (K, * TA:) or in this instance we may say long. (L.) -A2- Also A goat (As, O, K) that is a year old, (K,) or about a year old, (As, O,) and that takes [or crops ] of the herbage (As, O, K) and trees [or shrubs ] (As, O) with the side of his mouth: (K:) or (O, K) such as is termed Eatuwd [q. v.], (S, O,) when he rattles, and desires copulation: (S, O, K:) or a [ young ] goat above such as is weaned and below such as is termed ja*aE [q. v.]: or such as has pastured and become strong: or such as is termed ja*aE : or a young goat when he leaps the female: it is applied only to a male: the female is termed EariyDapN : with the people of El-Hijáz it means peculiarly such as is gelded: it is also applied to a gazelle that has nearly become a vaniY~ [q. v.]: (TA:) pl. EiroDaAnN and EuroDaAnN . (S, O, K.)

EiroDaAnN and EuroDaAnN . (S, O, K.)

sourceDefinition: [ Showing its breadth, or width; (see EaraDa , first signification;) or] having its side apparent: (TA:) and [in like manner] ↓ muEoriDN , q. v., anything showing its breadth, or width: [or its side: ] (TA:) [and hence, both signify appearing. (See again EaraDa .)] ― -b2- A collection of clouds appearing, or presenting itself, or extending sideways, (↓ muEotariDN ,) in the horizon; (S, O, K;) overpeering: (TA:) or a collection of clouds which one sees in a side of the sky, like that which is termed julobN , except that the former is white, whereas the latter inclines to blackness, and is narrower than the former, and more distant: (AZ:) or a collection of clouds that comes over against one ( muEaAriDFA ) in the sky, unexpectedly: (El-Báhilee, O:) or a collection of clouds that appears, or presents itself, or extends sideways, ( yaEotariDu ,) in the sky, like as does a mountain, before it covers the sky, is called saHaAbN EaAriDN , and also HabiY~N : (As, O:) pl. EawaAriDu . (TA.) [See also EaroDN and EiroDN .] In the phrase EaAriDN mumoTirunaA , in the Kur [xlvi. 23], mmTrnA means mumoTirN lanaA ; for as being determinate it cannot be an epithet to EaAriDN , which is indeterminate: and the like of this the Arabs do only in the instances of nouns derived from verbs; so that you may not say h`*aA rajulN gulaAmunaA . (S, O.) ― -b3- See also EaroDN , in the sentence commencing with “ A mountain, ” in two places: ― -b4- and again, shortly after. ― -b5- A gift appearing (As, S, O, K) from a person. (As, S, O.) [See an ex. voce EaAy^iDN .] ― -b6- [ Happening; befalling; occurring: an occurrence; as a fever, and the like. (See EaraDa lahu .)] A bane, or cause of mischief, that occurs in a thing; as also EaraDN , q. v. (TA.) And ↓ $ubohapN EaAriDapN A doubt, or dubiousness, occurring, or intervening, in the mind. (TA.) In the saying of 'Alee, yaqodaHu Al$~ak~u fiY mino $ubohapK ↓ qalobihi biA^aw~ali EaAriDapK , the word EArDp may perhaps be an inf. n., [or a quasi-inf. n.,] like EaAqibapN and EaAfiyapN : (TA:) [so that the meaning may be Doubt makes an impression upon his heart at the first occurrence of dubiousness. ] ― -b7- Whatever faces one, of a thing: (TA, and so in some copies of the K: in other copies of the K, this signification is given to ↓ EaAriDapN :) or anything facing one. (O.) ― -b8- Intervening; preventing: an intervening, or a preventing, thing; an obstacle: (TA:) a thing that prevents one's going on; such as a mountain and the like. (Msb.) [Its application to a cloud, and some other applications to which reference has been made above, may be derived from this signification, or from that next preceding, or from the first.] ― -b9- I. q. EuroDN , in the first of the senses assigned to this latter above; as also ↓ EaAriDapN . (The former accord. to some copies of the K: the latter accord. to others: but both accord. to the TA.) ― -b10- What appears, of the face, (K,) or of the mouth, accord. to the L, (TA,) when one laughs. (L, K, TA: but in some copies of the K, and in the O, this signification is given to ↓ EaAriDapN .) ― -b11- The side of the cheek (K, TA) of a man; (TA;) as also ↓ EaAriDapN ; (O, L, K;) the two sides of the two cheeks of a man being called the EaAriDaAni , (Msb, TA,) or the ↓ EaAriDataAni : (S:) the two sides of the face: (Lh, O, K:) or the side of the face; as also ↓ EaruwDN ; the two together being called the EaAriDaAni : (Lh, TA:) or this last signifies the two sides of the mouth: or the two sides of the beard: pl. EawaAriDu . (TA.) xafiyfu AlEaAriDayoni means Light, or scanty, in the hair of the two sides of the cheeks, (S, O, Msb,) and of the beard; (O;) being elliptical. (Msb.) But in a certain trad., in which a happy quality of a man is said to be xif~apu EaAriDayohi , the meaning is said to be (tropical:) His activity in praising and glorifying God; i. e. his not ceasing to move the sides of his cheeks by praising and glorifying God. (IAth, on the authority of El-Khattábee; and O.) ― -b12- The side of the neck; (K;) the two sides thereof being called the EaAriDaAni : (IDrd, O:) pl. as above. (TA.) [See also EuroDN , near the beginning.] ― -b13- The tooth that is in the side of the mouth: (TA; and K, as in some copies of the latter; but in other copies, this signification is given to ↓ EaAriDapN :) pl. as above: (K:) or the side of the mouth; (S;) and so, as some say, EawaAriDu ; (TA;) [meaning the teeth in the side of the mouth; for] you say AimoraA^apN naqiy~apu AlEaAriDi , (S,) and AlEawaAriDi , (TA,) a woman clean in the side of the mouth: (S, TA:) and Jereer describes a woman as polishing her EaAriDaAni with a branch of a beshámeh, [a tree of which the twigs are used for cleaning the teeth,] meaning, as Aboo-Nasr says, the teeth that are after the central incisors, which latter are not of the EwArD : or, accord. to ISk, EaAriDN signifies the canine tooth and the Diros [or bicuspid ] next thereto: or, as some say, what are between the central incisor and the [ first ] Drs [which is a bicuspid ]: (S, O:) some say that the EwArD are the central incisors, as being [each] in the side of the mouth: others, that they are the teeth next to the sides of the mouth: others, that they are four teeth next to the canine teeth, and followed by the A^aDoraAs : Lh says that they are of the ADrAs : others, that they are the teeth that are between the central incisors and the ADrAs : and others, that they are eight teeth in each side; four above, and four below. (TA [from the O &c.].) -A2- EaAriDN as applied to a she-camel, or a sheep or goat: see the paragraph next following. -A3- Giving a thing, or the giver of a thing, in exchange, for ( mino ) another thing. (TA.) ― -b2- A reviewer of an army, or of a body of soldiers, who makes them to pass by him, and examines their state. (S.) -A4- See also the next paragraph; last three sentences.

(S.) ↓ EaruwD has the signification above assigned to it in the saying, fulaAnN rakuwDN bilaA EaruwDK [ Such a one is running without any want that has occurred to him ]. (S, O. [In the K, in the place of rkwD , we find rabuwDN , which I think a mistake.]) [In Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 555, we find ↓ rakuwDN fiY kul~i EaruwDK , which is expl. as meaning Running swiftly in every region; and said to be applied to him who disseminates evil, or mischief, among men.] -A2- A she-camel having a fracture or a disease, (S, O, K,) for which reason it is slaughtered; (S;) as also ↓ EaAriDN : (O, K:) and in like manner, a sheep or goat: (TA:) pl. EawaAriDu . (S.) It is opposed to EabiyTN , which is one that is slaughtered without its having any malady. (S, O.) One says, banuw fulaAnK laA yaA^okuluwna A_il~aA AlEawaAriDa [ The sons of such a one do not eat any but camels such as are slaughtered on account of disease ]; reproaching them for not slaughtering camels except on account of disease befalling them. (S, O.) ― -b2- EawaAriDu , applied to camels, also signifies That eat the [ trees called ] EiDaAh , (S, L,) wherever they find them. (L.) -A3- [ A thing lying, or extending, across, or athwart; any cross piece of wood &c.: so in the present day.] ― -b2- The [ lintel, or] piece of wood which holds the EiDaAdataAni [or two side-posts ], above, of a door; corresponding to the A^usokuf~ap [or threshold ]; (S, L;) the upper piece of wood in which the door turns. (O, K. [In some copies of the latter, this signification is erroneously given to EaAriDN .]) The EaAriDataAni of a door are also [said to be] the same as the EiDaAdataAni . (TA, voce EatabapN .) ― -b3- A [ rafter, or] single one of the EawaAriD of a roof: (S, O, K: [but in some copies of the last, and in the TA, this signification is erroneously given to EaAriDN :]) the EwArD of a house are the pieces of wood of its roof, which are laid across; one of which is called EaAriDapN : and EaAriDN [a mistranscription for EawaAriDu ] also signifies the saqaAy^if [or pieces of wood which form the roof ] of a [ vehicle of the kind called ] maHomil . (L.) -A4- Also, (S, and so in some copies of the K,) or ↓ EaAriDN , (as in other copies of the K,) or both, (TA,) Hardiness: (S, K, TA:) and this is what is meant by its being said, in [some copies of] the K, that EaAriDN is also syn. with EaAriDapN ; (TA;) [for in some copies of the K, after several explanations of AlEaAriDu , we find waAlEaAriDapu waAls~in~u Al~atiY fiY EuroDi Alfami ; whereas, in other copies, the w before Als~in~u is omitted:] courage; or courage and energy: (S, K, TA:) power of speech: (S:) perspicuity, or chasteness, of speech; and eloquence: (K, TA:) or the former signifies intuitive knowledge ( badiyhapN ): or determination, resolution, or decision: (A:) and the trimming of speech or language, and the removal of its faults: and good judgment. (TA.) You say, fulaAnN *uw EaAriDapK (AZ, IDrd, S, O, TA) Such a one is possessed of hardiness; (S, TA;) as also ↓ *w EaAriDK ; (TA;) and of courage, or courage and energy; and of power of speech: (S:) or of eloquence, (AZ, IDrd, O,) and perspicuity, or chasteness, of speech. (IDrd, O.) And fulaAnN $adiydu AlEaAriDapi Such a one is hardy; (Kh, O, TA;) as also ↓ $adiydu AlEaAriDi ; (TA;) and courageous, or courageous and energetic. (Kh, TA.)

(O, K. [In some copies of the latter, this signification is erroneously given to EaAriDN .]) The EaAriDataAni of a door are also [said to be] the same as the EiDaAdataAni . definition: The place of the appearance, [or occurrence, ] and of the showing, or exhibiting, or manifesting, and of the mentioning, and of the intending, or purposing, of a thing.
sourceDefinition: The place of the appearance, [or occurrence, ] and of the showing, or exhibiting, or manifesting, and of the mentioning, and of the intending, or purposing, of a thing. (Msb.) You say, qatalotuhu fiY maEoriDi ka*aA I slew him in the place of the appearance [or occurrence &c.] of such a thing. (Msb.) And *ikoru A@ll~`hi A_in~amaA yakuwnu fiY maEoriDi Alt~aEoZiymi The praise and glorification of God is only in the place [or case ] of the appearance, [or of the manifesting, ] and of the intending, or purposing, of magnifying. (Msb.) [And hence, fiY maEoriDi ka*aA also signifies In the time, or case, or on the occasion, of the appearance, &c., of such a thing. And In the state, or condition, or manner, which is indicative of such a thing: thus virtually agreeing with the phrase fiY miEoraDi ka*aA , q. v. infrà.] ― -b2- Also A place for the sale of slaves or beasts. (MA.) -A2- And Pasturage that renders the cattle in no need of their being fed with fodder. (TA.)

definition: Anything showing its breadth, or width;
sourceDefinition: Anything showing its breadth, or width; [or its side; as also ↓ EaAriDN .] (TA. See the latter word.) [And hence, Appearing, as also the latter.] And i. q. muEotariDN [app. as signifying Presenting itself; or occurring ]. (Sh.) And Anything putting its breadth, or width, [or side, (as is shown by an explanation of A^aEoraDa ,)] in one's power. (TA.) You say, Al$~aYo'u muEoriDN laka , meaning The thing is in thy power; apparent to thee; not offering resistance to thee. (IAth, O. *) ― -b2- And TaA^o muEoriDFA Hayovu $iy^ota [ Tread thou or] put thy feet where thou wilt, fearing nothing, for it is in thy power to do so. (S, O.) ― -b3- Aid~aAna muEoriDFA (occurring in a saying of 'Omar, K, or, as some relate it, daAna muEoriDFA , K in art. dyn ,) means He bought upon credit, or borrowed, or sought or demanded a loan, [ doing so (TA)] of whomsoever he could, (AZ, S, A, Mgh, O,) not caring what might be the consequence: (S, O:) or addressing himself to any one who came in his way: (Sh, K:) or turning away from such as said Thou shalt not buy on credit, or borrow: (IAth:) or avoiding payment: (TA:) or from any quarter that was easy and practicable to him, without caring, (O, K,) and without being perplexed: (O:) or he incurred the debt without caring for not paying it, or for what might be the consequence: (As:) or he contracted a debt with every one who presented himself to him: (K in art. dyn :) Sh says that the making mErDA to signify mumokinFA is improbable; because it is in the accus. case as a denotative of state with respect to [the agent implied in the verb] Ad~An ; and if you explain it as meaning he took it from him who enabled him, then mErDA applies to him whom he accosts, for he is the mmkn ; [he suggests also, that the meaning may be he bought upon credit, or borrowed, largely; for] he adds that mErDA may be from A^aEoraDa vawobu Almalobasi , signifying Ait~asaEa and EaruDa . (TA.) ― -b4- A^aroDN muEoriDapN , or muEoraDapN , (K, TA, [the former only in the CK,]) means Land wherein is herbage which the camels, or the like, depasture [app. at random ] when traversing it. (O, K.) -A2- See also muEar~iDN , last sentence.

definition: An arrow having no feathers (As, S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) nor head, (As,) slender at the two extremities, and thick in the middle, (O, K,) being in form like the wooden implement wherewith cotton is...
sourceDefinition: An arrow having no feathers (As, S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) nor head, (As,) slender at the two extremities, and thick in the middle, (O, K,) being in form like the wooden implement wherewith cotton is separated from its seeds, or is separated and loosened [ by striking therewith the string of a bow ], (O, TA,) which goes sideways, (Mgh, [in the O and TA, musotawiyFA , app. a mistranscription, for musotaEoriDFA ,]) striking with its EaroD [or middle part, unless this be a mistake for EuroD , or side ], (Mgh, [in my copy of which, ErD is without any vowel-sign,] and K,) not with its extremity: (Mgh, K:) sometimes, it strikes with its thick middle part in such a manner that it breaks and crushes what it strikes so that it is like the thing that is beaten to death; and if the object of the chase be near to it, it strikes it with the place of the head thereof: if it make a hole, the game smitten with it may be eaten; but not if it strike with a middle part ( biEaroDK ). (O, TA.) -A2- An oblique, indirect, obscure, ambiguous, or equivocal, mode of speech; as when thou askest a man, “ Hast thou seen such a one? ” and he, having seen him, and disliking to lie, answers, “ Verily such a one is seen: ” (Msb:) from Ear~aDa [q. v.]: (Msb, El-Munáwee: the latter in explaining a trad., q. v. infrà:) i. q. taworiyapN [signifying as above; or the pretending one thing and meaning another; or the using a word, an expression, or a phrase, which has an obvious meaning, and intending thereby another meaning to which it applies but which is contrary to the obvious one ]; the original meaning of which is concealment: (Msb:) or language whereof one part resembles another in the meanings: (O, TA: [in the TA immediately follows the exemplification cited above, from the Msb; whence it seems that this explanation is itself somewhat of a mErAD , meaning what it does not clearly express:]) or AlmaEaAriyDu fiY AlkalaAmi [thus, with the pl. form, in two copies of the S, and in the TA,] signifies Alt~aworiyapu biAl$~aYo'i Eani Al$~aYo'i [the pretending, or making believe, a thing instead of another thing ]: (S:) and maEaAriDu AlkalaAmi and ↓ A^aEoraADuhu signify the same as maEaAriyDuhu . (TA.) [ maEaAriDu is a contraction of maEaAriyDu , like as miEorDN is said to be of miEoraADN when syn. therewith.] It is said in a prov., (S,) a trad., (TA,) A_in~a fiY AlmaEaAriyDi lamanoduwHapF Eani Alka*ibi [ Verily, in oblique, indirect, obscure, ambiguous, or equivocal, modes of speech is ample scope, freedom, or liberty, ( saEapN , S,) to avoid lying; or, as is said in the L in art. ndH , that which renders one in no need of lying ]. (S, Msb.) One says also, Earafotuhu fiY miEoraADi kalaAmihi , expl. voce EaruwDN which see in three places, and kalaAmihi ↓ fiY miEoraDi , rejecting the A : this latter is said by some of the learned to be a metaphorical expression, from miEoraDN signifying the “ garment in which girls are displayed, ” as though the meaning were (tropical:) [ I knew it ] in the form, or manner, and guise, and mould, of his speech; but this does not obtain in all kinds of speech; for it may not be said in cases of reviling; indeed it would be bad, in these cases, to use as a metaphor the garment of adornment: therefore the proper way is to say that miEoraDN is a contraction of miEoraADN . (Msb.) One also says AlA^alofaAZu maEaAriyDu AlmaEaAniY (tropical:) [ Words are the robes of meanings ]: and this phrase also is [said to be] taken from miEoraDN signifying the “ garment in which a girl is displayed; ” because words adorn meanings. (TA.)

definition: It (an affair) was, or became, hard, strait, or difficult, syn.
sourceDefinition: It (an affair) was, or became, hard, strait, or difficult, syn. Ai$otad~a ; (S, O, Msb;) and as though it were closed against one syn. Aisotagolaqa . (S, O.) You say, AEDl bihi AlA^amoru , (K, TA,) and bh ↓ EaDala , (IDrd, O, K,) and bh ↓ EaD~ala , (TA, and Ham p. 258,) and AEDlhu , (K, TA,) The affair was, or became, hard, strait, or difficult, to him, syn. A$td~ ; (IDrd, O, K, TA, and Ham ubi suprà) and as though it were closed against him, syn. Astglq . (TA.) ― -b2- And A^aEoDalaniY fulaAnN , (S,) or AEDl biY , (O,) Such a one's affair, or case, wearied me. (S, O.) Hence the phrase, in a trad. of 'Omar, A^aEoDala biY A^aholu Alkuwfapi , (O,) i. e. [ The people of El-Koofeh have caused that ] the means of effecting my object in their affair, or case, have become strait to me, (O, TA,) and the treating them with gentleness has become difficult to me: (TA:) from EuDaAlN , (O, TA,) as applied to a disease, (O,) or as meaning a “ hard, ” or “ difficult, ” affair, “ which one will not undertake, ” or “ [be able to] manage. ” (TA.) One says of a disease [such as is termed EuDaAl ], AEDl AlA^aTib~aA='a , and ↓ taEaD~alahumo , It overcame the physicians, (K, TA,) and wearied them. (TA.) ― -b3- See also 2.

definition: , (S, Mgh, L, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, L, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. , (L, Msb, K,) inf. n. EaqodN (Mgh, L, Msb) and taEoqaAdN [of which see an ex. in a verse cited voce ratamN , and which is properly an intensive or a frequentative form]; and ↓ Eq~dhu [which is also intensive or frequentative, inf. n. taEoqiydN ]; and ↓ AEtqdhu ; (L;) He tied the cord, or rope; knit it; complicated it so as to form a knot or knots; tied it in a knot or knots; tied it firmly, fast, or strongly; contr. of Hal~ahu ; (L;) syn. $ad~ahu : (K:) the etymologists assert that the primary signification of EaqodN is the contr. of Hal~N : that it was afterwards used in relation to sales, or bargains, contracts, &c.: and then, in relation to a firm determination of the mind. (MF.) [ Eaqada lahu liwaA='F He tied for him a banner, to a spear, is said of a man on appointing him to a command.] And one says, Eaqada Habolahu meaning (assumed tropical:) He exerted and prepared himself for action &c.: and laA yaEoqidu AlHabola (assumed tropical:) He is incompetent, or lacks power or ability, to do a thing, by reason of his abject state. (L.) ― -b2- Eaqada AlbayoEa , and AlEahoda , (S, L, Msb, * K, &c.,) and Alyamiyna , (L, Msb,) aor. as above, (L, K,) inf. n. EaqodN ; (L;) and AlEahoda ↓ Eq~d , (L,) and Alyamiyna , (L, Msb,) which latter form of the verb has a more energetic signification; (Msb;) He concluded, settled, confirmed, or ratified, the sale, or bargain, and the contract, compact, covenant, agreement, or league, (L, Msb, K,) and the oath. (L, Msb.) In the phrase waA@l~a*iyna Eaqadato A^ayomaAnukumo , or ↓ Eaq~adato , or ↓ EaAqadato , accord. to different readings, in the Kur [iv. 37], by the verb is meant ratification; and by AymAnkm , your oaths, or your right hands: (L:) [i. e., accord. to the first and second readings, the meaning is, And those whose contracts, or the like, ( Euhuwdahumo being understood,) your oaths, or your right hands, have ratified: and accord. to the third reading, and those with whom ( humo being understood) your oaths, or your right hands have ratified a contract, or the like.] One says also, Eaqada Ealayohimo EuquwdFA He imposed upon them obligations. (L.) And Eaqada Aljizoyapa fiY Eunuqihi He imposed upon himself the obligation to pay the [ tax called ] jzyp . (L, from a trad.) And Eaqadotu Ealayohi fiY ka*aA , and fY k*A ↓ EaAqadotuhu , I obliged him to do such a thing, by taking, or exacting, from him an engagement, or a security. (L.) Eaqada qalobahu EalaY Al$~aYo'i [ He settled, or determined, his heart, or mind, firmly upon the thing; (see the first sentence of this art.; and see also Eazama ;)] he held, adhered, or clave, to the thing [ with his heart, or mind; he knit his heart to it ]. (L.) See also 8. ― -b3- Eaqadato bi*anabihaA , said of a she-camel, (S, O, L,) She twisted her tail, as though tying it in a knot: (L:) this she does to make it known that she has conceived. (S, O, L.) ― -b4- Eaqada liHoyatahu He dressed his beard so as to make it knotted, and crisp, or curly: this they used to do in wars, and their doing so was forbidden by the Prophet: (O, L:) they did it from a motive of pride and self-conceit. (L.) ― -b5- Eaqada naASiyatahu [lit. He knotted his forelock ] means (assumed tropical:) he was angry, and prepared himself to do evil, or mischief. (A, O, L.) [See 2.] ― -b6- Eaqada Eunuqahu A_ilayohi (assumed tropical:) He had recourse, betook himself, or repaired, to him, for refuge, or protection; (O, L, K; *) heard by Is-hák Ibn-Faraj from an Arab of the desert: (L:) and so EakadahaA . (O.) ― -b7- Eaqada , (K,) or Eaqada biA^aSaAbiEihi , (O,) or Eaqada AlHisaAba , (MA,) aor. , (O, TA,) inf. n. EaqodN , (TA,) He numbered, counted, or reckoned, (M, A, O, K,) with his fingers [ by bending their tips down upon the palm, one after another, commencing with the little finger, and then by extending them in like manner ]. (MA, O.) ― -b8- Eaqada famu Alfaroji EalaY AlmaA='i [ The mouth of the vulva closed upon the sperma of the male]. (O.) ― -b9- Euqidati Als~ibaAEu (assumed tropical:) The beasts, or birds, of prey were restrained from injuring the cattle, and the like, by means of charms and talismans. (L, from a trad.) ― -b10- Eaqada Alt~aAja fawoqa raA^osihi , and ↓ AEtqdhu , He put the crown upon his head. (L.) ― -b11- Eaqada AlbinaA='a , (A, L,) [aor. ,] inf. n. EaqodN ; (L;) and ↓ Eq~dhu , (A, O, L, K,) inf. n. taEoqiydN ; (L;) He arched [or vaulted ] the building, or structure. (A, O, L, K.) ― -b12- And Eaqada AlbinaA='a biAljiS~i , aor. , inf. n. EaqodN , He cemented the building, or structure, with gypsum. (L.) ― -b13- Eaqada vamarahu , said of a plant, (M in art. vmr ,) or ↓ Eq~dhu , (K in that art., [in the CK Eq~d vamaruhu ,]) and Eaqada alone, (A, O, K, in art. Hbl , [see 4 in that art. and also in art. Elf ,]) [ It organized and compacted, or compactly organized, its fruit; and in like manner each verb is said of a fruit in relation to a fruit-stone, such as that of a date, and of a peach, &c.]. ― -b14- laA taEoqidu Ealayohi Als~aAy^imapu $aHomFA walaA laHomFA [ The pasturing cattle will not make upon it fat nor flesh ], said of a pasturage. (O in art. DrE .) ― -b15- Eaqada Al$~aHomu The fat became formed and compacted, and became apparent. (L.) ― -b16- Eaqada , (S, M, A, L, [in the O Eaqida , which is app. a mistranscription,]) aor. , (M, L,) inf. n. EuquwdN ; (A;) and ↓ tEq~d ; (Ks, S, O, L, K;) and ↓ AnEqd ; (M, A, L;) said of rob, (Ks, S, O, M, A,) and of tar, (Ks, S, O,) and of honey, (M, A, O,) and of expressed juice of fresh ripe dates, (K,) and the like, (Ks, S, M, O,) [generally meaning when boiled,] It thickened; became thick, or inspissated. (Ks, S, M, A, O, L, K.) ― -b17- [Hence, app.,] Eaqada baTonuhu [ His belly became constipated ]. (M voce Saraba , q. v.) -A2- Eaqidat , said of a bitch, (TK,) [aor. ,] inf. n. EaqadN , (O, L, K,) Her vulva clung fast to the head of the qaDiyb of the dog. (O, L, K, TK.) ― -b2- Eaqida , said of the tongue, (S, O, K, *) aor. , (S, [in the O , an evident mistake,]) inf. n. EaqadN , (S, O,) It had in it an impediment. (S, * O, * L, K. *) And, said of a man, He had an impediment in his tongue; was unable to speak freely; was tongue-tied. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, said of sand, It became moistened in consequence of much rain [ so as to cohere ]. (L.)

sourceDefinition: A knot; a tie; (L, Msb;) pl. EuqadN . (L.) [Hence Aln~af~aAvaAtu fiY AlEuqadi : see art. nfv . And AlEuqodapu meaning (assumed tropical:) The star a Piscium; as being in the place of the knot of the two strings: the same, app., that is called AlxayoTayoni ↓ Eaqodu , mentioned by Freytag under EiqodN . Hence also] one says, tHl~lt Euqaduhu [lit. His knots became loosed, or untied ], meaning (assumed tropical:) his anger became appeased. (S, A, O, K.) And fiY Euqodatihi DaEofN (assumed tropical:) In his judgment and his consideration of his own affairs is a weakness. (TA.) And HaSiyfu AlEuqodapi , occurring in a letter of 'Omar, means (assumed tropical:) [ Firm ] in judgment, and in the management, conducting, ordering, or regulating, of affairs. (TA in art. HSf .) And fiY lisaAnihi EuqodapN (S, O, L, K *) (assumed tropical:) In his tongue is an impediment [ as though it were tied ], or a distortion. (L. [See Eaqida .]) ― -b2- The knot, tie, or bond, (L,) or the obligation, (O, K,) of marriage, (O, L, K,) and of anything, (O, K,) as a sale and the like: (TA:) and the ratification (O, L, Msb) of marriage (O, Msb) &c., (Msb,) or of anything. (L.) It is said in a trad. relating to prayer, laka mino quluwbinaA Euqodapu Aln~adami , meaning [We offer to Thee, from our hearts, ] the ratification of the resolution to repent. (L.) ― -b3- A promise of obedience, or vow of allegiance, ratified to persons in acknowlegment of their being prefects, or governors: (O, L, K, * TA:) from Euqodapu AlHaboli [ the knot, or tie, of the cord or rope ]: (O:) thus in the saying, in a trad. of Ubeí, halaka A^aholu AlEuqodapi [ Those who have received the promise of obedience &c. have perished; virtually meaning the same as the saying in the sentence here following]. (L.) And [hence also] The prefecture over, or government of, a town, country, province, or the like: pl. EuqadN : (L, K, TA:) thus in the saying of 'Omar, halaka A^aholu AlEuqadi [ The possessors of the prefectures &c. have perished ]. (L.) ― -b4- Also A place where a knot, or node, is formed: and [particularly] an uneven juncture ( EavomN ) [of a bone] in the arm: (S, O, K:) thus in the saying, jubirato yaduhu EalaY EuqodapK [ His arm was set and joined unevenly, so that a node, or protuberance, was produced in the bone ]: (S, O:) and in like manner one says, jabara EaZomahu EalaY EuqodapK He set and joined his bone unevenly. (L.) ― -b5- [Hence also A joint, i. e. an articulation, of the fingers: and a bone of a finger, i. e. any one of the phalanges: it is used in both of these senses in the present day: and AlEuqodapu mina AlA^aSaAbiEi occurs in the Msb, in art. nml , in explanation of AlA^anomalapu ; which is generally expl. as meaning “ the head of the finger, ” or “ the portion in which is the nail. ” (See also maEoqidN .) ― -b6- A knot, or joint, of a cane and the like. And what is termed A knot in the horn of a mountain-goat (as in the S and K in art. Hyd ) and the like. ― -b7- A knot in a tree. ― -b8- A node, of a plant, whence a leaf shoots forth: a bud, or gem, of a plant: and any fruit, or produce, of a plant, forming a compact and roundish head; by some termed HasakapN , n. un. of HasakN , q. v. ― -b9- AlEuqodataAni signifies The nodes of a planet. (See tin~aynN .) ― -b10- And EuqodapN signifies also Any small nodous lump; such as the substance of a ganglion; see gud~apN : and a gland, or glandular body; see gunodubapN . And A knob in a general sense. ― -b11- And hence,] The penis of a dog (IAar, A, O, L, K) compressus in coitu, et extremitate turgens: otherwise it is not thus called: (IAar, O, L:) and when this is the case, the epithet ↓ A^aEoqadu is applied to the dog. (IAar, O.) -A2- Also An estate consisting of land, or of land and a house, or of a house or land yielding a revenue, or of a house and palm-trees, or the like, syn. DayoEapN , (S, A, O, L, K,) and EaqaArN , which a person has acquired ( AiEotaqadahu ) as a possession. (O, L, K.) ― -b2- Any land abounding with herbage (K, TA) and with trees. (TA.) A place abounding with trees or palm-trees; (S;) or with trees and palm-trees; (O, L, K;) or with trees of the kinds called rimov and Earofaj , or, accord. to some, not of the latter kind, (L, TA,) serving for pasturage: (TA:) or a garden of many palm-trees, surrounded by a wall: and a town, or village, abounding with palm-trees, the crows of which are not made to fly away: (Ibn-Habeeb, L:) [whence] it is said in a prov., A=lafu mino guraAbi EuqodapK [ More familiar than the crow of a place abounding with trees or palm-trees ]; because its crow is not made to fly away, (S, O, L, K, [or, as in some copies of the S and K, does not fly away,]) on account of the abundance of its trees; (K;) [or mino guraAbi Euqodapa than the crow of ' Okdeh; for] Euqodap is perfectly decl. as a name for any fruitful land, and is imperfectly decl. as a proper name of a particular land (O, K) abounding with palmtrees. (O.) Also Herbage, or pasturage, sufficient for camels: (O, K:) or a place abounding with herbage, or pasturage, sufficient for cattle. (TA.) And Pasturage such as is termed janobap , (O, L, K, [in the CK janabap , and in my MS. copy of the K junobap ,]) remaining from the next preceding year; also termed EurowapN : (O, L:) or remains of pasturage: (L:) pl. EuqadN (O, L) and EiqaAdN . (L.) And accord. to the copies of the K, it signifies also Camels, or cattle, that are constrained to feed upon trees: but [this is evidently a mistake; for] it is said in the L, [as also in the O,] sometimes camels, or cattle, are constrained to feed upon trees, and these [ trees ] are termed Euqodap and Eurowap ; but while the janobap exists, the trees are not termed Euqodap nor Eurowap . (TA.) ― -b3- Also Anything whereby a man feels himself to be well established, and whereon he relies; from the same word signifying “ a garden of many palmtrees, surrounded by a wall; ” because, when a man has this, he considers his condition to be well established: (L, TA:) or a thing, (K, TA,) or an estate consisting of land or of land and a house &c., ( EaqaArN , O,) in which is a sufficiency for a man: (O, K, TA:) pl. EuqadN . (TA.) -A3- See also EiqodN .

definition: A she-camel that has confessed herself to have conceived;
sourceDefinition: A she-camel that has confessed herself to have conceived; (S, O, K;) or that has closed her vulva upon the sperma of the stallion; (L;) for she then twists her tail as if tying it in a knot, and it is thereby known that she has conceived: (S, O, L:) and a she-camel twisting her tail as if tying it in a knot, (L,) or that has so twisted her tail, (O,) on the occasion of her conceiving; (O, L;) in order that it may be known that she has conceived: (O:) pl. EawaAqidu . (L.) ― -b2- And A she-gazelle having the end of her tail twisted [ as if tied in a knot ]: or bending her neck in lying down: or raising her head in fear for herself and her young one. (L.) And A gazelle putting his neck upon his rump, (O, L,) having bent it to sleep: (TA:) or having put his neck upon his rump: (K:) pl. as above. (O, L.) ― -b3- And one says, jaA='a EaAqidFA Eunuqahu , meaning He came twisting his neck by reason of pride. (A, O, L.) ― -b4- EaAqidN is also applied as an epithet to A^aqiT [q. v.] meaning That of which the water has gone, and which is thoroughly cooked. (AHát, TA voce kavo'N .) -A2- Also The [ space called the ] Hariym [q. v.] of a well; (S, M, O, K;) and what is around it, ( maA Hawolahu , S, M, TA,) i. e. what is around the Hrym : in the K [and O], mA HuwolahaA , i. e. what is around the well; but the former is the right. (TA.)

definition: The place of the Eaqod [or tying, &c.
sourceDefinition: The place of the Eaqod [or tying, &c.,] of a thing: (Msb:) pl. maEaAqidu . (S, O: in which this is similarly explained.) maEoqidu HabolK signifies The place of a cord, or rope, where it is tied, knit, or tied in a knot or knots. (L.) [Hence,] one says, huwa min~iY maEoqida AlA_izaAri [lit. He is, in respect of me, in the place of the tying of the waistwrapper ], meaning he is near to me in station, standing, or grade: (S, O, L, K:) and in like manner, maqoEada AlqaAbilapi : (TA:) maEoqida AlA_izaAri being an adverbial phrase having a special application, but used as one not having such an application. (L.) ― -b2- And A joint, an articulation, or a place of juncture between two bones. (L. [See also EuqodapN , in the latter part of the former half.]) ― -b3- A^asoA^aluka bimaEaAqidi AlEiz~i mino Earo$ika i. e. I ask Thee by the properties wherein consists the title of thy throne to glory, or by the places wherein those properties are [ as it were ] knit together, properly meaning by the glory of thy throne, is a phrase used in prayer, of which, IAth says, the party of Aboo-Haneefeh disapprove. (L.) ― -b4- For another meaning of the pl., maEaAqidu , see EaqodN .

sourceDefinition: I took to, or set about, the affair ( A^axa*otuhu [for A^axa*otu fiyhi or A^axa*otu A^afoEaluhu ]) with ungentleness, roughness, violence, or vehemence. (S, O, Msb, K, TA. [See also 4.]) I entered into, engaged in, did, or performed, the affair, ( A^atayotuhu ,) not having knowledge in it: (O, K, TA:) or (K) I was ignorant of the affair; (O, K, TA;) and found it troublesome, or difficult, and hard, to do; (TA;) whence the saying (O, TA) of Ru-beh, (TA,) biA^arobaEK laA yaEotanifona AlEanaqaA [ With four legs not ignorant of the pace termed Eanaq ]: (O, TA:) and [simply] I had no knowledge in the affair: (O:) and AEtnft Al$~aYo'a I took to, or set about, the thing, ( A^axa*otuhu [as above],) or I entered into, engaged in, did, or performed, the thing, ( A^atayotuhu ,) not being skilled, nor having knowledge, in it. (TA. (See, again, 4.]) ― -b2- Also [simply] I began, or commenced, the affair: (O, * K:) some of the Benoo-Temeem use the phrase [thus] in the sense of Aiy^otanafotuhu : (Lth, O, TA:) an instance of AlEanoEanapu . (TA.) See also Eunofap . ― -b3- And AiEotanafonaA AlmaraAEiYa We pastured [our cattle] upon the herbage that had not been pastured upon before, of the pasturages: (O, K: but the latter has AEtnf in the place of AEtnfnA :) an instance of the EanoEanap of Temeem. (O.) ― -b4- And AEtnf Almajolisa He removed from the sitting-place; (K, TA;) like Aiy^otanafa : (TA:) Esh-Sháfi'ee, after recommending that a man when he is drowsy in the sitting-place [in the mosque] on Friday, and finds another sitting-place without his treading therein upon any one, should remove from it, says, waA@EotinaAfu Almajolisi maA ya*oEaru Eanohu Aln~awoma [i. e. And the removing from the sitting-place is a cause of scaring from him sleep ]: making AlAiEotinaAfu to be the putting himself in motion, and removing from place to place; which is like AlAiy^otinaAf [or the beginning, or commencing, anew]. (Az, O.) ― -b5- AiEotanafotu AlT~aEaAma I disapproved, or disliked, the food that I had eaten; (El-Báhilee, O, K, * TA;) it disagreeing with me. (Az, TA.) And AiEotanafotu AlA^aroDa I disliked the land, (S, O, K, TA,) and deemed it insalubrious. (TA.) And AiEotanafatoniY AlbilaAdu , (O,) or AlA^aroDu , (K,) The country, or the land, disagreed with me, or was unsuitable to me. (O, K.) ― -b6- AEtnf AlT~ariyqu [perhaps AuEotunifa (see the part. n.)] The road swerved from the right course. (TA.)
