sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, * K, TA,) aor. yaEuwlu , (S, O, Msb,) inf. n. EawolN (S, O, Msb, K) and EiyaAlapN (S, O, K) and EuwuwlN ; (K;) He fed, nourished, or sustained, his family, or household, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, * K, [in the Msb, Alyatiyma , the orphan, ]) and expended upon them: (S, Mgh, O:) or he supplied them with what they needed of food and clothing and other things: (TA:) and ↓ A^aEaAlahumo and ↓ Eay~alahumo signify the same. (K.) One says, Eulotuhu $ahorFA I supplied him with his means of subsistence for a month. (S, O.) And it is said in a trad., AibodaA^o bimano taEuwlu i. e. [ Begin thou ] with those whom thou sustainest, and whose expenses are incumbent on thee; and if anything remain over and above, let it be for the strangers, or those who are not related to thee. (TA.) -A2- And EAl , (Ks, K, TA,) aor. as above, (Ks, TA,) inf. n. EawolN and EiyaAlapN (K, TA) and EuwuwlN , (TA,) He had a numerous family or household; (K, TA;) [and] so ↓ AEAl , (Z, Mgh, O, Msb,) and ↓ A^aEowala , (Z, O, K,) and ↓ A^aEoyala , (Msb, K, TA,) this last formed by the change of w into Y , (TA,) [or formed from EiyaAlN ,] and Eyl [i. e. ↓ Eay~ala ]: (Msb:) ↓ AEAl is also expl. as meaning [simply] he had a family, or household: and ↓ A^aEowalato , occurring in a trad., as meaning she brought forth children, is said by IAth to be originally A^aEoyalato , signifying she had a family, or household; but Z says that AEylt is formed with a regard to the word EiyaAlN , and is not the original form. (TA.) [See also 4 in art. Eyl .] maA lahu EaAla wamaAla is a form of imprecation, meaning [ What ails him? ] May he have a numerous family or household, and may he decline from the right course in his judgment. (K. [See another explanation in art. Eyl .]) And the saying, in the Kur [iv. 3], *`lika A^adonaY A^al~aA taEuwluwA has been expl. as meaning [ That will be more, or most, apt, fit, or proper, ] that ye may not have numerous families or households. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence, probably,] EAl , aor. as above, [and yaEiylu , (see 1 in art. Eyl ,)] signifies also He (a man) was, or became, poor; (Ks, TA;) [and] so ↓ AEAl . (K.) And Yoo says that laA yaEuwlu EalaY AlqaSodi A^aHadN signifies laA yaHotaAju [app. meaning No one will become poor, or in want, while following the right course ]: (TA:) and so laA yaEiylu . (TA in art. Eyl .) -A3- EAl AlmiyzaAnu , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor. yaEuwlu and yaEiylu , (K, TA,) inf. n. EawolN and EayolN , (TA,) The balance inclined, or declined, (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) and rose: (Mgh, Msb:) or one of its extremities rose above the other: (TA:) or it was, or became, defective, and declined from the right state: or [in the CK “ and ”] it was, or became, excessive. (K, TA.) And [hence,] EAl fiY AlmiyzaAni (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, unfaithful; or he acted unfaithfully. (Msb.) A poet says, qaAluwA A@t~aboEonaA rasuwla A@ll~`hi waA@T~araHuwA qawola Alr~asuwli waEaAluwA fiY AlmawaAziyni [ They said, “ We have followed the way of the Apostle of God: ” but they have rejected the saying of the Apostle, (assumed tropical:) and been false in the balances, i. e., unfaithful ]. (S, O.) ― -b2- And EAl , (inf. n. EawolN , Msb,) He (a judge, Mgh) deviated from the right course, or acted wrongfully, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) fiY AlHukomi [ in the judgment ]. (S, O.) Hence, in the Kur [iv. 3, mentioned above], A^al~aA taEuwluwA [ that ye may not deviate from the right course ], (S, Mgh, O, Msb, TA,) accord. to Mujá- hid, (S, O, Msb,) and most of the expositors. (TA.) ― -b3- And hence, (S, Mgh, O,) in the opinion of A'Obeyd, (S, O,) EaAlati AlfariyDapu , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor. taEuwlu , (TA,) inf. n. EawolN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) The fariyDap [or primarily-apportioned inheritance ] deviated [ by excess ] from the limit of the named [ primary ] portions [which are all fractions of four and twenty]; (Bd in iv. 3;) [meaning] it rose [ above ], (S, O, Msb, K,) or exceeded, (K,) in the reckoning, (Msb, K,) [ the regular sum of the fixed primary portions, ] i. e., its [ fixed primary ], portions exceeded [ the regular sum thereof ], occasioning a diminution to the sharers: (S, Mgh, O, Msb:) AlEawolu in this case being the contr. of Alr~ad~u [which I do not find in any lexicon, but only in dictionaries of conventional terms]. (Msb.) Az relates, of El-Mufaddal, that, application having been made to him respecting [the shares of inheritance of] two daughters and a father and a mother and a wife, said, “ Her [the wife's] eighth has become a ninth: ” and A' Obeyd says, he meant that the [primary] portions had exceeded [the regular sum] so that there fell to the wife the ninth, whereas in the original case she would have had the eighth; for if the fryDp had not exceeded [the regular sum], it would have consisted of four and twenty; but when it [so] exceeded, it became of seven and twenty; and there pertained to the two daughters the two thirds [of four and twenty], i. e. sixteen portions; and to the father and the mother the two sixths, i. e. eight portions; and to the wife three reckoned as of seven and twenty, i. e. the ninth, whereas, before the exceeding, it would have been three of four and twenty, i. e. the eighth: and this question is called AlmasoA^alapu Alminobariy~apu , because 'Alee was asked respecting it when he was on the pulpit, and said, without premeditation, “ Her eighth has become a ninth. ” (TA.) Hence the saying, in a trad. of Maryam, [i. e. the Virgin Mary, respecting a story to which allusion is made in the Kur iii. 39, (see a note on that verse in Sale's Translation,)] waEaAla qalamu zakariy~aA='a i. e. [ And the divining-arrow of Zacharias ] rose upon the water. (TA.) ― -b4- And one says also, EAl zayodN AlfaraAy^iDa , (S, Mgh, O,) or AlfariyDapa , (Msb,) first pers. EulotuhaA , (K,) meaning Zeyd made the frAy^D , or fryDp , to be as described above; as also ↓ A^aEaAlahaA ; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K; *) which latter is the more common. (Msb.) ― -b5- EAl said of an affair, or event, It was, or became, hard to be borne, severe, or distressing, and great, or formidable. (S, O, K.) ― -b6- And also, (S, O, K,) aor. yaEuwlu , (S. O,) inf. n. EawolN , (TA,) It (a thing) overcame a person; burdened, or oppressed, him; (S, O, K;) distressed him; (Fr, O;) and disquieted him, or rendered him anxious. (K.) [See an ex. in a verse cited voce masaAfapN , in art. swf .] One says, Eiyla maA huwa EaAy^iluhu i. e. guliba maA huwa gaAlibuhu [ May he be overcome! Of what is he the overcomer? ]: (S, Meyd, O, K:) a prov., (Meyd,) applied to him at whose speech, or some other thing proceeding from him, (S, Meyd, O, K,) of a like sort, (K,) one wonders: (S, Meyd, O, K:) it is of the nature of a prayer, (S, Meyd, O,) for the man; (Meyd;) like the saying, when a thing pleases one, qaAtalahu A@ll~`hu , and A^axozaAhu A@ll~`hu . (TA.) And Eiyla SaboriY My patience was overcome; (S, O, K;) and so EaAla SaboriY : (Abu-l-Jarráh, Lh, K:) or, accord. to Aboo- Tálib, the former may mean rufiEa [i. e., was taken away, lit. raised; and if so, the latter may in like manner mean AirotafaEa ]. (TA.) EaAlati Albayoquwra , occurring in a verse of Umeiyeh Ibn-Abi-s-Salt, refers to a year of drought, and means It oppressed the [ wild ] oxen, by occasioning their having salaE and Eu$ar tied to their tails and set on fire, and being made to ascend upon the mountain; by the doing of which, the Arabs asserted that they obtained rain. (S, O. [See art. slE .]) ― -b7- EaAlaka EaAliyFA [in which EaAlaka app. signifies properly rafaEaka , the agent ( A@ll~`hu ) being understood,] is like the saying laEFA laka EaAliyFA , (K, TA, [in the CK laEA laka ,]) and is expl. in the T as meaning Mayest thou rise, or be raised, after stumbling, or falling. (TA.) ― -b8- Eiyla Eawoluhu [app. signifying lit. May the wailing for him be raised (in the CK EawolapF )] means may his mother be bereft of him; as also EaAla Eawoluhu . (K, TA.)

And Yoo says that laA yaEuwlu EalaY AlqaSodi A^aHadN signifies laA yaHotaAju [app. meaning No one will become poor, or in want, while following the right course ]: (TA:) and so laA yaEiylu . (TA in art. Eyl .) -A3- EAl AlmiyzaAnu , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor. yaEuwlu and yaEiylu , (K, TA,) inf. n. EawolN and EayolN , (TA,) The balance inclined, or declined, (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) and rose: (Mgh, Msb:) or one of its extremities rose above the other: (TA:) or it was, or became, defective, and declined from the right state: or [in the CK “ and ”] it was, or became, excessive. (K, TA.) And [hence,] EAl fiY AlmiyzaAni (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, unfaithful; or he acted unfaithfully. (Msb.) A poet says, qaAluwA A@t~aboEonaA rasuwla A@ll~`hi waA@T~araHuwA qawola Alr~asuwli waEaAluwA fiY AlmawaAziyni [ They said, “ We have followed the way of the Apostle of God: ” but they have rejected the saying of the Apostle, (assumed tropical:) and been false in the balances, i. e., unfaithful ]. (S, O.) ― -b2- And EAl , (inf. n. EawolN , Msb,) He (a judge, Mgh) deviated from the right course, or acted wrongfully, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) fiY AlHukomi [ in the judgment ]. (S, O.) Hence, in the Kur [iv. 3, mentioned above], A^al~aA taEuwluwA [ that ye may not deviate from the right course ], (S, Mgh, O, Msb, TA,) accord. to Mujá- hid, (S, O, Msb,) and most of the expositors. (TA.) ― -b3- And hence, (S, Mgh, O,) in the opinion of A'Obeyd, (S, O,) EaAlati AlfariyDapu , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor. taEuwlu , (TA,) inf. n. EawolN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) The fariyDap [or primarily-apportioned inheritance ] deviated [ by excess ] from the limit of the named [ primary ] portions [which are all fractions of four and twenty]; (Bd in iv. 3;) [meaning] it rose [ above ], (S, O, Msb, K,) or exceeded, (K,) in the reckoning, (Msb, K,) [ the regular sum of the fixed primary portions, ] i. e., its [ fixed primary ], portions exceeded [ the regular sum thereof ], occasioning a diminution to the sharers: (S, Mgh, O, Msb:) AlEawolu in this case being the contr. of Alr~ad~u [which I do not find in any lexicon, but only in dictionaries of conventional terms]. (Msb.) Az relates, of El-Mufaddal, that, application having been made to him respecting [the shares of inheritance of] two daughters and a father and a mother and a wife, said, “ Her [the wife's] eighth has become a ninth: ” and A' Obeyd says, he meant that the [primary] portions had exceeded [the regular sum] so that there fell to the wife the ninth, whereas in the original case she would have had the eighth; for if the fryDp had not exceeded [the regular sum], it would have consisted of four and twenty; but when it [so] exceeded, it became of seven and twenty; and there pertained to the two daughters the two thirds [of four and twenty], i. e. sixteen portions; and to the father and the mother the two sixths, i. e. eight portions; and to the wife three reckoned as of seven and twenty, i. e. the ninth, whereas, before the exceeding, it would have been three of four and twenty, i. e. the eighth: and this question is called AlmasoA^alapu Alminobariy~apu , because 'Alee was asked respecting it when he was on the pulpit, and said, without premeditation, “ Her eighth has become a ninth. ” (TA.) [ And the divining-arrow of Zacharias ] rose upon the water. (TA.) ― -b4- And one says also, EAl zayodN AlfaraAy^iDa , (S, Mgh, O,) or AlfariyDapa , (Msb,) first pers. EulotuhaA , (K,) meaning Zeyd made the frAy^D , or fryDp , to be as described above; as also ↓ A^aEaAlahaA ; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K; *) which latter is the more common. (Msb.) ― -b5- EAl said of an affair, or event, It was, or became, hard to be borne, severe, or distressing, and great, or formidable. (S, O, K.) ― -b6- And also, (S, O, K,) aor. yaEuwlu , (S. O,) inf. n. EawolN , (TA,) It (a thing) overcame a person; burdened, or oppressed, him; (S, O, K;) distressed him; (Fr, O;) and disquieted him, or rendered him anxious. (K.) [See an ex. in a verse cited voce masaAfapN , in art. swf .] One says, Eiyla maA huwa EaAy^iluhu i. e. guliba maA huwa gaAlibuhu [ May he be overcome! Of what is he the overcomer? ]: (S, Meyd, O, K:) a prov., (Meyd,) applied to him at whose speech, or some other thing proceeding from him, (S, Meyd, O, K,) of a like sort, (K,) one wonders: (S, Meyd, O, K:) it is of the nature of a prayer, (S, Meyd, O,) for the man; (Meyd;) like the saying, when a thing pleases one, qaAtalahu A@ll~`hu , and A^axozaAhu A@ll~`hu . (TA.) And Eiyla SaboriY My patience was overcome; (S, O, K;) and so EaAla SaboriY : (Abu-l-Jarráh, Lh, K:) or, accord. to Aboo- Tálib, the former may mean rufiEa [i. e., was taken away, lit. raised; and if so, the latter may in like manner mean AirotafaEa ]. (TA.) EaAlati Albayoquwra , occurring in a verse of Umeiyeh Ibn-Abi-s-Salt, refers to a year of drought, and means It oppressed the [ wild ] oxen, by occasioning their having salaE and Eu$ar tied to their tails and set on fire, and being made to ascend upon the mountain; by the doing of which, the Arabs asserted that they obtained rain. (S, O. [See art. slE .]) ― -b7- EaAlaka EaAliyFA [in which EaAlaka app. signifies properly rafaEaka , the agent ( A@ll~`hu ) being understood,] is like the saying laEFA laka EaAliyFA , (K, TA, [in the CK laEA laka ,]) and is expl. in the T as meaning Mayest thou rise, or be raised, after stumbling, or falling. (TA.) ― -b8- Eiyla Eawoluhu [app. signifying lit. May the wailing for him be raised (in the CK EawolapF )] means may his mother be bereft of him; as also EaAla Eawoluhu . (K, TA.)

definition: , (S, M, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, Msb, K,) aor. yagoduw , (S, M, Msb,) inf. n. Euduw~N (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and gadowN (M, TA, and so accord. to the CK instead of guduw~N [which is the only inf. n. commonly known]) and gudowapN , (K,) He went, or went away, in the time called gudowap , (Mgh, Msb,) i. e. [ the early part of the morning, ] the period between the prayer of daybreak and sunrise: this is the primary signification: (Msb:) or i. q. bak~ara [ he went forth early in the morning; in the first part of the day; or between the time of the prayer of daybreak and sunrise ]; so in the phrase gadaA Ealayohi [ he went forth early in the morning, &c., to him, or it ]; (K;) as also ↓ AgtdY : (S, * K:) and ↓ gAdAhu signifies the same as gadaA Ealayohi ; (S;) or the same as baAkarahu [which is syn. with bak~ara Ealayohi as expl. above; and signifies also, like bak~ara Ealayohi , he hastened to it, or to do it, at any time, morning or evening]: (ISd, K, TA:) Alguduw~u is the contr of Alr~awaAHu [inf. n. of raAHa ]. (S.) Hence, in the Kur [lxviii. 22], A^ani A@goduwA EalaY Harovikumo [ Saying, Go ye forth early, &c., to your land's produce ]: and the saying of a poet, waAlT~ayoru fiY wukunaAtihaA ↓ waqado A^agotadiY [ And sometimes, or often, I go forth early, &c., while the birds are in their nests ]. (TA.) ― -b2- Afterwards, by reason of frequency of use, it became employed as meaning He went, or went away, or departed, at any time. (Mgh, * Msb, TA.) Hence the saying, (Mgh, Msb,) of the Prophet, (Msb,) in a trad., (Mgh,) Augodu yaA A^unayosu , (Mgh, Msb,) meaning Depart then, O Uneys (Msb.) ― -b3- [Freytag bas erroneously assigned to it another meaning, i. e. “ Nutrivit ” misled by his finding tagoduwo put for tago*uw in art. TlY in the CK.] ― -b4- gadiYa : see 5.

sourceDefinition: : see gudowapN , in four places: though [properly] fem., and not heard as made mase., it may be made mase. if meant to be understood as signifying the “ first part of the day: ” (IAmb, Msb:) it is originally gadawapN , because its pl. is gadawaAtN . (IHsh, TA.) One says, ↓ A=tiyka gadaApa gadK [ I will come to thee in the early part of the morning, &c., of to-morrow ]. (S, TA.) biA@logadaApi waA@loEa$iY~i in the Kur [vi. 52 and xviii. 27] means After the prayer of daybreak and [ after ] the prayer of [ the period of the afternoon called ] the EaSor : or, accord. to some, [it means in the morning and the evening, or rather in the forenoon and the afternoon, for they say that] it denotes constancy of religious service: Ibn-'Ámir and Aboo-'Abd-erRahmán Es-Sulamee read waA@loEa$iY~i ↓ biA@logudowapi ; but the former is the common reading; and A 'Obeyd says, we think that they read thus following the handwriting, for it is written in all the copies of the Kur-án with w like AlS~alawp and Alz~akawp , and this is not an indication of the reading [which they have adopted], as the w in AlSlwp and Alzkwp is not pronounced [otherwise than as an] of prolongation except that it requires the fet-hah that follows to be uttered with a somewhat broad sound]. (TA.) ― -b2- huwa A@bonu gadaAtayoni means He is a son of two days [i. e. he is two days old ]. (TA.) ― -b3- The dim. is ↓ guday~apN : (TA:) or this is the dim. of ↓ gudowapN : (EM p. 56:) one says, A^arokabu A_ilayohi guday~apF [ I will ride to him, or it, in a short period of an early part of a morning, &c.]: and one says also, ↓ *atayotuhu guday~aAnaAtK [ I came to him, or it, in short periods of early parts of mornings, &c.]; an anomalous [pl.] dim. like Eu$ay~aAnaAt ; both of which are mentioned by Sb. (TA.)

definition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) and ↓ gadowapN , said by MF to be well known, and ↓ gidowapN , said by him to be rare, or disapproved, (TA,) The early part of the morning; the first part of the day; (K;) or the period between the time of the prayer of daybreak and sunrise; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ gadaApN , and ↓ gadiy~apN , (K, TA,) the last [in the CK gadoyapi , but correctly] a dial. var. of gudowapN , like DaHiy~apN a dial. var. of DaHowapN : (IAar, TA:) or ↓ gadaApN is syn. with DaHowapN [meaning the early part of the forenoon, after sunrise; accord. to some, when the sun is yet low; or, accord. to others, when the sun is somewhat high ]: (Msb:) [it may therefore be generally rendered morning, before, or after, sunrise: ] the pls. are gudFY , which is pl. of gudowapN ; (S, Msb, TA;) and gadawaAtN , (S, Msb, K, TA,) which is pl. of ↓ gadaApN ; (S, Msb, TA;) and ↓ guduw~N , (K, TA,) which is a pl. of gudowapN , formed by rejecting the p [of the sing.], or, accord. to the M, an anomalous pl. of ↓ gadaApN , or, as J says, [in the S,] referring to the phrase biA@logaduw~i waA@loA=SaAli , in the Kur [vii. 204 and xiii. 16 and xxiv. 36], biAlguduw~i there means biAlgadawaAti , and is a verb [i. e. an inf. n.] used to denote the time, as [is TuluwE ] in the saying TuluwEa Al$~amosi meaning fiY waqoti TuluwEi Al$ms ; (TA;) and gadiy~aAtN , (IAar, K, TA, [in the CK, erroneously, gadayAtN ,]) which is pl. of ↓ gadiy~apN ; (TA;) and gadaAyaA , (K, TA,) which is likewise a pl. of ↓ gadiy~apN , accord. to IAar, and, if so, regularly formed from gadaAyiwu , in the same manner as has already been expl. in the case of Ea$aAyaA [pl. of Ea$iy~apN , q. v. voce Ea$iY~N ]; by some said to be a pl. of gudowapN , but this has been controverted by IHsh in the Expos. of the “ Kaabeeyeh ” and by its commentator ['AbdEl-Kádir] El-Baghdádee; (TA;) or gadaAyaA is not used except in conjunction with Ea$aAyaA ; (K, TA;) one says, A_in~iY laA=tiyhi biAlgadaAyaA waAlEa$aAyaA [ Verily I come to him in the early parts of mornings and in the late parts of evenings ], for the purpose of conformity. (S, TA.) Zj says that when gudowap means The bukorap [or early part of the morning, &c.,] of the present day, or of a particular day, it is imperfectly decl.: and AHei says that it is thus accord. to the opinion commonly obtaining, as is also bukorap , each as being a generic proper name, like A^usaAmapu ; and that when you mean to generalize, you say, gudowapN waqotu na$aATK [ An early part of a morning is a time of briskness, liveliness, or sprightliness ]; and when you mean to particularize, laA^asiyran~a All~ayolapa A_ilaY gudowapa [ I will assuredly journey to-night until the early part of the morning ]: (TA:) [in the latter case also] one says, A^atayotuhu gudowapa [ I came to him in the early part of the morning of this, or of a particular, day ]; gdwp being here imperfectly decl. because it is determinate, like saHara ; but it is of those adv. ns. that may be used otherwise than as adv. ns.: you say, siyra EalaY farasika gudowapa and gudowapF [i. e. Journeying was performed on thy horse, or mare, in the gudowap of this, or of a particular, day, and in a gudowap ,] and gudowapN and gudowapN [i. e. the journey of the gudowap of this, or of a particular, day, and the journey of a gudowap , was performed (lit. was journeyed ) on thy horse, or mare, gudowapu and gudowapN being for. masiyrapu gudowapa and masiyrapu gudowapK , like as $ahorN in the Kur xxxiv. 11 is for masiyrapu $ahorK ]; what is with tenween, of these, being indeterminate, and what is without tenween being determinate. (S. [In one of my copies of the S, siro is put in the place of siyra : that the latter is the right is shown by the addition of gudowapu and gudowapN ; for each of these must be what is termed naAy^ibN Eano faAEilK i. e. a substitute for an agent.]) See also gadaApN , in two places.

definition: ― -b2- Also Whatever [ offspring ] is in [ any of ] the bellies of pregnant animals (AO, K, TA) of camels and of sheep or goats: (AO, TA:) or peculiarly of sheep or goats;
sourceDefinition: : see gadiY~N . ― -b2- Also Whatever [ offspring ] is in [ any of ] the bellies of pregnant animals (AO, K, TA) of camels and of sheep or goats: (AO, TA:) or peculiarly of sheep or goats; (K, TA;) thus in the dial. of the Prophet: (TA:) or it [virtually, in a trad. mentioned in what follows,] means the selling a camel, or other [ animal ], for what the stallion begets: or the selling a sheep for the offspring begotten by the ram: (K:) in all of which senses ga*iY~N and ga*awiY~N are [said to be] syn.: (K in art. g*w :) or gadawiY~N , (TA,) or ga*awiY~N , or, as some relate a verse of El-Farezdak in which it occurs, gadawiY~N , (S in art. g*w ,) means the selling a thing for the offspring begotten by the ram [or, as appears from what follows, by the stallioncamel ] in that year: gadawiY~N being a rel. n. from gadN : as though they rendered one desirous by saying, “ Our camels will bring forth and we will give thee to-morrow ( gadFA ): ” (S in art. g*w , and TA:) what is thus termed is forbidden in a trad.: a man used to buy, for a camel or a she-goat or money, what was in the bellies of pregnant animals; and this is a hazardous proceeding, and was therefore forbidden. (Nh, TA.) See also art. g*w . ― -b3- And see Eadawiy~apN , in art. Edw .

definition: The morning-meal, that is eaten between daybreak and sunrise;
sourceDefinition: The morning-meal, that is eaten between daybreak and sunrise; i. e. the meal, or repast, of the gudowap ; (K;) or of the gadaAp ; (Msb;) the meal, or repast, that is the contr. of the Ea$A=' : (S:) [it may therefore be rendered breakfast: but it is now commonly applied to dinner, which is eaten soon after the prayer of noon, and which is a lighter repast than the Ea$aA=' , i. e. supper:] Algdwp [app. ↓ Algadowapu ] as meaning AlgadaA='u is vulgar: (TA voce Ea$owapN :) the pl. of gadaA='N is A^ago*iyapN . (K.) And The [ meal, or the draught of milk, called ] saHuwr is thus termed; because it is to the person fasting the like of what it is to him who is not fasting. (TA.) ― -b2- Also The pasture of camels in the first part of the day. (TA.)

definition: , (S, Msb,) [and galaba Ealayohi ,] aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb,) [and galaba Ealayohi ,] aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. galabN and galobN , (S, K, TA,) the former of which is the more chaste, (TA,) or the latter is an inf. n. and the former is a simple subst., (Msb,) and galabapN , (S, K, TA,) [the most common form,] or this is a simple subst. like galabN , (Msb,) which is perhaps formed from it by the elision of the p , (Fr, S,) and magolabN and magolabapN , (K, TA,) which last is rare, (TA,) and galaAbiyapN and [in an intensive sense] gulub~aY and gilib~aY (K, TA) and gulub~apN (Lh, K, TA, said in the S to be syn. with galabapN ) and galub~apN , with fet-h to the g , (K, TA, in the CK glab~ap ,) and gilib~aA='u , (Kr, TA,) He, or it, overcame, conquered, subdued, overpowered, mastered, or surpassed, him, or it; gained ascendency or the mastery, prevailed, or predominated, over him, or it; or was, or became, superior in power or force or influence, to him, or it. (A, MA, K, PS, TK, &c.) [See also 5.] ― -b2- One says, galabotuhu Ealayohi meaning [ I overcame him in contending for it; i. e.] I took it, or obtained it, from him [ by superior power or force ]. (A.) And guliba fulaAnN EalaY Al$~aYo'i Such a one had the thing taken from him by superior power or force. (Mgh.) Hence the saying, laA tugolabuwA EalaY SalaApK qabola TuluwEi Al$~amosi waqabola guruwbihaA Be not ye overcome and anticipated by others in performing prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, so that the opportunity for your doing so escape you. (Mgh.) ― -b3- And galabahu EalaY nafosihi He forced him, or constrained him against his will. (A, TA.) ― -b4- [And galabahu AlA^amoru The affair overcame, defeated, or baffled, him. ] ― -b5- And galabahu biAlxawofi He exceeded him in fear. (S in art. xwf .) ― -b6- And galaba EalaY fulaAnK Alkaramu Generosity was, or became, the predominant quality of such a one. (TA.) ― -b7- And galaba A^ano yuxoTama [ He refused to have the xiTaAm (or leading-rope ) put upon him ]; said of a camel. (TA in art. xTm .) ― -b8- And A^ayugolabu A^aHadukumo A^ano yuSaAHiba Aln~aAsa maEoruwfFA meaning A^ayaEojizu [i. e. Is any one of you unable to associate with men kindly? ]. (A.) -A2- galiba , aor. , (K, TA,) inf. n. galabN , (S, * TA,) He was, or became, thick-necked: (K, TA:) or thick and short in the neck: or thick and inclining in the neck: from disease or other cause. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, MA, Msb, K, *) from AlmaAl , aor. yagonaY , (Msb,) inf. n. ginFY (S, * MA, Msb, K *) and ganaA='N , (MA, K, * TK, [but the latter is app. held by some to be a simple subst.,]) He was, or became, free from want; in the state, or condition, of having no wants; and also, of having few wants; or in a state of competence, or sufficiency; or rich, or wealthy; AlginaY being the contr. of Alfaqoru , as also AlganaA='u ; (K, TA;) and thus denoting the absence, or non-existence, of wants, which is [properly, or strictly speaking,] attributable to none but God; and also the paucity of wants; (TA;) or syn. with AlyasaAru : (S:) and the epithet applied to him of whom this is said is ↓ ganiY~N , (S:) or ↓ gaAnK , (Msb,) [or both, for] both signify the same [as will be shown below]. (K.) sourceDefinition: see 4. -A2- gn~Y , (S, MA, Msb,) inf. n. tagoniyapN , (KL,) as syn. with ↓ tgn~Y , (S, MA, Msb, *) He sang, or chanted, (S, * MA, KL;) or he trilled, or quavered, or prolonged his voice and modulated it sweetly, singing, or chanting. (Msb in explanation of the former.) You say gn~Ahu Al$~iEora [ He sang, or chanted, to him the poetry ], and gn~Y bihi [ he sang, or chanted, it, i. e., the poetry], inf. n. tagoniyapN ; and bihi ↓ tgn~Y ; tgn~Y and gn~Y having one and the same meaning. (K, TA.) biAlquroA=ni ↓ yatagan~aY , in a trad. cited in the first paragraph of art. A*n , means, as expl. by EshSháfi'ee, Reciting [or chanting ] the Kur-án with a plaintive and gentle voice. (Az, Msb, TA. [See also that trad. somewhat differently related voce taran~ama .]) ― -b2- gn~Y is also said of a pigeon, meaning It [ cooed, or] uttered a cry; (K, TA;) and so ↓ tgn~Y . (TA.) ― -b3- gn~Y biAlmaroA^api means tagaz~ala bihaA , (K, TA,) i. e. He mentioned the woman [ in amatory language, as an object of love, ] in his poetry: (TA:) and gn~Y bizayodK He eulogized Zeyd: or he satirized him: like ↓ tgn~Y in these two senses: (K, TA:) in that of eulogizing and that of satirizing: or, in the opinion of ISd, both of the verbs are used in these two senses and likewise in the sense mentioned immediately before them; meaning that he did thus after prolonging and modulating his voice; singing, or chanting, the same, i. e. the gazal and the eulogy and the satire. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: He (i. e. God, S, K, TA, [but wanting in the CK and app. in several copies of the K,]) rendered him, or made him to be, in no need, or free from want; (S, * MA, K; *) [or in a state of competence, or sufficiency; ] or possessed of wealth; (S, * K, * TA;) [or rich, or wealthy; (see 1, first sentence;)] and ↓ gn~Ahu signifies the same; (K, TA; [but wanting in the CK and app. in several copies of the K;]) or, as some say, this latter is [used] in prayer [app. as meaning he said to him, May God enrich thee, or the like: compare saq~ayotuhu (“ I said to him, May God send down rain to thee ”), and Eaq~arotuhu (as expl. in art. Eqr ), &c.]. (TA.) [And AgnAhu Eano ka*aA He, or it, caused him to be in no need, or free from want, of such a thing. (See Ham p. 152.) And yugoniY Eano A^ano tafoEala ka*aA It renders needless thy doing such a thing: lit. it causes that there shall be no need of thy doing such a thing. ] ― -b2- And AgnY Eanohu ka*aA Such a thing sufficed him; or stood him in stead: whence the saying in the Kur [lxix. 28], maA A^agonaYEan~iY maAliyaho [ My property has not sufficed me, or stood me in stead ]: and [in iii. 8 and lviii. 18 of the same,] lano tugoniYa Eanohumo A^amowaAluhumo [ Their possessions will not suffice them in lieu of God]: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or this last means, will not defend them from God, i. e. from his punishment. (Jel in iii. 8.) And ↓ A^agonayotu Eanoka magonaY fulaAnK and ↓ magonaAtahu , (S, Msb, K, *) and ↓ mugonaY fulaAnK and ↓ mugonaAtahu , (S, Mgh, K,) and fulaAnK ↓ ganaA='a , (K,) I sufficed, or satisfied, or contented, thee, or I have sufficed, &c., as such a one; or I stood thee, or served thee, or I have stood &c., in the stead of such a one. (S, * Mgh, Msb, K.) And maA yugoniY Eanoka h`*aA This does not suffice, or satisfy, or content, thee; or stand thee, or serve thee, in any stead; and does not avail, or profit, thee. (S.) AZ mentions maA A^agonaY fulaAnN $ayoy^FA , thus, and with E , [i. e. A^aEonaY ,] as meaning Such a one did not avail, or profit, at all, in a difficult, or an arduous, affair or case; and did not suffice for such an affair or such a case, or for the supply of what was necessary for subsistence. (Msb, TA.) And he says also that he heard a man chide his slave, and say to him, A^agoni Ean~iY wajohaka balo $ar~aka , meaning Free me from, and avert from me, [ thy face, nay, rather, ] thy evil, or mischief: and hence the phrase $aA^onN yugoniyhi , [respecting which see the second sentence in art. EnY ,] in the Kur [lxxx. 37]. (TA.) [Hence also,] wamaA A^ugoniY Eanokumo mina A@ll~`hi mino $aYo'K , in the Kur xii. 67, means But I do not avert from you, by my saying this, anything decreed to befall you from God: the second mn is redundant. (Jel.) And one says, A^agoni Ean~iY ka*aA , meaning Put thou away from me, and remove far from me, such a thing: properly [ A^agoniniY Eano ka*aA , originally meaning render thou me in no need of such a thing, ] a phrase of the same kind as EaraDa Ald~aAb~apa EalaY AlmaA='i [for EaraDa AlmaA='a EalaY Ald~aAb~api ]. (Mgh.) -A2- A^agonaY Eanohu as intrans.: see 1, former half. -A3- maA A^agonaAhu [ How free from wants, or how rich, or wealthy, is he! ]: this and maA A^afoqarahu are [said to be] anomalous; for their [respective] verbs are AstgnY and Aftqr , from either of which the verb of wonder may not properly [or regularly] be formed. (S in art. fqr . [But see ganiYa as syn. with AstgnY ; and see also art. fqr .])

sourceDefinition: : see ganiY~N . ― -b2- [The fem.] gaAniyapN signifies A young woman who is sufficed by her husband; or satisfied, or content, with him, (S, Msb, TA, *) so as to be in no need, or free from want, of any other: (Msb:) and sometimes, also, applied to a woman, (S,) such as is sufficed by her beauty, (S, ISd, K, TA,) so as to be in no need of decoration (ISd, K, TA) with women's ornaments: (ISd, TA:) or such as is sought, or desired, by men, but does not seek, or desire: (ISd, K, * TA:) or such as has abode in the house, or tent, of her father and mother, and whom captivity ( sibaA=' ) has not befallen; (IJ, ISd, K, * TA;) which is the strangest of the explanations: (TA:) or such as is youthful and chaste, whether having a husband or not: (ISd, K, TA:) or, accord. to AO, one that is married: (Ham p. 226:) or, accord. to Az, such as pleases men, and is pleased by $abaAb [which means both youthfulness and youths or young men ]: (TA:) pl. gawaAnK ; (K;) with the article, AlgawaAniY ; [and also gaAniyaAtN : (see an ex. in a verse cited in the second paragraph of art. zj :)] in the saying of Ibn-Er-Rukeiyát, laA baAraka A@ll~`hu fiY AlgawaAniYi halo yuSobiHona A_il~aA lahun~a muT~alabu [ May God not bless those young women that are sufficed by their husbands, or by their beauty, &c.: do they enter upon the time of dawn without their having desire (lit. a time or place, meaning an occasion, of seeking, or desire ) ?], the Y is made movent by a poetic license: (S, TA:) and another poet uses AlgawaAni for AlgawaAniY . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: an inf. n. of 1: (S, M, A, &c.:) or a simple subst.: (Msb:) [as a subst. signifying] Badness, evilness, corruptness, unsoundness, wrongness, wrongfulness, impropriety, unrighteousness, wickedness, vitiousness, depravity, or dishonesty; the state of being devoid of virtue or efficacy; a corrupted, vitiated, perverted, marred, spoiled, deteriorated, or tainted, state; a state of disorder or disturbance, or of destruction, annihilation, consumption, waste, or ruin: (MA, KL, PS, &c.:) contr. of SalaAHN . (Lth, M, Msb.) And it is also [frequently used as a quasi-inf. n.] syn. with A_ifosaAdN [signifying The making, or rendering, bad, evil, corrupt, &c.: (see 4:) and, oftener, the acting ill, corruptly, wrong, wrongfully, improperly, unrighteously, wickedly, vitiously, or dishonestly; doing evil, or mischief; and creating, or exciting, disorder, disturbance, disagreement, discord, dissension, strife, or quarrelling ]: (L:) and [particularly] the taking property wrongfully. (O, K.) [Hence,] Harobu AlfasaAdi [ The war of evildoing ]: thus was termed a war that happened between [the two sub-tribes] banuw$k [in which the latter word is app. a mistranscription for $ibokK ] and gawov , of the tribe of TaY~i' : it was so termed because one party patched their sandals with the cars of the other, and one party drank wine out of the skulls of the other. (MF.) ― -b2- Also Drought, barrenness, dearth, or scarcity of good: (M, L, K:) so in the Kur [xxx. 40], Zahara A@lofasaAdu fiY Albar~i wa A@lobaHori i. e. Drought, &c., hath appeared in the land, and in the cities that are upon the rivers; (M, L, TA;) accord. to Zj; (M;) or accord. to Ez-Zejjájee. (L, TA.)

sourceDefinition: (K, TA) EalaY gayorihi , (TA,) inf. n. tafoDiylN , i. q. maz~aAhu , (K, TA,) i. e. He attributed to him an excellence distinguishing him from [or above ] another, or others: (TA:) or faD~alotuhu EalaY gayorihi , inf. n. as above, I judged him (S, O, Msb, * TA) to be more excellent than another, or others: (S, * O, * Msb, TA: *) or I made him (S, O, Msb, * TA) to be so. definition: [an inf. n.: (see 1, throughout:) and also a simple subst., signifying] An exceeding, a redundant, or a superfluous, quantum [of anything, good or evil]; an excess, a redundance, or a superfluity;...
sourceDefinition: [an inf. n.: (see 1, throughout:) and also a simple subst., signifying] An exceeding, a redundant, or a superfluous, quantum [of anything, good or evil]; an excess, a redundance, or a superfluity; syn. ziyaAdapN ; (Mgh, Msb;) contr. of naqoSN : (S, O, K:) [and often meaning superabundance, or exuberance; and surpassingness, superiority, or excellence. EalaY gayorihi over another, or others, than him, or it: and preponderance: ] the pl. is fuDuwlN (Mgh, Msb, K:) and this is sometimes used as a sing.; (Er-Rághib, Msb;) and [thus used] relates to a thing [or quality] in which is no good; (Er-Rághib, Mgh, Msb;) by a predominant application; whence the saying fuDuwlN bilaA faDolK [ excess without excellence ]; (Mgh;) and hence the rel. n. ↓ fuDuwliY~N is formed from it: (Er-Rághib, Msb, TA;) [see this last word, one of the explanations of which shows that a particular meaning of fuDuwlN is the quality of busying oneself with that which does not concern him: ] accord. to Er-Rághib, faDolN signifies an excess [in respect of a property or quality, or of an acquisition,] above moderateness; and this is of two sorts; such as is commended, as the fDl of knowledge, or science ; and such as is discommended, as the fSl of anger at that whereat it is not necessary: but faDalN is more used in relation to that which is commended; and [the pl.] fuDuwlN , in relation to that which is discommended. when the former is used of an excess [in respect of some attribute, of our of two things above the other, it is of three sorts; fDl of kind, as of the animal kind above the vegetable kind; and of species, as of man above other animals; and of the individual, as of one man above another; the first and second of which three are essential attributes, such that he who is deficient in [either of] them cannot do away with his deficiency and acquire fDl , as, for instance, the horse, and the ass, which cannot acquire the excellence ( faDiylap ) of the human being; but the third may be accidental, such that the way may be found to acquire it, and of this sort are ability, wealth, rank or station, and power: and it signifies also any gift whereof the giving to the recipient thereof is not obligatory: [i. e. a free gift, or gratuity; and an act of bounty or grace; a favour; a benefit; and bounty as an abstract term;] as in the saying [in the Kur iv. 36], waA@soA^aluwA A@ll~`ha mino faDolihi [ And ask ye God of his free gift, or of his bounty, or (as expl. in the Ksh and by Bd) of his exhaustless treasures ]; (Msb. [See also baloha , which is used in a somewhat similar manner.])

definition: , aor. yafuwtu , inf. n. fawotN and fawaAtN , originally signifies faAta waqotu fiEolihi [i. e. The time, or opportunity, of the doing, or performing, of the affair passed, passed away, elapsed, or...
sourceDefinition: , aor. yafuwtu , inf. n. fawotN and fawaAtN , originally signifies faAta waqotu fiEolihi [i. e. The time, or opportunity, of the doing, or performing, of the affair passed, passed away, elapsed, or escaped, neglected by him, without his doing it or performing it ]; and hence the phrase faAtati AlS~alaApu , meaning The time of prayer passed, passed away, elapsed, or escaped, without his performing it therein (Msb:) and ↓ AftAt is syn. with faAta . (M, O.) [And both of these verbs are trans.:] one says faAtahu Al$~aYo'u , (S, O, Msb,) or AlA^amoru , (M, K,) aor. as above, (O,) and so the inf. ns.; (S, * M, O, * Msb, K;) and ↓ AftAthu : (K;) The thing, or affair, passed, or passed away, from him [ neglected by him ]; (M, K;) [or the time, or opportunity, of the doing, or performing, thereof passed, or passed away from him neglected by him; ] or the thing escaped him, [or became beyond his reach, ] so that he was unable to attain it, or to do it, or to accomplish it. (Msb.) But this explanation is not applicable except in the case of prayer, and the like: in other cases, faAtahu signifies He, or it, preceded him; was, or became, or got, before him; outwent him; passed beyond him; or had, got, or look, precedence of him: and went, or passed, away from him: and the like. (MF, TA.) One says, faAtaniY ka*aA , meaning sabaqaniY [i. e. Such a thing preceded me, &c., app. so as to become beyond my reach ]: and fut~uhu A^anaA [ I preceded it, &c.]: (T:) and jaArayotuhu Hat~aY fut~uhu I ran with him until I passed beyond him, or outwent him: (A, TA:) and faAtahu fulaAnN bi*iraAEK Such a one preceded him, or outwent him, by a cubit. (Msb.) falaA fawota , in the Kur xxxiv. 50, means falaA fawota lahumo min~FA [ And there shall be for them no escaping from us ], i. e. laA yafuwtuwnanaA [ they shall not escape us ]. (Jel. [And Bd says the like; adding, “ by flight, or fortifying themselves. ”]) An Arab of the desert is related to have said, AlHamodu lil~`hi Al~a*iY lA yufaAtu walaA [expl. in art. lyt ) (T. And they assert that a man went forth from his family, and when he returned, his wife said to him, “ If thou hadst been present with us, we would have related to thee what hath happened; ” whereupon he said to her, lamo tufaAtiY fahaAtiY (M, Meyd) i. e. It has not escaped thee [lit. thou hast not been escaped ], so adduce what thou hast [to tell]: the saying is a proverb. (Meyd.) ― -b2- See also 5: and see 8, in three places. ― -b3- faAta is also syn. with faAda [as signifying He died; in which sense the aor. is yafuwtu , and the inf. n. fawotN ]. (A in art. fyd .) And ↓ A^fotiyta signifies He died suddenly. (TA in art. fA^t , q. v.)

sourceDefinition: see 1, first and second sentences. ― -b2- As, relating the verse of Ibn-Mukbil, yaA Hur~a A^amosayotu $ayoxFA qado wahaY baSariY waA@fotiyta maA duwna yawomi lbaEovi mino EumuriY [which may be rendered O ingenuous woman, ( Hur~a being an abbreviation of Hur~apN ,) I have become an old man, my sight has become weak, and what is anterior to the day of resurrection, of my life, has been passed, or has run out like water poured forth ( fariga )], says, it is from Alfawotu , and AlAifotiyaAtu [app. as the inf. n. of the pass. v. Aftyt used in this verse] signifies AlfaraAgu . (T.) ― -b3- See also 1, last sentence. ― -b4- AlAifotiyaAtu signifies also The betaking oneself, or applying oneself, before another or others, or hastily, (S, O, Msb,) to a thing, (S, O,) or to the doing of a thing, (Msb,) without obeying him who should be obeyed, (S, O,) or following his own opinion only, without consulting him who had the best right to order in the case: (Mgh, * Msb:) you say, AftAt Ealayohi biA^amori ka*aA i. e. bihi ↓ faAtahu [app. meaning He so betook himself, &c., in opposition to him: or fAth bh may be here used in the sense in which it is expl. above voce tafaw~ata ]. (S, O.) And you say, fulaAnN laA yufotaAtu Ealayohi Such a one, nothing is to be done without his order; (S, O, K; *) and so Elyh ↓ laA yufaAtu ; (Har p. 63;) or laA yufotaAtu Ealayohi $aYo'N duwna A^amorihi [which means the same]. (Msb.) A^amivoliY yufotaAtu Ealayohi fiY banaAtihi , (T, M, O,) or fiY A^amori banaAtihi , (S, TA,) occurs in a trad., (S, M, Mgh, O, TA,) meaning Shall such a one as I [am] have anything done in respect of his daughters without his order? (Mgh, * TA;) and was said by 'Abd-Er-Rahmán the son of Aboo-Bekr to his sister 'Áïsheh, on the occasion of her having given in marriage his daughter, the elder Hafsah, during his absence, to El-Mundhir the son of Ez-Zubeyr. (T, * O, TA. *) And you say, AftAt Ealayohi fiY $aYo'K , and b$aYo'K ↓ faAtahu , meaning He brought to pass a thing exclusively of him [i. e., of another person, without the latter's having any part therein]. (TA.) And AftAt Ealayohi fY ka*aA , and Ealayohi fiyhi ↓ tfw~t , He followed his own opinion only, exclusively of him [i. e., of another], in the disposal, or management, of such a thing: the verbs being trans. by means of EalaY because implying the meaning of Alv~agal~ub . (TA.) And AftAt Ealayohi fiY AlA^amori , (M, K, * TA,) and ↓ tfw~t Ealayohi fiyhi , (MA,) He decided against him in the affair. (M, MA, K, * TA.) ― -b5- And AftAt biA^amorihi He effected, or executed, his affair without consulting any one: thus accord. to As, without hemz: (T, TA:) and, as is related on the authority of ISh and ISk, one says, AftA^t bA^mrh , with hemz, meaning he was alone in his affair; and in like manner one says, biraA^oyihi in his opinion. (TA. [See also art. fA^t .]) ― -b6- And AftAt AlkalaAma He originated, or excogitated, the speech: (O, K, TA:) and he extemporized the speech; spoke it without consideration, or thought, or preparation, or without pausing, or hesitating; as also Aifotalatahu . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: an inf. n. of 1. (S, * M, &c.) ― -b2- fawota famihi and fawota rumoHihi and fawota yadihi [lit. Beyond the reach of his mouth and of his spear and of his hand, or arm (in several copies of the K erroneously written fawotu )] mean where he sees it but will not [ be able to ] reach it, or attain it. (K, TA.) A man said to another, reviling him, [or rather said of him,] jaEala A@ll~`hu rizoqahu fawota famihi i. e. [ May God make his sustenance to be beyond the reach of his mouth, ] where he shall see it and shall not attain it. (S, O. [And the like is said in the M and A.]) And one says, huwa min~iY fawota Alr~umoHi [ He, or it, is ] where my spear will not reach him, or it. (S, A, O.) And huwa min~iY fawota Alyadi [ He, or it, is ] beyond the reach of my hand, or arm: mentioned by Sb among what are peculiarly adverbial expressions. (M.) And A^afolatanaA fulaAnN fawota Alyadi and fawota AlZ~ufori [ Such a one escaped from us beyond the reach of a hand, or an arm, and beyond the reach of a finger-nail ]. (A. [Golius, as on the authority of the A, has ZuforK ↓ fuwayota , which he explains as syn. with fawota yadK ; but it signifies A little beyond the reach of a finger-nail. ]) ― -b3- A^asomaEu SawotFA waA^araY fawotFA means I hear a sound, or voice, but I see not a deed, or no deed. (TA in art. Swt .) ― -b4- fawotN signifies also The space between two fingers [ when they are extended apart (see buSomN )]: (S, M, O, K:) pl. A^afowaAtN . (S, M, O.) ― -b5- And you say, ↓ bayonahumaA fawotN faAy^itN like as you say bawonN baAy^inN [i. e. Between them two (meaning two men) is a wide distance; app. in respect of rank or estimation: the last word being in this case a corroborative, like the latter word in mawotN maAy^itN and liyolN laAy^ilN ]. (M.)

definition: A kind of thin, or fine, (Mgh, Msb,) white, (Mgh,) cloth, (Mgh, Msb,) of linen, (Msb,) made in Egypt;
sourceDefinition: A kind of thin, or fine, (Mgh, Msb,) white, (Mgh,) cloth, (Mgh, Msb,) of linen, (Msb,) made in Egypt; so called in relation to the qiboT , irregularly, to distinguish between it and the man, who is called qiboTiY~N : (Mgh, Msb:) so says Lth, respecting these two forms: (TA:) you also say, ↓ viyaAbN qiboTiy~apN , with kesr; but when you convert the rel. n. into a subst, you say quboTiy~apN , with damm, to distinguish the subst. from the rel. n. without vyAb ; like as you say, rimaAHN xaT~iy~apN , and xiT~iy~apN , with kesr, when you do not mention the rmAH : so says Kh: (Msb in art. xT :) it is said in the K, that AlquboTiy~apu , with damm, signifies a kind of cloths, so called in relation to the qiboT ; and sometimes it is with kesr; which is a plain assertion that the form with damm is the more common: but in the S it is said, that AlqiboTiy~ipu signifies certain white, thin, or fine, cloths, of linen, made in Egypt; and sometimes it is with damm, because they make a change in the rel. n., as in suholiY~N and duhoriY~N , which (as SM adds) are from saholN and dahorN ; and this indicates that the regular form, with kesr, is the more common: (TA:) the pl. is qabaATiY~N (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and qabaATiY : (K [but the latter, being indeterminate, should be written qabaATK , like mahaArK &c.:]) Sh says, that the qabaATiY~ are a kind of cloths inclining to fineness and thinness and whiteness. (TA.)

definition: -A2- (assumed tropical:) A man foul in language;
sourceDefinition: : see qa*arN , throughout. -A2- (assumed tropical:) A man foul in language; (Mgh;) evil in disposition: (Mgh, K:) one who cares not what he does or says. (TA.) ― -b2- (assumed tropical:) A very jealous man; syn. gayuwrN . (Lth, K.) ― -b3- (tropical:) A man who does not mix with others, (K,) or who does not associate as a friend with others, (S,) because of the evilness of his disposition, (S, K,) nor alight with them; (S;) as also ↓ qa*uwrN and ↓ qaAduwrN (K) and *uw qaA*uwrapK : (S, K:) or a man who shuns, avoids, or removes himself far from, others, not sitting unless alone, nor alighting unless alone. (A, TA.) See also qa*uwrN . ― -b4- Dainty, or squeamish; one who dislikes and avoids a thing, and will not eat it: (AO, M, Mgh, K:) the p is added to give intensiveness to the signification: (TA:) or one who dislikes ( yuqa*~iru ) everything that is unclean. ('Abd-el-Wahháb El-Kilábee.) It is said of Mohammad, kaAna qaA*uwrapF laA yaA^okulu Ald~ajaAja Hat~aY tuEolafa He was dainty; not eating the domestic fowl until it had been fed with vegetable food. (Mgh, TA.)

sourceDefinition: [The colocasia; or arum. colocasia of Linnæus: or its root: ] the root of a certain plant, which is eaten cooked, (AHn, K,) and used medicinally: (AHn:) the decoction thereof increases the venereal faculty, and fattens; but the taking it constantly engenders black bile. (AHn, K.) [See De Sacy's “ Relation de l'Egypte par Abd-allatif, ” pp. 94 — 98.]

sourceDefinition: , (S, A, L, K,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. qamoHN ; (S;) and ↓ AqtmHhu ; (S, A, L, K;) He ate it, or took it into his mouth, (S, K,) namely, meal of parched barley or wheat, &c., (S, A, L,) not bread nor dates nor the like, but only what is eaten in the manner termed saf~N , (L,) without moistening it, or kneading it with water &c.; syn. Aisotaf~ahu ; (S, K;) he took it in the palm of his hand (A, L) [ and conveyed it ] to his mouth (A) or licked it up. (L.) And qumoHapF minohu ↓ AiqotamaHotu [ I so ate a mouthful thereof, i. e. of what is eaten in the manner described above]. (A.) ― -b2- And ↓ AqtmHhu likewise signifies, (L, K,) as also qamiHahu , (L,) He drank it, namely, what is called nabiy* , (L, K,) and $araAb [app. as meaning wine], and water, and milk. (L.) -A2- And, from qamiHahu signifying as expl. above, you say, qamaHa Eani AlmaA='i , (A,) or [simply] qamaHa , (S, L, K,) with fet-h, (S,) aor. , (L,) inf. n. qumuwHN ; (S, L, K;) as also qamaha , aor. , inf. n. qumuwhN ; (L;) and ↓ qAmH , (A, L,) inf. n. muqaAmaHapN and qimaAHN ; (A;) and ↓ tqm~H , and ↓ AnqmH ; (S, L, K;) He (a camel) raised his head (S, A, K) from the water (A) or at the watering-trough, and refused to drink, (S, K,) his thirst being satisfied, (S, A,) or by reason of loathing, or of the coldness of the water, or of some disease. (A.) And AlA_ibilu ↓ qaAmaHati The camels came to the water and did not drink, (S, K,) but raised their heads, (S,) by reason of disease, or of cold, (S, K,) or of the coldness of the water, or because their thirst was satisfied. (TA.) And ↓ $ariba fataqam~aHa and ↓ A@noqamaHa [ He drank ] and raised his head and left drinking by reason of his thirst's being satisfied. (S.) And fulaAnN mina AlmaA='i ↓ tqm~H Such a one drank water, or the water, with dislike, or loathing. (AZ.) ↓ A^a$orabu faA^ataqam~aHu , said by Umm-Zara, means (tropical:) [ I drink ] and I satisfy my thirst until I am not able to drink more, so I raise my head like the [ camel that is said to be ] muqaAmiH : (A, TA: *) Az says that Alt~aqam~uHu primarily relates to water, but is metaphorically used by her in relation to milk: she means that she satisfied her thirst with milk until she raised her head from drinking it like as does the camel when he dislikes drinking water: (TA:) or, as some relate her words, she said, faA^ataqan~aHu , (A, TA, *) which [likewise] means, “ and I raise my head in consequence of the being satisfied with drinking. ” (A.) [See also art. qnH .] ― -b2- qamaHa , aor. , inf. n. qumuwHN , is also expl. by Lth as signifying He (a camel) became very languid by reason of vehement thirst: but accord. to Az, this is wrong. (L.)

A_iqomaAHN , (S,) said of a camel, (MA,) or of a man, and [in this case, but not when said of a camel,] tropical, (TA,) He raised his head, and contracted his eyes: (S, MA, K, TA:) [or he was made to raise his head and to contract his eyes: ] it is expl. by Z as in the K. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] one says, (S,) A^aqomaHahu Algul~u (tropical:) The gul~ [i. e. the ring, or collar, of iron, for the neck, or the shackle for the neck and hands, consisting of two rings, one for the neck and the other for the hands, connected by a bar of iron, ] caused his (i. e. a captive's K) head to be raised, by reason of the straitness thereof; (S, K, TA;) meaning that the bar of the gul~ , which [by its projecting above the ring around the neck] pricked his chin, did not let him lower his head; as is said in the A. (TA.) ― -b3- AlA_iqomaAHu [as inf. n. of A^uqomiHa , like A^ukomiHa (with k and H ) in form and in meaning,] also signifies (assumed tropical:) The elevating of the head by reason of pride: and so AlA_ikomaAxu . (L and TA in art. kmx : but in the CK, in that art, AlAiqomAxu , with x .) And AqmH biA^anofihi [i. e. A^uqomiHa ] signifies $amaxa [i. e. $amaxa biA^anofihi , (assumed tropical:) He magnified, or exalted, himself; was proud; behaved proudly, or disdainfully; or elevated his nose, from pride ]; (K, TA;) and raised his head, scarcely ever, or never, lowering it: as though the verb had two contr. significations. (TA.) ― -b4- AqmH said of thirst is expl. by Lth as signifying It rendered a camel very languid: but accord. to Az, this is wrong. (L.) -A2- AqmH Als~unobulu The ears [ of wheat ] became pervaded by the farinaceous substance. (K.) ― -b2- And AqmH Albur~u , so in the T and L and other lexicons, but in all the copies of the K Albur~u ↓ AiqotamaHa , The wheat becomes mature qamoH . (TA.)

definition: He made it much, abundant, many, or numerous, he multiplied it;
sourceDefinition: He made it much, abundant, many, or numerous, he multiplied it; as also ↓ kv~rhu , (Msb, K, TA,) inf. n. takoviyrN . (K.) ― -b2- A^akovarotu mina Al$~aYo'i and minohu ↓ Astkvrtu signify the same; (S, Msb;) i. e., A^akovarotu fiEolahu [ I did the thing much; lit., I made the doing of it much ]: or A^akovarotu mina AlA^akoli wanaHowihi [ I ate, and the like, much ] presents an instance of pleonasm, [being for A^akovarotu AlA^akola wanaHowahu ,] accord. to the opinion of the Koofees: or it is an instance of explication [of the vague signification of the verb], accord. to the opinion of the Basrees; the objective complement being suppressed, and the complete phrase being A^akovarotu AlfiEola mina AlA^akoli : and so in the like cases. (Msb.) [You say also A^akovara fiY AlkalaAmi He spoke, or talked, much; was profuse, or immoderate, in speech, or talk. And in like manner, fiY AlA^amori ↓ kavura He did, acted, or occupied himself, much in the affair. ] ― -b3- Akvr [as an intrans. v.] signifies A^ataY bikaviyrK [ He brought, or he did, or he said, much ]. (K.) ― -b4- Also, [ He became rich; he abounded in property; ] his property became much, or abundant. (S, Msb, K.) -A2- Akvr It (a palm-tree) produced, or put forth, its TaloE [or spadix ], (S, K,) i. e., its kavar , whence the verb. (TA.) -A3- [ maA A^akovara maAlahu How abundant is his wealth! or how numerous are his cattle! ]

definition: [ He endeavoured to acquire much, or abundance, of a thing].
sourceDefinition: [ He endeavoured to acquire much, or abundance, of a thing]. You say tkv~r mina AlEilomi liyaHofaZa [ He endeavoured to acquire much knowledge, in order that he might preserve it in his memory ]. And takv~r minohu liyafohama [ He endeavoured to acquire much thereof in order that he might understand ]. (A.) See also 10. ― -b2- He made a vain, or false, boast of abundance, or riches; or a boast of more than he possessed; and invested himself with that which did not belong to him. (TA, voce ta$ab~aEa , which signifies the same.) You say tkv~r bimaA layosa Einodahu He made a boast of abundance, or riches, which he did not possess; syn. ta$ab~aEa . (Msb, art. $bE .) And fulaAnN yatakav~aru bimaAli gayorihi [ Such a one makes a vain or false show of abundance or riches with the wealth or property of another ]. (S.)

sourceDefinition: , masc. and fem., (S, K,) [ A bay, or dark bay, or brown, horse &c.:] of a red colour mixed with blackness: (Kh, Sb:) or of a red colour mixed with qunuwo' , (As, S, K,) which latter is blackness that is not pure, or clear: (TA [app. from As]:) [see kumotapN , above:] a camel is called A^aHomaru if of an unmixed red; but if of a red colour mixed with qnw' , it is called kmyt : (As, S:) the difference between kmyt and A^a$oqaru , as applied to horses, is in the mane and the tail: if these are red, the animal is called A$qr [i. e. sorrel]; and if they are black, it is called kmyt ; (AO, S, TA;) and the warod is between these two: (AO, TA:) [all bay horses have black manes, which distinguish them from the sorrel, that have red or white manes: (Farrier's Dict., quoted in Johnson's Dict., voce “ bay ”:)] an epithet applied to the horse and the camel and other animals: (ISd:) you say farasN kmytN , and muhorapN kmytN , and baEiyrN kmytN , and naAqapN kmytN : (TA:) accord. to the Kh, as cited by Sb, it is of the dim. form because it denotes a colour between black and red, as though to imply that it signifies what is near to each of these two colours. definition: , (S, K, * &c,) [originally kawida ,] first pers.
sourceDefinition: , (S, K, * &c,) [originally kawida ,] first pers. kidotu , accord. to the usage of most of the Arabs, (IKtt,) aor. yakaAdu , (S, K, &c.,) the form used by all the Arabs, (IKtt.) or yakuwdu [is also used, by some of those who make the pret. to be originally kawuda ], (Lth,) inf. n. kawodN (Lth, S, M, K, &c) and kaAdN (M, IKtt) and makaAdapN (Lth, S, M, K, &c.) and makaAdN ; (Lth, M, K;) and kaAda , originally kawuda , deviating from constant rule, (MF,) first pers. kudotu , (S, IKtt, MF,) in the dial. of the Benoo-'Adee, (MF,) mentioned by Sb as heard from some of the Arabs, (S,) aor. yakaAdu , (IKtt,) deviating from constant rule, (MF,) [and yakuwdu , mentioned above, agreeably with rule;] as also kaAda , (Msb, K, art. kyd ,) originally kayida , first pers. kidotu , aor. yakaAdu , (Msb, art. kyd ,) inf. n. kayodN ; (L, art. kyd ;) and kiyda , (S, K, &c.,) a form mentioned by Abu-l-Khattáb to Sb, as used by some of the Arabs, who in like manner said maA ziyla yafoEalu ka*aA , for kaAda and zaAla ; (S;) He was near to doing so; he nearly, well nigh, or almost, did so; he wanted but little of doing so; (Akh, S, M, K, &c.;) he purposed, or intended, doing so; (Lth, M, IKtt;) but did it not, [or did it not immediately ]. (Akh, S, K, &c.) kaAda is applied to signify the being near to doing a thing whether it be [afterwards] done or not done. (S.) Without a negative, it enunciates the negation of the action; and coupled with a negative, it enunciates the happening of the action. (S, K.) [This will be explained in the course of the following observations.] It is (as Es-Suyootee says in the Itkán) an incomplete [i. e. a non-attributive] verb, of which only the pret. and aor. are used. It has a noun as the subject, in the nom. case; and an aor., [generally] without A^ano , as the predicate. (TA.) Sometimes they introduce A^ano after it, likening it to EasaY ; as, for ex., in the saying of Ru-beh, qado kaAda mino Tuwli AlbilaY A^ano yamoSaHaA [ It had nearly come to nought from length of wear ]. (S.) Used affirmatively, it is affirmative of the being near [to doing a thing, &c.]; and used negatively, it is negative thereof. It is a well-known opinion of many, that, used affirmatively, it is negative; and used negatively, it is affirmative: so that kaAda zayodN yafoEalu means [ Zeyd was near to doing; but ] he did not [or did not immediately ]; as is shown by the expression [in the Kur xvii. 75, where A_ino is a contraction of A_in~a ,] waA_ino kaAduwA layafotinuwnaka [ And verily they were near to seducing thee ]: and maA kaAda yafoEalu means [ He was not near to doing; but ] he did; as is shown by the expression [in the Kur ii. 66,] wamaA kaAduwA yafoEaluwna [ And they were not near to doing ( it ); but they afterwards did ( it )]. I'Ab is related to have said, that wherever kaAda and A^akaAdu and yakaAdu occur in the Kur-án, they denote a thing's never happening. Some say, that kaAda [with a negative] denotes an action's happening with difficulty. Some, again, say, that the pret. preceded by a negative is affirmative [of the action &c.]; as is shown by the expression wamaA kaAduwA yafoEaluwna [quoted above]: and that the aor. preceded by a negative is negative; as is shown by the expression [in the Kur xxiv, 40,] lamo yakado yaraAhaA [ He is not near to seeing it ]; meaning that he sees not anything: [though this phrase is said to bear a different meaning, which see below]. But the correct opinion is the one first mentioned; that, used affirmatively, it is affirmative [of the being near to do a thing &c.]; and used negatively, it is negative [thereof]: so that kaAda yafoEalu signifies He was near to doing; but did not [or did not immediately ]: and maA kaAda yafoEalu He was not near to doing; much less did he do [or do immediately ]; the denial of the action [or of the immediate performance of the action] being necessarily understood from the denial of the being near to do it. sourceDefinition: , aor. yakiydu , (S, L, Msb,) inf. n. kayodN (S, L, Msb, K) and makiydapN , (S, L, K,) or the latter is a simple subst.; (Msb;) and ↓ kAydhu , (A,) inf. n. mukaAyadapN ; (S;) or this implies reciprocation; (TA;) [and ↓ AktAdhu , which see below. app. signifies the same as kaAdahu like as AixotadaEahu signifies the same as xadaEahu ;] He deceived, beguiled, or circumvented, him or he deceived, beguiled, or circumvented, him; and desired to do him a foul, an abominable, or an evil, action, clandestinely, or without his knowing whence it proceeded; i. q. makara bihi (S, L, Msb, K) and xadaEahu : (Msb:) or, accord. to some, mkrbh implies the feigning of the contrary of one's real intentions; whereas kAdh does not: or this latter signifies he did him harm, or mischief; and the former, he did so clandestinely. (MF.) ― -b2- kaAda , aor. yakiydu , (L,) inf. n. kayodN and makiydapN , (L, K,) [or the latter is a simple subst.,] He acted deceitfully, mischievously, or wickedly. (L, K.) ― -b3- Also, inf. n. kayodN , He practised an evasion or elusion, a shift, a wile, an artifice, or artful contrivance or device, a plot, a stratagem, or an expedient; or he exercised art, artifice, cunning, ingenuity, or skill, in the management or ordering of affairs,, with excellent consideration or deliberation, and ability to manage with subtilty according to his own free will; syn. AixotaAla ; (L:) and of the inf. n., HiylapN . (L, K.) ― -b4- kaAdahu He taught him Alkayod [i. e., to deceive, beguile, or circumvent, &c., or, to act deceitfully, mischievously, or wickedly; or, to practise modes, or means, of evading or cluding, &c. ]. So some explain it in the Kur xii. 76. (TA.) ― -b5- It is said in a trad., maA qawoluka fiY EuquwlK kaAdahaA xaAliquhaA What sayest thou of intellects to which their Creator hath desired to do evil? (L.) So some explain the verb in the Kur xxi. 58. (TA.) ― -b6- yakiyduwna kayodFA waA^akiydu kayodFA [Kur lxxxvi. 16, They practise an artful device, and I will practise an artful device ]. kayodu A@ll~`hi lilokuf~aAri [ God's practising an artful device towards the unbelievers ] means his taking them unawares, so that they do not reckon upon it; bestowing upon them enjoyments in which they delight, and on which they place their reliance, and with which they become familiar so as not to be mindful of death, and then taking them in their most heedless state; A_isotidoraAjuhumo mino Hayovu laA yaEolamuwna . (Zj, L.) ― -b7- kaAda , aor. yakiydu , inf. n. kayodN , He contrived, devised, or plotted, a thing, whether wrong or right. Ex. fulaAnN yakiydu A^amorF maA A^adoriY maA huwa Such a one contrives, devises, or plots, a thing: I know not what it is. (L.) ― -b8- kaAda , aor. yakiydu , He worked, or laboured, at, or upon, anything; he laboured, took pains, applied himself vigorously, exerted himself, strove, or struggled, to do, execute, or perform, or to effect, or accomplish, or to manage, or treat, anything; he laboured, strove, or struggled, with anything, to prevail, or overcome, or to effect an object; syn. EaAlaja . (S, L.) ― -b9- kaAda , inf. n. kayodN , He strove, or laboured; exerted himself, or his power or ability; employed himself vigorously, laboriously, sedulously, or earnestly; was diligent; took extraordinary pains. (L.) -A2- kaAda , inf. n. kayodN , He (a raven or crow) exerted himself in his croaking. (S, K.) -A3- kaAda binafosihi , (K,) aor. yakiydu , (S, L,) inf. n. kayodN , (L,) (tropical:) He gave up his spirit: (S, L, K:) endured distress in giving up the ghost. (A.) ― -b2- kaAda , (K,) inf. n. kayodN , (S, K,) He vomited. (S, K.) ― -b3- kaAda , inf. n. kayodN , It (a zanod ) emitted fire. (L, K.) ― -b4- kaAdato , (L, K,) aor. takiydu , inf. n. kayodN , (L,) She had the menstrual flux. (L, K.) -A4- laA A^afoEalu *`lika walaA kayodFA walaA ham~FA I will not do that, nor do I desire, nor do I purpose, or intend. (K, * TA.) See kaAda in art. kwd . -A5- kaAda yafoEalu ka*aA , (L. Msb, K,) originally kayida , first pers. kidotu , aor. yakaAdu ; (L, Msb;) and kiyda : (L, K:) see art. kwd . [It is mentioned in arts. kwd and kyd in the L, K: in the former only in the S: and in the latter only in the Msb.]

A sheep or goat ( $Ap , K), or a sheep only, not a goat, (ISk, S,) of which the milk has become little in quantity: (S, K:) or a sheep or goat ( $Ap ) which has passed four months since her bringing forth, and of which the milk has in consequence dried up: (As, S:) or it is an epithet applied specially to a goat: (K:) a poet (Muhelhil, TA,) says, Eajibato A^abonaAw^unaA mino fiEolinaA A_i*o nabiyEu Alxayola biAlmiEozaY All~ijaAbo [ Our sons wondered at our action, in our selling horses for goats of which the milk had become little, or dried up ]: (S:) and contr., abounding with milk: (K:) a poet applies the two epithets lajobap and HaA$ikap to the same sheep or goat; but he may mean that her milk was little at one time, and abundant at another. [of lajobapN ] lijaAbN (S, K) and lajobaAtN (this being allowed by Mbr, agreeably with analogy, TA) and lajabaAtN (S, K): the last dev. with respect to rule; for by rule it should be lajobaAtN ; unless it be originally a subst. used as an epithet, like as one says A_imoraA^apN kalobapN ; or unless ↓ lajabapN be a syn. of the sing. sourceDefinition: , aor. yalyitu , (inf. n. layotN , S,) as also laAtapu , aor. yaluwtu ; or laAtahu Eano wajohihi ; as also ↓ A^alaAtahu ; (and A^alatahu ; S, K, art. A^alt ;) He withheld him, or restrained him, and turned him, or averted him, from his course, purpose, or object. (S, K.) The Rájiz says, walayolapK *aAti dujFA sarayotu walamo yalitoniY Eano suraAhaA layotu [ During many a dark night (or many a rainy, or wet, night, accord. to the reading in the TA, namely *At nadFY ) have I journeyed; ] and no hindrance hindered me from journeying during it: (S:) or the meaning is ― -b2- and no averting thing averted me, &c.; layotu being put for laAy^itu : or, nothing made me to repent, and say, layotaniY maA sarayotuhaA Would that I had not journeyed during it! or, no deficiency, nor any impotence, averted me, &c., accord. to the T. (TA.) ― -b3- laAtahu Haq~ahu , aor. yaliytu , inf. n. layotN ; and ↓ A^alaAtahu ; but the former is the more approved; as also A^alaAtahu and A^alithu ; He diminished unto him his due, or right: [or defrauded him of part thereof. ]. (TA.) It is said in the Kur, [xlix. 14,] laAyalitokumo mino A^aEomaAlikumo $ayoy^FA He will not diminish unto you, nor defraud you of, aught [ of the reward ] of your works. (Fr, Zj.) ― -b4- maA A^alaAnahu $ayoy^FA ; as also maA A^alatahu (and maA A^altahu ; TA;) He did not diminish unto him aught. (Fr, S, K.) In maA A^alatonaAhumo mino Eamalihimo mino $aYo'K , in the Kur, [lii. 21, q. v. in art. A^lt .] the verb may be from A^alata or from A^alaAta . (TA.) ― -b5- AlHaq~a ↓ bit~u A^uliytu in a verse of 'Orweh Ibn-El-Ward, signifies A^uHiyluhu and A^uSorifuhu [ I passed the night putting away ( from my mind the thought of ) death: the poet having just before mentioned the death of certain of his camels]. (Sh, L.) ― -b6- In the following saying, AlHamodu lil~`hi Al~a*iY laA yufaAtu walaA yalaAtu walaA ta$otabihu Ealayohi AlA^aSowaAtu [ Praise be to God, whom nothing will escape, (lit., who will not be escaped, see Kur xxxiv. 50, and 1 in art. fwt ,) and —, and to whom voices will not be confused, or undistinguishable, one from another! ], lA ylAt is from A^alaAta , a dial. var. of laAta , aor. yliytu , in the sense of naqaSa , and signifies unto whom one cannot diminish [ aught that is his due ], and whom prayer cannot be hindered from reaching: so accord. to IAar: or, accord. to Khálid Ibn Jembeh, upon whom nothing that any one saith can have any power; (expl. by lA yA^xd fyh qwl qAy^l ;) i. e., who obeyeth no one. (L.) ― -b7- laAta $ayoAF , aor. yaliytu , He concealed a thing that he knew, and told, or narrated, something different from it. (TA, art. lwv , q. v.) ― -b8- laAtahu , aor. yaliytu , inf. n. layotN , He expressed to him the news, or information, obscurely, or enigmatically, or obscured it to him, or concealed it from him: so accord. to As, and the like is said in the L: but accord. to some, the verb is laAtahu , aor. yaluwtu , q. v., in art. lwt . (TA, art. lwt ) ― -b9- walaAta Hiyna manaASK , occurring in the Kur, [xxxviii. 2,] (S,) [there meaning, accord. to the general opinion, When ( it, or the time, ) was not a time of flight: in other cases, and ( it, or the time, ) is, or was, not a time of flight ]. lAt is here likened to layosa ; and the name of the agent is understood. (S, K.) So says Akh, accord. to J; but this is the opinion of Sb: so in the margin of some copies of the S. (TA.) Or lAt is originally lA ; and the t is added, as in vum~ata [in the CK, vam~at ,] (El-Muärrij, S, K,) and rub~ata . (El-Muärrij, S.) ― -b10- With respect to the proper meaning and etymology of lAt there are four opinions. First, that it is a single word, a verb in the pret. tense: and some say, that it is originally laAta in the sense of naqaSa , and afterwards used as a negative, like qal~a : so says Aboo-Dharr El-Khushanee, in his Expos. of the Book of Sb: others, that it is originally layisa ; that its s is changed into t , and then the Y into A , because it is movent and preceded by fet-hah: so says Abu-r-Rabeea. Second, that it is two words, the negative lA , with the fem. t , added to make the word fem., as say IHsh and Er-Radee, or to render the negation more intensive, as is said in the Expos. of the Katr by the author of the latter work: and this is the general opinion. Third, that it is an independent word, not originally lys nor lA ; as related by the sheykh Aboo-Is- hák Esh-Shátibee alone. Fourth, that it is a word and a part of a word, namely the negative lA , and t prefixed to Hyn ; which opinion is ascribed to A'Obeyd [as is mentioned in the S] and Ibn-El-Taráweh: the former of whom argues in favour of this opinion from the fact that t is found so prefixed in Othmán's copy of the Kur-án; but this is no proof, because there are found in the writing of that copy things at variance with analogy. (TA.) taHiyna [however] occurs, without lAt , in the following verse of Aboo-Wejzeh: AlEaATifuwna taHiyna maA mino EaATifK waAlmuToEimuwna zamaAna A^ayona AlmuToEimu [ The persons who act affectionately in the time when there is none ( other ) that acts affectionately; and the feeders in the time when ( it is said ) Where is the feeder? ] (S.) The general opinion is favoured by the following facts: that lAt is pronounced in a case of pause laAto and laAho : that it is written separately from Hyn : and that it is sometimes written laAti , with kesreh to the t , as is mentioned by Z, agreeably with the fundamental rule with respect to the concurrence of two quiescent letters [when followed by a conjunctive A ]; whereas, were it a verb in the pret. tense, there would be no reason for its being written with kesreh: it is also written laAtu , with dammeh to the t : and both these variations occur in readings of the Kur-án: but laAta , with fet-hah to the t , is the most common. (TA.) ― -b11- With respect to its government there are also four opinions. First, that it has no government: that if a noun in the nom. case follow it, it is put in that case as an inchoative of which [as is mentioned in the S] the enunciative is suppressed; and that if a noun in the acc. case follow it, it is put in that case as an objective complement of a verb suppressed; which is the opinion of Akh; the meaning of lAt Hyn mnAS being, in the former case, lAHiynu manaASK kaAy^inN lahumo [ A place of flight not existing for them; which does not imply that there was none for others; as lA here has the force of a particular, not a general, negation]; and in the latter case, the meaning being, laA A^araY Hiyna manaASK [ I see not a time of flight ]. Second, that it governs in the same manner as A_in~a ; which is another opinion of Akh and the Koofees. Third, that it is a particle governing the gen. case; an opinion ascribed to Fr by Er-Radee and IHsh and others. Fourth, that it governs like layosa ; and this is the general opinion; but IHsh restricts it by two conditions; that the two nouns which it governs must be significant of time, and that one of them must be suppressed. (TA.) [It is generally the subject, rarely the predicate, that is suppressed.] ― -b12- lAt [when it has grammatical government] does not occur without Hyn [or, as many say, some word syn. therewith, as waqot , &c.]. (S, K.) So says Akh, accord. to J; but this is the assertion of Sb; because the latter holds it to have the same government as lys ; whereas Akh assigns to it no government [as explained above]. (IB.) But [it is said that] Hyn is sometimes suppressed, (in poetry, S, [or in prose,]) though meant to be understood; as in the following saying of Mázin Ibn-Málik, [respecting 'Abd-Shems, surnamed Makrooa, the son of Saad the son of Zeyd-Menáh the son of Temeem, and respecting Heyjumáneh the daughter of El-'Ambar the son of 'Amr the son of Temeem, (S, art. qrE ,) who was enamoured of Makrooa,] waHan~ato walaAta han~ato waA^an~aY laki maqoruwEN [ And she conceived a longing desire; but it was not a time for her conceiving such a desire. And how (O Heyjumáneh) should Makrooa be thine? See Freytag, Arab. Prov. i. 343 and ii. 525.] (S, K.) This, however, is said to be not poetry but a prose-example. (TA.) Moreover, it is observed, that lAt , in this instance, has no government, and that a word signifying time is not meant to be understood after it: [so that the meaning is, And she conceived a longing desire, but it was as though she did not conceive such a desire: ] (MF.) for when lAt has government, the subject and predicate cannot both be suppressed. (AHei, MF.)
