(Sh, L.) ― -b6- In the following saying, AlHamodu lil~`hi Al~a*iY laA yufaAtu walaA yalaAtu walaA ta$otabihu Ealayohi AlA^aSowaAtu [ Praise be to God, whom nothing will escape, (lit., who will not be escaped, see Kur xxxiv. 50, and 1 in art. fwt ,) and —, and to whom voices will not be confused, or undistinguishable, one from another! ], lA ylAt is from A^alaAta , a dial. var. of laAta , aor. yliytu , in the sense of naqaSa , and signifies unto whom one cannot diminish [ aught that is his due ], and whom prayer cannot be hindered from reaching: so accord. to IAar: or, accord. to Khálid Ibn Jembeh, upon whom nothing that any one saith can have any power; (expl. by lA yA^xd fyh qwl qAy^l ;) i. e., who obeyeth no one. (L.) ― -b7- laAta $ayoAF , aor. yaliytu , He concealed a thing that he knew, and told, or narrated, something different from it. (TA, art. lwv , q. v.) ― -b8- laAtahu , aor. yaliytu , inf. n. layotN , He expressed to him the news, or information, obscurely, or enigmatically, or obscured it to him, or concealed it from him: so accord. to As, and the like is said in the L: but accord. to some, the verb is laAtahu , aor. yaluwtu , q. v., in art. lwt . (TA, art. lwt ) ― -b9- walaAta Hiyna manaASK , occurring in the Kur, [xxxviii. 2,] (S,) [there meaning, accord. to the general opinion, When ( it, or the time, ) was not a time of flight: in other cases, and ( it, or the time, ) is, or was, not a time of flight ]. lAt is here likened to layosa ; and the name of the agent is understood. (S, K.) So says Akh, accord. to J; but this is the opinion of Sb: so in the margin of some copies of the S. (TA.) Or lAt is originally lA ; and the t is added, as in vum~ata [in the CK, vam~at ,] (El-Muärrij, S, K,) and rub~ata . (El-Muärrij, S.) ― -b10- With respect to the proper meaning and etymology of lAt there are four opinions. First, that it is a single word, a verb in the pret. tense: and some say, that it is originally laAta in the sense of naqaSa , and afterwards used as a negative, like qal~a : so says Aboo-Dharr El-Khushanee, in his Expos. of the Book of Sb: others, that it is originally layisa ; that its s is changed into t , and then the Y into A , because it is movent and preceded by fet-hah: so says Abu-r-Rabeea. Second, that it is two words, the negative lA , with the fem. t , added to make the word fem., as say IHsh and Er-Radee, or to render the negation more intensive, as is said in the Expos. of the Katr by the author of the latter work: and this is the general opinion. Third, that it is an independent word, not originally lys nor lA ; as related by the sheykh Aboo-Is- hák Esh-Shátibee alone. Fourth, that it is a word and a part of a word, namely the negative lA , and t prefixed to Hyn ; which opinion is ascribed to A'Obeyd [as is mentioned in the S] and Ibn-El-Taráweh: the former of whom argues in favour of this opinion from the fact that t is found so prefixed in Othmán's copy of the Kur-án; but this is no proof, because there are found in the writing of that copy things at variance with analogy. (TA.) taHiyna [however] occurs, without lAt , in the following verse of Aboo-Wejzeh: AlEaATifuwna taHiyna maA mino EaATifK waAlmuToEimuwna zamaAna A^ayona AlmuToEimu [ The persons who act affectionately in the time when there is none ( other ) that acts affectionately; and the feeders in the time when ( it is said ) Where is the feeder? ] (S.) The general opinion is favoured by the following facts: that lAt is pronounced in a case of pause laAto and laAho : that it is written separately from Hyn : and that it is sometimes written laAti , with kesreh to the t , as is mentioned by Z, agreeably with the fundamental rule with respect to the concurrence of two quiescent letters [when followed by a conjunctive A ]; whereas, were it a verb in the pret. tense, there would be no reason for its being written with kesreh: it is also written laAtu , with dammeh to the t : and both these variations occur in readings of the Kur-án: but laAta , with fet-hah to the t , is the most common. (TA.) ― -b11- With respect to its government there are also four opinions. First, that it has no government: that if a noun in the nom. case follow it, it is put in that case as an inchoative of which [as is mentioned in the S] the enunciative is suppressed; and that if a noun in the acc. case follow it, it is put in that case as an objective complement of a verb suppressed; which is the opinion of Akh; the meaning of lAt Hyn mnAS being, in the former case, lAHiynu manaASK kaAy^inN lahumo [ A place of flight not existing for them; which does not imply that there was none for others; as lA here has the force of a particular, not a general, negation]; and in the latter case, the meaning being, laA A^araY Hiyna manaASK [ I see not a time of flight ]. Second, that it governs in the same manner as A_in~a ; which is another opinion of Akh and the Koofees. Third, that it is a particle governing the gen. case; an opinion ascribed to Fr by Er-Radee and IHsh and others. Fourth, that it governs like layosa ; and this is the general opinion; but IHsh restricts it by two conditions; that the two nouns which it governs must be significant of time, and that one of them must be suppressed. (TA.) [It is generally the subject, rarely the predicate, that is suppressed.] ― -b12- lAt [when it has grammatical government] does not occur without Hyn [or, as many say, some word syn. therewith, as waqot , &c.]. (S, K.) So says Akh, accord. to J; but this is the assertion of Sb; because the latter holds it to have the same government as lys ; whereas Akh assigns to it no government [as explained above]. (IB.) But [it is said that] Hyn is sometimes suppressed, (in poetry, S, [or in prose,]) though meant to be understood; as in the following saying of Mázin Ibn-Málik, [respecting 'Abd-Shems, surnamed Makrooa, the son of Saad the son of Zeyd-Menáh the son of Temeem, and respecting Heyjumáneh the daughter of El-'Ambar the son of 'Amr the son of Temeem, (S, art. qrE ,) who was enamoured of Makrooa,] waHan~ato walaAta han~ato waA^an~aY laki maqoruwEN [ And she conceived a longing desire; but it was not a time for her conceiving such a desire. And how (O Heyjumáneh) should Makrooa be thine? See Freytag, Arab. Prov. i. 343 and ii. 525.] (S, K.) This, however, is said to be not poetry but a prose-example. (TA.) Moreover, it is observed, that lAt , in this instance, has no government, and that a word signifying time is not meant to be understood after it: [so that the meaning is, And she conceived a longing desire, but it was as though she did not conceive such a desire: ] (MF.) for when lAt has government, the subject and predicate cannot both be suppressed. (AHei, MF.)

definition: a word denoting a wish [signifying Would that —;
sourceDefinition: a word denoting a wish [signifying Would that —; I wish that —;] (S, K;) generally relating to a thing that is impossible; rarely to a thing that is possible: (IHsh, K:) governing the subject in the acc. case, and the predicate in the nom. case, (S, K,) like kaA^an~a (or [rather] A_in~a , MF) and its coordinates, because it resembles verbs in their force as words, [being composed of at least three letters, and the last being meftoohah,] and in their admitting most of the pronouns as affixes, and in their meanings. (S.) Ex. layota zayodFA *aAhibN [ Would that Zeyd were going; ] (S;) and layotaniY faEalotu ka*aA waka*aA [ Would that I had done so and so. ] (TA.) You say layotiY as well as layotaniY , (S, K,) like laEal~iY and laEal~aniY , and A_in~iY and A_in~aniY : (S:) but lytnY is more common than lytY ; whereas lEl~nY is less common than lEl~Y . (TA.) You also say yaA layota O, would that —;.] As to the saying of the poet, yaA layota A^ay~aAma AlS~ibaA rawaAjiEaA meaning lanaA rawaAjiEa , [ O, would that the days of youth were returning ( to us )!] rwAjE is put in the acc. case therein as a word descriptive of state: (S:) or it is governed in the acc. case by a verb understood, as A^aqobalato , or EaAdato , or some other verb suitable to the meaning: so says Sb: (TA:) or lyt in the above verse may be used in the manner of wajadotu , [see below], (S,) for lyt is sometimes used in the manner of wajadotu [I found], (Fr, S, K,) in government, not in meaning, (MF,) as related by the grammarians on the authority of certain of the Arabs, so that it is doubly transitive, and used in the manner of verbs: (S:) you say, layota zayodFA $aAxiSFA [ Would that Zeyd were going away, &c. ]: (S, K:) this is done to give intensiveness: one says, for this purpose, layota zayodFA qaAy^imFA ( Would that Zeyd were standing ) putting both the subject and the predicate in the acc. case. (Msb.) ― -b2- layotamaA : see De Sacy's Gr. Ar. ii. 63. ― -b3- See also an ex. of lyt as a subst. voce sawofa .

sourceDefinition: , (aor. , inf. n. marodN , S, L,) He steeped bread, (S, L, K,) or corn, (Msb,) in water, and mashed it with his hand, so as to soften it: (S, L, Msb, K:) or he soaked bread in water; (M, L;) and so marava , and mara*a , with the dotted * ; or he softened bread in water, and crumbled it with his fingers. (As, L.) ― -b2- maradahu He rubbed it (a thing) in water. (TA.) ― -b3- maradahu , inf. n. marodN , He crumbled it [namely bread &c.], or broke it into small pieces, with his fingers; syn. varadahu . (TA [but only the inf. n. is there mentioned.]) ― -b4- maradahu , aor. , inf. n. marodN , He made it (a thing) soft. (L.) ― -b5- maradahu and ↓ mr~dhu He made it (a thing) soft and smooth; he polished it. (L.) See also 2. ― -b6- marada , (inf. n. marodN , S, L,) He (a child, S, L) mumbled ( marasa ) the breast (S, * L, * K) of his mother: (S, L:) or sucked it. (IKtt.) ― -b7- marida , aor. , He continued to eat mariyd , i. e., dates soaked in milk until rendered soft. (K.) ― -b8- marida (tropical:) It (a branch) was, or became, destitute of leaves. (IAar, L.) ― -b9- maridati AlA^aroDu , inf. n. maradN , (tropical:) The land was, or became, destitute of herbage, excepting a small quantity. (TA.) ― -b10- marida He (a horse) was, or became, without hair upon the fetlock. (IKtt.) ― -b11- marida , aor. , (L, Msb, K,) inf. n. maradN (S, L, Msb, K) and muruwdapN ; (L, K;) and ↓ tmr~d ; (S, A, L, K;) He (a youth, or young man,) was as yet beardless: (Msb:) or had no hair upon his cheeks: (IAar, L:) or remained to a late period without his beard having grown, (L, K,) or without the hair of his face having grown forth. (S, L, Msb) -A2- marada aor. , (A, L, Msb, K,) inf. n. muruwdN (A, L, K) and marodN ; (IAar, L;) and maruda , aor. , (S, L, Msb, K,) inf. n. maraAdapN (S, L, K) and muruwdapN ; (TA, and some copies of the K;) and ↓ tmr~d ; (A, L;) He exalted himself, or was insolent and audacious, in pride and in acts of rebellion or disobedience; (IAar, L;) he was hold, or audacious; (M, L, K;) and immoderate, inordinate, or exhorbitant; or excessively, immoderately, or inordinately, proud, or corrupt, or unbelieving, or disobedient or rebellious; or exalted himself and was inordinate in infidelity; or was extravagant in acts of disobedience and in wrongdoing; or was refractory, or averse from obedience: (S, M, A, L, Msb, K:) or he went to such an extreme as thereby to pass from out of the general state [or category ] of that species [ to which he belonged ]. (M, L, K.) ― -b2- So in the phrase mrd EalaY AlA^amori He was bold or audacious, and immoderate, &c., in the affair: (M, L:) and in like manner, ElY Al$~ar~i , in evil, or mischief: EalayonaA ↓ tmr~d He acted immoderately, inordinately, or exorbitantly, &c., towards us, or against us. (L.) ― -b3- Some explain maruda as syn. with xabuva [signifying He was bad, evil, wicked, malignant, noxious, corrupt, &c. ]. (MF.) ― -b4- maAridN waEaz~a AlA^abolaqu ↓ tamar~ada (tropical:) [ Márid hath resisted the attempt to take it, and El-Ablak hath proved strong ]: a proverb: (S:) originally said by Ex-Zebbà, the Queen of the Arabs, with reference to two fortresses which she had failed to take. (TA.) -A3- marada , (L,) inf. n. marodN , (L, K,) He (a sailor) pushed, or propelled, a ship or boat, with a murodiY~ . (L, K.) ― -b2- He drove vehemently. (L, K.) -A4- marada EalaY $aYo'K , [aor. ,] (K,) inf. n. muruwdN ; (S, L;) and ↓ tmr~d ; (L.) (tropical:) He became accustomed, habituated, or inured, to a thing. (S, L, K.) ― -b2- maraduwA EalaY Aln~ifaAqi [Kur., ix., 102,] (tropical:) They have become accustomed, habituated, or inured, to hypocrisy: (Fr., A, L:) or they have exalted themselves, or become insolent and audacious, in hypocrisy: (IAar:) accord. to Er-Rághib, it is from $ajarapN marodaA='u “ a tree without leaves; ” meaning, (assumed tropical:) they have become destitute of good. (TA.) ― -b3- marada EalaY AlkalaAmi (tropical:) He became accustomed, or habituated, to what was said, so that he cared not for it. (L.)

(K.)

definition: [ A razor; ] a certain instrument of iron, (M, Msb, TA,) with which one shaves: (Lth, L, K, TA:) of the measure fuEolaY , (Ks, M, Msb, K,) from Almawosu , [inf. n. of maAsa ,] so that the m is a...
sourceDefinition: [ A razor; ] a certain instrument of iron, (M, Msb, TA,) with which one shaves: (Lth, L, K, TA:) of the measure fuEolaY , (Ks, M, Msb, K,) from Almawosu , [inf. n. of maAsa ,] so that the m is a radical letter, (K,) accord. to Lth, (TA,) [for] Lth says, (L, TA,) Almawosu is the root ( taA^osiys [lit. foundation]) of AlmuwsaY , (L, K, TA,) the thing with which one shaves; (L, TA;) therefore, (Az, Msb, K,) it is imperfectly decl., because of the short fem. A [written Y ], (Msb,) without tenween; (Az, K;) and Fr cites a verse [of obscene meaning] in which it is made fem.: (TA:) or it is from A^awosayotu raA^osahu , meaning “ I shaved his head, ” (ISk, M, * Msb, K,) of the measure mufoEalN , (ISk, Msb, TA,) so that the Y is a radical letter, as El-Umawee and Yz say, and Aboo-'Amr Ibn-el-Alà inclined to think it so, (TA,) and therefore it is perfectly decl., (Msb,) with tenween, (Msb, K,) when indeterminate; (Msb;) or it is of the measure mufoEalN because this measure is more common than fuEolaY , and because it is perfectly decl. when indeterminate, whereas fuEolaY is not so when indeterminate and when determinate: (Ibn-EsSarráj, TA:) but IAmb says, that it is masc. and fem., and perfectly decl. and imperfectly decl.: ISk says, that the approved way is to make it perfectly decl.: (Msb:) [but] he says that it is fem. [also, and if so it is imperfectly decl.]: (TA:) and it is related of A'Obeyd, in the Bári', that he said he had not heard it made masc. except by El-Umawee; (Msb;) who asserted it to be masc. only: (TA:) the pl., accord. to him who makes it imperfectly decl., is muwsayaAtN ; and accord. to him who makes it perfectly decl., mawaAsK . (Msb.) The dim. of mwsY , in the sense above explained, [not as a proper name, in which case it is muwsaY only, without tenween, and has no relation to the same word signifying a razor,] is muwayosiyapN , [but by rule it should be muwayosaY , like HubayolaY ,] accord. to him who says h`*ihi muwsaY ; and muwayosK accord. to him who says h`*aA muwsFY . (ISk, TA.)

sourceDefinition: and ↓ A^anobijN The fruit of a certain Indian tree, (K,) which is preserved, or made into a confection, with honey; in form like the peach, with the head edged ( muHar~af ); [but this seems rather to apply to a kind mentioned below, resembling the almond;] it is brought to El-'Irák; and has within it a stone like that of the peach: (L:) an arabicized word, from [the Persian] A^anobo [or A^anabo ]. (L.) ― -b3- Accord. to AHn, Anbj is the name of Certain trees abounding in Arabia, in the districts of 'Omán; planted; they are of two kinds; one of these has a fruit resembling the almond, which is sweet from the commencement of its growth; the other has a fruit in appearance like the Damask plum ( A_ij~aAS ), is at first sour, and then becomes sweet when ripe: each has a stone, and has a sweet odour: the fruit of the sour kind is pressed down in jars, or earthern pots, [ HibaAb : so I read for jbAb :] while fresh, and kept until it attains to a ripe state, when it becomes as though it were the banana, in its odour and taste: the tree grows great so as to become like the walnut ( jawoz ), which it resembles also in its leaves: and when it attains to perfection, the sweet [fruit] is yellow; and the bitter, [or sour, ] red. (L.)

sourceDefinition: and ↓ najasN (S, A, O, Msb, K) and ↓ najusN and ↓ najosN and ↓ nijosN (A, O, K) Unclean, dirty, filthy, or impure: (A, Msb, K:) the last of these is only used when the word is preceded or followed by rijosN : (ISd:) or only when it is preceded by rijosN : (Fr, S, * and Har in the Durrat-el-Ghowwás:) but this remark correctly applies only to the greater number of instances: (M, F:) the second of the above five forms is an inf. n. used as an epithet; (A, Msb;) and is [therefore] used as sing. and dual. and pl. and masc. and fem., without variation: (TA:) [and the first and last are also used as pls., as will be seen below; but when so used, I suppose qawomN or some other coll. gen. n. to be understood:] the pl. [of every one of the other forms] is A^anojaAsN (A, Msb, TA) and [of the fourth and fifth, and perhaps of the first and third also, though I do not remember similar instances,] nijosapN . (TA.) [See also najaAsapN , below.] najisN and ↓ najosN [&c.], applied to a man, signify Unclean, &c., [both properly and tropically]. (TA.) [The two following examples are said in the A to be tropical.] Aln~aAsu A^ajonaAsN waA^akovaruhumo A^anojaAsN (tropical:) [ Men are of several kinds, and most of them are unclean. ] (A, TA.) And A_in~amaA A@lomu$orikuwna najasN (tropical:) [ Verily the associaters of others with God are but unclean ], said in the Kur, [ix. 28,] (S, A, TA,) or najisN , or ↓ nijosN , accord. to certain readers. (TA.) -A2- Also, all the above forms, A man having an incurable disease. (TA.) ― -b2- See also naAjisN .

definition: The name of a thing, either something unclean, or bones of the dead, or a menstruous rag, which used to be hung upon him for whom there was a fear of the jinn's, or genii's, being attached to him:...
sourceDefinition: The name of a thing, either something unclean, or bones of the dead, or a menstruous rag, which used to be hung upon him for whom there was a fear of the jinn's, or genii's, being attached to him: (K:) or the hanging of some such thing upon such a person, as a child or any other; for they used to say that the jinn would not approach those things: (TA:) or a thing which the Arabs used to do, as an amulet, to drive away thereby the [ evil ] eye: (S:) ↓ munaj~isapN also is the name of a kind of amulet: (IAar:) and ↓ nijaAsN is syn. with taEowiy*N ; [by which may be meant either that it signifies an amulet, or that it is a quasi-inf. n. of 2; for it is said that] it is app. a subst. from naj~asa lahu , or naj~asahu , as signifying Eaw~a*ahu . (IAar.) See also 2.

definition: One who hangs, upon him for whom there is fear, unclean things, such as bones of the dead, and the like, to drive away the jinn, or genii;
sourceDefinition: One who hangs, upon him for whom there is fear, unclean things, such as bones of the dead, and the like, to drive away the jinn, or genii; because these beings shun such things; (S, * A, TA;) one who fortifies by charms or amulets [ of the kinds above mentioned ]; syn, muEaw~i*N : (K:) pl. munaj~isuwna : (A:) and ↓ nujusN [a pl. of which the sing. is not mentioned] is syn. with muEaw~i*uwna . (IAar.) -A2- Also, A little piece of skin that is put upon the notch [ which is the place ] of the bow-string. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (L, K,) inf. n. nasoxN ; and ↓ Antsx ; (L;) He, or it, annulled, superseded, obliterated, effaced, or cancelled, (L, K,) a thing, bi$aYo'K A=xara by another thing. (L.) It annulled, or superseded, a thing, and took the place of it. (L.) Ex. nasaxati Al$~amosu AlZ~ila , and ↓ Antsxth , (tropical:) The sun annulled, or superseded, the shade, (S, L,) and took the place of it. (L.) nasaxa Al$~ayobu Al$~abaAba (tropical:) Hoariness took the place of youth. (A, Msb.) Also, nasaxa He annulled, superseded, abolished, or made void, a thing, substituting for it another thing. (K.) Ex. nasaxa A=yapF He (God) abrogated, annulled, or superseded, the verse of the Kur-án, (Lth, Fr, S, L,) substituting for it another; (Lth, Fr, L;) biA@loA=yapi by the [i. e. another] verse: (S:) or he changed it by substituting for it another: nasaxa signifying he changed a thing by substituting for it another thing. (IAar, L.) [See also 4.] Legal nasox , or abrogation, may respect the letter and the force of command, or one of these; whether the command have been performed, as is generally the case, or have not been performed, as in the case of the sacrifice of Ishmael, [or, as some of the Muslims say, agreeably with the Bible narrative, Isaac,] for Abraham was commanded to sacrifice him, and then the command was abrogated before its execution. (Msb.) ― -b2- Also, nasaxa He, or it, changed, or altered, a thing. (K.) Ex. nasaxati Alr~iyHu A=vaAra Ald~aAri The wind changed, or altered, [or, it may also be rendered, obliterated, or effaced, ] the traces of the dwelling. (S.) ― -b3- nasaxahu He transformed him, or metamorphosed him, into a worse, or more foul, or more ugly, shape; i. q. masaxahu : (K:) ex. nasaxahu A@ll~`hu qirodFA God transformed him into an ape. (Fr, Aboo-Sa'eed.) ― -b4- [Also, as used in post-classical, and perhaps in classical, times, He (God) caused his soul to pass into the body of another man. ] The connexion of the soul of a human being, after its departure from the body, with the body of another human being, is termed nasoxN ; with the body of a beast, masoxN ; with a plant, fasoxN ; and with an inanimate and not-increasing body, rasoxN . (Marginal note in a copy of the KT.) [But see 1 (last sentence) in art. fsx . See also 6.] ― -b5- nasaxa He transferred a thing from one place to another, it remaining the same: (TA:) he transferred what was in a bee-hive to another [ hive or place ]. (K.) ― -b6- nasaxa AlkitaAba , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. nasoxN ; (Msb;) and ↓ Antsxhu , (S, Msb, K,) and Astnsxhu ; (S, K;) are syn., (S,) signifying He copied, or transcribed, the writing, or book, (T, Msb, K,) letter for letter. (T.) ― -b7- maA nasaxahu waA_in~amaA masaxahu [ He has not copied it, but only corrupted it by changing the diacritical points and altering the meanings ]. (A.) ― -b8- ↓ nasotanosixu , in the Kur, xlv. 28, signifies We set down, or register, and preserve: (Jel:) or We command to be transcribed and to be set down, or registered. (T.)

sourceDefinition: The things succeeded one another, one taking the place of another. (A.) tanaAsuxN (S, K) and ↓ manaAsuxapN (K) in the case of an inheritance, (S, K,) or with respect to the fixed primary portions of an inheritance assigned by the Kur-án, is The dying of heirs after other heirs while the original inheritance remains undivided. sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. naEo$N , (S,) He (God) raised him; lifted him up; (S, K;) as also ↓ AnE$hu ; (Lth, Ks, K;) which is disallowed by ISk, who says that it is a vulgar word, and by J after him, but is correct; (TA;) and ↓ nE~$hu , (AA, K,) inf. n. tanoEiy$N : (AA, TA:) or He (God) set him up, or upright; as also ↓ AnE$hu : (Msb:) [see an ex. in a verse cited voce $amolN :] or be [app. a man] raised him, or lifted him up, after a stumble, or trip. (Sb.) You say also, naEa$otu Al$~ajarapa I set the tree upright, when it was leaning. (TA.) And naEa$a Tarufhu He raised his eye, or eyes. (S, * K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] aor. and inf. n. as above, (TA,) (tropical:) He recovered him from his embarrassment, or difficulty: (A:) (tropical:) he restored him from a state of poverty to wealth, or competence, or sufficiency: (K, TA;) as also ↓ AnE$hu : (TA:) and (tropical:) he recovered him from a state of perdition or destruction. (TA.) And naEa$aka A@ll~`hu (tropical:) May God restore thee from poverty to wealth, or competence, or sufficiency: or make thee to continue in life; preserve thee alive. (A.) And ↓ AnE$hu (assumed tropical:) He set him up, and strengthened his heart. (TA.) And Alr~abiyEu yunoE$u Aln~aAsa (tropical:) (A, TA,) [ The spring, or spring-herbage, or the season, or rain, called AlrbyE ,] makes men to live and enjoy plenty of herbage or the like. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] naEa$a Almay~ita , (Sh, K,) aor. as above, (Sh,) and so the inf. n. (TA) (tropical:) He eulogized, or praised, the dead man, (Sh, K,) and exalted his praise, or fame, or honour. (Sh.) ― -b4- naEa$uwA Almay~ita also signifies They carried the dead man upon the naEo$ , q. v. (q. v. infra) in the TA.]) ― -b5- nuEi$a EalaY jinaAratihaA A naEo$ [q. v.] was made for her bier. (Mgh, from a trad. of, or relating to, Fátimeh.)

definition: He rose; or became raised, or lifted up: (TA:) he rose after his stumble, or trip: (S, A, Msb, K:) and in like manner you say of a bird, (A, TA,) meaning it rose [ after falling or alighting ], (TA,)...
sourceDefinition: He rose; or became raised, or lifted up: (TA:) he rose after his stumble, or trip: (S, A, Msb, K:) and in like manner you say of a bird, (A, TA,) meaning it rose [ after falling or alighting ], (TA,) and he raised his head. (TA.) Hence the saying, taEasa falA A@notaEa$a May he fall, having stumbled, or stumble and fall, and not rise [ again ]: a form of imprecation. (TA.) And hence the saying of 'Omar, AinotaEi$o naEa$aka A@ll~`hu Rise thou: may God raise thee: or nE$k All~`h has here one of the two meanings assigned to it before, in 1. (TA.) ― -b2- [And hence,] (tropical:) He recovered, or became recovered, from his embarrassment, or difficulty. (A, TA.)

definition: A state of elevation, or exaltation.
sourceDefinition: A state of elevation, or exaltation. (Sh.) See 1. ― -b2- A state of remaining; lastingness; endurance; permanence; or continuance; syn. baqaA='N . (Sh, K.) -A2- [ A kind of litter, or] a thing resembling a miHaf~ap , upon which the king used to be carried. when sick: (IDrd, Msb, K:) not the naEo$ of a corpse. (IDrd, Msb.) This is said to be the primary application. (TA) ― -b2- And hence, (TA,) A bier, (S, A, Msb, K,) when the corpse is upon it. for otherwise it is called sriyrN : (S, IAth, Msb:) it is called by the former name because of its height, or its being raised: (S, TA.) pl. nuEuw$N : (Msb:) also, a reticulated thing. (Az. Mgh, TA,) resembling a mHaf~p , (Mgh,) which is put as a cover over a [ dead ] woman when she is placed upon the bier; (Az, Mgh, TA;) but this is properly called HarajN , though people called is naEo$N , which is properly only the bier itself. (Az, TA.) ― -b3- [And hence,] banaAtu naEo$i AlkuboraY [or banaAtu naEo$a AlkuboraY , together with naEo$N or naEo$u , constitute (assumed tropical:) The constellation of Ursa Major: or the principal stars thereof: ] seven stars; whereof four [ which are in the body ] are called naEo$N [or naEo$u ], and three [ which are in the tail ] are called banAtN , (S, K,) i. e., bnAt nE$ (TA:) and to like manner AlS~ugoraY , (K,) or bnAt nE$ AlS~ugoraY [together with nE$ AlS~ugoraY constitute [ the constellation of Ursa Minor: or the principal stars thereof; seven in number; whereof the four in the body are called nE$ , and the there in the tail are called bnAt ]: (S:) [the former four] said to be likened to the bearers of a bier, because they form a square: (IDrd, TA:) [the bnAt being so called as being likened to damsels or to men for bnAt is pl. of AibonN applied to an irrational thing as well as pl. of binotN ) following a bier:] Sb and Fr agree that nE$ is imperfectly decl. because determinate and of the fem. gender: (S:) or it is perfectly decl. when indeterminate, but not when determinate [by having the epithet AlkuboraY or AlS~ugoraY added to it]: (Aboo-'Amr Ez-Záhid, K:) banw naEo$i also occurs, in poetry; (Sb, S, K;) because a single one [of the stars thereof] is called Abonu naEo$i , (Lth, K,) being made to accord. in gender with kawokabN ; but when they say valaAv or A^arobaE , they say banaAt : (Lth, TA:) [this is agreeable with a general rule; accord. to which, banaAtN is the pl. of AibonN applied to anything but a human being:] the pl. of bnAt nE$ is Aln~awaAEi$u ; like as A^abaAriSu is pl. of saAm~u A^abaraSa . (L, TA.) See also nuEayo$N . ― -b4- Also naEo$N A piece of wood, (K, TA,) of the length of twice the stature of a man, (TA,) upon the head of which is a piece of rag, (K, TA,) called HarajN , (TA,) with which young ostriches are hunted or captured. (K, TA.)

(TA,) She (a goat) did what was like sneezing ( navarato [app. meaning scattered forth moisture or the like ]) with her nose: (ADk, S, K:) or sneezed. (K.) It is said in a proverb, laA tanofiTu fiyhi EanaAqN meaning (assumed tropical:) Blood-revenge will not be taken for him; i. e. for this slain person. definition: A hand ulcerated by work: or blistered, or vesicated;

sourceDefinition: [The ichneumon; so called in the present day;] a certain small beast. (IKt, El-Fárábee, S, M, Msb, K,) broad, as though it were a piece of qadiyd [or salted or sun-dried flesh-meat ]. (S) found in the land of Egypt, (S, K, *) one of the most malignant of wild animals, (M,) that kills the [ kind of serpent called ] vuEobaAn : (IKt. ElFárábee, S, M, Msb, K:) the keeper of vines or palm-trees or seed-produce ( Aln~aAZirN ) takes it for his use, when he is in vehement fear of serpents of the kind above mentioned: for it attacks them, making itself thin and slender as though it were a piece of rope; and when it winds itself upon them, they draw back their breath vehemently, and it take their breath; thus the serpent becomes inflated in its inside, and is cut asunder: (TA.) or i. g. Aibonu EirosK [the weasel ]: (IKt, TA:) or a certain small beast, resembling the cat, generally frequenting gardens; accord. to IF, also called dalaqN [q. v.]; (Msb;) the beast called dalaho [the Persian original of dalaqN ]; [see Aibonu miqoraDK , in art. qrD ;] called nms from nam~asa in the first of the senses explained above: (A;) or i. q. ZaribaAnN : (El-Mufaddal Ibn-Selemeh, TA:) from these various sayings, it appears that several species are called by this name: (TA:) pl. [of pauc.] A^anomaAsN (TA) and [of mult.] numuwsN . (Msb.) You say, fiY Aln~aAsi A^anomaAsN [app. meaning, Among men are some that are malignant as the animals called AnmAs ]. (A. TA.)

definition: A secret: (Seer, M:) [pl.
sourceDefinition: A secret: (Seer, M:) [pl. nawaAmiysu .] ― -b2- [Hence, app., rather than from the Greek νόμος as some have supposed,] Revelation. So in a trad respecting fines for bloodshed: in which it is said, qaDayota fiynaA biAln~aAmuwsi [ Thou hast pronounced judgment respecting us according to revelation ]. (Mgh.) [Bat see a remark on this signification in what follows.] ― -b3- [And hence,] The law of God. (KT.) ― -b4- [And from the first,] An evasion, artifice, or expedient, by which a man conceals himself; expl. by maA yan~amisu bihi Alr~ajulu mina AlA_iHotiyAli ; (S;) or maA tunum~isa bihi mina AlA_iHotiyaAli (K [but here, app., tunum~sa is a mistake for tan~amisu :]) deceit; guile; circumvention. (A, TA.) You say, fulaAnN SaAHibu naAmuwsK , and nawaAmiysa , Such a one is a person of deceit, &c., and of deceits. &c. (A, TA.) And hence the phrase nawaAmiysu AlHukamaA='i [app. meaning The artifices of the wise men ]. (TA) ― -b5- [Also, in post classical writings, A man's honour, or reputation which should be preserved inviolate; syn EiroDN .] ― -b6- [The remaining significations I regard as being derived from those above mentioned; supposing a prefixed noun to be understood; in some instances, SaAHib , or *uw ; in others, makaAn , or maHal~ ] ― -b7- A confidant; one who possesses, or is acquainted with, secrets, or private affairs; (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) of a king, (Mgh, TA,) or governor, or prince, (A,) or other man; (A'Obeyd, S, M, Msb, TA;) whom are acquaints with his private affairs, and distinguishes by revealing to him what he conceals from others: (A'Obeyd, S:) or one who possesses, or is acquainted with, secrets, or private affairs, of a good nature: (K, TA:) and jaAsuwsN signifies one who possesses, or is acquainted with, secrets, or private affairs of an evil nature. (TA.) [The author of the Mgh thinks that the second of the significations mentioned above, i. e. “ revelation, ” is derived from this; a prefixed noun [such as kitaAb , perhaps,] being understood.] Hence, (Mgh,) Aln~Amuwsu , (A'Obeyd, S, M, Msb, K,) or Aln~aAmuwsu AlA^akobaru , (A, TA,) is applied to [ The angel ] Gabriel; (A'Obeyd, S, M, A, &c.) by the people of the scriptures; [meaning, the Christians, and perhaps, the Jews also;] (S, Mgh;) because God has distinguished him by communicating to him revelations and hidden things with which no other is acquainted. (TA.) ― -b8- A repository ( wiEaA=' ) of knowledge. (M.) ― -b9- Skilful; intelligent. (K, * TA.) ― -b10- One who enters into affairs with subtle artifice. (As, K. *) ― -b11- A calumniator: syn. nm~aAmN ; (K;) as also ↓ nam~aAsN . (A, K.) ― -b12- A liar. (M.) ― -b13- The burking-place, or covert. ( qutorap , q. v.,) of a hunter, (S, M, A, K,) in which he lies in wait for the game: (TA:) sometimes written with ' [ naA^omuwsN ;] but for what reason [says ISd] I know not. (M.) ― -b14- A snare: syn. $arakN : (K:) because it is concealed beneath the ground. (TA.) ― -b15- The covert. or retreat. of a lion; as also ↓ naAmuwsapN . (K.) ― -b16- The chamber. or cell, of a monk. (TA, K, * voce taA^umuwrN )

sourceDefinition: , first pers. wadidotu , (S, M, L, Msb, K, &c.) and wadadotu , (Ks, Z, K,) [but most disallow this] aor. yawad~u , inf. n. wud~N and wid~N and wad~N , (S, M, L, K,) of which three forms the first is the most common, (MF,) and mawad~apN , (S, M, L, K,) or this last is a simple subst., (Msb,) and miwad~apN (CK and some MS. copies of the K) and mawid~apN , (accord. to some other copies of the K, this and the next preceding deviating from the common forms of inf. ns., TA,) and mawodidapN (M, Kz, K) and mawodadapN , (TA,) but these last two are allowable only in poetry, and deviate from constant rule, the former doubly, (Kz, MF, TA,) and widaAdN and wadaAdN and wudaAdN , (M, L, K,) the first of which last three forms is the most common, (MF,) and wadaAdapN (M, L, K) and, accord. to some, widaAdapN and wudaAdapN , (MF, TA,) and, as in a copy of the K esteemed of good authority, mawoduwdapN , (TA,) He loved, or affected, him, or it, (S, M, L, Msb, K,) i. e. any means of attaining or doing good. (AZ, M, L.) The form wadadotu is disallowed by the Basrees who hold it to be erroneous: and Zj says, We know that Ks did not mention wadadotu without having heard it; but he heard it from him who was no authority. (T, L.) ― -b2- A^awodidohu , an imp. form [of ↓ A^awad~ahu ], without idghám, accord. to the dial. of El-Hijáz, occurs in a trad., meaning Love thou it, or affect it. (L.) ― -b3- wadidotu lawo tafoEalu *`lika . and wadadotu lawo A^an~aka tafoEalu *`lika , (S, L,) aor. as above, inf. n. wud~N and wad~N and wadaAdapN (S, L, Msb) and wadaAdN (S, L) or widaAdN , (T, in TT,) I wished that thou wouldest do that. (S, L.) ― -b4- wadidotu lawo kaAna ka*aA I wished that it had been so. (Msb.) ― -b5- wadidotu Al$~aYo'a I wished for the thing. Fr says, This is the more approved form; but some say wadadotu : in both cases the aor. is yawad~a only. (L.) [Respecting the latter form of the pret., see above.] This is a secondary signification of the verb. (TA.)

definition: A skin ( siqaA'N ) in which milk is put, (S, K,) specially used for that purpose: (S:) or a skin in which are put clarified butter and milk: (Mejma' el-Bihár, &c.
sourceDefinition: A skin ( siqaA'N ) in which milk is put, (S, K,) specially used for that purpose: (S:) or a skin in which are put clarified butter and milk: (Mejma' el-Bihár, &c.:) it is made of the skin of an animal such as is termed ja*aEN , [ meaning a goat in its second year, ] or what is above that [ in age ]: (ISk, S, K:) the skin of a sucking kid, in which milk is put, is called $akowapN ; and that of one that is weaned, badorapN ; and the like of a $kwp , in which clarified butter is put, Euk~apN ; and the like of a bdrp , misoA^adN : (ISk, S:) see also badorapN : pl. of pauc. A^awoTubN , and of mult. wiTaAbN (S) and A^awoTaAbN , (dev. with respect to analogy, (TA,) [accord. to most grammarians; but not so accord. to Fr, because its first radical letter is w ;] and pl. pl. (i. e. pl. of AwTb , TA,) A^awaATibu . (K.) ― -b2- waTobN (tropical:) A hard, rough, rude, or coarse, man: syn. rajulN jaAfK . (S, K.) ― -b3- waTobN (tropical:) A large breast: (K:) likened to the skin so called. (TA.) ― -b4- Safiratu wiTaAbuhu (tropical:) He died: or he was slain: (K:) the body's becoming empty of the soul is compared to the skin's becoming empty of the milk: or the meaning is his blood issued forth from his body: or, as some say, his skins became empty of their milk; a hostile attack having been made upon his camels, and no milch camel remaining in his possession. (TA.) [See similar sayings voce rfodN ; and see Ham., p. 34.]
